As you can see, I've hardly played this game at all.  This is mainily due to the fact that I don't enjoy spending log que times waiting to join a game, which will happen if you download this game.  I did manage to get into a few battles despite the long wait times, and this is what I found:
Graphics:  Very good.   I was excited at first due to the good graphics and realistic feel, it reminded me of my favorite WW2 FPS, Red Orchestra 2/Rising Storm.
Controls:  I like the fact that you can customize the controls to what you're used to using.
I didn't try the 'generals' portion as you need to reach a higher tier, again I haven't played much at all so I'm only speaking on the FPS portion.  Riding the bicycle was pretty cool also.
Realism:  Aside from good graphics, the realism absolutely sucks.  I snuck up to a capture territory, as it was being captured, and sure enough, I spot a german in there.  I take careful aim with my beautifully textured M1 Garand, line it right up on his chest, and fire 3 times.  I get a message that he has 'taken damage', then he promptly turns and shoots once, killing me instantly.
Now I don't claim to be a medical expert or anything, however if a person is hit 3 times with a .30-06 round, I tend to imagine that he will not be in any shape to fight back.  After reading more on this game, I realize it is truly PTW.  I'll go back to my favorite WW2 FPS, RO2, where 1 shot from a high caliber rifle will put your foe down.  It's not PTW and it's worth every penny I paid for the full game.
I realize this game is early access and will revise this review if the developers fix these problems, I believe this game has potential but I would rather pay to purchase a game and not have it be a pay to win game.

When it comes to Call of Duty, I kinda lost interest after Modern Warfare 3. Black Ops 2 still held up and I thought to myself that let's see if IW can top Treyarch with the latest CoD. As it turns out, Call of Duty: Ghosts may be the worst purchase I have made this year.
Let's start off with 6-7 hour single player. The story itself is ridiculous. It barely makes any sense and a majority of the characters are bland and completely forgettable. It's usually a bad sign when I actually want most of the good guys to die a horrible painful death. On top of the story and lame characters the game is littered with quick time events, a game concept I absolutely hate if used in the wrong way. I can understand a QTE every now and then and if they're done well. In this game, they slow the game down and it feels like a chore every time one pops up. If we need to jump out of a helicopter to start the stage, the game can do it for us. If we need to rappel up onto a catwalk, I don't want to hold 'F' to do it. It breaks the immersion from the game and you don't feel accomplished when it's done. It's literally "Push button, you are winner!". No thought and very boring. And where did the branching storyline from Black Ops 2 go? It may have not been anything new in games, but it was new and interesting in CoD as a series. But nope, IW needs to be as arrogant as possible when it comes to expanding upon things made by Treyarch. IW, you can advertise your single player for having a writer who has won multiple awards writing your game, it's not gonna change the fact that this story is crap, and it's only made worse by the lack of enjoyable gameplay. (And that twist ending... With that scene alone you just made a majority of the CoD: Ghosts campaign null and void and are already sequel baiting for CoD: Ghosts 2)
Multiplayer, on the other hand, is the same as ever, if not a little worse. If you like IW CoD multiplayer before, you'll probably like it now. If you liked Black Ops 2 (I admit, I feel it's on par with CoD4), then you will be disappointed. Most of the new good features that Treyarch implimented into BO2 are nowhere to be seen. I think the only feature that survived was a strange version of the loadout points, except now they determine the amount of perks. There's a few new gamemodes that I find interesting and such. I don't know how many of them are original ideas and how many of them have been done before, but new gamemodes are always fun. But with the game as is, it's the same old CoD on the same old downward slope as the series has been on since MW2 (or what I think at least)... And where's theater mode!?
The only gamemodes left to talk about are Squad mode and Extinction mode. To be honest I hadn't tried Squad mode, but I probably won't either, due to lack of overall interest in the game already. I tried Extinction mode, and to be honest, it's not that bad. As horde modes go, I liked it and it is on par with Treyarchs Zombie mode. However, it's nothing game changing. It doesn't help the game in any way really. I think the only reason they did it is because Treyarchs Zombie mode was popular and Activision just wanted to milk some more money out of another horde mode. Extinction isn't bad, but it doesn't save the game either.
On top of all of these things, the PC port just seems dreadful. Plenty of FPS drops all around, and I've heard that the PC version might be locked at a low framerate. I haven't even really checked for my max FPS, but I've heard others have had a problem like this before. Also, this might be a problem on my end, but I can't seem to get the game to run on my native resolution (1920x1080), which does bug me a lot. It often opens in a borderless window instead of the fullscreen I wanted. IW, do you just hate PC gamers?
Now I'm almost always on the line that graphics don't make a good game, but I think it needs to be mentioned: for a "Next Gen CoD" the graphics are far from impressive. It still looks pretty much the same as MW2 or MW3. If this is what it's like to step into the next gen of CoD, then please count me out.
Overall, both this game and this port are terrible. The single player is forgettable, the multiplayer is less impressive and the extra modes are not a selling point. I think I used about 50-60€ on this game when I bought it and I feel that this is the worst thing I have spent it on this year. Just do yourself a favour and don't buy this game. Or if you really feel the need to buy this game, if you absolutely positively have to get this game, then I suppose you could buy it on a console. But honestly, I still wouldn't recommend this game. I don't know how to play this game. Even after many hours playing (not enough I might add), there's still a lot of complexity that goes over my head and helps to immerse me in the game.
Today, the games graphics do not hold up all that well, but what they lack in appeal they make up for with performance. With hundreds of troops battling on screen in some fairly large environments, as well as all the activity going on on the world map, M&B manages to keep your frames high and provide some rather spectacular battles. The soldiers don't have many animations but react well when killed. That said, if you're looking for a beautiful game you're in the wrong franchise (until Bannerlord is released). Hearing arrows wiz past as you charge into the enemy ranks is very thrilling, and the sounds of men roaring and swords striking shields helps immerse yourself in the battle. And of course, hearing your men shout "Victory!" as you wreck an enemies forces makes you feel unstoppable! There is however a rather large lack of dialogue in the game and some units or NPC's could greatly benefit from a few more generic lines of dialogue.
Gameplay is complex but feels fairly fluid, there's quite a lot you can do ranging from organising your ranks to managing inventories to charging into battle yourself. It does suffer from certain OP tactics and weapons, such as the lance or backpeddling while blocking to avoid damage. For content, not much can be said other than YOU WILL NEVER RUN OUT OF THINGS TO DO, thanks especially to the modding community for when you master the base game.
Overall the game isn't the greatest looking, but makes up for it with performance, immersive gameplay, a world's worth of content, and some satisfying battle sounds. If you're looking for a fairly hardcore RPG with a lot of content, you've come to the right place.=

First off i'd like to say that i've tried to make this review as unbiased as I can.
Pros:
Really interesting new story, with nice cinematics. A little too linear for my taste but I really enjoyed some of the new features (like driving helis and tanks)
Pretty good audio and music
Good graphics ONLY if you have a beast gaming rig. I couldn't play Ghosts at all on my computer, it came up with an error that couldn't be fixed, but luckily i managed to get it going on a family computer. At the moment I can run it on lowest settings (except image quality, so i have the top resolution) with a moderate fps.
Larger maps in multiplayer!
Less air based streaks
Well designed maps with logical features
Hit detection is quite a bit better than Mw3 I find :)
Extinction mode is fun
Squads bots are actually sort of smart!
MP Music has a Crysis 2 feel at certain points
No OP gun like Mw3s Mp7! Most weapons seem pretty balanced
This is kinda off topic but on lower graphics some moments in SP took me back to the Cod4 days, only briefly.
Cons:
You drop super fast in MP
Very buggy spawns, even in the biggest maps I spawn right in front of enemies. Also I seem to spawn where they can shoot me, but when they spawn it's right behind me so they get me too..
Slight menu lag
A few weapon animations are copied from previous CoDs, most obviously the Bizon and the Remington R5
Not fun to play if you have a low resolution and lag lots
SP AI seem a bit dumb, if only they were like the squads bots
Poorly optimized for PC. Not many options for audio and other things, buttons for the menu seem to be directly ported from consoles just with a different key name (I.E. press f2 to customize soldier)
customization is sort of bland. We were promised loads and loads of combinations to make our characters unique, but no matter what you do with your limited unlocked items the soldier always seems to look the same (also, we are shown multiple character camos that 'change' depending on the map, but they all tend to revert to the default blueish one)
Extinction mode does not alter its difficulty if a player loses connection and only 3 or 2 players remain, meaning it's harder to survive and destroy more hives.
Overall a good buy IF you can run it well!! I suggest you get a friend that has it, have him let you log into his account on your computer and install ghosts, then try it before you buy it.
I think it has been a bit of a let down due to consoles getting more attention by the developers at IW, definitely not as solid and FPS as the Modern Warfares.
I am pretty happy with it, although i missed double xp on release due to the error i mentioned in the Pros.
A lot of people who are not game developers like myself don't understand how hard it is to make a game like this, I definitely was expecting more from IW, but it is what it is now, so give it a go if you can run it!

Call of Duty: Ghosts is a little brother simulator.
You play Logan somethingsomething and you're dad is a ghost (Not like Patrick Swayze), some sort of phantasm-based special forces unit that he told you about moments before GI Joe 2: The rise of Cobra entered the game in the prologue.♥♥♥♥♥♥happens for some reason, the european union (which is now entirely spanish) has invaded America and some other guy is trying to kill your guys because he used to be one of your guys.
Its a strange game because you're there. You're walking around. Fighting.♥♥♥♥♥♥is happening, but you're rarely ever really involved. Oh, you have to shoot EVERYONE because the elite special forces ghost-men will clump behind the same cover and bark at you to get moving. A lot. They'll also walk past bad guys all the damn timed, but I don't blame them because everyone looks the same. But when it comes to opening doors, advancing the plot or, god help, you anything else its time you sat back and let the big boys handle it.
There is also a dog that you share an (Implied) psychic connection with, like its AD&D and its you're familiar. But its there, then its not, then it is, then its shot and then it gets a purple heart and a retirement package.
Other things to watch out for, they've always had a habit of copying scenes from films and using them as set pieces (Because its not theft if its 'homage'), but usually without anything that made the original scene great. Earlier games got it, or at least got some sort of pass, but after so many years its hard to clap at the same tricks. They even call-back to earlier Call of Duty games, just with the effort and attention to detail of someone who works 9/5 in accounting.
It also features the worst tank section of any game I've ever played. Think the tank section from BF3 (because its basically the same thing), but with ugly, muddy textures, tanks that operate like dune buggies on ice and someone screaming in your ear to 'GET MOVING BRAVO' every five seconds. It'd be a little forgiveable if it was pretty, thats what got BF3's campaign off the hook (in my books, at least. Well, that and the last sections).
Its short. Five hours, and that was with a few resets after script errors (movement scripts, not story).
There are extra modes, extinction (Because Zombies is a blackops thing) and Squad mode (You and an AI Team VS another guy and his AI team. Its multiplayer if you dont have the twitch reflexes of someone younger then you)
Its like a bad Tom Clancy novel/game, except even a bad Tom Clancy game is at least interesting. Sort of.

That said, the game was a beautiful and visceral shooter, you have to commend all the movement and combat actions they incorporated into the game. Getting the colorful world to run at the full framerate of my 144Hz monitor was really rewarding and I did overall enjoy the experience. Open world issues aside, I felt the story was very strong and don't regret at all the 13 hours it took to complete.
For anyone looking for immediate and mindless fun, this is one of the best games you could get. But any fan of its predecessor and everything it achieved should be prepared for a very different entry.

I don't know how to play this game. Even after many hours playing (not enough I might add), there's still a lot of complexity that goes over my head and helps to immerse me in the game.
Today, the games graphics do not hold up all that well, but what they lack in appeal they make up for with performance. With hundreds of troops battling on screen in some fairly large environments, as well as all the activity going on on the world map, M&B manages to keep your frames high and provide some rather spectacular battles. The soldiers don't have many animations but react well when killed. That said, if you're looking for a beautiful game you're in the wrong franchise (until Bannerlord is released). Hearing arrows wiz past as you charge into the enemy ranks is very thrilling, and the sounds of men roaring and swords striking shields helps immerse yourself in the battle. And of course, hearing your men shout "Victory!" as you wreck an enemies forces makes you feel unstoppable! There is however a rather large lack of dialogue in the game and some units or NPC's could greatly benefit from a few more generic lines of dialogue.
Gameplay is complex but feels fairly fluid, there's quite a lot you can do ranging from organising your ranks to managing inventories to charging into battle yourself. It does suffer from certain OP tactics and weapons, such as the lance or backpeddling while blocking to avoid damage. For content, not much can be said other than YOU WILL NEVER RUN OUT OF THINGS TO DO, thanks especially to the modding community for when you master the base game.
Overall the game isn't the greatest looking, but makes up for it with performance, immersive gameplay, a world's worth of content, and some satisfying battle sounds. If you're looking for a fairly hardcore RPG with a lot of content, you've come to the right place.=

Go in expecting frustrations and flaws, and you might just have a great time.

The open-world freedom provided by this game is offset by the lack of a story and repetitive grinding. The combat gets boring and repetitive too. Still, I recommend it based on the ability it gives you to create your own path, your own story.

Mount & Blade: Warband is the epic medieval adventure game you always wanted that does not follow a story line like Skyrim but is an open sandbox where you are free to do anything. While the Native singleplayer is not the greatest thing in the world you can (If you're like me) find yourself clocking in hour after hour playing it. The game was developed to be easily modded to fix that issue, and the community does not hold back, you can get mods from American Civil War to Zulu Wars.
Single player is one thing, but more importantly we have multiplayer, Mount & Blade can boast 24/7 active servers that can hold up to 200 players. You can play Native multiplayer, Napoleonic wars multiplayer, or get a mod for multiplayer like the mod I listed above "Zulu Wars"
One thing to keep in mind is Warband was actually a low budget game, it is quite apparent hence the graphics are not the most amazing thing in the world, and the animations are a mere decent, but that is more like the cover of a book in this game. What it has to offer inside is amazing and shows overly much potential. Tale World's next game in the Mount & Blade series "Bannerlord" is going to be a high budget game since they got alot of money from Warband. So support this game and it's devs and you can see an even greater game.
Warband and the entire series is definitely a 10/10 and worth every penny.

Charge into battle. Ride into legend. This non-expensive sandbox masterpiece brings together the opportunity to do anything, from being a sellsword bandit mercenary trader to a kingmaking politic-intrigued warband-leading vassal, into strange places such as Calradia's three bickering kingdoms, its adjacent horseloving khanate and the neighbouring haughty sultanate. This game is full of surprises as battlefields change depending on your map's terrain and your party's location.
Inspiring one of the largest modding communities, Mount & Blade holds a great module system which prevents mod conflicts unlike other games (ahem BGS) and lets you fall on your knees to worship the old gods. You could go on an adventure into 1257 where religious war spreads its flame throughout the middle east and engulfs eastern europe, where the golden horde still scours for tribute in places where no king is seated, and where blood and steel would make a peasant into one of his lordships. This module would be one of my personal favorites.
Of course I've left out one of many people's favorites, the multiplayer of Warband. Whether it be cRPG, Napoleonic Wars, or just the native module, the multiplayer experience is enjoyable. Personally, I'm not a big fan of the multiplayer (probably because I don't have anybody to play with) since there are always other games when I want to be competitive. Therefore, I won't say much on multiplayer.
Are you still reading this? Man, you either must be really bored or really skeptical. I would have bought this game right off the bat after I read the words "non-expensive sandbox" but you know, that's just me. If you're into medieval galore, this game is a must buy. If you love sandboxes or maybe games which allows you to build armies and lead them into battle, this game is definitely for you. If you're into steampunkish or cyberpunkish games like the bioshock series and the fallout series respectively, then this game might not be for you. But who knows? You might like it.

They're many good aspects about this game, and many bad, but first the good. You do feel like you are part of a large conflict, yet you are not strewn across the battflefield where you may have to walk 5 miles only to be killed in your mundane trek. Basic infantry vs infantry combat does feel balanced and won't leave you feeling cheated. Those first few matches you'll be facing riflemen and jeeps, all the while having a blast being a gunner, going rambo with your SMG, or using excellent teamwork. This game appears very enticing when you realize that pershing tanks and airplanes await for your efforts, however that can be compared to the cake is a lie.
What makes this game bad is not the controls, the graphics, the sound, nor the RTS/FPS mechanic; it is the P2W mechanic. As you progress in the game you are thrown out of training matches into full blown war. You are armed with a rifle or SMG against swarms of tanks. Will there be an an Anti tank gun waiting in your newly captured position? Nope. You better darn hope one of your mates has a bazooka or a stuart, and that they know how to use it. With your m1 or 43 rifle you face swarms of snipers, aircraft, and tanks to add to it. You are merely cannon fodder in this ludicrous mess. This is no longer a war for you, but survival. See a sniper in the distrance? Have him in your sights? Pull the trigger and it'll take 4 rounds, as for your bewildered target just a 1 on you. They're only two solutions in this scenario, one is to fork out actual cash for better weapons and equipment, or grind to the point that you can finally purchase that bazooka or sniper rifle you longed for.
Say you went with the latter, like me. You run out onto the field waiting in ambush, or pushing with a strike force, decimating tanks left and right; saving the lives of your squad and yourself. Alast, this can't last forever as P2W puts an end to your triumph. That expensive bazooka came with 50 rounds to stop your foes over all matches, no not one match, all matches. You can find a resupply crate but you ain't getting more rockets. Here's the deal, you can spend in game currency, you earned, on another 50 rounds or pay actual money for it. Like War Thunder or WOT, most players would choose the former, however this game creates a dilemma. The cost was 22,800 of in game currency for another 50 rockets. In perspective that was nearly all I earned for 10 matches. I would have had no funds to upgrade my arsenal, or my current weapons; all that effort for some more ammo. The only way out of this cycle is an insanse level of grinding, or your bank account funds. I'm sure this holds true for much more than what I experienced.
This game has an excellent concept going for it, backed up by solid infantry gameplay and a sense you are making a difference in a large conflect, however its boggled down by far too much. Balance issues between the Americans and Germans, a glitchy auto match system, and to top it off a P2W structure that is all too sadly obvious. I would like to see this game suceed, but so far it's an unwelcoming experience.

TL;DR Version:
Pros: Experience World War 2, bicycles, a mix of FPS and RTS and intense teamwork gameplay (if the team works that is)
Cons: Pay2Win, hours upon hours of grinding, unbalanced and unoptimized
Long but, detailed version:
I really wanted to recommend this. But now I just can't.
Let's start with the good. You get to experience World War 2 with dozens of players and strangely enough, you get to ride bicycles. This game is also teamwork heavy and it can turn for the worst if your team doesn't cooperate. Like say if you have a griefer or a nazi spawn killer hidden nearby.
This is also a strategy game as well once you get to the rank of General. I never gotten to General rank so, you'll have to experience it yourself.
But, here's where the bad comes in.
First, whenever you unlock and buy something, it's for your soldier only. If you get another soldier, you'll have to unlock and buy them again. Which means, you're constantly grinding to get better with each new soldier you get.
Hey developer, this isn't an old fashioned RPG game on the Nintendo where you have to grind experience to get stronger. Unnecessary grinding makes the game just unenjoyable and flat out boring to play. It's common sense that no one likes to grind up in order to become better than everyone else. It's bad game development and it bores the player to the extreme.
And another thing. I also hate it when I join a server to where we have jeeps and bicycles, where the Germans have are tanks and planes. This is unbalanced gameplay to the max and needs to be taken care of because, no one wants to spend hours upon hours grinding ranks just to get what the germans got. But then again, World War 2 wasn't fair to begin with so, I'll let this slip by.
This game is also a bit buggy and is poorly optimized. I've played this until suddenly I got frame drops. Now don't start that "your computer is a toaster" bullcrap because, that's not the case here. I can run Farcry 3 with my computer.
The hitboxes are also broken as heck. I could be just shooting at someone and I would see blood spray out of them, but guess what? It didn't even hit him. He just shrugged it off like he was Ironman. How do I prove this you say? Because a notification pops up saying "Damaged "player name." I hit him with my Grease Gun and I saw blood. No damage notifcation. Hense, he didn't get hit for some dumb reason.
Developer, please do me a favor and play other MMO  games and see what makes them better like Team Fortress 2 for instance before you start making a good  MMO  game. Change this game from a Pay2Win to a Play2Win. Change it from an unbalanced and unfair game, to a balanced and fair game.
If you don't fix any of these issues, the distant future of this game is hours upon hours of wasted development. Not to mention the amount of credits you get are wasted upon refilling your grenades and fixing your vehicle seems a bit cheaper than refilling grenades.

Minimal GUI immerses you even more. I haven't tried Generals yet though. Runs at a decent FPS on my machine (modest gaming machine), which is more than I can say for other early access games.
Cons: The bullets you fire seem, for lack of other terms, "slow" to me. Like they don't hit the target as soon as they should. Aiming is, well, as difficult as I expect it would be to use those old weapons in real life.  So far, every match i have played was on the same map with the same vehicles, which were only bikes. I haven't tried Generals yet though.
So, overall, it's pretty good for an early access game, I can definitely see a LOT of potential for this game, and I do enjoy playing it.

Interesting game concept. Progression is very slow but feels incredibly rewarding. There is a significant difficulty curve, but after a few hours of practise and a few tutorials you shouldn't have any problems competing with other more experienced players. Vehicles and more complicated game mechanics can take a while to understand, and there aren't many tutorials past a "beginner's guide."
PROS:
-Fun and original game mechanics
-Very satisfying kills
-True sense of progression, rewards feel rewarding
-Tactical gameplay, actions must be well thought out
CONS:
-Poor load times on startup
-Low resolution textures on terrain etc
-Connectivity and ping issues, not many lowe-ping servers
-Vehicles and weapons can be buggy/unresponsive
With all this said, you need to keep in mind the game is still in beta, and was only recently released on steam. I'm sure the quality will improve given time and frequent updates.

This was the game of the series that I had heard the most about from reading reviews and whatnot. This is the first game where I’ve actually found real enjoyment from playing it and I’m so glad that most of my biggest issues with Far Cry 2 were extinct when I played this one. For once, I’ll actually be talking about how good the game is and just not relentlessly bash it.
In this game, your character Jason Brody and his friends were on vacation and after skydiving over a random island get captured by natives/slavers. You escape and have to explore the island, rescue your friends, and help the natives, the Rakyat, deal with pirates. It’s a simple premise, but it definitely works. The island is beautiful. This is by far the best looking game in the series so far. It’s exciting to wander around seeing all the various plant life, the waterfalls, and everything else the island has to offer. It’s a gorgeous game.
This is once again an open world shooter, which means you can approach missions however you like. Once the game finally gave me a sniper rifle with a silencer attachment, I was unstoppable. There are outposts you can clear of pirates all over the island, and for me, all I would do is snipe all of them and go undetected most of the time. Unlike the previous game, when you clear out an outpost, the Rakyat warriors move in and hold the outpost, and there will be fewer to no pirates spawning in the area ever again. This was one of my top 2 problems in Far Cry 2 eradicated. Awesome.
The wildlife…what can I say? There’s a variety of wildlife that you can hunt, or be hunted by, for you to collect pelts to craft upgrades. The crafting system is pretty good, letting you create things to restore health, enhance senses to detect enemies or wildlife, increase ammo capacity, or carry more money. As for the wildlife, there’s goats and deer, as well as more exotic creatures like komodo dragons and tigers. Tigers are really annoying to deal with if you run into them a lot early in the game like I did, but it keeps you on your toes and keeps your twitchy trigger finger happy. If you feel slightly less adventurous, you can just hit the animals with a vehicle. This was the best method I found to reliably kill skarks, using the propeller blades of the boat to decimate them. I ended up getting most of my upgrades done pretty early in the story.
There’s a couple types of side missions you can do, such as hunting rare animals, knife assassination missions, types of racing missions, and various others which I haven’t really tried. Aside from the hunting the rare animals to get all the best upgrades, I didn’t really bother with doing other side missions because they just weren’t all that interesting to me, and I got bored of them pretty quickly.
There’s a skill system which is solid. You get xp from kills and missions and everything just as you would expect, and when you earn skill points from getting enough xp, you can put points into one of three skill trees to increase things like your survivability, how fast you can reload, boost accuracy, new types of takedowns, and all sorts of things. There are few skills I would call useless which makes deciding where to use skill points all that much harder.
I think my only major problem with this game is that the stupid, inhumanly smart AI from both of the previous games is back, and god is it annoying. I tend to use weapons with silencers on them so that I can stealth kill from afar. Yet when I happen to miss a shot just barely, or even when I kill someone who was near another enemy, they know exactly where to look for me somehow. How? Do they just happen to automatically know the bullet trajectory? It makes sniping a little bit harder, and on one particular outpost, clearing it out this way was just impossible, and I had to clear out waves of reinforcements before finally claiming it for the Rakyat. Also, AI pixel perfect accuracy is still bull.
Far Cry 3 is the game that finally gets me to genuinely like the series. The only real frustration I had was caused mostly by my own incompetence rather than bad game design, which is definitely good. It improves upon everything that made the previous two games unique and/or good, and for me at least, finally made the game enjoyable. Everything is better, the wildlife is a unique challenge at times, the story is interesting, and the game is just gorgeous.
TL;DR Best game in the series so far, with few major flaws

It advertises itself as an MMOFPS, but really it is no more an MMOFPS than CoD or Battlefield in the grand scheme.  If you were looking for a WW2 Planetside, than you will be disappointed.
That said there are some other flaws, still keeping in mind this is a beta, and this is only from my experience as infantry.  For one, the movement seems clunky, and the game feels dated despite being relatively recent.  It doesn't seem to really offer anything new over previous releases of the same nature.
Some good qualities though was that it was very easy to pick up and play, and didn't try to ram any strange mechanics down your throat.  It also does force you to move a bit more tactically as infantry, using cover, and trying to get the drop on your enemies rather than just run and gun everywhere.  The weapons out the gate seem decent with maybe some tweaks here or there, but that is a minor issue.  SMGs are good close but terrible at range, but seem to lack alot of recoil, rifles tend to be better at range but ok up close and reward good trigger discipline.  Grenades have a cool "aim" mechanic that forces you to arc it properly, but the coolness of this is diminished by clunky motion and design.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game at it's current Beta state.  That said, it could be better given some enhancements to motion fluidity, gun tweaks, and trying to offer something slightly more than what my first impression gave me.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a fun, adventurous RolePlaying Game set in the Medieval Era. As a newcomer to the world you must work your way across the map and across nations to build riches and survive.
I've played Mount & Blade since the original version and I have always loved it. It's a very open game, there is no actual aim. You make your own goal and something to aim for. That might sound boring for some, but it makes the game a lot more open. Before the game starts, you need to make your characters back story. This shapes their starting attributes.
Once you emerge into the world you will discover that you can literally do anything. You can be a merchant for nations, become a raging lunatic and crush farmers, or become a honourable knight and fight for the Lords of the land.
There are many different factions you can fight for or against, all of them have their different units and lands.
There are many good points to this game:
1) It's fully open world, you do whatever, whenever.
2) The combat system is not the best, but it gets the game going.
3) A wide range of horse mounts and siege situations to experience.
4) The combat areas are pretty much always different.
5) You can have 100 man vs 100 man battles. They are hectic, but so much fun.
Alas, when there are pros, there are cons.
1) The multiplayer is very difficult as all the players insta-kill you with giant swords.
2) The AI can be a bit buggy at times, but otherwise they are well made.
Overall, Mount & Blade: Warband is a very enjoyable expansion to the original as it brings new ideas, factions and units to the game. If you played or haven't played the original, but enjoy open world RPG's; I strongly recommend this game

*Note: I just recently realized this game was on steam, so I have far more hours into it, than what steam suggests.  Guesstimating at this point, probably around 30-40 hours as of now*
With the gaming market being saturated with modern and futuristic shooters, sometimes it feels nice to revisit a genre that had faded out in the past years: The World War II shooter.  I was quite a fan of Battlefield 1942 back in the day, and what better way to recapture that feeling than…
Heroes and Generals, though currently in open beta, is a free to play WW2 shooter available on steam, or you can play straight through browser if you wish.  It does have a class system, though you must unlock them through progression, which is done in an interesting fashion.  You start as infantry, and as you level up through the 14 ranks in the game, you unlock other branches of soldier you can you can transfer to (for a fee, earned currency or paid currency).  Don’t worry, once you transfer, you always have the option to transfer somewhere else (again for a fee, earned or paid).
Each class has their own bonuses, but often have disadvantages as well.  For example, tank crewmen can spawn tanks but are limited to smgs in their weapon load out.  Another example would be infantry being able to use a bolt-action rifle, but only recon can use scopes and other attachments.
You also have perks you can unlock through completing challenges, which give you combat badges you can equip on your soldier like a Call of Duty perk.  These get greater bonuses as you level them up and ultimately reach “gold” level which give you a huge bonus in which ever perk you selected.  For example, there is a a perk for longer sprinting called “marathon man” that starts at 15% more sprint, but can be leveled to 50%.
When you first create an account, you will be asked to choose your faction, you only have German or US to pick from as of now, and the choice is pretty much cosmetic, as from what I’ve seen, everything appears to be functionally identical.  All weapons you unlock with the character you create will only apply to that character.  You can make more soldiers, but they will start from scratch, so make sure you find the niche you like before moving on to a new one.
The cash shop system is very good, and does not have a “pay to win” feel, as everything can be unlocked through points with some very minor grinding.  No weapon has felt broken, and they all feel to be side-grades of each other.  In short, the cash shop is a good way to get that one weapon you want early, and not have to worry about grinding through points, or profession trees, to earn it.
While it is fun, it’s not perfect yet, the early levels, say 1-3, can have a slight “pay-to-win” feel, as those who’ve thrown in money to get vehicles will have a serious advantage over those who don’t have them.  This part passes very quickly and doesn’t affect every single game.  There are sometimes issues with the matchmaking as well, roughly 1 in every 10 games will have you on a team with small arms vs a team loaded to the teeth in armored vehicles.  Again, this does not happen often either, but you can definitely have hopeless battles from time to time.
My final issue is there is not a huge variety in the maps, there are 3 small maps, with mostly infantry, and 4-5 (from what I could count) Battlefield-style maps with large scale battles with planes and tanks.  This will hopefully get some additions in the future, but don’t be surprised at seeing the same maps over and over.  All maps are “capture point” game-types as well, so if you want more variety, you may want to wait a little bit.
If you loved Battlefield 1942, and have been hoping for a long time to see the game get a face-lift, this might be what you are looking for.  No cost of admission, and have fun conquering your opponents.

Took me about 13.5 hours to beat. Fun mix of action and stealth. The game changes it up and managed to stay interesting even when I was spending extra time with sidequests / taking outposts. First person perspective is a nice change for an open world game for me and I enjoyed the precise shooting mechanics and the customizability of the weapons.
One major complaint is audio fidelity. The audio quality of the voice over is just terrible coming from playing other open world games (like Sleeping Dogs). It's hard to describe, but it just sounds fuzzy and overall unpleasant to hear.
I'm not going to complain about the writing, despite a lot of contrived and unrealistic situations and character behavior - I actually thought it was interesting overall and just wanted to keep playing to see what happened, but I didn't really feel that immersed by it. There's a lot of plot holes and things like that that don't really matter overall - the story is just a device to give you a bit more of a reason to enjoy the core gameplay. It does that fine and does so in an interesting way that made me feel like there was more thought put into it and more to get out of it (in terms of analyzing the deeper meaning of it) than I got from my initial playthrough.
If you like open world games, I think you'll definitely like this. There's lots of activities to do, but, unlike in other games, I felt like I could be powerful enough only spending a small amount of time going out of my way to accomplish them. It doesn't feel overwhelming, but if you want to keep playing after experiencing the main story, there's plenty to do. The movement, geometry, overall area design, and traversal mechanics could've done a lot to harm the open-ness of the game, but I never really got frustrated with things like trying to climb hills or find a good route to sneak around to take over an outpost. The game rewards you with a surprising amount of power as you acquire new guns and skills, but you'll probably feel like you've hit the upper limit about 2/3rds into the game.
If you like FPS games, you'll probably enjoy the variety of guns and quick, satisfying gunplay. Playing on a mouse and keyboard, I found it fun even though most encounters were easily overcome by pulling off headshots. As the game progresses, they change up the enemies in ways that keep the challenge consistent with your skills as you get more experienced with the mechanics.

I've played all the far cries except for 4 (now i'm going to get it), and this was the first one I finished (1 and 2's memory got deleted from the steam cloud). I did, however, complete most of far cry 1's campaign, and did a bit of 2's. From what I've played, I think I like this the best. The AI is very good, so the stealth aspect is fun. It's also encouraged, so if you get in a gunfight, you need to stay back since you can easily die. Overall, this is right up there with the first game for me (the lack of human-monkey hybrid enemies in 3 give it a plus in my book). Now for the campaign. First let me say this: Vaas was amazing! He was ver insane and I really hated him. They did alot of bad things to you and your friends, so you really want to keep playing to get some good old-fashioned revenge. Still, about 3/4 into the campaign, when you go to the second island, the story quits being as interesting. Also, you were trying to save your friends, which was nice and all, but none of the friends really mattered to me. Neither did the protagonist, Jason. He seemed a little cliche, and had average voice acting. Lastly,  the worst things in the game are the heavies on the 2nd island. They are like bullet sponges, and take lots of them to die. I eventually resorted to just throwing c4 at them, but the ones with the flamethrowers still made me rage quite a few times. Still, it was a great game, and it has my seal of approval! Sorry about the infromal review, I just really want to go play FC2's campaign now!

I REALLY recommend this game. Before I go over why however let me tell you something. If you wish to get this game, remember, it's a DLC not a full game. If you want to play this game you will need to buy "Mount and Blade: Warband" AND this.

Along with those are some more melee weapons, some special classes that will be useful depending on the map and more. If you're going to get this game for the singleplayer you're REALLY getting it for the wrong reason. The main kicker for this game is the online mode. Servers sometimes w/ up to 200 people battling it out in Team Deathmatches, Commander Battles and so forth.
I love this game because I personally don't see many games have this time period as their setting so it feels unique. That's not all I like about it though. The combat is something you work on overtime to get yourself constantly better it's not something you can master in an instant. This is nice because that gives you more reason to keep playing. If you could kill anything in your path it would become boring quickly. Most of the maps are also nicely designed and I think this game is a prime example of: "You don't need masterful graphics to be a good game."
So, what are you waiting for, buy this DLC and the game you need for it all for the surprisingly low price of $30.

One of the best FPS single player campaigns I've ever played.
- Very comfortable gameplay. Aiming, running and crouching transitions feels smooth. Stealth is one of the best parts of the gameplay for me. The FOV works better than other games.
- Melee kills :D
- The islands and the variety of environments, caves, interiors, exteriors, on the sea, on the air etc.
- The vehicles, the fauna.
- The tagging system and the multiple approaches to one situation. Curious how much "MGS V The Phantom Pain" ripped of even from the UIs.
- 38 main missions.
- Hard mode is well balanced if you like stealth.
- Vaas Montenegro, Sam Becker and the other characters. There're no tons of cutscenes but you feel every single one of them had some good moments.
- Apocalypse Now references and of course "Ride of the Valkyries" haha! (now I wanna play Blood Dragon again!)
- I find the voice acting very well done and natural for the situations each character goes through
- Visually it looks amazing for its time and even for today's standards. Again...the island the vegetation etc...The character facial expressions are the bests from all Ubisoft games. Even secondary NPC's have good care in details and it's nice the few different kind of shaders like the glossy ones for eyeballs, the more anisotropic looking for hair, bamboo etc and the standard ones. About Ubisoft...personally I hate the work about this aspect in Assassins Creed games. Of course is a different team but a different engine. In this case Dunia Engine 2 which is very optimized and works outstanding.
It's not a con but...The only bad thing that looks completely horrible are the cloud and atmospherics facing camera sprites. The can turn 180° too easy if you break its axis.
- Every time you take a screenshot DOF bokeh looks natural (one of the few games did this on the 7th gen).
-  Oh! I forgot the OST  with In-Game tracks from Die Antwoord, M.I.A., Skrillex and Noisia, Losers and The Glitch Mob for the trailers among others. Also the incidental tracks are outstanding. Another good one "I'm Sorry" by Brian Tyler.
- Now that I play all Far Cry 3 I can say the game is not that far from the retouched screenshots Ubisoft always make public before releasing a game (without mention the E3 demonstration)
- It rainned only once during my whole playthough.
- I would love to had better side-quests. They're not bad but more of those related to the main campaign.
- Who mapped the skills upgrades button to a "double click"? I thought the entire game skills were blocked and I ran through all the mess of explosions and bullets with only two health bars xD...in hard mode... OK, OK...mostly my mistake!
- SPOILER ALERT! Killing Vaas before the end of the game and the lack of a cliche twist about him.
- I can't confirm this but people say multiplayer is not that good.
Is just will say that this game is very valuable.

The fact you can play this game for free and it is quite enjoyable makes it easy to recommend. The best part is how you can have multiple soldiers and customize them to specific roles. It's not really pay to win better tactical moves, good situational awareness, use cover properly and even a level 1 solider will destroy the best equiped player in the game. It's pay to have it a little better and progress a little faster. Unlock cool toys more quickly. Even though tactics are very important this doesn't mean that it is a realistic sim like Arma 3... but it is certainly not a run and gun type game. It is somewhat in between and some of the decisions I believe are for balance and playability over realism. For example if you have a bolt action rifle and someone storms you at close range you can shoot them right in the stomach and it does little to stop them. In real life what would fatal is at an extreme disadvantage at close range. It means you should have the weapon equiped that best fits the range you are fighting at to be most effective.  That is probably a good thing for gameplay but it can be a little frustrating to fire rifle rounds into someone at close range and have it almost be ignored to a degree.
A lot of teams you get put on are very bad. People don't work together and people seem to not quickly get how powerful grenades are and how careful you need to be with them around friendly troops. Just in the past 24 hours our team has lost two games in which I had battled through several defenders to take a control room to only have one of my teammates lob a grenade into it about 30 seconds later and me and himself.
The combined arms are good and reasonably balanced but not perfect. Again I think the developers are doing a good job trying to weigh realism vs gameplay.
If it were not for the over arching leveling and ribbons and upgrades this game would be pretty marginal. But when you have that sense of progression and your character building stronger it makes it more exciting. Still at the core it is hard to call this an MMOFPS. It feels more like a multiplayer game with a very well integrated meta game achievement system on top of it. The feeling of the persistent war and the bigger picture of things or a 'shared world' feeling is pretty much lost. Think LoL or DOTA 2 but in WW 2 and with more players.
If I were going to give it a score I'd say 7.5 but could easily become 8.5 with better balancing, more weapon choices and maybe another couple of specializations.

I recommend this game if you have a powerful enough rig to enjoy its crisp DX11 visuals (thanks to next-gen consoles). Though I notice a lot of players with older, mid-range GPUs complain of FPS lag, the graphics is definitely a step up from its DX9 predecessor, Black Ops 2.
Gameplay and feel is similar to MW3, but with Squad and Extinction mode. So really you get more for your buck than previous IW games. As an aside, I truly enjoyed the Single Player campaign, it's pretty immersive and much better made than Black Ops 2 SP.
Quite upsetting however is the lack of dedicated servers, which enables cheaters to roam freely in any game lobby without swift repurcussions. It will be up to every other player in the lobby to back out and find another lobby, in hopes not to land in another lobby with a cheater, rather than kick the offending player; it's seriously quite aggravating at times.
Overall, I'm having loads of fun in this game, and because of its stunning visuals, immersive SP and added Squad/Extinction content, I recommend this game.

A year ago I did a review of this game, and gave a big thumbs down, however my views have changed.
I gave the game another try, and they fixed almost every issue I had a complaint about.
Lag is gone for the most part, joining a game doesn't take 30 minutes and is reduced to only a couple minutes. (Big Plus)
After the playing for a while and actually enjoying it, I discovered some issues that are still very prevalent.
Your equipment has a life span that requires you to repair it often, not just your guns but your grenades, mines bazookas you name it. Everything has a shelf life. Thats all fine and dandy, but when the cost of repairs is more than you earn in each game you can get to a point where you cant repair your equipment.
And guess what, you can fix your gear with real money.... Not a fan of the repair system.
Also the modification system for your guns seems a bit, unbalanced....
You can modify a sniper rifle to do over 100 damage to personnel, even so it sometimes isn't a one shot kill via chest. So apart from a few quirks that still need fixing, the game is still fun.
Better than battlefield in many respects. No scope glint for you snipers out there. (Love That)
Anyway, its worth a play, you start of with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ equipment and it takes a long time to unlock good stuff, but it's still playable. Good luck

Very fun, well put together game. Plenty of stuff to do in the vanilla game, with hundreds of mods that range from unit skins and textures to entirely new maps and stories. The vanilla version has hours upon hours of playability, and high replayability as well. You throw in mods, and you get even more hours out of it.
You create a hero and embark on a journey to Calradia, the main continent in the game. From there, you begin a tutorial quest (which is optional) and from there, the world is your oyster. Do you become a noble hero, fighting off bandits and war criminals and hunting down wrong doers? Or do you become a cutthroat bandit, raiding villages and peasants? Will you become a lord in service to one of the many kings? Or will you set out to become king yourself? The possibilities are endless, only limited by your imagination.
Combat in my opinion is smooth and works well, and there are a multitude of mods to change it should you not like it. Graphics are decent, and again there are many texture, model, skin, animation, and map mods available. The world is large enough to be interesting to explore and take time to travel, but small enough that you won't get lost and it doesn't take too long to get from point A to point B.
There is multiplayer, and although it is not what I wish it was (a bordelands-ish invite friends to your world) it is very fun, as you engage in battle and siege mode and lead soldiers with and against other players. There is also MP dlc, which places you in the era of muskets and cannons for multiplayer battles. Very fun when you are in the mood for it.
Here you have a great game with many hours of gameplay and high replayability, with heavy mod support and a multiplayer feature that works well. All in all, I'd give it an 8/10 personally, and would highly reccomend it.

Obviously I love this game by how many hours I have put into it. It is very replayable most thanks due to the amazing mods out there. The graphics aren't amazing, but it makes up for it in gameplay. The Mount and Blade series is a one of a kind. Think Total War and Skyrim. You start out as a humble adventurer with a rusty sword and peasants clothing (Sometimes you get a bow or crossbow, depending on what you spent your first skill points on). You then proceed to hiring men in the surrounding villages, eventually training them to full-fledged mounted kinghts, or master archers, while you yourself become a master of whatever you wish. You can capture castles, raid villages, take enemy lords prisoner and then proceed to ransom them off. Or you can become a vassal of one of the existing kings.
The map is filled with bandits, deserters, mercenaries, and enemy parties. The battles start out as somewhere around 5v5 and can scale as high to 500v500. There are mods that allow you to break this cap, enabling you to fight as many as your PC hardware can handle.
Overall this is a pretty entertaining game. The graphics are kinda meh, the animations are good, overall gameplay is good, but the spearman (Rhodok faction) do not know how to properly use their pikes to their advantage. When facing cavalry the run around fighting man vs. man so they get demolished by an cavalry. The factions are unbalanced in strength, but I suppose that is realistic.
If you like to shoot muskets and swing swords, First Peson or Third.. This is the game for you.

Far Cry 3 is a solid game. I recommend it to everyone who enjoys FPS or sandbox genres. It had surprisingly well designed game play which made the game feel fresh for the whole time I played it. Graphics looked good on my 5 year old pc and sounds were even better apart from music. Voice acting was nice and sounds of the jungle felt good if not great. So it is definately a better game than FC2 or first Far cry. What surprised me most is the fact that this game really feels like both of those games thought they were nothing alike when compared to each other.
Sneaking is decently done, and variety of weapons and different missions kept the game going for around 30 hours. Although the jungle looked good, it never really felt in any way threatening and was kinda like walking in a zoo or something. I hope we'll see more dense, darker and frightening jungles in the future. And more varied landscapes, these islands felt a bit too dull in a way that it all looked pretty much the same apart from some swamps. As I realised that the Island looks pretty much the same all around, I kinda stopped looking after the chests and relics. Didn't bother looking for them from the south island at all compared to the fact that around 60 % of the chests in top island was gathered and all the relics.
That being said, I still didn't think this was a GOTY or even 9/10 game. I would give it 8.5/10. Main flaws of the game is the story and the characters. Story is thin and empty: about rescuing your brothers and friends and becoming a "warrior" for the local tribe. The story makes little sense and feels very weird time to time, especially towards the end. The atmosphere changes drastically between characters that are meant to be funny and the few minute drops of serious conversations with your friends. Combined to the fact that between missions the protagonist is running around picking flowers, hunting, flying, playing cards and doing whatever, the story feels disconnected from the world. I got the same feeling that I got from Far Cry 2; Someone wanted to make a serious game with serious plot about insanity, but at some point someone wanted to water it down and make it more relaxed and funny. The result is mish mash that's neither funny nor serious. Then again I felt that I played the game wrong. So I first reviewed this game some time ago. Returning to the review now, over a year and a half later, my opinion hasn't really changed. But I figured it was out of date, so why not rewrite it?
So, let's begin. Heroes & Generals is a Free to Play First Person Shooter developed by RETO-MOTO, set in the midst of World War II; with a bit of a twist. That twist being that the FPS battles (The 'Heroes' aspect), are determined by a sort of Strategy game controlled by the players. (The 'Generals' aspect). Both of which work together to produce the result of the current "War", which resets each time one of the three factions captures a certain number of Key Cities, those factions being The United States of America, the Soviet Union, and Germany.
The "Heroes" aspect plays pretty nice. The battles can be between any 2 of the factions, or all three at once. What types of units are in play are determined by what the "Generals" players send in, whether it's tanks, infantry, planes, paratroopers, snipers, or a combination of them, they all battle it out against the other "Generals'" forces. The controls are responsive, and it feels rewarding to shoot up the enemy. Overall it's very fun, but there are still some problems. One major one being the sound design. Each gun sounds like an airsoft rifle; just a collection of clicks. Another problem being it isn't to pretty to look at. The models and textures all seem fine, it's mainly the colours. Everything looks dark, gloomy, and desaturated. Also noticeable is the lack of variable maps. A lot of models are just reused in a different setting to determine a new map, which becomes obvious after playing a while.
The "Generals" aspect is a sort of strategy game, played in real-time, where you move assault teams across a map that includes Europe, and parts of Africa and Asia, to do battle against the enemy generals' assault teams. When two or even three opposing assault teams meet, a battle is queued and played by the "Heroes". To play the "Generals" mode, you must make a commitment on which side you wish to play for, and stick with them until that "War" ends, and must be in a leadership rank, which starts at rank 12.
It plays nice enough, but is slow at times due to the fact that all the battles must be resolved in real-time, so don't be expecting a game like Hearts of Iron or Panzer Tactics. After surpassing rank 17 to rank 18, your character can become a full  time general, which grants you more assault teams, and allows you to use any type. However, that character will not be able to play the "Heroes" aspect after that, so don't proceed to be a general if you want to stay in the FPS game.
Lastly, I may as well list some pros and cons.
PROS
-fun gameplay
-ongoing development
-large-ish playerbase
-rewards squad play
-interesting side-game ('Generals')
-interesting arsenal
CONS
-horrible sound design
-bad optimization
-clunky animations
-desaturated colours
-toxic community
-long grinds for progress

Call of Duty's multiplayer stopped being relevant to me after Modern Warfare 2. That said, I have fun with the campaign. I enjoy the over-the-top silliness and the expert scripting and animation. It itches my military porn cravings. I was super happy with Black Ops 2 for introducing something new to the series and I was hoping Ghosts would be continuing that streak. Unfortunately, this game is the pinnacle of terrible. With the exception of bugs (which is rare in a CoD game but Ghosts is rife with them) the campaign is poorly paced, has a terrible aesthetic, has a really barebones plot with a meaningless narrative, and lacks any of the surprises or suspense that previous CoD games featured. It introduces a sordid world that is so unbelievable as to warrant complete disinterest in everything you do in the game. I appreciated a few rather stunning levels and there is a greater degree of world-building than previous CoD games, but at least those games had cool characters. This game has you stuck with your dumb brother and a useless dog that, yes, you will be forced to save at the cost of life or limb. At least the Extinction mode is pretty interesting. Sadly the multiplayer is about as bad as it gets. All of the guns perform and sound the same and the maps are tinier than ever. Obviously I love this game by how many hours I have put into it. It is very replayable most thanks due to the amazing mods out there. The graphics aren't amazing, but it makes up for it in gameplay. The Mount and Blade series is a one of a kind. Think Total War and Skyrim. You start out as a humble adventurer with a rusty sword and peasants clothing (Sometimes you get a bow or crossbow, depending on what you spent your first skill points on). You then proceed to hiring men in the surrounding villages, eventually training them to full-fledged mounted kinghts, or master archers, while you yourself become a master of whatever you wish. You can capture castles, raid villages, take enemy lords prisoner and then proceed to ransom them off. Or you can become a vassal of one of the existing kings.
The map is filled with bandits, deserters, mercenaries, and enemy parties. The battles start out as somewhere around 5v5 and can scale as high to 500v500. There are mods that allow you to break this cap, enabling you to fight as many as your PC hardware can handle.
Overall this is a pretty entertaining game. The graphics are kinda meh, the animations are good, overall gameplay is good, but the spearman (Rhodok faction) do not know how to properly use their pikes to their advantage. When facing cavalry the run around fighting man vs. man so they get demolished by an cavalry. The factions are unbalanced in strength, but I suppose that is realistic.
If you like to shoot muskets and swing swords, First Peson or Third.. This is the game for you.

Warband is the stand alone sequel to Mount & Blade.  It has all the features of the first game plus some additional new features.
Graphics: 4
Below average, even for the age of the game.  Characters, objects and buildings all have low poly counts and low resolution textures.
Sound: 5
Below average sound, the standard screams, grunts and kills. But impact noises, sword clashes, etc.  Make no sense and don't sound right at all.  But aren't so bad that they distract from the game either.  They are simply there.
Music: 8
Above average, the music does a good job of setting the mood of the game.  You may actually feel hyped before a battle.
Gameplay: 9
Excellent gameplay, sword motions feel smooth and fluid.  Easilly controllable as you gallop on your horse mowing down enemies.  It does however take lots of practice.  Don't expect to hop on your horse and be the medival rambo immediately.
Impressions:
The game drops you in the world and lets you get started.  It gives you no direction at all and it's up to you to figure out what to do.  Such is the nature of a sandbox game.  The poor graphics do break some immersion until you get used to them, sort of like playing an old PS1 game.  The graphics these days are garbage, but if done correctly they can still immerse you.
The game starts off very difficult and slowly gets easier as you get better and your character gets stronger.  The reverse difficulty curve can be problematic but also exciting as you feel yourself getting stronger and better at the game.
Value: 10
As this is a sandbox game, you will get many hundreds of hours trying every angle of the game.  And your money supports the developers, telling them you want more of these games, more of this niche genre, less AAA garbage.
Summary:
If you can ignore the poor graphics, this is a very good game, ready to let you do whatever you want

Ubisoft should be commended for their ability to tinker with the Far Cry series. While they didn't initially develop the first game, once Crytek signed a deal with EA, Ubisoft could have just left the Far Cry series to rot. Instead, we got a rather interesting sequel with a totally different setting and style of gameplay.
The main problems with Far Cry 2, though, are a lack of meaningful side content, horrible navigation and a rather pointless open-world to explore. While there were moments of beauty and the AI was super deadly, the game ended up being a bit of a drag. It simply wasn't fun for a majority of the campaign, even if it's fleeting moments of entertainment were blissful.
Far Cry 3 took things even further. In adapting a more complex story, the game is immediately more urgent than it's predecessor. While I can't say that all the characters are fully fleshed out human beings, at least having a motivation to explore a jungle island makes sense. The villain is quite a trip.
The island is also more conveniently spaced out. Instead of a vast terrain devoid of life and fuana, almost every area on the "Rook Islands" contains something to do. Those somethines usually end up being random loot, hidden treasures, animals to hunt for upgrades or outposts to capture for quick travel points.
Quick travel really is what helps move this game along. It may end up being a bit too easy, but not having to trek a quarter mile to get to the next mission is a joy. It keeps to engaged in the story while also opening the possibility to indulge in some of the side missions.
I do have to say that the driving is beyond awful. Far Cry 2 managed to get that one better. The boss battles are also hugely underwhelming. As manic as some of the antagonists can be, finishing them with QTEs is pretty lame.
I also don't know if I enjoy the Radio Tower quests. They are functionally the same as the viewpoints from Assassin's Creed. Ubisoft just loves homogenizing their titles into one super game (which ended up being the deplorable Watch_Dogs). It is cool to see the vistas, but it feels like a missed opportunity to do something more unique.
I also kind of dislike the main player character. Everything in his world seems catered toward a male audience. While that is mostly a personal complaint, I don't see how a female gamer would find anything interesting about this. The "love interest" (if you can even call her that) is so bland, but she shows a lot of skin, so clearly shes targeted at a male demographic.
I can't really come up with any other complaints. Far Cry 3 is just stellar throughout. It may be a bit on the easy side and have some heavily scripted missions, but it's just super fun. That almost every little distraction provided actually provides bonuses to the player is super great. More games should allow their side missions to be meaningful.
So if you can get past some of the story issues and lack of difficulty, I would recommend this game. It's got a pretty decent length and even has co-op. You will more than likely spend a good deal of time playing it.

Warband made some definite improvements over Mount & Blade - hopefully this trend will continue - I’m optimistic about their potential, but at the moment, I can’t recommend the series.
The colour scheme is well suited to the repetitive, boring environments – both on the overworld map and when in towns and combat. Everything is identical and grey/brown.
The sounds – music and effect, are repetitive as well.
The levelling and followers system is never properly explained – I hope you didn’t put all your points into “weapon master” thinking it’d make you better with weapons – it doesn’t.
Better documentation would help. It's well worth going through some guides or the manual first - there's quite a few interesting mechanics, such as trade, town development, etc. that you otherwise wont' find.
The game begins – you start fighting, getting better equipment and maybe building up your army. So far so good. Then the game stops – you’re too strong for the enemies you’ve just been fighting, but you’re so far below the “proper” enemies – the lords whose land you need in order to build up an army. This leaves some 50 levels of beastly slow grinding, till you get ~ 100 plus army with well-equipped followers.
At this point the game properly starts – however, the combat becomes a mess - You head into battle, both armies get wiped out and you have to build up your army again. You will then do this for every battle –the system seems to be that, unless you are maximum level, micromanaging your army and depending on your allied AI armies (which take even longer to set up) you will be thrashed, as you and your enemy wipe each other out 1 for 1, with a slight favour due to your actions.
You will be horribly outnumbered for most of the game – your army mostly maxes out at ~ 120 members. The smallest your enemy will have is 300 plus. If the enemy mobs for over 500, you’ll just have to accept losing.
The siege mechanism, a crucial part of obtaining territory is frustrating as well. You have one ladder/tower 2 people wide. You have a 100 people in your army. It takes ages to get them up onto the walls. When there the combat just disintegrates into a mess as everyone fights for space.
Despite all of this, the game is strangely compelling, especially, if you use cheats to boost yourself to the higher levels, which is where to game actually starts. There are some decent mods available too.
Overall, I can’t really recommend this game – it’s getting a couple of sequels and expansions that will hopefully fix some of these issues - I’d look at those instead.

Quite truthfully the most infuriating game I have ever played. You have to pay OBSCENE amounts of in-game money to get ANYTHING that makes you even remotely effective in combat. E.G.
BEING A TANKER: The beginning german tank is a tank with two machine guns on it that fires "Armor piercing" rounds. However, when facing another tank, you are done for. It maybe allows 1 bullet in 10 out of a 50-round magazine to damage the other tank. The next step up is 46000 credits, and you get about 2-3K a game. But then, you've ranked up to the point that you can finally buy another tank. This tank? 56000 credits. Oh but wait, then you get THAT tank, finally feel useful, and some kid who got sick of all the♥♥♥♥♥♥and bought the first anti-tank weapon available for infantry (He used real money because a bazooka costs 86000 credits for infantry!!!!!) blows you to pieces in 2 shots. 2 shots, from some average♥♥♥♥♥♥in fatigues. Did I mention there is a huge aim-delay? There is. Someone get's behind you, you are ♥♥♥♥ed. Done. Tanks=Metal coffins. Then, you realize that the tank character, outside of his tank? Can only use a single gun, can't even carry grenades, and has the health of a Turtle with Cancer.
BEING A PARATROOPER: You can drop on ANY POINT ON THE MAP! Awesome right?
Wrong.
You fall out of the sky in plain view of EVERYONE at the speed of Snails trying to copulate. ANYONE that has a machine gun (And believe me, they all do because the starter gun is nearly impossible to aim and you are dead in a close combat fight) will shoot you out of the sky before your legs even have a chance to taste dirt. You think they'd have some compensation, like having a better starting weapon or better health. Nope. You can carry a single gun. No grenades, or anything.
Also, if you miss the drop zone you are stuck in that plane (which can be shot down with you in it waiting) for another 4-5 minutes while it makes another pass.
BEING A PILOT: The planes could be fun. They sort of are. Once you get the hang of the wildly erroneous controle system where the mouse makes your plane go screwy directions while the keyboard only controls throttle and yaw, (Which in the end is what you have to use to do anything, because a single twitch of the mouse and you are flying at a 90 degree angle) you could manage to possibly enjoy being a pilot. Except for a couple of things: There is no HUD, you can't switch views for a better look at what is even possibly on the ground to compensate for a lack of HUD and 90% of the game is spent teamkilling because you finally see a silly little truck running around on the ground with NO MARKER DEPICTING FRIEND OR FOE (Which usually means it's an enemy, because if there is no marker in the other classes it means enemy) so you drop a bomb on it thinking "FINALLY! Someone to kill!" and you NAIL THAT TRUCK. I mean, you really DECIMATE it. A more beautiful act of flying and bomb-dropping ballet you have never seen! I mean, truly remarkable! Even the TEAMMATE YOU JUST KILLED says, after raging at you, "But hey...that was a great shot man. I have to admit, you really nailed me spot on. Too bad you CAN'T DO THAT TO THE ENEMY"
So you spend the next 30 seconds before you CRASH the thing into trees (Because that's the only way to get low enough to attack anything safely by seeing what it is) waiting for the 3-minute delay before your bombs resupply.
But since you've crashed, you realize everyone else in your squadron has done the same because the planes handle like flying great white sharks with 800-pound weights attached to them and your assault team is out of spawns and that's the end of the game.
BEING INFANTRY: I don't even want to write about this. I damaged my LCD screen playing this class. Somehow, every time you spawn, there is someone there to headshot you in a single pop.
EVERY...SINGLE....TIME
Aim delays, bullets flying slower than bullets should, immediate death.
RECON: I am uninstalling before reaching this class. If everything else blew chunks, so did this one.
Don't bother with this game. Please. For the sake of your system and personal health.

First of all - It's a BETA
So maybe this game will change a lot if it reaches the final stand.
But I write this review about the current stand - BETA.
So lets start with the options. There are only a few graphic options. You can adjust texture quality etc. but the game looks still like shi*. I know, gameplay is much more important than graphics but this game looks so sad. The colors are washed out etc.
I don't like the look, but maybe its a question of taste.
Another graphical shortcoming is the anti aliasing. You can only activate FXAA. No MSAA/SSAA/SMAA or something. Probably you can force it with your graphics driver, I don't know.. But it's not available ingame.
So, enough said about graphics ... Now let's talk about the game itself.
It's free to play and Pay 2 Win. And thats the biggest mistake, which a developer can do to the game.
The start weapons are just underpowered. There are 2 fractions ( The americans and the germans ) and I choosed the americans.
You start with a M1 Garand and the first what you think about this weapon ( or what I thought about that weapon ): It must be so powerful. It is, but otherwise its not . In almost every game, where this weapon exist, this weapon is accurate and powerful. But in this game, it has no accuracy. You can kill other players with it but if shot it a few times, it gets so inaccurate even if you stop shooting for a sec or something. I don't know why, maybe the developers are still trying to balance the weapons or they messed up this weapon because there's a item shop ingame with other weapons etc.
I think they did it because of the 2nd reason.
But if you hit with that weapon, it's very powerful based on the damage. If you hit the head of enemy, it's a instant kill. And if you hit his body, you need to hit im 3 times to kill him.
I don't like that very much, because its hard to know if you hit him or not. Because there's not hitmarker or something, only a small blood spread which is hard to realize.
A cool thing are the vehicles ingame. I like them. The controls are not well for me, but they are acceptable. You can drive bicycle, a tank, a jeep with an MG on the top etc.
I'm not sure how to get them, but I think you have to increase your rank to get them.
Yes, you have read correctly... There's a rank system.
I don't get how its actually works but it exist. You can earn XP if you kill enemies, hit hostile vehicles and receive badges for doing things like running etc.
So as I said. I don't like this game. But it's just a BETA, maybe the final version can change my mind... we will see.
So far, I can't recommend this game. There are still some bugs but that's normal for a BETA.

Far Cry 3 is really easy to recommend but it's also a really easy game. I can't recall ever having a hard time doing anything. The game is beautiful, feels great, plays great, sounds great, but lacks a large amount of challenge. Most of the sections of the game which didn't just throw you into the action are all able to be completed with stealth. You're even rewarded extra experince for being stealthy, so it's not like the game isn't encouraging it. But when the action picks up, its still pretty easy. Headshots aren't difficult to pull off, plus you're practically invincible, all you have to do is keep pulling that bullet out of your left arm and snapping your finger back into place and you'll be A okay. The AI isn't briliant, the enemy will just be trained on your position and move forward, nothing complex coming from them. Plus your skills encourage easy mode, like the takedown ability. Next thing you know your knife is the primary weapon. The story is interesting and goes places, some of the characters are alright, some are great but they don't all come together in a good way to really make the story. The whole idea of the game is based around you saving all your friends and thats all but a fragment of what the game wants to tell you instead. It's a bit jarring to go back to the little cave you're hidding you're friends in because it really chops the game up. Far Cry 3 is worth playing at a cheap price, because it is a fantastic open world game, just don't expect much of a challenge at all.
