Far cry 3 is the third installment of the far cry series developed by Ubisoft.
The gamplay is solid. You have dozens of weapons to choose from including bow, assault rifles, pistols etc. Weapons can be bought or unlocked by spending money or going to radio towers restpectively. The guns look and sound great, as well as having dozens of upgrades to choose from to suit your playstyle. You also a variety of vehicles such as humvees, cars, handgliders and a wingsuit. You can also hunt animals which you can skin to upgrade various gear. There is also plenty of foliage to hide in for stealth lovers.
The story is a step up from far cry 2. You basically play as a guy who's holiday with friends go horribly wrong as you get captured by maniacs and have to try to escape the island. The voice acting is great (with special credits to the voice actor of Vaas and do a great job at setting the scene. Aside from the campaign there are plenty of side activities such as racing, knife throwing, hunting quests which you can undertake as well. Furthermore you as you play the campaign you can unlock a large variety of skills which  range from increasing health to adding a variety of stealth kills.
The graphics are absolutley stellar. There is plently of foliage in the lush jungles including a wide variety of flowers,
bushes and trees. If you go on a high vantage point (ie mountain, tower), you can see just how beautiful this game really is as you see the surrounding area covered by thousands of lush trees and wildlife below you.
The multiplayer is probrably this game's weakest point. The main game mode is team deathmatch where two teams face off against each other until a certain number of tickets are reached. The maps aren't that big which means that although firefights occur more often, there aren't alot of areas to hide in/manouvre. You can create your own classes and customise loadouts. You also level up depending on your kills which unlocks new weapons and modifications.
The co-op campaign is good fun. It borrows elements from Left 4 Dead as you and 3 others move from one point to another, fighting enemies and completing objectives along the way. You get to select the loadout from the ones you created from multiplayer. There are plenty of different levels to chooses from too.
I highly recommend this game for fans of shooters and adventure games alike.

All of the aspects of this game are just downright FUN and it is one of the most cinematic experiences I have ever had as a gamer. My rating was going to be a 9/10 but it earned an extra point for the helicopter and 'Flight of the Valkyries'.
Well done Ubisoft, I tip my hat to you.

These are just my thoughts written down in 10 minutes, excuse grammar, or spelling mistakes, i tried to avoid the most of them. I might exaggerate my expressions, but principally this fits to my attitude towards this game in every point.
- Lagg compensation, makes players seeing you 1-2 seconds earlier than you can see them, of course you will lose the gunfight because of that.
- Bad map design: they look pretty, if you could run the game flawlessly. Moreover and most important the maps are way to big, which forces players with lower gunskill or inferior tactics to camp, through the whole game on one spot. This forced playstyle has huge influence on the course of the game. To be more detailed, this map design makes the action running slower, and basically having less fun, cause you die on a streak because of a guy in his tent, cooking some food. This playstyle forces a player to pay more attention, attention which makes you to put huge effort into looking at every spot.
- Unbalanced weapons: This over defensive playstyle is supported with some overpowered weapons, some shotguns are to strong in mods like cranked, and small parts of maps. These small areas are used as camping spots, where players are going on patrol with their shotguns. IEDs help the player to be safe in their camping areas, IEDs are replacing bouncing betties and claymores in one not dodgeable equipment. Everyone is using the same weapons for a reason, probably the ak-12 is the most used weapon in the game, autosnipers, which oneshot you like more difficult snipers, the vector machinepistole which can kill you across the whole map, with even less shots than a assault rifle, and the mentioned shotguns.
- Perk system: Actually you need to run specialist, to have the essential perks that are needed to win gunfights, surviving sound whoring guys, which is, and can be used as another camping tactic, explosives and flashbangs. At all getting to a higher killstreak. Even though running specialist is closely enough to provide you with a balanced basic and same requirements to play against other players.
- Laggs: Due to bad programming or a sophisticated marketing strategy, to make the player buy new hardware make the feeling even worse, decent hardware is not enough anymore to run the game flawlessly.
- Worst Anti-cheat ever: In the last days I have seen one up to three cheaters, who enjoyed their games with their rage settings, killing you with a headshot through 6 walls, or their legit settings, which correct their aims when they are near to the part where they want to shoot at. They can't be asked to use a wallhack, it is more of a foundation nowadays on call of duty ghosts.
- Matchmaking system: It feels like there is no system behind the matchmaking, dicing out the teams, no matter which level they are or which kill/death ratio they have, so the game is usually decided before it even started.Once you left a game, because of a hacker, or because you don't give it a chance, you accepted that you will get one lose for it. So you search again, now it is your turn to guess, which game you will join.
- Spawn system: If players tell you, that people are spawning in a circle around them, might be an exaggeration but there is some truth behind it. Your Killstreaks are often ended by People spawning arbitrary in your face or 10 centimeters behind your back. Once you are dead, you will probably die 2-3 times again, because your next spawn will be at 3 enemy players who directly kill you, again and again.
The gameplay is more sophisticating than in earlier cod's, more tactical,  just because of the lower amount of bullets players can stand. Sadly this improvement gets disturbed by all these mentioned facts. Ghosts prevents you from having a constant, liquid competitive gaming, which in the end, arouses fun to you.
There might be some well done realized concepts, and I have fun at the game sometimes, but weighing up all the pros and cons on a gold balance, the cons just outweigh the pros.
And that I do not forget to mention, i see alot of potential in this game, but it needs to be realized, work needs to be done for this, we will see if that will happen.

I love turn-based strategy games, and this is a perfect example of why.
First of all, the combat system, is just a marvelous recreation of medival combat I would personally say that the combat system alone could compete with Chivalry and other purely combat system driven medival and early ages games.
Secondly the campaign has a great system. Typically in turn-based strategy games, you are a part of a large faction or something of the sort, but the fact that you are just a single person who has to build up an army, freshens it up and creates a whole other aspect of gameplay to be explored. In addition to the great gameplay, the game also has full character customization, which goes into more detail than any game i've ever seen, allowing you to munipulate everything about you character, including facial structure. But this game, too a much more extreme extent than i've ever seen give graciously and takes ruthlessly, one second you are one of the most powerful people in the world and then next second you're a peasant with only a small amount of money to your name and no army.
Thirdly, the multiplayer on top of all this is just amazing, up to 200 player games, huge siege battles. Fairly balanced gameplay(meaning you won't get bent over and ♥♥♥♥ed just because you're young to the game) and weapon system, which is some kind of mixture of the weapon system in CS:GO and Chivalry, just the cherry on top. The chocolate drzzle on top is the bot battles, not too dificult as to make you angry, but still not too easy.
One of the few descrepancies i find in the game is the graphics, but being a person with a sub-par computer effects me in no way. The graphics aren't great in the campaign overwolrd map, but in combat they improve significantly. Other than a few other UI annoyances, for example when you kill a group of enemies you have to click over each weapon or armor piece instead of having a "loot all" option, i haven't found any other significant annoyances.

I finally bought this during the 2014 holiday sale. I'm playing the hell out of Far Cry 3 and really enjoying it, but holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ it's completely indefensible. A real shame, because the game is really fun and well designed.
Problematic themes and depictions include:
A raging case of Last Samurai Syndrome. A white man comes to an exotic foreign world and is quickly adopted by the oppressed natives not only into their culture but as their savior, despite the fact that he knows nothing about their environment and has no applicable skills. We're supposedly a tribe of island warriors who've been living here since time immemorial but only you can save us, scrawny Californian douchebro who's never handled a gun before!
As such, the Rakyat can't do anything for themselves. Only Whitey Samurai has any kind of power in deciding how the Rakyat fight for freedom. After the heroic white boy singlehandedly liberates an enemy outpost, a half dozen Rakyat warriors show up in jeeps to secure his conquest, AK47s at the ready, but they're only there for atmosphere. They're unable to take outposts themselves or even help the hero out. I know that having the player be the only being in the world with agency is a convention of open world games going back farther than GTA, but it's pretty ♥♥♥♥ed that these people literally have to wait around for the white hero to save them.
Citra. The spiritual leader of the Rakyat is a colonial fantasy straight out of Victorian pulp fiction, the hypersexual female native drawn to the white savior, despite being surrounded at all times by hunky warriors from her own culture. Weirdly, she doesn't even look like she's the same ethnicity as the other Rakyat, who are supposedly... Polynesian? (The game never says exactly where Rook Island is.) Citra is ethnically unplaceable, and definitely has more "caucasian" features than the rest of her people, presumably to maximize her sexual appeal to the game's target demographic. Also, the warrior initiation ceremony of the Rakyat involves Citra straddling you while topless and grinding on your junk. Whoops, that was a spoiler, sorry.
Dennis. At the beginning of the story, the white hero is rescued and guided by a magical negro witch doctor. Dennis has been adopted by the Rakyat years before, but is not worthy to be their savior himself. He can only assist our white hero, despite being depicted as much more competent and experienced.
There are two enemy factions, the savage bloodthirsty "Pirates" and the professional mercenary "Privateers". The disorganized and drug-addled Pirates are all Afro-Caribbean, while the much more competent Privateers are (mostly white) Americans.
The main bad guy is a white South African who is of course depicted as a genocidal monster. Poor Afrikaners, no other ethnic group is so easy to demonize in video games and action movies. It's not their fault that their accent makes them all sound like Bond villains.
In conclusion, buy it cheap during a Steam sale, enjoy exploring the gorgeous world, the awesome stealth killing mechanics, and the wide variety of customizable guns, and shake your head at the tone-deaf racism.

I hated Far Cry 1 with its eagle eye AI spotting you in bushes 100 yards away.  I skipped FC2.  I wasn't going to play FC3 until persuading by a few friends insisted I buy it during the Steam sale.
I'm glad I listened.  Far Cry 3 was an awesome dynamic fps experience.  The exploration alone is impressively massive, and it's fun to watch all the AI animal life interact with each other.  It creates a living world that's constantly keeping you busy and on your toes.
There's so much to see and do in FC3 from hunting game to poker games.  From climbing tower puzzles to camp liberating missions you do your own way (stealthy or guns blazing).  You'll never be without something to do.  This game has so many memorable moments created by some really cool story missions, but also in the dynamically open world environment.
I'm now a Far Cry fan again.  Looking forward to FC4.

This is actually a pretty good game.
Is it perfect? No. It has it's fairshare of infuriating glitches (It is still in BETA) that can cause a man to descend into a blind rage and possible destroy his marriage... but if you like large-scale Battlefield-esque time of games with a WWII feel, well this is probably the best the genre has to offer. For a WWII history fan like myself, it's a huge amount of entertainment. If you're a fan of the WWII era and fps games, you should definitely play it.
I have played this game a lot longer than my steam playtime would lead one to believe, and overall I have enjoyed nearly every second of it. Keep in mind however, this is not a game that favors a player who does not think about cover and just runs into the open. You will get shot. This game forces you to be aware of your surroundings at all time, including available cover.
Sometimes, the matches feel unbalanced. The reason for this is that one side might have tanks while the other does not. It is completely possible for your team to utitlize the a rocket spawn on the map to take enemy tanks out and many players should have anti-tank measures unlocked and equipped. With all that said, the match might not be in your favor but you can still win. Both sides have this problem, largely because tanks and other "divisions" in each match are determind by the RTS side of the game. I like to think the game is somewhat realistic, because in reality, both sides did not always have tanks in every battle they were in during the war. Sometimes you'd attack a point or defend a point with no tanks while the enemy had some. Just how it is, it's not game breaking. Just somewhat frustrating until you get used to it.
I could go on describing every aspect of this games, but I would have to write a book. Play it for yourself and be patient with it, it will quickly grow on you once you get past the glitches and the terrible unmodded M1-Garand/Gewehr 43 starting guns.

After a long play period, and just now getting done with my first match from the most recently, awaited for update, (Which proceeded to lose connection and force me to quit) I think it's time I gave my word on this game. Heroes & Generals is a mediocre attempt at an untapped genre, blending together strategy and shooter style game mechanics, yet failing at both. One would expect better than what this eternal beta delivers. Maps are often boring, heavily one-sided with large open areas, bland asset reuse, and poorly thought out layouts with gameplay befitting of the same status.
Gameplay itself feels like it belongs in a fifteen year old game. (I know; "Go back to Call of Duty" is what you fanboys love to say) and not to defend Call of Duty in any shape or form, but maybe you should give it a try before jumping mindless band-wagons and realize that these two games are more similar than you think.
Gameplay in H&G can go as far as to feel nostalgic at times, reminding me of the days of Battlefield 1942, the issue is... It reminds me a little TOO much of Battlefield 1942. Almost like the game was just a reskin of it, a game that came out over TWELVE years ago. The actual gameplay has no balance, going as far as to list all the weapons in tiers as if you're playing an RPG, not a shooter. Every tier of automatic weapon is always better than the one before, throwing actual damage and accuracy out of the window, making the most important traits firerates and clip sizes, leaving the (expensive and tedious to unlock) bolt action (that's right, UNLOCK. You have to unlock the primary infantry rifle) in the dust of the semi automatics when BOTH need only two shots to the body to kill. This draws up an unreasonable balance issue, when the bolt action has half the clip size, and a fifth of the fire rate. Sure, it has better range. Sure it can be MODED to one-shot people. But the time, and money to get there on top of constant upkeep fees for those mods becomes ridiculous. Especially due to the fact the last update seems to have nerfed the bolt action's effective range, rendering it useless. I won't begin to say this game is 'pay-to-win' even if you CAN pay for a slight advantage, but it remains constantly unbalanced. Being free to play is no excuse for a lack of updates, and public beta is no excuse for a lack of testing.
Machineguns, weapons normally seen with three or four man crews setup in a defensive position are touted about as the be-all, end-all weapon like every other person was Rambo, himself, carrying around this heavy firearm as if it weighs nothing and cutting through waves of enemy troops without the slightest hint of recoil. Being the biggest, and baddest gun on the field, it can only be paired with the sniper rifle, making any person wealthy enough to own one or foolish enough to pick the recon class a long-ranged assassin. Ultimate firepower vs ultimate range is where these weapon tiers end. (Imagine if TF2 only had the heavy and sniper as classes and everything else was just a weaker substitute used to grind to that point. Yeah, it's sort of like that.)
Of course, you don't HAVE to be an infantryman. You could choose the (Expertly thought-out) earliest class possible; THE TANKER! Hide behind layers of armor and use your machine gun on infantry until you've been awarded enough XP to unlock an actual tank. It will be weak at first, only able to withstand two explosive hits. But don't fret. Just grind for that next tier that can now take two... explosive hits...? Yeah, other than looking imposing, there is little difference between the tanks you can pick. Even more so between the axis and allies. After all, who cares about historical accuracy? Tanks can drive faster than you can run, turn faster than you can run and SHOOT faster than you can run. In fact... They seem to shoot a little too fast. As in, the earlier mentioned bolt actions take longer to chamber a new shot than these things do. OH, and their scopes are free. Still think the game's balanced? Grenades are often your only means of dealing any explosive damage. As well as your entire team, most of the time... After all, why would a tank need to be killed with a grenade down the hatch or something? It's not like they're overpowered (Or just 'a tank' to those who know tanks are and well.. SHOULD be a little OP) and sitting in your outside spawn or anything.
Oh right. The developers decided making you a ghost for three seconds was somehow going to prevent spawn killing. Well.. It probably WOULD if you actually spawned in your base where you have things like cover you could run to in those three seconds. But if one enemy is even near your base, you will be forced to spawn a few dozen meters away in the open. You have no choice. You MUST spawn here to prevent 'spawn camping' (because the initial step taken wasn't enough apparently) but instead ends up causing it. Having a tank or two simply move in and shoot anybody who spawns on the brilliantly placed position on the barren hillside instead of the warm, safe environment of your own base.
"Well that's strategy!" some of the morally ambiguous or skill impaired might say. Sad to say, they're right. But it's also sad to say, that's about the extent of any kind of 'strategy' that's used in a game about strategy. The lack of any actual strategy quickly becomes apparent. MGs can be fired from the hip, there's zero sort of suppression, meaning you can get shot at as long as you have health and will remain calm and unflinching even during the most heated of fire-fights, keeping perfect accuracy and sight lines. The lack of map or team navigation or even a stable chat system renders little to no teamwork. The generals simply have to push the capital to win with no thought or care put into anything else on the map. How this game gets away with having 'strategy' anywhere in its features is beyond me. There's about as much strategy in the game this aspires to be.

I'll be honest, I read some of the reviews on the Steam page about this game, and I was doubtful it was going to be any good, but it was free, and I'm always on the lookout for a fun, new FPS game.
I played a couple hours and was pleasantly surprised at how good this game was, without paying a cent to play it.
The people complaining about "pay 2 win" are mistaken, this is "pay 2 NOT PLAY", basically you can pay money to unlock things early and without working to earn enough coins to pay for it.
Basically you earn X amount of coins for whichever level you are, as long as you play more than 50% of the battle, so if you come in a minute before it end you won't be getting paid your "wages".
The game does have some annoying features, such as paying to refill your grenades (you pay with coins or gold (gold you pay for IRL).  You start off with 60 and I've played at least twenty battles and I haven't run out yet, I refilled accidentally when I had 45 left, and it cost me very little in game coins, less than 100 I believe.
Yes, some of the guns are extremely expensive, the bolt action rifle (right now) is 71000 coins, but you earn 3000-7000 each battle depending on your wages (level) and captures/kills.  You start off with one very solid gun, which is semi-auto and is decent damage, and when you level up the game gives you enough coins to buy the second gun, which is a sub-machine gun, once again very well balanced, and actually quite good.  You also earn quite a bit when you go into a "profession", which I'll talk more about later.
The game doesn't leave you high and dry, and the players that are paying a lot of extra money are just robbing themselves of the satisfaction of earning their weapons/vehicles, which, to me, is the point of playing a game, to improve your skills, and to earn new gear.
It's a good game, and I'm usually very hard on these types of "pay 2 play" games, which charge you for everything, but honestly you can play this game for a very long time and never pay a cent.
The only reason to pay, if you don't mind "grinding", is to get something you want, and to support the developers.
The professions are something I haven't delved into a lot, as I've been staying as a regular soldier trying to get the "recon" profession but as I understand it they're "specializations", such as tank driver (this is self explanatory) ranging to paratrooper (once again...self explanatory).  You unlock each specialization by levelling up as a base soldier, and then you branch off when you pick a specialization, and you unlock special content for each specialization.
In the end the game is quite enjoyable, and if you don't mind having some fun and spending some time killing your enemies to earn enough coins to buy a new gun or a new vehicle (vehicles are actually cheap compared to guns) then you'll really enjoy this game, especially when you level up enough and unlock the Assault missions, which can last up to (and beyond) and hour.
By downloading and playing the game you lose nothing but a small amount of your time, give it a chance to prove itself to you, and you'll be hooked.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a first sequel to original medieval action RPG video game Mount & Blade. Warband was developed by TaleWorlds and was published by Paradox Interactive. This highly anticipated indie video game won numerous rewards and also was nominated “Best Indie Game of the Year“.
While most RPGs with medieval time setting involving magical events, supernatural entities, Warband strikes you with realistic combat without any fireball spells.  Mount & Blade: Warband is a mix of action RPG and turn-based strategy games. You travel on world map as in turn-based strategy game and fight or explore villages and cities in third-person or first-person perspective. In Mount & Blade: Warband your goal is simple: rule all of the Calradia. You start as a simple mercenary but later you can become faithful vassal or even the king. While there is no actual story other than rule Calradia, you can do various quest to earn gold and improve relations with other lords or cities. Quest differs from simply delivering goods to capturing enemy lords.
There are total 24 different skills which you can improve by leveling up. You get experience points from battles or doing quest. Those skills affect how you perform in actual battles, travelling in world map, trading, maintaining your army. Graphics are not top quality but in won't prevent you from enjoying the game. In fighting mode you can command your troops with simple tasks such as follow, stand ground, charge and to choose what type of weapon to use. Every field battle usually turns into over 100 troop mosh-pit and picking the retreating enemy troops one by one. City and castle sieges or defenses can be more enjoyable as you can explore city or castle. After capturing or being awarded a fief you can improve it with new building which gives you various bonuses, for example, you can start a production to earn more additional gold. Also Mount & Blade: Warband can be enhanced by various mods from simple textures to total conversions.
The main difference from the original Mount & Blade is the multiplayer. Default number of players is up to 64. Modded servers can hold more than 200! Game modes include well-known Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, Assault (similar to conquest mode seen in Battlefield series) and also Siege (where you need to capture or defend a castle), Battle (last standing man wins) and Duel (one to one combat).
To sum up, I would recommend Mount & Blade: Warband to anyone who always imagined what it would feel to actually be in a medieval battle not just command your troops from above. Multiplayer mode with various maps both official and fan made can keep you logged in for a long amount of time and total conversion content will enrich your singleplayer experience.

I honestly do have a fun time playing this game, which I do with all Call of Duty's, and is the reason why I buy it every year. But it is unfortunate that a company on the level of Infinity Ward can mess up so much on a PC port of their game, the platform that their foundation is built on. I am somewhat sympathetic for them since they did have to create next gen versions of the game as well, on a two year development time, but I draw the line when they make a PC version that is sometimes almost unplayable, in multiplayer atleast. The single player portion runs great for me, all of my setting can be put at the highest, and the game truely looks good. I really enjoyed the single player, I liked the new characters and the whole concept of this small team of so called Ghosts. The storyline was also a refreshing break from the last 3 Modern Warfare games, which is nice. Unfortunately, multiplayer is a different story. The framerate and stuttering are ridiculous at times, leaving the game virtually unplayable at times, forcing you to lower your settings and possibly even the resolution to smooth out the gameplay experience. It feels like a mediocre company ported the multiplayer, while IW did the single player, they almost feel like to completely different games from a graphical and technical standpoint. This is a shame considering that the engine this game runs on is 10 years old, and they make these high requirements for this game that could easily be run on a decently powered PC. Although I do have fun with the multiplayer, and Extinction mode is all kinds of fun, I would say that you should wait to see if Infinity Ward patches things in the near future, or wait for the price to go down drastically.

-Brandon

This game is hands-down one of the best WWII era game I've played. Pretty much the online, multifaceted version of IL2-Sturmovik. As a fan of Counter-Strike and other great, challenging shooters, Heroes & Generals feels like it's got some of those "Special Sauce" ingredients that will keep this an epic gameplay experience for years!
So TLDR;
- WWII era
- Giant battlefields
- Multiple paths of gameplay
- Infantry (on ground)
- Tanks / Trucks / Bikes driveable!
- Planes and paratroopers playable!
- Smooth, familiar controls

Far Cry 3 is the best in the series. I still enjoy it more than Far Cry 4! The graphics are amazing! You don't need a high end computer to enjoy the beauty of this game. The acting is great! I love the actors and the entire plot while I'm at it! Honestly, if Ubisoft decided to polish this game up with new graphics, story missions, side missions, and another island as a new game for 2015, they would have my $60.
Nitty-gritty stuff:
Plot - Amazing. Better than any other game, even the Telltale Walking Dead games. You can actually sense the character development! In the beginning, Jason Brody is a typical college kid on vacation and it ends up being a disaster because Pirates take his friends and... I won't go any further because spoilers. But in the beginning, he is a kid that can't handle the sight of blood to a maniac that exclaims, "Holy sh*t! Did you see that explosion!?" Like, this is the best character development I have ever seen. Ever. It's amazing. 11/10 plot.
Gameplay - It's solid. Rock solid. Titanium solid. Want to be stealthy? Here, take a bow and a couple rocks and go all metal gear solid, I don't care. Go loud? Take explosive tip arrows, an LMG, and 6 packs of C4! I could care less! Want to snipe people with exploding, armor and material penetrating, .50 caliber rounds? Go ahead! It's Far Cry! Do whatever the he*l you want to do! IT'S OPEN WORLD!!! That's the best part too, the open world. Plenty of enemies to kill, which is also good. There are types of enemies that actually make you THINK on how to eliminate them.
Fixes - LOTS of fixes from Far Cry 2 that are amazing! Like dirty guns? No more! Even if you pick up a gun that's been lying in mud for 100 days it will still be in pristine condition, so you can dazzle yourself with that chrome Deagle you;ve always wanted time after time! Weapon jamming is gone. Never had a picked up AK jam on me. It's a good thing! Remember those stupid maps you had Far Cry 2 that you had to keep flipping through each time to find the right one after you passed through a town? Only one now, and you can set waypoints! Waypoints are a necessity in this game.
Okay, the part you've been dreading. The bad things about the game. But have no fear, for this is a GOOD PC port! The FOV goes all the way to 120! *Screams like a school girl* The only bad thing is is that there's no hotkey for the craftig menu. You have to hit ESC or whatever you have pause assigned to and then hit crafting. It gets annoying after a while. That is pretty much my only complaint with the game. Well. I wish it could have a longer story, regenrating headhunter missions, and maybe another island, but yeah. You know, it's not going to get fixed now that they're already working on Far Cry 5, which please please please make it take place in the tropics again! It's so cool!
Verdict: Buy. This. Game. Story only about 15 hours long, but around 50 hours to actually COMPLETE the game, as in do all the side missions, headhunter and hunting missions, and find all the specialty weapons. Even then, it's just hilarious to jump in and take the .50 cal and shoot a guy in the chest and watch him go flying 15 feet back! P.S. If you shoot the ground, sometimes the body will go flying into the air! Hilarious!

The game is great except for the fact that looting bodies is very finicky and Jason is incapable of climbing stairs. When the game does this, you have to jump to get up the stairs. This is especially frustrating when you are trying to activate a radio tower. If Far Cry 4 fixed these problems, then skip this game and go straight to Far Cry 4.

Mount and Blade: Warband is a sandbox RPG with a medieval setting, featuring a deep system of combat for melee weapons, archery, horse combat, and massive battles. Players can do anything from herding cattle and raiding villages, all the way up to becoming the Emperor of Calradia by one's own bloody hands. Somewhere in between, you will likely do a lot of it. There are many things to do in this game. One can go in search of tasks to help out the peasantry, lords and kings in the various factions of the war-torn lands of Calradia. There are tournaments to fight in, wars to take advantage of. It even has a large bandit problem, and someone's gotta get rid of them. If you don't want to do any of that, you can take advantage of the local economies. The game has a functional economy, and by exploiting trade routes and purchasing businesses, you can gain massive profits.
One can become a lord, put a pretender on a faction's throne, and even do mercenary work. But the higher your ambitions rest, the more you will need support. Bump elbows with Calradia's rich noble class and this will become significantly easier. That's right, there are feasts in this game. Be careful when you enter the courts, for the nobility are scheming and trying to profit as much as possible. Calradia is hardly a land that espouses the values of Chivalry. Despite Chivalry being something of a thing. There is an in-game honor system. It's not a cut black-and-white morality system. Generally, if you make people suffer, you lose honor. If you help people and act benevolently, you gain it. But does the game ever tempt you to dishonor yourself. War is highly profitable, and peasants are defenseless. Moreover, they have very valuable things to take. And it destroys your opponent's economy when you raid, which will help your war efforts. There's a macabre decision making process as to when to be a shining knight.
The game's combat system as mentioned before has a lot of depth to it. It can take a little time to get a hold of. Especially when you factor in massed battles, mounted combat, and fortress assaults. All of which require different tactics. You can order your soldiers around, tell them where and when to attack. It adds yet another level of this game to be able to fight alongside your own men. The melee combat system is particularly in-depth. It has a basic "Simon Says" system, where you can attack left, right, overhead, or to thrust. And you can both block and parry those individual attacks. Correct timing, and watching your opponent's movements are required to survive the battlefield. The weapons also have functioning speed and reach. A sword is quicker than a longaxe, but doesn't reach as far. So the person with the longaxe will try and keep his opponent away, while the sword user will want to close. You also can't use a big weapon in a shoulder-to-shoulder formation. You won't have the room.
There is also the ability to do ranged combat. Throwing weapons, crossbows and archery mainly. In some mods, guns are available, but that will be discussed later. Each of the first three are different. Thrown weapons let you keep your shield up, but don't fly very far, and usually don't have much ammunition. But they can make a huge difference. Being able to throw spears or axes at your opponent before closing on them will give you a considerable advantage. Crossbows fire slowly, only require strength to equip, and are highly accurate. They also break through armor with ease. Bows have a draw system. The longer you hold your arrow, the more inaccurate you are, as you struggle to hold your bow taut. So you pick out your target, lead and arc your shot, and fire. It takes considerable mastery, but a bow can be especially deadly.
Mounts are in this game as well, and they add even more to the game. You can engage in combat from horseback with nearly any melee weapon, lances, and even thrown weapons, bows and some crossbows. Horse archery is a tough skill to master, but is highly effective, as one should suppose. Melee combat on the mounts features the same system and strengths that the foot combat has. Charging down enemies with a lance and an axe can be highly satisfying. You can make passing attacks, or choose to charge your opponent. When you're fighting other cavalry, the option to go for the horse is present. It's not only an option, it's highly recommended.
Armor also changes how you fight in this game. It will slow you down, but it will also protect you. If you plan on getting stuck in a fight, I reccomend lots of it.
The setting itself is fairly bog-standard medieval setting fare. You have various kingdoms based from our real world peoples, all having different strengths and different tactics. It's somewhat anachronistic, with Not-Mongols fighting Not-Vikings and Not-Italians fighting Not-Russians. But this is explained in the backstory. Which brings us to one of the flaws in this game. The  setting and characters are not especially well developed. This is to leave the game's story open, as so many playthroughs will be different. After the game's start point, the AI factions react to each other and the player appropriately. Meaning that the game's story is precisely what you make it. But the lords and other important characters come off more as tour guides than as real people. The amount of open-endedness also gives you the feeling of being thrown into a pool and being told to swim.  But when you float, and start to swim, you get the feeling that you're creating the story. The ink is the blood, the quill a dagger and all of Calradia is the parchment. Each playthrough will be different. I have had one particular kingdom dominate the game in one playthrough, only to be crushed in the next. And that is part of the attractiveness of this series of games.
The game boasts a skill and levelling system as well, typical for an RPG. You level stats, and choose what skills and weapon proficiencies to level. There are no classes, and no need for them. Skills run the gamut of things like first aid, pathfinding, leadership, and combat skills like power strike. You can find companions, who can take care of these skills for you. Companions are additional characters that you can fight alongside, level up and equip as you desire. Which brings me to the recruitment system. One can go from town to town, recruiting soldiers for their cause. Whatever that may be. Soldiers will also level up, when given battle experience and training.
One of the game's largest strengths is the mod support. Modding the game is easy, often times one just has to integrate files to the appropriate folder, or simply install a mod and run it from the launcher. Mods run the gamut of small tweaks, such as Freelancer, Diplomacy and Pre-battle orders and deployment. Which allow the player to fight in someone else's army as a soldier, increase the amount of options for diplomatic actions, and to arrange your soldiers before a battle, taking some of the tedium away from command. Also available are gameplay overhauls like Floris, which keep the main setting, but offer so many tweaks that the game is nearly different. There are also completely new campaigns, in new settings. You can find many different ones. Europe in the medieval ages, dark age britain, completely original settings, and even Westeros are available. Respectively, they're named 1257AD, Brytenwalda, Prophesy of Pendor and Clash of Kings. There are many more mods available that I will not list, since it would take too long to list it all.
But the game is not without flaws, for all the praise I just showered on it. The game's graphics are extremely poor. As mentioned before, the story leaves much to be desired, same with characters. The game's animations are also quite cumbersome and static. The combat can also feel slow, until you get ahold of it. I would reccomend it. There's a free demo offered here on Steam, if you're not sure you'll enjoy it.

Mount & Blade: Warband is a first sequel to original medieval action RPG video game Mount & Blade. Warband was developed by TaleWorlds and was published by Paradox Interactive. This highly anticipated indie video game won numerous rewards and also was nominated “Best Indie Game of the Year“.
While most RPGs with medieval time setting involving magical events, supernatural entities, Warband strikes you with realistic combat without any fireball spells.  Mount & Blade: Warband is a mix of action RPG and turn-based strategy games. You travel on world map as in turn-based strategy game and fight or explore villages and cities in third-person or first-person perspective. In Mount & Blade: Warband your goal is simple: rule all of the Calradia. You start as a simple mercenary but later you can become faithful vassal or even the king. While there is no actual story other than rule Calradia, you can do various quest to earn gold and improve relations with other lords or cities. Quest differs from simply delivering goods to capturing enemy lords.
There are total 24 different skills which you can improve by leveling up. You get experience points from battles or doing quest. Those skills affect how you perform in actual battles, travelling in world map, trading, maintaining your army. Graphics are not top quality but in won't prevent you from enjoying the game. In fighting mode you can command your troops with simple tasks such as follow, stand ground, charge and to choose what type of weapon to use. Every field battle usually turns into over 100 troop mosh-pit and picking the retreating enemy troops one by one. City and castle sieges or defenses can be more enjoyable as you can explore city or castle. After capturing or being awarded a fief you can improve it with new building which gives you various bonuses, for example, you can start a production to earn more additional gold. Also Mount & Blade: Warband can be enhanced by various mods from simple textures to total conversions.
The main difference from the original Mount & Blade is the multiplayer. Default number of players is up to 64. Modded servers can hold more than 200! Game modes include well-known Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, Assault (similar to conquest mode seen in Battlefield series) and also Siege (where you need to capture or defend a castle), Battle (last standing man wins) and Duel (one to one combat).
To sum up, I would recommend Mount & Blade: Warband to anyone who always imagined what it would feel to actually be in a medieval battle not just command your troops from above. Multiplayer mode with various maps both official and fan made can keep you logged in for a long amount of time and total conversion content will enrich your singleplayer experience.

I figured out a fix that worked for me regarding the UPlay issue:
I got the error that wouldn't launch [UPlay] from Steam. I had bought the game and everything. I had already bought Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon: Future Soldier, which also requires UPlay, last year. I launched that game and UPlay worked fine; no problems at all. So there shuldn't be a problem with Far Cry 3 either, but a way around it without tampering with the files and etc...
What I did:
Open up your UPlay account or access it with another game that requires UPlay that works. Find the option that allows you to ENTER YOUR ACTIVATION CODE. I believe it is found under the Games tab in UPlay. Copy that Key code you get from Steam and Paste it into the Game Activation thing in UPlay. Once your game is activated and added to your Library in UPLAY, then try to open the game from UPLAY. *Make sure you are logged in on Steam though...* I have tried multiple times launching the game through UPLAY and it has worked successfully.
Note: This is a fix i found through the "Error in UPlay Crashing and failing to launch game through Steam." It would close every time I tried launching the game BEFORE I did this. The game is running fine, no issues. If anyone has/ had the same issue as this one, give this troubleshoot a try!

The way they made it is a far cry from how wars are fought you don’t give your soldiers inadequate gear and weapons then send them off to the slaughter and expect them to win you give them equipment that is better suited for the situation and is capable of standing some sort of a stance.
“Sir the enemy has a squad of tanks what should we do?”
“Well we have a ton a bikes… use those.”
“B-but sir!”
“Did I stutter? saddle up and peddle on out there son!”
The tanks vs bikes battles come to be because of the differences in sources that each faction has. From my understanding, the unbalance is partially caused by the people playing on the Axis side have had way more warfunds to buy resources with than the people in the Allied side. This causes the unbalance in battles and the one-sided wars that have occurred for some time now. Additionally, since the Axis side ends up wining more often, players switch factions and thus more players end up joining the Axis which doesn’t help much with the balance.
If you are on the Allied side, the above reason is the likely cause of the bikes vs tanks battles. Additionally, if you want to avoid these sort of battles when playing on either faction, when you click on “enter combat”, select “find mission” and when you click on a battle, you can view the resources available at that time. Admittedly, I had high expectations for this game... but after several hours playing, here's my breakdown:
1 - Graphics - The graphics are pretty good, and fit to the WWII style quite well.  However, the landscape textures have way too much contrast.  Running through the hills, you think you see something, like a helmet sticking out, shoot at it, and think wtf... only to find out it's a branch from a nearby tree that glitched out.  I find it very difficult to see (and ESPECIALLY to hit) anything from over 100m away.
2 - Physics - So... many... flipped... jeeps/tanks/bicycles.  Driving one of these vehicles over the terrain is like how I'd imagine learning to ride a bicycle on a tight-wire for the first time.  On flat road, it's no problem.  But even the smallest rocks or cracks will flip your vehicle, with no way to upright it.  Don't believe me?  Try running a tank over a bicycle.  The tank will flip.
3 - Bullet physics - Accuracy appears random at best.  As I mentioned - hitting anything from 100m+ is ridiculously difficult.  You start with the M1G Garand, and having played for about 10+ hours, I still haven't unlocked the next rifle.  Close combat is sparodic as well...  I can come up behind a sniper, start shooting him on the ground... and while one or two bullets (out of 6 or 8?) might hit him, he still has time to stand up from prone and start shooting.  My clip runs out, and I'm standing there reloading while he kills me.   It's almost as if you're better off NOT shooting first.
Also had a case today where I was in an upstairs room in a barn.  I knew an enemy was downstairs, and might come up the stairs.  I stood at the top of the stairs, and when he was 2 rungs from the top, I began shooting down at him.  2 shots are taken directly at his helmet (this is POINT-BLANK now)... while 2-3 others should hit his body while he's climbing off the ladder.  Again, my clip runs out and I'm reloading, while he guns me down.
Games that had successful runs for several years did so because they were accurate and consistent in their gameplay.  Not because they were a new style/genre, had cool new graphics, etc.  Once the shininess of the "new" game wears off, players have to have a familiar feeling with consistent gameplay.  Playing this game almost feels like the success of every encounter is based on a dice roll, Dungeons and Dragons-style, like old pencil-and-paper RPGs.
Ultimately, having been a gamer for 20+ years, I fully expect more from these games by now.
I hope developers stop rushing out these games to make a quick buck, and start TESTING these games to make them BETTER... not just FASTER.  :-/

Mount and Blade is a hard game to describe. All of the elements it has are very basic. The overworld is basic. The character development is basic. The control of your army is basic. Initially, everything can seem outdated and underwhelming. But if you get into it MnB is a great series. Few games offer the same thrill of charging across a field with 100 of your soldiers behind you into an enemy army and manually controlling each sword swing, or storming up the ladder of a castle to fight your way into it. This is a game where you can be a simple trader having an army of bodyguards or an aspiring dictator who tries to control the world. Or you can just enter tournaments and beat people over the head with wooden sticks. The combat system is fantastic, allowing you full control of each swing and block. You have to time you attacks right to hit your opponent otherwise you're just bashing their shield, leaving yourself open to retaliation. A very fun game that everyone should have in their collection.

If you like the idea of fighting on a medieval battlefield, BUY THIS GAME.
Pros:
-The innovative direction-based melee combat system is a centerpiece of the game's features.  It's an easy-to-learn, hard-to-master system that makes the swordplay much more fun and engaging than simply clicking to swing.
-The single-player open-world campaign can be very engrossing at later levels, as you attempt to achieve political and conquest goals you set for yourself.
-Multiplayer is fast-paced and well-balanced, and is a great test of skill.  Multiplayer alone is worth the price.
-There are many, many, many great mods for the game, ranging from minor tweaks to full blown conversions.  Star Wars, the old west, sword & sandals, sword & sorcery, the list goes on.
Cons:
-Single player campaign can be somewhat boring at lower levels, as you're more or less limited to running the same quests over and over for different faction lords, or finding bandits to fight.  The game doesn't start to shine until you're powerful enough to make friends and enemies of AI faction lords.
-Micro-managing and positioning your armies during battles is tedious.
-The game's visuals are pretty rough around the edges.  Also, the animations, though an improvement over the original, are still pretty wonky.

Far Cry 3 is a blast! Immersive landscape and environments, living wilderness, lots of enemies and multiple possibilities to take them down. Will you raid a camp Rambo-style, gun-blazing everything and everyone? Will you put C4 bombs on your car and use it to make a diversion? Will you open a cage to release a goddamn tiger on your enemies? Or will you sneak your way through? The choice is all yours.
The story is simple but feels alright, the characters are all pretty charismatic and have their own personalities; the game has humour and dramatic moments. It is beautiful and immersive. The gameplay is varied enough, and when you think it might become boring, new gameplay elements come in. The best way I can sum up this game is potential. Everything is there for this to be a successful game in the future, but it has a few issues.
Likes:
-Solid tactics and gunplay, a far cry from the high profile shooters on today's market
-A decent unlock system, where nothing is truly handed to you but doesn't cater specifically to the people who spend money in game
-A work in progress combo of RTS and FPS elements
Dislikes/Room For Improvement:
-Feels like 2 separate games, RTS element is very limited.
-Doesn't feel like an MMO. A game like Planetside has a roamable battlefield that feels massive, and this game has nothing more than instanced combat placed on a map.
-Controls and movement are still clunky. This game will need more polish in those areas, but I expect this to improve over time.
Despite its flaws, I highly recommend this game due to its potential and the fact that it is free. While it may never achieve the gameplay of more heralded shooters or the massive following of the larger MMOs, this will be a solid game for years to come.

I rarely play these kind of big budget, AAA games, but I saw this on sale and decided to gave it a whirl. I'm glad I did.
The game is a wild ride, with a large variety of over-the-top vehicles, gadgets & weaponry at your disposal. The voice acting and dialogue are first grade, comparable to what you'd get in a first-rate action film.
The combat and stealth are implemented quite well, despite an overreliance on QuickTime events. Those QT events make the game feel very "console" at times. Veteran gamers will know what I mean. It's hard to really *lose* here.
The story is compelling and well told, despite the protagonist being a typical Joe Sixpack American-type. The villains are some of the most outrageous and cruelly entertaining I've ever seen in any video game. There are also some brilliant sections simulating drug-induced hallucinations that reveal a great depth of creativity.
Be warned, you have very little control over the plot of the game. The only real chance to influence the plot comes at the game's very end.
Highly recommended, if you can get past the highly scripted nature of the game and ignore its clear console origins.

M&B: Warband is a fantastic game. Whilst it's graphics aren't pretty, I find they look good in terms of aethsetic. I'm not too bonkers about the RPG bits, which are quite deep, with players able to marry into certain families, become fiefs, or become king of an entire faction, but what I really like is the combat. Nearly every aspect of it is wondrous. The actual act of clubbing, slashing, and chopping feels nice and meaty. The combat is highly skill based, with players being able to attack in four directions, slash, backslash, uppercut, and downslash. You can block all four of these attacks with respective blocks, or use a nice thick shield, if you're lazy like me. But t doesn't end there, there's ranged weapons, which can be bows, crossbows, or thrown weapns. All of these weapons do different damage to different body areas. I especially enjoy tossing a javelin into an enemy player's horse, hearing a big meaty thunk as it connects with its face. Then walking over to the prone cavalier, still recovering from his fall, and slicing open his face. Which brings me to horses, cavalry is wonderful, as you get a new level of depth, from fighting atop a mighty steed. Another great thing is the single player combat system, in which you can command your army, although options are rather limited. The single greatest thing about the game is the moddability. You can turn the game into any setting you wish, from ancient Rome, to dark-age UK. I've even seen a mod that takes place in WW2 China!
All in all, this game is an absolute masterpiece, I can get past the shoddy graphics and spammy players, because the good severely outweighs the bad. I wholeheartedly reccomend this game.

FarCry 3™ is one of the best in the franchise. The story is self driven and immersive. You'll find yourself getting emotionally attached to your character Jason Brody, but not so much your friends or the Rakyat. The Rakyat is a tribe that begins to influence you and pushes you into become a warrior that sets a large part of the theme to this game. A large arsenal of weaponry compliment the game, but you'll find yourself sticking and mastering only a few weapons you feel comfortable with.
You can raid enemy camps using stealth, or through direct assault. The latter probably being good only if you're fast on your feet and quick with the trigger. Situations can always go out of control and you can find yourself biting off more then you can chew if you're not careful. Firefights are almost always satifying, complimenting both the mechanical side of the AI and intensity in which each fight can bring. I found using proper battle logistics and pre-planning my attack to always give me success, while driving straight into the fight on a jeep giving poor results and alot of death activated loading times.
What really makes this game however, are the enemies and the main antogonists. Playing the game, you come to personally hate Vaas and are upset at each missed opportunity to kill him. All the antagonists in this game are real hardcore killers that really leave a mark with their inhumanity and brutality to life. You'll enjoy taking theirs away from them when given the chance.
Wait for it to go on special, or not. You'll enjoy the game.

An epic title -- if you have an imagination. A Brief but utterly honest review.
Mount & Blade: Warband is a somewhat brilliant concept. You are plonked down in a land of opportunity to seek out fame and fortune. The only problem is; no-one tells you exactly how you are meant to achieve your goals. You could wander aimlessly around the map from pillar to post just generally getting your♥♥♥♥♥kicked.
However; through a bit of trial and error and a bit of internet surfing, you discover what you're meant to do. Get recruits and fight!
Though that is not all. This is a Sandbox title, which means that they have given you this big area to play in, thrown in a couple of toys, but it's really upto you what game you play. This is where your imagination comes in.
You could decide to be some Just band of crusading knights, join up with a kin and fight down his enemies, always doing what you believe is right. On the other hand, you could run around, killing farmers, ran-sacking caravans and pillaging villages. You could decide to join high society and gain the favour of all the lords so that you can gain a political victory -- or even strike out on your own and forge your own kingdom.
This game is hugely punishing when you get defeated, but hugely rewarding when you find the sweet spot -- But you're only really going to enjoy it if you use your imagination and decide how you want to play. That said, it gets my thumbs up and I recommend this title to those with a little patience who enjoy an immersive experience.

This game, quite frankly, is amazing. For one, this game has done what a ton of other games have failed at: actually functioning horse combat with axes, swords, maces, and most impressivley, lances. As far as medieval games go, this is by far the best. Whether you want to be a loyal vassal of a king, helping him conquer his enemies, or carve out your own kingdom in the midst of this massive land, or even be a mercenary just selling your sword for the money to upgrade gear or build a huge independent army, the possibilites are endless. For the price, this game has excellent replay value. There's something extremely gratifying about being able to roleplay as anything you want while directly leading your troops in battle as you yourself fight amongst them. Moreover, this game doesn't favor one style of combat over another. You can be an amazing swordsman and tank damage as well as dealing it, or you can be a marksman bowman or crossbowman and deal out just as much damage or more from horseback or on foot, if you perfect the skill. This is the first game of its style that I have personally played where you can actually lead a host of 150+ men into battle and besiege take castles, or just smash foes on the field. The commander's choices of being able to order certain troops to follow, charge, or hold a position also makes the battles an especially enjoyable experience. 10/10 fantastic game. More than worth the money.

If you follow games at all, you already know that Far Cry 3 is one of the best, most immersive single-player first-person shooters to come along in years. It combines a chilling story, thought-provoking themes, solid gunplay, beautiful graphics, an excellent soundtrack, and jam-packs all of them into an expansive and immersive open-world that is just as fun to explore as it is to kill baddies in.
The intriguing main storyline will pull you in from the start. The main character undergoes a bone-chilling and believable transformation from a priveleged, pampered rich boy to an angry, ston-cold killer. The rest of the story is also full of complex and entertaining characters (not to mention one of the best villains in recent memory), and yet you will be just as pulled in by the opportunities to hunt, craft, kill pirates, liberate forts, and explore the beautiful Rook Island for side-quests, relics and assorted goodies that allow you to build up your skills and expand your arsenal.
The combat, while far form the only draw, is exceptional. In this open-world, the choice is yours: would you prefer to go in stealthy, set-up shop on a tall hillside with your silenced sniper rifle, or go in guns blazing with a wide variety of SMGs, shotguns, assault rifles, and explosives? The shooting mechanics are very well done - the guns have a real punch to them - and there are plenty (30+) to choose from. The AI is also solid; your enemies will take cover, try to flank you, and will kill you easily if you play foolishly.
The graphics are excellent, and the design of the island is beautiful. Water ripples in the moonlight, sun-rays glimmer on your screen, bullets ricochet to and fro, and explosions look and feel powerful - as do the after-burning effects that can quickly consume a small forest. The electronic soundtrack is also great: it ebbs and flows with combat, and becomes somber in more heartfelt moments. It's integrated excellently throughout the game - you won't often be able to tell it's there, but it will get your heart pumping.
While exceptional, the game is not perfect. Exploration might have even been even better if the map was revealed more naturally instead of through radio towers, and I often found I had way too much money and not near enough to spend it on. The interface, crafting and customization options could also be improved. Still, as a whole, Far Cry 3 is a fantastic game that you will easily get 25-30+ hours out of and enjoy every minute of. There's much more that could be said, but this game is incredible value for anything less than $10, and you should really enjoy and explore the beatufiul but dangerous Rook Island for yourself!

I apologize for that! Don't mean to slander this behemoth of an RPG. But it encompasses your actions within the Fiefs rather aptly. As a character you trade in goods which include the usual garbage RPGs deal in; food, weapons, armour, gold, frankincense and myrrh. But also beasties of an equestrian persuasion which you can ride depending on your riding skill obviously. This makes getting about way faster which does make a dfference on the war map when you become tin soldier in scale and hurry about as the cosmic fluctuation in light levels tell you day and night are passing as your tiny horse dances along between the province capitals. And in battle when you charge the enemy and slap the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s away you feel alot more powerful too (This is the mount bit). Then you gather men around you to be able to hold your own in a fight as well as leveling up yourself, meaning you can take on larger groups of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s (this is the band bit). You see mount and band, the war blade bit just sounds right to me. Screw it! The title is irrelevant this is a unique and addictive RPG, one could write stories based on the military adventures your avatar can partake in here. It can be a slog though and I'm not talking about the creatures in Oddworld. Warband is a hefty brute and requires attention to detail, patience and guile. If your level or the difficuly is high you might get maimed. The game has options to escape capture sometimes when you lose a fight but this means getting away from your captors on the war map and reasembling an army just to cover yourself. Evading fast travelling squads is harder if you have no horse, but generally as a rule the larger the force is the slower it is, ergo you can skirt arround larger armies too big to combat successfully.
The combat here is fun though, I just suited my guy up with knight armour and a massive cleaver or axe and went to town on my opponant. Riding into war is particularly high on the agenda. Many armies are large in size often dwarfing your own, but when you rally under the king you follow whole sieges are won with you and your men in the ranks. When the day is finally yours everyone cheers like off a scene from a period movie. There is alot to balance here but this guy (Me) had a good time playing warband leading to a solid 8/10 the repetition gets a little boring after a while. But for the first 40 hours of game play you won't be disappointed!

Ah, Heroes & Generals.
Let me start off by saying, this type of  game is not for everybody. Nor is it finished, However I do believe the game warrants
a chance to try.
Gameplay:  4/5
Heroes & Generals is a FPS set during the WW2 war. Many of its gameplay elements is grounded in realism, as well as the arsenal of guns. You begin the game by creating an account, then choosing a side. The 2 current teams players can choose are  Allied forces, and Axis forces. Both complete with thier own infantry classes, weapons, vehicle and planes. All players start out  as infantry, and can later decide to branch  to different subclasses, such as tank crew, pilot, or paratroops corp.
I describe guns as having tiers, as players start out with usable weapons, or later unlocking them later. Actual gameplay consists of up to 20 players per side in an attempt to  capture points on the map, similar to how Battlefield operates. Controls are a bit clunky, reminiscient  to Arma II vets, it could use a little work. Recoil and distance are a factor in this game, so its highly reccomended to keep shots to single shots or controlled bursts. As mentioned range is a factor so lead  your shots as well. There are somewhat a good variety of maps, most are recycled variants of base maps with additional components such as fog. There is also a stragety side to the game, where you manage AT (assualt teams) to do battle on fronts to win wars. however I lack experience in this tab so I won't mention most of it.
Graphics: 3.5/5

Overall, I think it's an amazing game and if you enjoy FPS and open world games, you really should get it.

How do I start with Mount & Blade: Warband? You see, that's a very hard thing to do, when a passer-byer might look at this game, they might view it with just a passing glance, the graphics can look very dated, and the game itself is getting up in age, but dang if that isn't absurd. To be able to proberly grasp what I'm saying, you'd need to play the game. Getting into Mount & Blade Warband can be rather intimidating, first of all, this is not modern fighting game, you don't have any kind of firearms at all without Napoleonic Wars, so for a regular gamer, this could be intimidating, but fret not, for the learning curve may be steep, after a few days, it's going to be nice and even, the controls for this game might be a bit tricky at first, especially the blocking, however melee controls are very reponsive and feel right, nothing like hearing that satifying sound of a sword piercing through the gallbladder or spleen of your enemy. Aside from Melee combat, the game has a fairly well done archery system, it even has the archer's paradox incorporated. You hold you bow too long, your arrow will have to much power, and will bounce in the air, not long enough, and it might travel but five feet. The game's combat feels quite real this way. The roleplaying elements of the single player are really basic but quite satisfying, the overall feel for the era is well captured, and the world while feeling slightly dejointed, as if incomplete, is built quite well, with only a few glitches in terrain.
The Napoleonic Wars DLC brings line combat into the game, with realistic unrifled smoothbored Flintlock rifles and handguns, the Bayonet will more often then not be your main weapon, I can go on forever, but trust me when I say Mount & Blade: Warband is worthy of a 10/10, the game is solid, addictive, it has nice mods, and a active community. It's a must have.

I do not get the Far Cry hype.  Way back when I bought this, it was advertised as "Skyrim, with guns."  This is not Skyrim with guns.  Skyrim is a huge open world style game with dynamic random quests, hundreds of caves and other things to explore.  Far Cry 3 is a boring game set on an "open world" island where everything is locked behind plot quests.
When you do gain access to a new area of the island, you shoot a couple of guys and climb a tower, then walk around and collect things until you get to one of the outposts where you shoot a few guys to take over the outpost.  Outpost secured, you look at a board and pick up essentially the same quests over and over (Go somewhere and stab a guy, or go hunt and animal).  Then you do it again.  And again.
The only saving grace of this game is Vaas.  And when you are ready to have a big gunfight showdown with the guy who has tormented you all game, you don't.  You do a quick time event and push the buttons on the screen to win.  That's how I like my final bosses in games.  No skill, or planning, or anything like that.  Just quick time events.
Online multiplayer is terrible.  Other than the game play itself just being poor, the servers don't seem to have any type of team balance, so many matches just turn into a 6 on 2 and you get stomped.  Co-op is disappointing as it is quite short, and very glitchy.  Many times we would complete the objective, but the progress never moved forward, so we'd have to suicide and play the level again.  Desyncs happen constantly in co-op, where one player sees an enemy standing there shooting and the other sees a corpse.  Some of the AI is borderline useless.  You'll be "defending the object", which actually means kill all the enemies, and you are seemingly done but it continues.  You run around looking for who's left and 5 minutes later find an enemy walking aimlessly into a wall or glitched through the ground.

After playing Heroes and Generals for a considerate amount of time, I have decided to change my review. In my original review, I decided to give Heroes and Generals a negative review, because the game was flawed in many ways, despite the combat being fun, maps being huge and the access of infantry, tanks, planes, recon and paratroopers in one game.
I came back to this game a couple of weeks ago, and I was surprised in the positive way! Here are some really visible changes since 2014:
- Addition of a third faction: Soviet Union
- Optimization of the game: it now runs really smooth for a game this big, lag is very rare
- Snipers are still mostly accessible through the cash shop, but they are less P2W now, normal infantry can still kill them with a fair chance (I even have hunted snipers in some matches with success).
- On top of that, the Standard Assault Rifles and Bolt Action Rifles have been improved, SMG are not the only useable guns now!
- Balance also has improved, most probably because there's now a third faction in the game, and there are now matches that are threeway!
- Glitches have been brought to a minimum. I haven't died randomly as far as I can remember, except when I suicided by driving my car against a tree (and that was me to blame for xD)
All in all, most of my original cons have been improved on or neutralized. This makes me happy to announce, Heroes and Generals is the game for you, if you like large, realistic and still awesome World War II fights.

I really like games with the WW2 setting, but that's not the case in H&G, although I really tried to enjoy it. Now, I know this game is still in beta, but I don't like where it is going. First of all, some people say that the game is NOT pay to win. But I can tell you it is striving to become one, and it is not even officially released! All weapons, vehicles, upgrades etc. are extremely expensive, and you gain experience and in-game currency at a pretty low rate. Then, the graphics aren't great, but I think that we could live with it. But I personally can't stand all the bugs and overall imbalance between the factions and players as well. Those who are willing to pay, have quickly access to scoped rifles, while others stay with deafult rifles and can only watch while being head-shoted by snipers every few seconds. Then, those, who don't want to pay have no access to advanced vehicles such as planes, or advanced soldiers such are parachuters, because you have to unlock them with the special - golden currency, which can only be bought with real money (as far as I know). Furthermore, to participate in the so-called general mode, you have to 'buy' units, which are again unlocked by spending experience points, those you get by playing the fps (Heroes) mode. Again, this is slow procedure. Ok, I get it, this game isn't Battlefield (although it bears many similarities) and it is suposed to be 'hard' or more realistic. But again, in this state, soldiers can only be completely and utterly alive or dead as bunch of dodoes. There is absolutely no injuries simulation, and that is in my opinion a mere spit in the face of realism. Maybe this will be added as the game updates, but at this moment, I could hardly recommend the game to more casual players.
-----------------------------------------------
Update to this review, 12.9.2014:
I've waited for a few patches and decided to give the game another try. It seems that apart from the updated menu the things have gone from bad to worse. Now there are even more unbalanced matches with even more players with sniper rifles that can shoot you across the half of map (you of course cannot spot them at a distance, which could be a slight glimpse of realism, but I think the reason are washed textures and limitation of the graphical engine). Not to mention that those things occur in the so called 'training matches', which should be made for 'new', unexperienced players. Also, I've noticed that you really have to pay for everything in this game, even if you want to merely CHANGE A NAME OF YOUR SOLDIER, you have to pay 7,500 units of in-game currency, which approximates to the money earned in several good matches.
So, clearly, with every update the game is becoming more pay to win, which leads me to another question, which deals with pretty every f2p game: why on Earth have the developers ability to charge for the in-game stuff when the games are still in betas?
I doubt that I'll give the game another try anytime soon. Sadly, the developers have managed to ruin it completely.

I will come back within a year or so to do a more comprehensive critique, when the game is more finished, and dare I say, playable.

Don't get me started on planes. I hate them, so much. You know how annoying it is to have a Fighter/Bomber just pop you to pieces as you support your team capping a point? It sucks. That's why I play Recon Defense. Never really "In" the fight. Just, quietly helping your buddies out.
The teamplay has a lot to offer, with the Assault Teams and the war itself. Up the US!
But there are still a few bugs. I like how the American Sherman can't drive through a pile of ADAMANTIUM FREAKIN' LOGS.
WTH. Flipping your tank on a ROCK.
And then getting your tummy blown to smitheroons.
Not impressed by that.
But all in all, a good game. :D 8.5/10!

Never have I played a game so massive, so open and so modable. Now don't get me wrong, vanilla in this game wasn't half bad. Heck the first mount n blade was great first time I played it, It was so very original from the games I usually played. A trait trully unique to the few gifted developers in todays gaming society. I soon promptly bought warband however, since many many mods have been migrating and popping up in this game. Not to mention its essentially a "upgrade" to the original, such as adding new animations, better graphics, more units, an entirely new nation and all that good snaz a remake does.
What makes it stand out from previous games is that you're able to go out, carve some cozy fields and settlements for yourself, grab a castle here and there and call yourself King. You can make your own empire, ruling with an iron fist, craving more lands as you eventually swallow up Calradia in your imperial gain. Or as usual, a jackass nation will declare war on your pettyass kingdom and kick the♥♥♥♥♥♥outta you until you beg for mercy wondering why you thought you could ever become a king. It's still pretty fun though.
Another aspect that made this game fun, as I said before, was the modding scene. There...are TONS of mods out there. A lot of them are fantastic and really change the game into something entirely different yet keep the good old base ideas. Just to name off a few there is the 1257ad mod (personal fav) which sets it in Fuedal Europe during that year, Clash of Kings mod which is pretty self explainatory, and many improvement mods such as Floris and Native expansion. Which in themselves add thousands of items to the game. And thats just scrapping the surface of the modding scene. It's so beautiful.
In the end this game is so god damn open source that I managed to pour 627 hours (and counting) into it, and have yet to expierence being a King since I be but a humble nooblet. An easy 9.5/10 in my book.

Let me start off by saying that the best part of this game is not the game itself.  That would be the modding community that have collectively spent thousands of hours developing and updating the many mods available for this game.  Want to control an army of elephants? There is a mod for that.  Want to participate in the world of Game of Thrones?  There is a mod for that.  Even if you just want to put a little more spice in the native game mode, there is a mod that will just do that for you.
The storyline in this game is weak, if you are looking for a standard RPG-esque feel.  You create your own story, you control your own destiny, and you ultimately decide how the game is won.  Want to conquer the world, go for it.  Want to be the most notorious bandit in the world, go for it.  Even if you want to just be a very rich trader, utilizing the market's highs and lows to cut a profit, that is possible as well.  Once again, I will state that certain mods have expanded on these possibilities giving you a more rich story for yourself.
If you want a competitive feel and desire to use your combat skills you learned online, there is still an active community for you.  The community is more rich in Europe, but there is still a few good servers to find for the Americans.
There are still downsides to this game.  This is not a game for a casual gamer who tries to fit in an hour between work, family and school.  The "mid-game" can become quite bland, there comes a point to where you are too strong for bandits, but too weak to fight lords or take castles with nothing else in between but to grind it out.  The AI can also be frustrating to deal with at times.  You can see lance and shield equipped nights stare at each other for quite some time without knowing what to do as they are too close to stab eachother, but too dumb to pull out a sword or mace and start swinging.
All that aside, I highly recommend this game and wish more people (especially in the US) played this game.

If no one sends tanks and planes to a battlefield, then that team does not have tanks or planes to use ingame.  It is a fun game, but it can be one sided at times, but that happens in an game like this for the most part.
