Presentation:
Been there, seen that.
Scripted scenes here and there.
Same gameplay mechanics for the last 7 years !
It's all the same whether you're in space, under water, on foot, tank, drone, A-10, Osprey, Apache, Zzz...
The story was...wait, was there a story ?
The most memorable thing was the dog. Puppy!
Don't let me started on the lousy drama !
Riley's (dog) death would have been a much more saddening event that papa ghost's (Elias) funny/funky death scene.
It meant a lot for so many players losing "SOAP" on the 3rd Modern Warfare 3 title, compared to a cheap death of a character that barely grew on you in Ghosts !
Gameplay:
Very FEW memorable fights and scenes.
Press F,E,G,N,V,Q,E RMB,LMB, Press both LMB + RMB !
What is this ? CoD or God of War ?
Visuals:
If that's supposed to be next gen I wonder what Crysis 3 was all about.
i7 4770K + 32 GB Ram + dual GTX680 4GB in SLI with shadow/texture flickering plus frame rate drops. Disturbing !
Solution to shadow flickering ? Turn off SLI. Really ?!?!
Sound:
Expect to hear many of the same things as in CoD MW1. (breath hold, grunt, grenade rolling...).
Wasn't that game almost 7 years ago ?
How can so many antagonists sound the same while holding their breath or falling of a 2 story building ?
The best part is when the credits start rolling. You'll feel delighted the nightmare is over !
Over all score ? 4/10

It's a an absolute SHAME that what could have been an amazingly fun game, similar to the original Modern Warfare was half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥when being ported to PC - the netcode is horrible, lag is tremendous, everything that has to do with the network seems odd. It is so rushed that we don't even have the NETWORK BARS. We got used to not being able to see our ping on PC but now we can't even see the crappy network bars.
The singleplayer campaign is fun and has an entertaining story as always. But, the game is LOCKED at a FOV of 60, which makes it pretty much unplayable and makes several people dizzy (you sit much closer to a monitor than a TV) and, it is locked at around 90FPS. At the beginning, if you had under 6 GIGS, yes, 6 GIGABYTES of RAM, the game wouldn't even open. No game that I've played uses a full 4 GB of memory, let alone 6.
If you have a sweet gaming rig with SLI and an i7 Extreme, none of that matters. The game is locked at 90FPS, that's that. To make matters worse, the game seems to favor people with worse computers, so you're better off just ditching your 780Ti and using the graphics card integrated on your processor.
It's a real shame that the COD series went from such greatness, 64 players, dedicated servers, mods, and an amazing community to just giving PC players a crappy port woth 60€ - and that's the thing, it's worth 60 freaking euros. If the game were worth 20, I would understand. But we definitely expect more from giants such as Infinity Ward and Activision.
Technicalities aside, the game IS very fun, but the technical problems get so much in the way of what COD: Ghosts tries to achieve and does achieve on consoles.
If you want this game, suggest you wait till its on a huge sale. Otherwise, the technical shortcomings just don't make it worth its 60€. Honestly, for that price, Battlefield 4 is now the better game - even though it, too, has its fair share of problems, the dev team seems to actually be doing something about it. However, for Ghosts, the community needs to fix these problems.
For the next release, IW/Treyarch need to get their stuff together if they don't want to lose many, many loyal PC customers.
Bottom line -  If you're rich, get it. If your clan plays it, get it. If you're going to play by yourself, wait.

Heroes and Generals is a surprisingly good game that is free. And, unlike most "Free" to Play games, you do not actually have to pay money in order to advance and unlock cool and new things.
You do need coins to upgrade and advance your weaponry, but you earn coins by fighting battles, and the more battles you fight, the more coins you will come to earn.
The only downside to that is that a lot of things cost a lot of coins to buy. For example, it takes 92.000 coins to buy a German Panzer Mark III. Good news is that you can earn that much money after a couple days of fighting, and this system always makes sure that people keep playing the game.
Unlike other games that usually go dead after a while, this game keeps expanding to the point where the server system have had to be updated and enlargened in order to deal with the mass of people.
Choice of Combatants:
- Germans
- Americans
Classes you can be in the game:
- Infantry
- Pilot
- Tanker
- Paratrooper
- Recon (Sniper)
Cool Special Weapons and Vehicles:
- King Tiger
- PPSH
- MG42
- Schwerer Panzerspähwagen!
- Shovels (the real mans tool)
- Jeeps and Kübelwagons
As a German tanker, my personal goal is to eventually unlock the King Tiger.
Downside of the game:
American weapons are wwaaaaayyyyy too overpowered. They need to be nerfed. Somehow an American bazooka can kill a German tank in one shot, yet it takes four shots from an American tank to kill a German tank. How does that make sense?
Its also like how a M1 Garand somehow does better a close quarters fighting than a MP34, despite having a much slower and less efficient firing rate (atleast in real life).
The developers, in their efforts to eliminate the usual "Germans dominate the game with their epic weaponry and technology" have inadvertedly made the Americans into the new "dominating Germans". American weapons need to be nerfed a bit in order for the game to be truly equal.

Note: I am a big fan of the Modern Warfare series.  The single player & spec ops there was great.  I hated Black Ops.
Setting aside the copy/paste model that is Call of Duty, this felt really lazy.  A lot has been lifted from the MW series and the levels are formulaic and generic.  Now, that's not to say I didn't have fun.  The levels are entertaining, the gameplay is entertaining, this wasn't a waste of time.  The problem is that it's 1, maybe 2 non-story related achievements per level.  Instead of 3-4 intels per level, its 1 per level for a total of 18.  More than half of the intels are unmissable, unlike in the MW series where they spent effort hiding them.
I realize these games aren't supposed to be realistic, but they really jumped the shark to where I'm just going "Oh come on, really?  Really?"  The space fights are fun, but they're so over the top & silly that it just underlines what the series has become.  The story is very forgettable, the characters are boring, the writing is full of clichés.  The villains in the MW series had legitimate reasons, they were memorable, they were interesting.  The main villain in Ghosts is just a stereotypical bad guy.  His reasons are "Because I'm the bad guy.  Argh!"
When one of the characters predictably dies in the cheesiest, clichéd way possible, I didn't care.  I care more about the dog, Riley, than any of the human characters.  The writing, gameplay & storytelling are all very lazy.  The game is a parady of itself.  They need to stop pooping out this model every year until they can come up with something original.  Oh, and then they try to brag about their graphics.  I mean, it looks nice but it's not going to blow you away.  The graphics in the Metro series look better, and nobody cares about graphics so try again.
I do emphasize that I had fun playing the game, but I can have fun throwing a tennis ball against the wall repeatedly.  That doesn't mean Tennis Ball Wall-Thrower Simulator 2013 would worthy of a recommend from me.
I could recommend this game at $5 as a mindless, popcorn action shooter, but greedy Activision won't even bring it down to $9.99 until about 2018.  At least the MW series I could say has replay value, redeemable qualities & is worth $10-15.  This is quite worthy of all the hate it gets.

Although this game does require a beefy computer to play (Like mine), it's nevertheless fun to play.
The single player campaign is simply incredible. Probably the best part of the game. Previous Call of Duty games have not impressed me the way Ghosts did. New storyline, new characters, new feel. Multiplayer, on the other hand, does feel a little bit repetitive compared to Infinity Ward's previous installments in the CoD franchise such as Modern Warfare 2 or Modern Warfare 3. I have been a fan of Infinity Ward's development of multiplayer since MW2, so I don't expect Ghosts multiplayer to disappoint me as time goes on. The upcoming map packs do seem promising as well.
I haven't spent too much time in Squads, so I can't really give a fully constructed review on it, but the one or two games that I did play were - let's say - interesting.
And as for Extinction, I have not played any of it at all yet. But based on reviews I've read about it, I would safely assume that it's different from Treyarch's Zombies, but familiar. Like Apple's iOS 7.
In short, Infinity Ward has not disappointed me yet, even in past Call of Duty games. I don't expect them to let me down any time soon. I recommend this for those who have a powerful computer. If you don't have a reliablly powerful computer, invest your money elsewhere.

This is an edited review, after retrying the game after giving it up for about, half a year.
Money Spent: $200, mostly for Tanks and badges.
Rating: 3/10
It's bad.
Imbalances everywhere, p2w written all over it, and you gotta be FAR too dedicated to the game for it to matter.
List of imbalances from my viewpoint
BASE DAMAGE UPGRADES - If a gun is already designed to take away 90% of the person's health, and you can BUY an upgrade to make it one shot kill, everytime, that's bad. Base damage upgrades will literally ruin a good game and create tons of imbalance.
EXPERIENCE - You cannot just, "jump in" to this game. Even in the low-level matches, you are gonna be fighting a few credit card warriors or people that have been playing since release. You have to dedicate yourself to the game, and even with that, you still have MONTHS of grinding in order to get to the level you need to get to be equal to others. Unless you wanna shell out some dosh to speed things up.
WEAPONRY SELECTION - I'm not 90% sure, but with the Soviet update, they added an Anti-Tank grenade that can one-shot light tanks, no matter what. The Soviets can get this SUPER early on in their gear tree, iirc. Also, LMGs should not just be in the game, make it a dedicated class, or make them super restrictive(bipod setup, bracing, etc.), because it is FAR too easy to spray and pray with an automatic.
AUTOMATIC VS SEMI-AUTO/BOLT ACTION - Automatics are the most overpowered weapons in the game, due to their damage output. Yes, a rifle may do more damage per shot, but the automatic can prolly fire 4 bullets in the time it takes for you to♥♥♥♥♥♥your bolt action. And accuracy is not a thing in this game, seriously, I've been sniped by more stolen Thompsons than I can count.
WEAPON THEFT - You die with your precious P2W weapon, and someone can just go over and pick it up. What was the point of it being YOURS if anyone can pick it up after you die? Not really and imbalance, more of a complaint, I'll admit.
FACTION WEAPONRY - The Garand is a piece of garbage compared to the Gewher and the SKS, both of which contain 2 more rounds than the Garand. And no, it does not do more damage than thos two, it does LESS. Also, the Kar98 and the Mosin are MILES ahead of the Springfield as well. The most infuriating thing I've dealt with as to Faction weapons is the PTR-D. That thing is so unfair and overpowered, it needs to be either thrown out, or toned down. Seriously, it can kill HEAVY TANKS, as well as SNIPE INFANTRY.
VEHICLES - Prime example of this are the Jeeps/Mobile Cars. Look at a Jeep has no side doors, big open top, easy to see the guys inside, right? The KUBELWAGEN, however, makes it to where you can maybe see the top of a German's head. Also, they need to do away with the turning out nonesense. What is the literal point of sitting in your super cool heavy tank, if you turn out for less than a second and some guy just snipes you, and then hijacks it. That isn't fun, that's FRUSTRATING.
TROOPS IN WAR - My favorite thing to talk about, in all honesty. It's really unfair when you enter a batlle, and all you guys have are Jeeps, while they have TIGER IVs and AIRPLANES. Why even play? I've played this game off and on over the years and experienced it in a variety of it's developmental stages.  I still really enjoy it.  I prefer to play Assault rather than War matches.  I also haven't even looked at the strategic "Generals" side of the game in quite some time.
I've seen a lot of negative comments and reviews about it recently.  Sure it has it's flaws, but I mostly look at it with a different perspective.  Here are a few common complaints and my view of them:
1. "It has bugs" - I've encountered very few that have detracted from my quality of play.
2. "New players just get slaughtered by veterans with better weapons" - I find that weapon upgrades and mods are nice, but it's more about how well you use the weapon than what mods are on it.  New players get killed because they haven't learned to play yet.  If you get frustrated easily when you get killed alot, this might not be the game for you anyways.  Give it some time and your skills will improve.  If I can learn to be a decent player, anyone can.
3. "It's pay to win" - I've put less than $20 in this game the entire time I've played it.  You don't have to pay anything, although it will speed up your progression a bit if you do.
4. "It's laggy" - This issue may affect different players to different degrees.  For me, I sometimes notice a little lagginess towards the end of matches.  I rarely experience lag to the degree it prevents play.
The bottom line is I find it enjoyable.  I only play the Assault battles though with an occasional Skirmish.  These are like pickup games.  You just jump in and play.  Each side is given even resources.  You are a bit at the mercy of who actually joins each side.  Sometimes one side quickly rolls over the other, but it might be the other way on the next battle.  Most of the battles are pretty good ones.
Again, I don't play in the War matches or Strategic side of the game anymore.  They could be a little unbalanced.
It's free to play, you might as well try it.

I must say I cannot recommend this game.  Generally the maps are very open with small towns or buildings acting as objectives.  Sounds pretty standard right?  Well, for someone getting into the game, it's terrible.  First off snipers generally dominate the infantry portion of the game.  The map layout encourgages snipers to essentially spawn camp objectives at such ranges that the standard rifle or smg simply can't deal with.  The problem is escalated by the fact that the sniper rifle is very hard to unlock without paying a significant amount of real money.  This makes the game very paytowin, and it's not limited to snipers and snazzy russian weapons.  Because of the maps, tanks play a dominant role on the battle field.  The problem is, only the germans actually get decent armor and if you as a German want access to it, you will inevitably end up paying big money.  Basically if the Germans have tanks, the Americans lose.  You would think that the devs would balance this with readily availble anti-tank for the Americans?  Nope, if you want a bazooka you're going to end up paying for it.  Furthermore, the game has mechanical bugs and issues that make it annoying to play.  For example, if you're in a squad with your friends and you as an individual quit the game, you are instantenously loaded back into the game.  Signing in glitches, loading glitches, and general gameplay glitches plague Heroes and Generals and if you say the excuse of "It's in beta", it doesn't matter, it's still frustrating to deal with and really isn't worth your time.
Basically if you are looking forward to a somewhat balanced, arcady ww2 large world shooter, go play battlefield 1942.  The graphics are old but the game functions and is playable to the point where you can justify sinking hours into it.  If you want a serious, intense ww2 large world shooter, go play Red Orchestra 2, it is fantastic and doesn't have the balance issues or the glitches Heroes has.

At this time, I can not recommend this game to people.  The good: Speaking of multi-player, I do like the new maps, although some are large for the amount of players (6v6 in regular TDM) in the game.  The customizations on your load-outs are decent, not as diverse as Black Ops 2, but I thought that game went overboard with equip set-ups.  It also offers a variety of game modes for different tastes.

Now for the bad: The game is almost a month old, and after two patches, the game is still somewhat broken.  My multi-player locks up frequently and I haven't tried to play the single-player after the first week and a half due to it crashing.  On-screen artifacts, stuttering, and possible lag have plagued my GTX 670s in SLI, so I disabled one of the cards to play the game more fluidly.  I think AMD crossfire users have had similar problems.  At this time, there are no dedicated servers and we are playing P2P.  There will likely never be rentable servers for this mess.  In prior COD titles, MW2 and MW3, you at least had the bar displays to tell you what type of connection you had with the host.  In Ghosts, there is nothing to indicate what type of connection you or others have.  FPS are currently capped at around 90 FPS.  FOV is locked at a nauseating and headache inducing level of 65, but at least there are third-party programs available to help in this area.  Some of the game modes are virtually empty and the game is not even a month old.  I think the total players fell to between 2000-3000 people this evening.  Check for yourself how the community is supporting this game at
.
In summary, I think Activision and Infinity Ward have abandoned PC gamers where COD is concerned.  This game was originally touted as next-gen, but in my opinion, they have actually gone backwards.  If this is next-gen, then we are in serious trouble.  COD: Black Ops is a helluva lot better than this steaming pile and that game is now three years old, plus it had dedis.  I doubt I am alone in thinking that we paid full price to be beta-testers.  They should have paid us to play this jewel.

Call of Duty: Ghosts is the tenth, most recent entry in the popular shooter franchise -- it’s also the worst. With years of experience creating games under the developer’s belt, and the leap to next generation consoles, one might expect drastic improvements in this year’s installment. But in several ways -- the campaign, the multiplayer, the features -- Ghosts is a significant step back from Black Ops II.
The problems begin with the single-player story. Black Ops II, the last Call of Duty game, made impressive strides to make the campaign more meaningful. Players could make choices that heavily affected the story, there were optional missions, characters were at least half-developed, and the near-future setting allowed for some interesting new gameplay mechanics.
Ghosts ignores all of these advancements, going back to the linearity and contemporary setting of the Modern Warfare games. Once again, America is under attack from a foreign threat. This time, it’s the “Federation”, a wholly contrived and under-explained foe made up of every country in South America who somehow manage to take over a US satellite weapon (think a drone on steroids) and destroy half the west coast.
There are also some deliciously misguided attempts at creating an emotional connection to the characters, eschewing actual character-building in favor of cheap emotional moments. Specifically, the exchanges with the main character’s father ring as incredibly manipulative and false, with a lot of unearned “I’m so proud of you, son!” moments. Dialogue is often risible as well, with such gems as, “You were never a Ghost, Rorke…” “I’m better than a Ghost now!” when the main villain of the game is confronted. This is a shame, considering Ghosts was written by the Academy-Award-winning screenwriter of Traffic, Stephen Gaghan.
The gameplay itself during the story is a dull rehash of the previous entries in the series. One could almost go through the single-player with a checklist of once-impressive events from past Call of Duty games and tick off every box. Slow-motion door breaches? Check. Dramatic first person deaths? Check. Running through chaotic, exploding environments in a linear path? Double check. Between these bombastic moments is the same aim and shoot gameplay from every previous game; the player slogs through dozens of enemies to shoot at a time. Besides some fleeting moments of interest, like an underwater stealth sequence and a heated firefight on top of a speeding train, the campaign is a chore -- or, it would be, if it was any longer than a paltry four hours.
The multiplayer fares better, but only barely. Players still customize the weapons they use and the “perks” they have, choosing unique abilities such as replenishing ammo for their guns or not showing up on the enemy’s radar; the shooting still feels snappy and agile, letting the player quickly take opponents down. All of these features have been great in past Call of Duty games, and they’re still fun here.
This is undermined by every other aspect of the multiplayer, which, for the most part, has been changed for the worse. Plenty of emphasis is put on the “Squads” system, which lets the player outfit multiple soldiers with different loadouts and take their “squad” into several new game modes. This sounds interesting in theory, but unfortunately, in practice, this means having to level up several different characters, and starting with basic equipment multiple times if the player wants to have an effective squad. Unsurprisingly, this isn’t fun, and leads to an entire section of the multiplayer feeling pointless. The normal game modes don’t come out unscathed, either, with several fan favorites from previous entries -- like Headquarters -- being gutted. Most of the maps -- with the exception of Sovereign, which is a fantastic, multi-layered factory -- are mediocre and too large for their own good, making it more common to look for opponents than actually fight them. Overall, the multiplayer can still be enjoyable, but it has lost its lustre.
Which can be said for all of Ghosts, really; time has not been kind to the Call of Duty formula. The single-player is a hollow, laughable affair with but a few redeeming qualities. Shooting other people in the face over and over in multiplayer can still be fun, but most of the changes made noticeably detract from it. Compared to Black Ops II, and even on its own merits, Call of Duty: Ghosts is a sparsely entertaining experience, one that’s mildly amusing at its best; it’s not worth its $60 price tag to all but the most desperate Call of Duty fans.

I say sandbox-ish, because while you can do other missions and activities than the main story, it feels like it's not that much that you can do and half of it feels the same.
That said, this game is certainly not bad. Actually, it's really good.
The story goes where your friends, brothers and you go on an exotic, adventurous vacation. What they didn't saw coming was that you all would be captured by swashbuckling pirates who want to sell you for ransom money. That is certainly not what the brochure said...
You manage to escape and you have to find and safe your friends and brother.
All in all, it's pretty good but it has some flaws of which mostly: Character Progression.
The game starts as you, scared and unexperienced. Never killed a man before but the moment you get a weapon in your hands, the main character goes pretty much berserk. While it is understandable that you can't limit the skills of the player, the story doesn't make this progression better and soon you will be the Berserker Warlord of the Jungle.
It has potential but it goes just a bit too fast to believe it.
Gameplay feels smooth and feels right. From the firefights to the stealth, nothing to really complain there.
There really is a bunch to do and terrain to see and it looks damn good.

All in all, a beautiful game with a name story and lots of things to do!

A gorgeous game, sandbox-ish game where you are a jungle warrior instead of just having a vacation.
I say sandbox-ish, because while you can do other missions and activities than the main story, it feels like it's not that much that you can do and half of it feels the same.
That said, this game is certainly not bad. Actually, it's really good.
The story goes where your friends, brothers and you go on an exotic, adventurous vacation. What they didn't saw coming was that you all would be captured by swashbuckling pirates who want to sell you for ransom money. That is certainly not what the brochure said...
You manage to escape and you have to find and safe your friends and brother.
All in all, it's pretty good but it has some flaws of which mostly: Character Progression.
The game starts as you, scared and unexperienced. Never killed a man before but the moment you get a weapon in your hands, the main character goes pretty much berserk. While it is understandable that you can't limit the skills of the player, the story doesn't make this progression better and soon you will be the Berserker Warlord of the Jungle.
It has potential but it goes just a bit too fast to believe it.
Gameplay feels smooth and feels right. From the firefights to the stealth, nothing to really complain there.
There really is a bunch to do and terrain to see and it looks damn good.
The biggest problem I had with Far Cry 3 is that the Field of View returns to default in cutscenes, making it look like every character is invading your personal space.
All in all, a beautiful game with a name story and lots of things to do!

After having finally completed the game I can say this much: The art, sound direction and acting are freaking superb. The vast majority of the gameplay mechanics are fun but aren't exactly unique (this is Ubisoft we're talking about here). 90% of the main storyline felt very engaging but there were often immersion breaking moments where story missions suddenly became soul-wrenchingly difficult and I'd have to play through them a dozen or so times to move forward in the story.
While I appreciate a difficult mission, I don't appreciate being led in to a situation that feels like it's supposed to be an interactive cinematic experience that at the same time forces me to die repeatedly to unexpected obstacle after obstacle until I learn its redundant pattern as the same electronic music blares at me in perfect timing with the action on screen... By the time I actually complete the mission the "awesomeness" is lost and the on-screen characters exclaiming "That was so freaking cool!" at that moment is just short of laughable.
With this one big personal gripe in mind; it's still an astounding game. It's huge, hilarious, exciting and amazing yet repulsive, frustrating and terrible all at the same time and I loved the hell out of it. There were times of frustration but with the story (and a decent one it is) behind me, I'm free to continue to discover the rest of the secrets of the island and unleash general havoc on its inhabitants with the incredible combat system that Ubisoft has so lovingly crafted in to something very fun and unpredictable... Giving me all the reason to play this game from the beginning a second time just to force things to unfold differently.
I'd wholeheartedly recommend this game... especially during a sale.

Call me defective but I really do not understand why this game got such rave reviews. Don't get me wrong, I really wanted to like this game. Granted, the game looks beautifull and the sandbox is massive, but the constraining, repetitive missions and the frustratingly clunky interface ruined the whole experience for me.
There is no way to accomplish missions in batch. For example, when you do a picture taking mission, you cannot attack a pirate base nearby  without the picture mission failing. You end up redoing a lot of stuff because you get killed stupidly by a random tiger or fall off a ledge. If there is one thing I hate in video games, it is getting the feeling I'm doing work or being constrained.
Also, missions get repetitive pretty quickly: hunt animals that move like they have ADD, attack bases, clib up towers, yada yada yada... boring.
Those 2 things would be enough to justify calling it quits. Add Uplay (why does this thing even exist?) and the frustrating "connecting to farcry3 servers" everytime I open a menu just sealed the deal. Everything just felt incredibly tedious.
Yeah, pretty graphics are nice, but when I play video games, I want to get a feeling of freedom and power that I don't get in real life. This game just feels like work, with a poorly designed interface, a bit like entering expenses on Lotus123, albeit with better graphics.

Call me defective but I really do not understand why this game got such rave reviews. Don't get me wrong, I really wanted to like this game. Granted, the game looks beautifull and the sandbox is massive, but the constraining, repetitive missions and the frustratingly clunky interface ruined the whole experience for me.
There is no way to accomplish missions in batch. For example, when you do a picture taking mission, you cannot attack a pirate base nearby  without the picture mission failing. You end up redoing a lot of stuff because you get killed stupidly by a random tiger or fall off a ledge. If there is one thing I hate in video games, it is getting the feeling I'm doing work or being constrained.
Also, missions get repetitive pretty quickly: hunt animals that move like they have ADD, attack bases, clib up towers, yada yada yada... boring.
Those 2 things would be enough to justify calling it quits. Add Uplay (why does this thing even exist?) and the frustrating "connecting to farcry3 servers" everytime I open a menu just sealed the deal. Everything just felt incredibly tedious.
Yeah, pretty graphics are nice, but when I play video games, I want to get a feeling of freedom and power that I don't get in real life. This game just feels like work, with a poorly designed interface, a bit like entering expenses on Lotus123, albeit with better graphics.

Having drained several hours and days into this game, I can comfortably say that this game is one of my favorites.  I've installed three single player mods, and all of them have saves running into 1000 in-game days.
Vanilla Mount and Blade: Warband is still, on its own, a great experience if you get into the game.  While I was never able to play with a high-tier computer, I was always able to have a firm grasp on whatever I did, from town exploring, sieges, and battles with 100+ AI fighters.  Arguably I was attracted to this game by the battles, and my ability to have a good time while doing everything else in the game is what kept me playing.  I played with several different factions and I found my niche.  However, as my game ran into it's 1000th day, and it's 2000th day, it got boring.  I knew what to do, and I knew what I had to do, but it eventually gets monotonous.
Enter the mod community.
I've recently invested in the Diplomacy Mod, and Tocan's Calradia.  Both of these mods let me have a ton more fun and put in more time.  While there are many more mods out there with much more content, a simple game changer is enough to get yourself going again.  I have maybe 7 saves all around with 1500 in-game days logged, and I'll still be playing as I look at more mods.  Prophecy of Pendor, Floris, Anno Domini 1257, the Japan mod, the feudal Europe mod, and finally the Napoleonic Wars Mod are all examples of really great mods brought forth by the community, and looking around, everyone can find their own niche with this game as long as they start looking somewhere.

I love this game as much as I do Skyrim even though they're both quite different. Skyrim is open-world and this one is limited open-world, but do NOT let that deter you.
CAMPAIGN:
The best of the game. You create your own legend of a character; be famous or infamous. You may choose to be a small renegade or control half of the world. You can rule with fairness or govern with dictatorship. It's your choice.
CUSTOM BATTLE:
Something simple to start with but most certainly not the best of your choices. It's simply battles of a specified character you choose vs. an army. Not much to see here.
MULTIPLAYER:
Two words. Pure genius. The community is not that underpopulated and many servers are running daily. Many use mods which is not my forte as I like normal M&B:WB, but this is okay. The players can really care about your skill and understand if you're new or a veteran. I've experienced this first-hand several times. Many gamemodes are available as well. Here are some:
-DUEL
No one can hurt each other unless they challenge one another for a one-on-one duel. Very satisfying.
-BATTLE
A realistic medieval battle. Choose your equipment and battle and make sure you don't die. You won't respawn until the next round.
-DEATHMATCH
Exceedingly obvious, you kill anyone and everyone and upgrade your equipment.
-SIEGE
Defenders vs. Invaders. Defenders guard their castle and keep the Invaders from getting in via gate, siege tower, or ladders.
-CTF
Good ol' Capture the Flag. Two teams, each with one flag, must capture the other flag. Simple.
-TEAM DEATHMATCH
Think deathmatch but with teams.
If I've missed any please comment.

I would like to say that the gameplay might be good but the game on PC is not. This is a horrible port, only after multiple tweaks it will run decently on my PC. I have an OC'd 2600k 4.5GHz and a GTX 580, I have to run this on low for it to be playable at 1440p. It looks pretty bad on low and it STILL has micro-stutters and random FPS drops. Mouse feels really weird, especially compared to the excellent port of BO2. If you want to play Ghosts, don't get it on PC.
Now for the gameplay:
Story: I thought it was good, but not great. It is extremely typical COD so to speak and it's extremely short (I finished it on Hardnened in 6 hours). It's very similar to Homefront if you're familiar with that, there's an alliance that attacks the US and basically wins but your superhuman squad of 4 people ruin their plans and save the day. The ending is also saying there will be a sequel, it is not a definitive ending at all.
Shooting mechanics: At first it felt rather weird, but after playing more it's not that bad. It's similar to previous CODs and the overall feeling is good. Dual rendered scopes are a nice visual touch, but if you don't run the game on low it will destroy your FPS. Also to keep in mind is that the FOV changer (which you should use) does not alter the scopes or ADS in multiplayer.
Multiplayer: I didn't play as much as I'd like for a good review of it. I can say though that the game modes are extremely short on players. Anything outside of TDM and DOM has very little players in it, which basically means you have a big chance of ending up with people far away so get ready to lag. Time to kill is very fast, run and gun like in the past will NOT work. You might get kills, but you'll die a lot. It is much harder to go in and out of cover like you could in BO2, it is much harder to turn on people if they get the first shots on you. Well lets get into some pros & cons about the game.
Campaign:
+Pros:
-Cons:

Multiplayer
+Pros:
+ Gunplay is good as usual
+ Plenty of soldier customization this time around, including female soldiers.
+ A far better gun and attachment unlock system
+ Improved prestige system
+ Kill time is faster which I enjoy a lot more.

-Cons:

- New game modes are fun but unpopulated
Overall:
+Pros:
+ Graphics look fairly nice on ultra, a bit better than Black Ops II but nothing too amazing
+ Gun sounds are good
+ Gamepad support
-Cons:
- Volume options lacking
- Lack of dedicated servers

Call of Duty Ghosts comes out as the weakest installment to the series.  If you were hoping to get a new Call of Duty drug fix for the year, Call of Duty Ghosts isn't gonna do it for you.  On max settings there are some spots here and there where you will see some beautiful hi res textures. Unfortunately, that's only on some cases.  Most of the times this "next-gen" game pulls out muddy textures lathered in feces throwing it at your face like it's all that.  In the campaign, the levels play out as highly choreographed cutscenes of some of the most common hollywood action movie cutscenes.  They can be really cool at times, but have no lasting power and end way too fast (really short levels).  The campaign for any experienced fps player will take less than 6 hours to beat, considering that some time is placed on setting up the game first.  You'll forget about the campaign the moment you beat it, because it took so little time with uninspired levels.
By now this game is notorious for being a poorly implemented console port thrown together by a small team of rotting zombie brains.  Some people simply can't start the game; most have constant stuttering issues.  Those with SLI/Crossfire have graphical distortion, flickering, and major stuttering, which also occurs for single graphics card users.  Random fps drops occur for many people.  The game also has a memory leak where if it doesn't load in another level after a certain amount of time, it'll crash.  Of course that is after a very long time (several hours) before it decides to go hay-wire.  Character models have puddy ugly faces and an ominous glow around them for some nonapparent reason. A developer choice to make it easier to spot players?
Everyone on the forums seems to have the mindset that the game doesn't run as well as it should, being a call of duty game.  People with monster rigs of a Titan or even SLI Titans get stuttering and random fps drops too.  Graphical anomoles are present in many places in the campaign, especially the jungle escape level with the river and water causing a massive blue glow pixallation all over the screen making it hard to see anything.  After a certain amount of time playing in the campaign (again a couple of hours), the game will fail to load textures causing everything to be black with grey flickering geometry.  It's like the characters are in the dark.  It takes a restart of the game to fix it, implying that the game isn't utilizing resources correctly.
Multiplayer is severely underpopulated making it hard to get a game of for instance search and destroy/rescue.  That makes it uneasy on the mind on how long this game may last on pc.  Some modes such as Capture the Flag failed to make an appearance this time around for no apparent reason at all.  Field of View is locked at 60-65 just like MW3 and there is no official word on if it'll change or if using the FoV unlocker is allowed.  Frames per Second is locked at 91 fps again with no word on whether IW/Activision will change it or allow for the FPS unlocker.  If you have a fancy 120hz or 144hz monitor, there's little use for it in this game.  Nearly every gun in the game takes 3 bullets to kill someone giving no differences between one gun to another causing the guns to have little "personality" to them.  They don't really stick out to me.  Couple the fact that it only takes about 3 bullets to kill and the massive lag that everyone experiences, you most often die instantly upon seeing another player, because that player saw you a second or two ago and already shot and killed you before the game even shows it to you.  The lag is preposterous happening in all games to varying  degrees of extreme to minor and unfortunately mostly moderate to extreme.  Multiplayer literally has no anticheat program in it.  The only thing that can barely be considered an anticheat is the submit a player as cheating button, which is like Treyarch's player submission except your submission goes into a pile of crap to be burned as there seems to be no one at the other end that cares to review them.  There is no VAC protection, because of IW/Activision's choice to turn the game into 64bit.exe.  VAC works only with 32bit.  So, there is essentially no anti-cheat.  Cheaters publically mock players over their defenselessness doing whatever they please.  Cheaters are in every other lobby and sometimes in groups or clans together.  Literal actual cheaters using blatant wallhacks and super aimbots among several other cheats like lobby manipulation, not just a suspicion of a good player in-game.  All the "next-gen" Dx11 features seem to be poorly implemented and combined with the transition to turning the game into 64bit is probably a lot of the reason for all the performance problems of the game.  Also, the game required at least 6 gigs of RAM despite really only using around 2 gigs and used to lock people from launching the game that had <6gigs of RAM.  The game requires over 40 gigs of HD space despite having such little content and many bland textures making you wonder why the hell the game requires so much damn space, like giving a basket ball stadium to a damn mouse.
The gun sounds are thankfully nice and powerful sounding.  The multiplayer maps however are very boring.  They're too large for a small 6 vs 6 game causing a lot of just wandering around with your♥♥♥♥♥♥in your hand before you stumble upon another player wandering around with their♥♥♥♥♥♥in their hand.  IW/Activision also didn't take into account that they should've added a lot more stuff into the very large maps causing a lot of the maps to have large barren areas of nothing.  leading players to constantly follow the edges of the map.  The "destructable" environment is really not destructible with only a few or single pre-defined set piece(s) being allowed to fall down in a pre-defined animated way the same way each and every single time.  There are no dedicated servers, which IW/Activision lied so damn hard about.  So, every match you join is a peer to peer match with a person from Uganda.  The game doesn't match players closely together.  So, you're always matched with someone half way around the world.  Considering that there are so few players in this CoD on PC, it's no surprise.  So, super lag for everyone!  Patches role out like snails and for most do nothing, for some do very little improvements, and others actually makes it worse.
This game was a disappointment, and the only fun I have now is from playing squads with bots as multiplayer is infested with horrendous lag and cheaters.  I recommend those who haven't bought the game to save their money for Treyarch's rendition of Call of Duty as they place some effort into catering to PC players.

Heroes and generals is essentially CoD1:United Offensive - crossed with Battlefeild 1942 and Command and Conquer
With reasonable graphical fidelity, and the combined mayhem of aircraft, tanks, light infantry vehicles, and good old grunts on the ground - there's plenty to choose from.
Weapon choice however is limited, and linear in nature. You'll start the game with a set of basic gear - and through capping control points, and embedding bullets in your enemies - you'll unlock access to other weapons, modifications for said weapons, vehicles - and 'badges' which are Heroes and Generals equivilent of perks.
H&G does however, have its flaws. The game has been in 'Beta' for the past 3 years, and despite numerous builds - Reto Moto (of the 'Hitman' series fame) - seem unable to decide whether they want a realistic WW2 experience, or a more arcady wolfenstein-esque power fantasy. Certain weapon modifications and badges are flat out damage and health bonuses - and although there are more sidegrade style options availible - your average faceless opponent will rarley choose them.
The game also suffers from issues with hit detection, and network stability. Servers are often down for maintainence - and when they are up - the games matchmaking system seems insistent on connecting you to servers on the other side of the planet. Be sure to manually browse for, and choose missions you have a good connection to - to avoid warping, teleporting, and enemies simply not receiving any damage.
On the topic of damage, bullets in H&G are supposed to behave akin to their real-life counterparts, with realistic drop over range, and the need to lead one's target. However with player animations that look as though soldiers are skating across the ground - and the disturbing requirement to lead all of your targets by the same distance - regardless of what range they are at - you'll often find yourself cursing this so called 'feature' as you miss your fifth shot in a row.
The RTS aspect of the game, dubbed "Generals mode" - is something I've yet to engage in, RTS's not really being my thing. One aspect of the top-down mode I did appreciate, was the commonality of 'unfair' engagements. Players in the role of the  Generals dictate the resources that are availible in each match of the 'Heroes' (FPS) mode. So just like their historical counterparts - players in H&G will often encounter battalions of tanks, they must defeat with a few panzerfausts, and a couple of 'civilian bicycles.' Frustrating at times, but boldly realistic.
On the whole Heroes and Generals offers a fun jaunt back to the theatres of WW2. You can quickly hop in, grab your rifle - and join the fight. But don't look for much depth or expect your targets to always catch your bullets. After three years in beta, H&G doesn't seem to be going anywhere fast.

*This review does not include Extinction-Mode as I have not played it.
-Small but more meaningfull iterations of existing systems change the pace. What might be welcome for some might break the experience for those used to the old stuff. Like that old cushion you have, which gets replaced without your consent. Yeah, eff that!-
I never was one with a lot of love for the solo portion of the game, not because I do not enjoy such a thing in general but the way COD  does it leaves me repeatedly unimpressed. The introduction of 2 brothers and their dog was promising. The whole cast of the Modern Warfare brand never clicked for me so I was willing to give this fresh start a chance. The opening chapter managed to suck me in  immediately even though I felt pushed a little too fast through different events, completing it within minutes. This is not a big drama by itself  but it became evident rather fast how this was the way it would continue. Beyond the impressive beginning I found myself caught in the same structure of modern warfare 1 and 2 that I dreaded so much. Stiff gameplay, constant urgency pushing you through tunnel levels driven by corny writing and some bogus backstory. This time around I couldn't bring up the motivation to at least finish it. The only section I enjoyed out of the ones I have played was the infiltration of the skyscraper. The pacing felt right, the scripted events were not all about explosions and the amount of opposition felt somewhat reasonable. The assets built for this and other sections are worth mentioning but they feel like such a giant waste considering how little time you actually spend seeing them.
The visuals really are nice at times, especially smoke and dust emitted from grenades look totally competent. It would be quite a stretch, though, to say that Ghosts really moves the industry forward in the slightest with its presentation. It only looks as good as it needs to. Not more, not less. Some muddy textures and god-awful foilage further illustrating the point once you take your eyes off those flashy things that scream: “Please look at me! Ignore that corner there!“
“Squads“ is the game's training ground. Here you will be able to fight against bots that are geared based on other players setups stored in the cloud (use buzzword: check). As far as AI goes, it is not that clever and the game resorts to plenty of “cheating“ to offer some kind of challange. Sometimes they are dead on, sometimes they miss every shot or they straight up track you through walls. It feels awkward at times. It is good for a couple of relaxing matches inbetween though, to cool down or to warm yourself up before jumping into the meatgrinder that is the multiplayer. Beside this, squads contains some okay horde-mode variations as well as the option to play 1v1 matches against a real player with both of you bringing in 5 personalized bots to populate the map. Since it is really just an addition on top of the core game, there is no harm done having it in, even with the couple of quirks it has.
So, here we are. The multiplayer presents itself in the usual fashion with some new modes such as cranked and tweaked  ones like search and rescue which fuses classic s&d with kill confirmed, where dropped tags are used to allow or deny revival of fallen players. Right off the bat I had no trouble getting into the game. Whether it's the movement or the shooting, it does not feel vastly different from all the previous games. Killstreaks are still there, again bundled up into strikepackages, a loadout system which allows you to customize equipment and perks – yep, seems like COD.
I'm really happy with the current base concept of the equipment system. For me, perks and gear have always been merely tools to avoid the things that I dislike the most about this franchise. I hate the idea of ironsights in fast paced shooters and the slow movement associated with it – There is a perk for me named Stalker. I hate the concept of a radar that serves as a crutch for bad players – there is stuff for me called „off the grid“ and a silencer. I hate randomly placed explosives... you get the idea. I really feel like I'm given enough options to work my way around the things that aggrevate me the most as a result eliminating them as an annoyance for the largest part. Oh, and I can finally throw that sidearm away, too, that I   n e v e r   use. Killstreaks also received some love making them first and foremost less prominent/dominant while still maintaining their reward like nature. One of my biggest issues was the constant bombardement from the air with all kinds of metal/explosives distracting from the core game – shooting dudes with a gun... preferably in the face. There are way less air based streaks to begin with and the ground based ones can be avoided or countered reasonably well while leaving enough room for skilled players to turn a dog, turret or knife-wielding armored maniac into a deadly weapon. An indirect reason of the killstreaks feeling different is the overall fragmentation of the map. They are bigger and populated by smaller player numbers – I like almost all of them. This gives more breathingroom for planned choices in contrast to the previously  chaotic and random gameplay flows. The pace got knocked down a notch to “less hyperactive“. It's by no means slow-slow but definitely slower. Spawns are fine, but gradually get worse the lower the playercount. Whenever I find myself playing 3v3 because some people dropped the game I notice an increase of “Well great, here I spawn with a shotgun barrel on my forehead“-moments. Thanks to the bigger maps, explosives are also used more sparingly, further reducing the randomness by which they so often killed me in the past. Last but not least: zee knoife. When you stab someone, the game locks you into a short animation, effectively making it imbossible to play as a racecar with a katana mounted on the bumper. I like it. It is still a great tool and very satisfying but finally comes with the drawbacks it should have, making it a more difficult rushing someone to gut him in the middle of 4 of his friends – and then them.....
Bottom line is: The campaign is still hot garbage for me while the multiplayer experience has been greatly improved by mostly subtle changes to already existing mechanics. However, if you never thought something was wrong with any of the things I mentioned to begin with, chances are, you will have trouble adjusting to this or will plainly dislike what they did.

Over 100 hours put in and I'm still enjoying this game.  It reminds me of and plays a lot like BF1942 for those interested.  I loved that game and hope this becomes something even greater!   I've longed for another WWII type MMO that allowed you to fly planes, drive tanks, or play various infantry roles since BF1942, and this is it.  For now, the sides are US and German, but Soviets and British seem to be in the works.  Matches are typically 16-20 players per side, so there is a good community of players.  While it is still in beta and needs refinement, those looking to play different roles in a battle can do so with this game.  Want to drive a Tiger II or Pershing tank?  Done.  Want to fly a BF109 or P38? Done.  Want to be a long range sniper?  Done.  Paratrooper?  Anti-tank infantry?  Jump in a jeep or APC and drive players to capture points?  Done.  It's all here.  You can specialize your soldiers and give them upgrades on equipment (explosives) and guns.  As you progress and earn credits, you can unlock different weapons, weapon mods, vehicles, equipment, badges, and ribbons.  Most maps revolve around either defending or capturing certain objective sites, similar to BF1942, but you have to capture certain points before others.  In BF1942, you could rush behind enemy lines and capture the other side's starting point.  No so with H&G.  It forces you to capture points that are connected to the starting points and in this sense, I enjoy it better.  It forces your team to act like a team and focus on a certain point.  A couple maps are skirmish based and require you to hold at least 2 out of 3 points to progress over time to victory.  Typically matches are around 30 minutes, but can vary on how one team does over the other.
Some minor gripes at this time for me are weapon mods, no engineer type class for repairs (who didn't love repairing your own tank or plane in BF1942?), and plane controls.  I've become a pretty good keyboard pilot, but the controls need refinement.  You use your mouse for pitch and roll and A/D for yaw.  Since the game does not yet separate mouse sensitivity for planes and infantry/tanks, you really need a mouse that can do it on the fly.  I use a G700s.  You can use a joystick, but you will have to manually edit the controls.  Weapons can become pretty powerful with the right upgrades, but are costly to buy and repair.  Yes you will have to repair mods, which can dip into your credit earnings per match.  The game is Free to Play. I will be the first to admit that the PC port of this game was a mess when it first launched. However, the recent patches have improved my experience substantially.
As for the game itself, I am going to post my review I did for the Murfreesboro Pulse as I write their video game reviews for them. It should be visible by the first week of December as the next issue has not been published yet.
"It is that time of year again for gamers. With November comes another Call of Duty, and with it, all the scorn, vitriol, and downright mind boggling hate toward it. Call of Duty Ghosts will not change that. If you hated this series before, there really is nothing here that is going to change that. If you like it, you will more than likely like this one, though I would not be surprised if quite a few were underwhelmed, and even disappointed.
At least for this reviewer, the most disappointing aspect of Ghosts is its campaign. The story goes that you are part of an elite squad known as the Ghosts who are fighting back against the Federation. The Federation is an alliance of South American countries, who have managed to significantly weaken the United States to the point where they have a strong foothold in the south. While the premise may seem odd or even ridiculous, my hopes were pinned on the writer, Stephen Gaghan, who did one of my favorite political thrillers Syriana and who had also won an academy award for Traffic. Unfortunately those hopes were dashed.
As a fan of the Call of Duty campaigns, this iteration falls surprisingly short from the standards set by previous games. The writing is lackluster at best. The story gets you where you need to go, but does not compel you to care. It is predictable without being engaging, in large part due to the lack of character in this story. Case in point, there is hardly any character in Ghosts.  The people you meet and fight with are, at least for the most part, stoic to the point of boredom. Even the voice acting is mostly bland and lacks passion, almost like they phoned it in at points, which surprising considering that Call of Duty usually nails that aspect of itself. Ironically, the non-human in the game, Riley the dog, ends up being more engaging and worthy of your attachment than the humans.
On the flipside, though hardly compelling, the campaign itself is still entertaining enough to compel you to finish it. The set pieces continue to amaze and it provides a good variety of different sequences to keep you engaged. In fact, some of the more creative level designs of this franchise can be found here, from gun battles in space, battles under the sea, to very smooth tank battles, and even a stealth sequence in a bog that this reviewer found very engaging. Oh, and you get to sick the dog on soldiers. It never gets old!
Whereas the campaign falls short, the multiplayer portion is where Ghosts stands back up and delivers in spades. Ghosts is probably the most refined Call of Duty experience yet. The overhauled engine looks very good and shows off much improved animations.  An optional contextual lean element allows you to lean from cover whenever they aim down the sights, and a slide mechanism lets players slide when they are sprinting. While these may seem like gimmicks, they are actually clever gameplay elements that will force players to learn and master if they want to be among the better rankers. This reviewer had a first-hand account of such mastery. Upon dying, I saw my killer’s killcam: he was coming up the stairs, sprinted to the window, slid to the side and then leaned down his sights and shot me. His/her timing was impeccable.
The multiplayer itself is brimming with a stunning amount of content, refinements, and additions. While I cannot talk about all of them for the sake of brevity, I can rundown the major points that shine in this iteration.
New modes such as Cranked and Blitz bring some unique variety. In Cranked, when you kill someone, you get bonuses to your character that last for 30 seconds. If you do not kill someone in that time frame, you die. This is great for discouraging camping. In Blitz, it is almost like a soccer match where you have to get to your opponents’ goal line to score while stopping them from getting to yours. I have found this mode to be quite fun. In-game there are field orders that you can grab upon an enemy’s death that offer you a challenge such as getting a certain number of headshots or melee kills. Upon completion of such challenge, you receive an award in the form of replenished ammo and a care package.  New and modified killstreaks along with surprisingly large and varied maps help to differentiate Ghosts from the pack. Those expecting the close quarters combat of previous titles are in for a surprise.
One of the biggest overhauls though is the character customization and squads mode. You can now create your own solider down to their gender. It is not Skyrim level, but it at least allows for players to input their own personalities into the characters.
Squads mode is where I will be finding myself spending the most time. The major draw point here is that you can now customize and build your own squad to take on other players’ squads. There is almost a simulation feel to the whole thing, though not quite at that point yet. For this reviewer though, the best thing about this mode is Safeguard. Building on one of my favorite modes in Modern Warfare 3, Survival, Safeguard is a horde mode where you hold out against increasing waves of enemies. Up to four players (up from two in MW3) must hold out as long as set, using guns, knives, care packages, and pretty much everything at your disposal. It is a lot of fun, though admittedly tough.
The final and most unique addition to Ghosts has to be Extinction mode. Piggy backing off Nazi Zombies in previous games, you and up to three others must destroy alien hives while also holding off waves of alien foes. It may sound like another horde mode and in a sense it is, but it is more hectic and has its own style of play that will require multiple attempts and experimentation to master.
A final note on multiplayer, thank you for bots! If you want to hone your skills or just do not care for playing against real players, this option is a godsend.
In the end, Call of Duty Ghosts comes down to, what are you looking for? A compelling campaign like the previous titles? Look elsewhere. Major shakeups to the Call of Duty formula? Nope. However, if you are looking for content and refinement in a slick package, you need not look further.  Call of Duty Ghosts is the game for you.
4/5"

Hands down easiest game I have ever played on the hardest difficulty. Best far cry for Vaas, worst for everything else.
Problems I had:
-Spotty spotting. AI can't see you crouching in a bush that barely goes to your chest (while crouching), but can see you through walls and bushes completely covering your body.
-Bow and arrow somehow makes more noise than a silenced weapon (almost any attack brought them down on my exact location, but with a silenced sniper rifle at point-blank they would continue as if they suspected the dog had farted, knocking their partner out). Not to mention the instant kill ambush attacks, during which the enemy cries out as he dies while his friend stands less than a meter away without noticing.
-Outposts were obscenely easy, unless you were spotted, at which point you had to be fast or they would cycle the alarms, bringing a ridiculously large number of enemies down on you. But you can always just walk away and come back in about thirty seconds, when everything has reset.
-Radio towers.... This I just didn't get this. Maybe it would have been a good idea if it wasn't just an attempt to redo some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t idea from Assassin's Creed, a game where it made sense and didn't seem gimmicky (until now that I noticed Ubi will use both the stupid climbing to the top of a tower AND the stupid camera crap in every game they make until it's pounded into dust). Oh, and here's a free gun, which makes absolutely no sense. Just give me the map and let me actually have to try to get weapons, please. I have it on the hardest difficulty for a reason.
-Combat.... I WALKED THROUGH AN OUTPOST KILLING EVERYONE WITH HEADSHOTS USING MY PISTOL. They rang the alarm and I WALKED THROUGH AGAIN KILLING EVERYONE WITH HEADSHOTS USING MY PISTOL. They rang the alarm again and I pulled out my silenced assault rifle to kill the helicopter pilot and unlock the fast travel location. The whole time I did this, I lost just under two bars of health, without body armor. Did I mention hardest difficulty?
-Quick Time Events.... I dont' think any first person shooter should have Quick Time Events. I honestly only think it works in a game like God of War.... I'm running around, shooting animals and people, then am thrown into a stupid "fight" comprised solely of quick time events.... It didn't make sense, and it took the best enemy from the game.
-Syringes.... Health syringe, I understand, but it ended up serving no purpose as I never lost more than three health bars unless I was instantly killed, like the time I jumped off a cliff and deployed my wingsuit right before slamming my forehead into the invisible ground (This was right above the entrance to the submarine pen for the mission with the crazy "German"-American "undercover agent" with the USMC and Army tattoos, which completely lost me). I honestly avoided health syringes at all costs. It was easier and more fun to watch me pull a stick out of my♥♥♥♥♥to cram it into my arm and pry off a bullet that mystically stopped when it struck me, magnetizing to my arm, or snap my thumb back in place for the five hundredth time.
-Money was too easy to come by.... I could kill anyone and wander away without anyone else noticing, then steal their torn teddy bear, thinking only of how much money it will get me at the crazy lady's shop.... Not only does every bad guy have a teddy bear in various states of distress, but the shopkeepers just love the things.
-The story feels like it was written by one person, then torn up by another for thinking it was too good before being given to a third to piece it back together and force a choice for the "should I stay or should I go" ending. Great, I killed Vaas and saved all the friends I know are alive, plus I've been told the brother that didn't die in front of me is dead by another friend, someone I trust, so what is keeping me here? More blood to be spilled, and for no reason other than I'm an angry twenty-something year old who has been thrown a decade back in time to my angsty idiot teenage years, when I never got what I wanted and I always has stupid people telling me what to do.
-Music. The music didn't fit with anything I was doing at any time. I ran from place to place 90% of the time, and the music would go from silence to this clash of noise making me think I had entered a fight or something.
-Crafting. I always seemed to be cutting the leg off a goat, even when it was a bear, or a shark, or any other creature. I called it 'skin', and I made a full set of everything before I met Vaas the second time. I never touched an animal again, mainly because the game crashed every time I attempted to sell a "skin" (I found the way around this was to sell the second slot until all I had was the one "skin" left, at which time it let me sell it), but also because it was a waste of time.
-Boss fights.... Boss fights? We're talking about a man with guns and knives, shooting at and stabbing other men with guns and knives, why would we need boss fights?
-Armored enemies. What's the point? They have big guns but only shoot every once in a while. They can take a lot of bullets, but two-to-three knife hits and they're done. Or you can just run into a bush and wait for them to walk right up to your face so you can just instant kill them.
-Not enough enemies. I would have said the opposite when I first started the game, as any time I came anywhere near a road, ten cars rolled by, but once I "fixed" the radio towers and/or took over the outposts, I never saw them again.
-Brother who can fly planes can magically fly a helicopter. No it's not the same. And why does he, when he's clearly able to control it enough to fly in a straight line, does he do strafing runs on the place we're trying to escape from?
Things I liked:
Well, I can't really say the graphics were better than the others.... Sure, they were better than the original Far Cry, but I felt looked exactly the same as Far Cry 2, just less brown and more green. Even some of the plants were exactly the same as in Crysis, which I would have preferred any bit of that piece of trash to have been left to rot.
Ummm....
Well, Vaas and most of the story leading up to his disappearance, I guess. What the hell is with the "boss fights"? You fade into some alternate dimension to kill the enemy, then fade back into a room filled with a large amount of dead people - excluding the person you just fought to the death....
All in all, it looked just like the others, the music was annoying, and the game was by far the most easy. I mean, even Crysis' hardest difficulty setting made hiding difficult, even though all you had to do was turn invisible....

So, if this is "next-gen" in Activision's mind, then I fear for the future of that company, because it is not only not an improvement on the previous title (Black Ops II), but it is a bad game. The graphics are no better, and the lack of colour in the environments makes the game look worse than BO2. The gameplay is boring, with the changes to the multiplayer reverting back to the inferior MW3 system, and in other cases breaking them all together. There is no FOV option, which makes it painful to play unless you use the recently C&D'd FOV changer tool for the title, but even with this the aim-down-sites FOV is still painfully low, meaning it is still unplayable. The single player is dire. Squads is not even remotely interesting. The survival alien mode is no where near as good as zombies, and the game is generally uninteresting. Also, it is terribly optimised, meaning barely any GPUs can actually get stable framerates, and the 6GB ram requirement (along with the 50GB install limit I suspect) is completely artificial in nature, and is only there for Activision to pretend this game is "next-gen"!
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. If you want Call Of Duty, buy COD4 if you want something competetive, or Black Ops 2 if you want something dumb and mildly amusing. Ghosts is a waste of money and time, and I would get a refund if I could.

Once again, a developer is completely oblivious to what's required in order for a game to be properly developed for PC.  This game has serious performance issues.  A game like this should be running at 60fps with max settings easily.  But instead, it's performance is so completely bonkers that you are forced to dial down the graphical settings in order to get a steady framerate.  Oh, and if you have an SLI or CFX rig, then you'll need to disable one of your GPUs in order for this game to run.  There's also no FOV setting in order to alleviate the default tunnel vision, and the mouse acceleration is so bad that you WILL miss your shots by overreaching the mouse cursor.
It's sad, too, because this could have been one of the better entries to this franchise.  The new maps are large, and with more vertical design.  Long sightlines and less cramped corridors.  The class system is very flexible in creating your own unique soldier.  Extinction Mode is better than Zombies, in my opinion, because you have an actual endgame to work towards.  Unlike in Zombies, where even the best laid plans are eventually fruitless to the invincible hordes of the undead that keep coming round after round.
But none of these things can be enjoyed to their full extent with a game that performs this poorly.  Infinity Ward needs to address these issues with a serious update.  Everyday I see less and less players in every game mode at every time of the day and night.  Players are migrating away from this game, and it's understandable why.
Not recommended as a purchase until these problems are fixed.  Stay away.
EDIT:  Oh, and even though it says that I only played 2 hours of this game, that's the stat for the singleplayer game.  I have over 30 hours into multiplayer.  The review is only attached to the singleplayer page.

For some time now, Call of Duty has been regarded by a vocal minority as a soulless annual cash grab, lacking innovation and epitomizing everything that's wrong with modern gaming.  I've always felt this reputation was undeserved. Each of the Modern Warfare games still rank among my favorite games of all time; they had tight gameplay mechanics, amazing action set-pieces, and in spite of their over-the-top ridiculous, sometimes nigh incomprehensible plots, the characters were well-written and voice-acted and genuinely likeable. I felt that Modern Warfare 2 was the highlight of the series, and I put more than 300 hours into the game between the campaign and multiplayer.
I'm disappointed, then, that with Ghosts I'm beginning to understand what detractors have been saying about Call of Duty for so long. There is almost nothing novel or interesting in this game to someone who has played previous Call of Duty titles; the sole exceptions, in my mind, are the space and underwater missions, but they're far too short-lived to redeem the overall experience.  The characters are bland at best and actively irritating at worst, and all attempts at emotionally involving the player fall completely flat.
The multiplayer doesn't fare much better.  Call of Duty has always made itself more accessible with a compressed skill gap relative to games like Counter-Strike and Battlefield, but that's been fine until now.  Previous titles have been well-enough balanced to support different playstyles and allow players to capitalize on their unique capabilities.  But with each new game the balance has shifted further and further toward being a complete spray-fest with enough random elements to render all skill (or lack thereof) moot.  In Ghosts, many if not most guns kill in only 2-3 shots, and most of the maps are small enough that there's rarely any advantage to opting for semi-automatic gun with greater accuracy.  The best strategy is always to just pick an assault rifle or SMG and spray, spray, spray.
I miss Modern Warfare 2.

This is Call of Duty in its finest form yet, as far as the series is concerned. However, as far as the PC iteration goes, this is Call of Duty: Ghosts in its worst form, as the optimization in this port ranks just under 'Utterly Unplayable' for most.
While some users can play the game just fine on rigs of varying power, there seems to be no rhyme or reason as to what causes the game to lag, stutter, freeze or otherwise graphically glitch for others.  However, it is prevalent enough that the community has made an outcry as to what needs fixed and how little fun they're having until it does.  Patches that have dropped thus far for the game have had results across the grid varying from fixing some players' problems to causing problems for another whom never had any to begin with.
It's not to say that the PC version of Call of Duty: Ghosts isn't fun, or even that it's terrible, but until further patches may alleviate the issues plaguing this port, it's best to steer clear and play on the consoles for this game.

Call of Duty: Ghosts is yet another Michae Bay-fest. Its Single Player campaign is nothing special and Multiplayer is the same Call of Duty-fans have been playing for the last 6 years, but with a few missing options. Infinity Ward tries to mimick the succesful Zombie Mode with a 'new' co-op multiplayer mode called Extinction. You and your teammates have to drill Alienturds while several uninspired creatures try to kill you. While I was playing this, I was wondering why the developers just didn't add the zombie mode with new maps?
This sounds like its 'okay', but it's not. The graphics are terrible. Looks like a Xbox 360 game from 2007. Dirty textures, the same animations and invisible walls all over the place. Even though the engine is 6/7 years old, they haven't been able to keep performance up.
The maps in Team Deathmatch are a big step down. Call of Duty has always been about seeing the other player and reacting to it as quick as possible. If you shoot before your enemy does, you win.. most of the time. However, these maps are 'too big' for 12 player Team Deathmatch. When you enter a room and want to check every corner.. well, you can't. There are just way too many directions from which you can get killed. There is not one safe spot. Offcourse, it motivates people to keep moving. But how can you motivate this, when you're dead within half a second when you get shot?? I'm not talking about Sniper Rifles, but i'm talking about the lowest level SMG.
If you want a Good Call of Duty Experience, get Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare or Black Ops. Those are worth your money.
