Ok, i know this is in early access and things can change, but for the game that is right now,  this is my rant:
It manages to portray the life a private forced to fight a war managed by corporations that make a profit off the pain and suffering of others. (embelishment for the sake of the rant)
Here's the deal:
- you start out as infantry and you get a basic rifle and a stock of 60 grenades.
- after the first mission, you are encouraged to buy an automatic rifle, which is ~11000 credits. It may seem a lot at first, but that's basically the cheapest ranged weapon you can get.
- as you play, you get xp, useful to increase your rank, salary per battle, change clasas and earn medals which provide extra small bonuses.
- if you change to tank crewman, you get the basic tank - which gets screwed fast by everything and you can only kill infantry and other basic tanks. Also, you unlock better tanks by killing tanks btw, with that. So you better hope the other team also has pseudotanks too.
- if you change to pilot, you get the faction specific plane for free, but you can't use the rifle anymore and have to buy a machine gun or use the knife or grenades.
- Ah, the knife. It sucks. It doesn't work. It's useless.
Funny story about the knife... There was a pilot who landed near me once as i was loading my weapon and he had a knife. As i was running around trying to not get killed and him chasing me, we both noticed that the knife... did absolutely no freaking damage at all. So i stopped running. And he attacked me, and attacked and sliced and diced and did 0 damage, so i shot him in the head.
Moral here: melees don't work. (at the moment)
And now, my personal beef and what led me here: Scoped Rifles AKA Sniper Rifles.
Basic rifle sucks. The scopeless sniper is kinda pointless without the scope, but it gives you ranks in its medal thing, which if you level it up to 11, which takes a freaking long fraking time, gives you access to the scoped version.
However, if you get enough xp and unlock the Recon class, you get proeficiency automatically.
Man how glad i was when i got enough xp to become Recon. Then i did and i saw that you don't get the scoped gun for free, you buy it, with ~220k credits. With the class' buy price of 25-30k credits, that makes it about 250k credits just to get to play sniper.
Now, let's take a minute to talk about salary. What is salary? Well, for 15 minutes spent on a mission, you get paid. How much? That depends on your rank. I think you start at 1k credits at first rank and as you rank up, you'll get closer to 3.5k credits at rank 14. The rest is bonus for your performance. Oh, and killing other players is worth zilch, so you'd best focus on capturiing points.
Anyway, i'm rank 10 now, getting 2.5k credits per battle. Assuming i spend at least 15 minutes in it with the current soldier ( yes, it checks your soldier's presence, not the player's) and the average of each battle is ~30 min, with bonuses i average around 3k credits per battle, won or lost (extremes went from 0 credits to 6500 credits depending on length of battle and soldiers used).
That's 250.000 / 3000 = around 83 missions, with highs and lows in time and rewards.
83 * 30 = 2490 min  / 60 min = 41.5 hours of  total play time just to get the sniper rifle, if you solely concentrate on that, ignoring everything else.
Now, consider the fact that not everyone has the time, desire and patience to wait that long to get to play with a sniper rifle? Also consider that not everyone knows what you need to do to get the damn rifle.and that they spend their credits on trying out different classes.
And that the enemy already has bigger, better weapons of mass destruction and that you're going to die quite often. And that after all the patience and waiting and suffering, you finally unlock the scoper and find it disappointing. How would that make you  feel?
Like all of this was a giant waste of time, no?
So, from the point of view of a f2p player, which this game entertains itself as, that damn scoped rifle beetter be damn worth all the freaking obstacles to getting it, because it's damn annoying to deal with all the unbalanced, unfair crap while having to buy your damn weapons.
"Congratulations Soldier! You've been promoted to Recon! Here's the way to our store. Go buy your weapon."
All the rant aside, it does portray war realistically:
- unfair
- unbalanced
- expensive
- miserable
- you can only use a knife if you don't bring anything else with you.
- the Tommy Gun rapes everything

Pros: the game can be fun, and I was pleasantly surprised with many of the game mechanics.
Con: As part of the current game design, spawn-killing is indirectly encouraged.  I played the Allied side for a few hours tonight, and for more than half of the battles the Axis side eventually surrounded our only spawn point with tanks and just kept shelling us.  I would spawn, have about 5 seconds to try to run to cover, and then be blown to pieces by one of the Axis tankers. Eventually I gave up trying to re-spawn.  So, the majority of my games came down to having to choose between giving easy xp to the enemy for spawn-killing, or abandoning my squad by not re-spawning.
There is nothing in place to prevent or punish spawn-killing. In fact, it is the one of the easiest methods for players to earn credits and experience points.
Therefore, I can't recommend the game as it is right now - though admittedly the Axis side may be more fun as they seem to consistently have more tanks and airplanes at their disposal.

I stayed up until 5 AM liberating the top half of the map from pirates, weaving in and out of the jungle like a Navy Seal gone AWOL. That is fun. Pure adrenaline-pumping fun. The best story mission in the game is where you have to destroy pirate-controlled drug fields with a flamethrower. I felt like a kid on Christmas morning as I set pirates and plants ablaze, in a maniacal frenzy.
Hunting is pretty easy when animals regularly pop out of Jason's anal cavity. Watching the same looting / harvesting / skinning animations play hundreds of times is not fun. Neither is playing pointless minigames, like poker (cash is easy to come by, don't waste your time). The supply drop missions were fun for the first couple of times, but they ultimately didn't stand up to repetition.
The story is a loose deconstruction of Hollywood action flicks and club culture. Jason is a funny and sympathetic character, and so is the rest of the cast, especially Vaas. I got from start to finish without any complaint about the story, so that's an achievement.
I won't be returning to Rook Island for quite some time due to the game's repetitive nature, but there are a handful of brilliant moments among the monotony. Just make sure to use a mouse and keyboard.

This game is completely and totally unbalanced.
There are two sides in this game, the US and the Germans.
The American generals deploy all the assault teams (These are what you spawn from; they give you vehicle tickets and spawn tickets) at the beginning of the war which makes for some interesting battles where some americans might win, but the American generals do not resupply the assault teams, but the Germans do.
Can you see where this is going? Americans might win the first few battles of the war and might even make a small bit of progress but the generals will just stop providing the tickets and the few good American generals will just get zerged.
If you mainly want to play as US, stop. Uninstall the game or go German.
If you want to play as German ("GM"), take this review as a recommendation.

With the (at the time of writing) recent release of Far Cry 4 I think the best way to sum up Far Cry 3 is “Still entirely relevant”
Far Cry 3 is a beautiful game and an absolute joy to play. The atmosphere and the vibrancy of the island you have at your disposal is such a wonderful contrast to most games with the First-Person Shooter classification. One of the most compelling parts of the Far Cry formula is the freedom to approach a situation in whatever way you can dream up. As a fan of stealth games, my mindset was to wipe out an entire enemy force and either make it look like a tragic accident or a nightmarish ninja slaughter. Another aspect that oddly sticks out in my mind is the guns; they all sound unbelievably real and deadly. I’m not sure how they crafted the sound effects for gun fire but they nailed it in Far Cry 3.
So again, my best summary of Far Cry 3 is still “very relevant”. It is a fantastic open world, first-person, sandbox shooter with light RPG elements and I highly recommend everyone pick it up while it’s cheap!

Honestly, I want to like CoD: Ghosts. I do. After all, I paid full retail price for it on launch. That being said, I just can't. The singleplayer campaign is mediocre. There's no emotional buildup, but the game asks you to feel badly when bad things happen to your 'family' and your AI-controlled dog. The plot makes some sense, but it's not coherent - the singleplayer feels like a series of setpieces strung together with an afterthought of a story. At this point I can hear the clamor of fans claiming that "No one plays CoD for the singleplayer!" but even the most hard core of fans will see that the campaign was phoned in. As for the multiplayer, it's not bad. I've played a fair amount of it on PC and PS3, and it's enjoyable. That being said, it's not as fun as Black Ops 2's multiplayer (or MW3's, my current favorite) and the maps are ok but nothing to write home about.
Technically speaking, the game (before the patches started!) ran great on my computer, except for the graphics settings. With everything maxed out, the game looked terrible! I had to set certain settings on 'High' and others on 'Extra,' otherwise the game looked like I was running it in 'Extra Extra Extra Low and Pixelated' graphics quality. After the patches, the game crashes every few minutes for me. The screen locks up and the game won't quit, even by forcing an end to the process tree. I have to manually restart my computer.
Is this game worth the investment? To me, no. It's not bad, but it's not great, and the technical issues have bothered me so much that I've uninstalled it from my library for good. If Steam offered refunds, this would be the first game in line for one, right ahead of Duke Nukem Forever.

I absolutely freaking love this game! It has got to be the most immersive and amazing gaming experience that I have ever experienced before. The way that Far Cry 3 puts you into the jungle, the conflict, the character, and every single thing about the game is amazing! The Ai mechanics and realism of the game is absolutely outstanding. The stealth possibilites in this game are limitless. There isn't very many better feelings than releasing caged jungle animals to prey on enemies, then stealthily murdering the remaining gaurds all of which you did without revealing your existance. . . or you could just go in guns blazing and throwing molotavs or whatever you choose to destroy all opposition. The way they incorporated skinning animals and crafting your own gear makes you feel like a real guerrilla warrior badass. You can hand craft tons of awesome medicines, drugs, ammo packs etc. from simple things you find or hunt for around the island. Transportation is amazing the way that they incorporated hang gliding, tons of different vehicle types, and lots of different boats to choose from. At every moment, you have to watch your back though because you will be hunted by people and animals if you aren't careful. As soon as you think you're invincible, something shows up to kick your♥♥♥♥♥and remind you just how fragile life is which makes you careful and precise in how you approach different situations.
I've heard a lot of complaints about UPlay being problematic, but at least for me, I had absolutely no issues with it which makes me wonder what the problems actually were in the first place. It is inconvenient of course to get UPlay, but after you get it there shouldn't be many issues or at least I certainly didn't have any problems with it.
I did have a few very minor problems such as the fact that walking through small bumps and doorways can be difficult because of my crappy graphics card, but that problem is very limited to my own pc and the very bottom line graphics cards so most people shouldn't have any problems with it. I did notice that modes of transportation tended to be very conveniently placed at times, however their presence in my opinion really enhanced the gameplay.
All in all, this game was well worth the investment and I wish there were more games out there that would follow suit with this game because it's absolutely freaking amazing. I would reccomend it twice if I could!

While it may say beta, this game should still be in alpha with all the issues. Ill break it down for those that actually read it.
Interface:
The limited interface doesn't just make getting anything a pain but also complicated. The interface itself is laggy and lack of options. Sometimes if you miss-click outside of particular buttons, you enter window mode.
Game-play:

I am a long time COD fan, but I feel more than a little let down by this title.  I'm not really sure why they bothered with a single player mode here.  It is too short (3-4 hours with a lot of cutscenes), too predictable (yes, you do have to fend off enemy vehicles from the back of a truck)  and they copied whole scenes from past games...It feels like an afterthought.
I really want to like this game.  The multiplayer is fun, but it  was clearly designed for platform gaming.  The PC release is horrendous, plagued by lag, bad optimization and massive stuttering.  Getting better, but for weeks it was completely unplayable...
The squads mode is a nice touch if you like playing with bots.  In fact, this is one of the few modes that is currently playable if you don't mind the game crashing every 4 or 5 maps.
They relegated clans to 4x4 games.  Not implemented well.  It is so cumbersome to sign people up and there are rarely people playing that mode so you can't find a game.
Rarely can you find more than a few hundred playing any particular mode.  The only modes that seem popular are team deathmatch (normal) and Domination (hotpoint)  If you are more of a lone wolf, you will have a hard time finding a game.
The less popular modes are often less than 100 players while some of the big team modes have a few thousand.
I think the PC version was released far too soon, a lot of players who were excited about the release just stopped playing a week after the release because of the bugs and failed implementation.
What I really wanted out of this game was a way I could play with my friends and the closest this comes is you forming a squad with your friends and playing against bots, or you can form a party and join a team match...
There are some things I really like about this game, some of the maps are fairly large for COD, the perks and loadout customization are interesting.  Allowing you to purchase multiple squad members to load each one differently is a nice change of pace.  It plays a lot more like Battlefield 3 than COD.
I think the game is getting more stable and more playable with each patch.  I would recommend it, it is fun, but given all that went wrong with this releaseI would only have given it 2 out of 5 stars at release.  I will bump it up a star because it is more playable.  I would give another star if they would implement dedicated (ranked) servers.

Call of Duty Ghosts review:
To conclude, Call of Duty Ghosts isn't a massive step up from the previous game and sits firmly within the safe constraints of what is expected from the series. In its own right, there's an encompassing and dramatic campaign filled with variety and enough thrills to keep players well entertained although sadly doesn't offer much incentive to replay. Luckily the extra features of the multiplayer game which can be played solo, add some much needed legs to the overall experience.
Call of Duty Ghosts comes in as a welcome addition to the series that's big on scripted moments, and offers an over the top experience as expected. With a well entrenched multiplayer format, and plenty of willing fans, you can't go wrong with the game, unless you're after  any sort of realism or more open ended gameplay. If you like shooters, then this is well worth picking up, simple as. If you're not a fan of Call of Duty, then what's on offer here is unlikely to sway you over to the dark side.

To my opinion this is potentially the worst COD release by far. It's not the gameplay, but the technical problems that are killing this game for me. For one, the lag (or is it the lag compensation) is truly unacceptable. You might expect to see some tiny differences between what you experience in game and what you get back from the kill cam, but in Ghosts I often experience quite significant differences. For instance when sneaking up on an enemy from behind, shooting at him as he turns, in the kill cam shot my opponent has already turned completely and was able to shoot me down without showing any shots fired from my side. The second problem are spawn points. Even after the patch I often find myself only a few feet away from an enemy as you spawn. I know Infinity Ward and Treyarch are not sharing the same bed, but maybe they should team up to fix these kind of problems once and for all, because now I feel like they are trying to reinvent solutions to the same problem with each release. For now I'm back to Black Ops 2. This game might not be free of technical problems as well, but it is way better than with Ghosts. Good luck out there and game on!!!

The first few hours of this game I really enjoyed.  After that the game began to show its cracks.  In the first three hours you can craft all non-quest items (and the quest ones you can get in the next two hours), but most skills remain locked until you "complete more missions".  Dispite completing all non-plot related missions they remained locked.  Finally trying the plot related ones to unlock skills the game quickly went down hill.  Every lame cut scene I had to sit through to get to a few moments of play time, every "Mash Space" prompt made me more and more aggravated at the game.
If you find Dragon's Lair style controls on a modern game fun then this might be the game for you.  If you actually want to play a videogame I recommend avoiding it and trying something else, anything else.
Pros:
- One or two descent dialogs made me laugh
Cons:
- "Mash Space"
- Skills remain locked well into the game
- Tutorial prompts such as "Pull Trigger to Fire" as late as the forth and fifth Plot quests
- About 5 hours of actual playtime
- Being a console port some UI elements are not well thought out for a PC (crafting "Use" moving "Make" position throws off mouse clicks for example)
- The rest of the dialogs
- Antagonist is repetative and predictable

This game is incredibly unpolished and not worth anybody's time. The crafting aspect is just a gimmick to inconvenience the player for about 4 hours, and then quickly just becomes an awkward way to generate syringes (medkits). The entire UI is obviously a quick port from consoles- terribly clunky. The protagonist's hitbox feels like a large rectangle that barely fits on any staircase- I literally spend 10-30 seconds trying to get on a staircase.
Slightly uneven floors gets you stuck, and sometimes it seemed that corpses did it too- maybe the controls are just unresponsive. On the note of unresponsive controls, the RPG-7 is a great example. After reloading then ADS, there is a good 2 seconds where the game refuses to let you fire. The inconsistency with takedown prompts makes the cool knifing sequences not worth it- easier to just gun people down with a silenced weapon. First, I want to note this is still in BETA testing. With that said, let's get to the review.
Conclusion: Try it first. If you love the gameplay in the first hour or two, feel free to grind to your heat's content. Otherwise, avoid like the plague or fork over some cash for goodies.
Details: This game is a WWII European front First Person Shooter pitting the Allies/Americans versus the Axis/Nazi Germans. The first two hours you will experience the core mechanics to the game, infantry vs. infantry combat. In my opinion, the mechanics are excellent, especially for the era being portrayed. While it is not hyper-realistic like Arma 3 nor look as realistic, the game has basic shooting mechanics keeping the gameplay fluid and fun with nearly no BS events to happen.
<I have yet to dive into all the tank and plane gameplay yet as I need to grind more on another soldier for that.>
Is this pay to win? Yes and no. You can easily unlock all the content without paying a single dime, however you will have to grind many hours in order to unlock all the weapons and a single attatchment for each. The starting carbines, which are called SA-Rifles (for semi-automatic) are the M1 Garand and the Grewehr 43, both of which are pretty weak compared to nearly every other gun in the game. They can still top the early machine rifles at a distance however. H&G does show some heavy pay-to-win items such as the bazooka and panzarshrek requiring a butt ton of grenade kills to unlock to purchase at a large price of in game currency. This has not seemed to be a problem as the servers are usually resrictive on who can join which servers based on the inventory the soldiers have before they join. You do not need to worry about rank 9000s facing level 1's in the same server. Typically you should be rank 3 before you leave the original "Noob" Servers.
All in all, you will either love this game or hate it. If you happen to be one of the people who just love it, expect to play a lot of this game as you will need a huge chunk of time to grind to the soldier cap, and then rinse and repeat for a new soldier.

I have played every notable shooter under the sun in recent years, and this is by far at the top of my list as my favourite. This game just nails it at basically every turn. The guns are the best I have played with in recent memory – they all sound and FEEL fantastic and fun to use (asides from maybe the pistols). The developers know that a shooter, at its core, is only as good as its guns, and they really kicked some goals in this department. The environment is beautiful, alive and dynamic, and the story packs a punch and is plenty engaging with some great central characters.
With a great world to explore, plenty of things to do and skills to upgrade throughout your lengthy and action-packed journey, it’s hard to not love this game and how it packs in so many great mechanics and gameplay into one seamless package that boasts extraordinary value. It really is everything you want in a free-roaming, RPG-esque, AAA shooter.
My one gripe is that Ubisoft’s completely unnecessary Uplay service was ham-fisted into this game like no-one’s business, so if you’re without an internet connection make sure you look up how to switch Uplay into offline mode so it doesn’t endlessly annoy you (no problems if you have a steady connection though).
Lastly, I advise Normal mode, even for the relatively experienced, as you die just a little too quickly in Hard mode and you can’t play like Rambo that easily (and you’ll definitely want to go guns blazing!).

The inability to change your Field Of View bothers me, even though it's a easy fix by downloading a third-party program I think there's no excuse to not include it in this game.. ESPECIALLY since it was available in previous Call of Duty games. The campaign? I enjoyed it a lot, just that the ending was pretty stupid in my opinion.. If you know what I mean, it was all great until those last like 20 seconds.. But I guess that's there way of making an excuse for a sequel. So onto  the multiplayer, it's pretty much the same. Except, Infinity Ward changed how the perks work which I really really like, but I feel like you run out of perk combonations relatively quickly through-out playing the game. I also think there's not enough game modes, and there's not enough guns. I mean-- I thought there was supposed to be a new engine.. So wouldn't that allow more content? Right right? Nope! Apparently not.  The character customization is different, but not *that* great.. I mean it's not like anyone was begging for it, I think it's just another gimmicky feature added to try and reel people into buying their game in my opinion. The extinction mode is cool, but nothing new. They should really just make those survival modes Call of Duty makes standalone games.. I mean, aliens are a baby step away from zombies but at least they introduce different kinds of them you have to take down, instead of them just getting more health every round. I've heard it's similar to Gears of War's survival mode but sadly I wouldn't know, I've only ever played it once and I vaguely remember my experience. As far as I remember, you could buy defenses and guns just like in this but whatever.
Overall? It's an ok game, it's a Call of Duty game. Definately not worth 60 dollars, wait until the price drops on black friday if it even does but I highly doubt it. I wouldn't really recommend this game to anyone, it's just a game I have for when I get bored of other first-person shooters. Spend you money wisely!

A poor, disjointed and scrambled attempt at a game that doesn't do Call of Duty's formula justice.
The single player is laughable, in the bad way. When the game isn't blatantly ripping off things from others, like The Dark Knight Rises's plane hijacking scene, or reusing ideas from Modern Warfare 1 and 2, it still ends up becoming a confusing mess. Even when the game does evoke something genuinely interesting, often it will shoot itself in the foot a moment later.
The multiplayer is just as much of a mess, but this hurts the game much more than a bad single player campaign. The game's maps are overly-large and lack any real coherent design to them. It feels like they were designed only to show off next gen hardware. Couple this with a confusing metagame/unlock system, and some poor optimization for a game that is still using the same modified engine it always has, the game ends up failing at being a polished shooter. And as the final nail to the coffin? The game is still Peer-to-Peer, despite the promise of dedicated servers.
An abysmal failure for the series; they broke their formula, and ended up with nothing to show for it.

By far the worst COD I have played (I've played every COD since COD4, as well as the original).
This does not, however, mean that the game is totally trash.
I will point out the good things first.
Like every COD, this game has fairly solid mechanics. Gunplay feels good. Movement feels smooth, especially with the new movement system. Animations, are, as usual, top of the line (though I did spot a few re used animations).
Unfortunately, that's all the game has going for it. (For MP, at least).
One of the main problems is the lag. IW promised dedicated servers. They did not deliver. If you get a crap host (listen servers), the game will be horrible. And this happens a lot, unfortunately. Many people's connections are not designed for hosting servers. In addition, the game also suffers from sever FPS issues. The game is not well optimized for PC. It dips, stutters, and is generally unstable. Mind you, I am running a very high end rig (GTX680, i5 3570K).
The maps...the maps are OK. They are not like old COD maps. They are big, with lots of flank routes. They are not bad. Unfortunately, the spawn system really lets them down. For maps so big, you'd think they'd have worked out the spawns in 6v6. But no. No. It's horrible. Everyone WILL be spawning behind you.
In addition, IW seem to have gone with the MW2 approach - make everything overpowered. Instead, this time, everything is one or two hit kill. They seem to have tried to make everything as noob friendly as possible.
To conclude, at this state, the Multiplayer is not worth your money.
But how about Single Player and/or Extinction mode you ask? Single Player is alright. Story is solid, nothing special, but OK. Extinction mode is also OK. Not great. Certainly doesn't make up for the Multiplayer.
Wait for some significant patching and discounts before buying. Black Ops 2 is vastly superior.

I am not interested in the slightest to play the CoD: Ghosts multiplayer. It is the same exact boring playstyle that was old by the end of CoD4.
So far I have enjoyed the single-player campaign, but overall it is not that great either. Forcing mouse acceleration makes me wonder if they have a child that has never played a computer game making the design decisions.
Then we run into the big problem. DX11 is required to play. That is the most outrageous thing I have ever heard of and it is absolutely unacceptable. The is nothing in the CoD game engine that makes it so the game requires DX11. This is just lazy and yet another middle finger to the consumer from Infinity Ward. Not to mention that the requirement for DX11 is not highlighted in the least.
With a requirement that is unheard of, as in I don't know of a single game other than CoD: Ghosts that requires you to have a DX11 video card, Infinity Ward should face some serious penalties monetarily for sneaking that in. I can list about 50 games that absolutely blow CoD: Ghosts out of the water when it comes to graphical requirements, and not a single one of those games even require DX10 to play. Sure you need DX11 and an awesome card to experience those games to their fullest potential, but you can play.
The Radeon HD 6850 I am using won't work with CoD: Ghosts. The reason? DX11. The card supports it, but you have to flash the bios to update it to work with DX11. Flashing a video card bios, even to extremely avid gamers, is not something that is easy to do. Most people just don't have that technical skill. Not to mention that flashing your bios is a dangerous task even if you know what you are doing.
Overall I give the game a 6 out of 10 for the single-player campaign. I give it a 2 out of 10 for multi-player, as there is nothing new or innovative about reskinning some weapons and making some maps that take about 20 minutes. Factor in the required DX11 and I give it a 0 out of 10 for one of the most ridiculously idiotic decisions to have ever come from a major game studio.

Mediocre graphics, stupid plot, short campaign.  I am having a hard time thinking of the POSITIVE things to say about this game.  Infinity Ward should be removed as the developer of the next CoD game.  Because there WILL be a next CoD game.  At this point, for this franchise, money matters more than quality.  And Ghosts seems to have made a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of it.
Too often the missions in the single player started with "shhhh... " or something to that effect.  The problem is that I did not purchase a stealth game.  There are much better stealth franchises out there, if that is what I wanted to play.  When we are  inevitably discovered, it became a by-the-numbers run to the exit, or hatch, or helicopter, or tank... whichever.
And by the way: these have to be the loudest 'ghosts' ever.
Riley the gimmick (sorry, the dog) is an afterthought for the most part.  As a matter of fact, there seem to be only two characters that you develop any kind of emotional response to and they are not Riley or the brothers.
In an era that is producing games like Grand Theft Auto 5, Bioshock Infinite and FarCry 3, just to name a few,  it IS possible to produce quality and sales in sequels.  Activision seems to have given up on quality for this franchise if the evidence is the last two games they have thrown out: Black Ops II and Ghosts.  Both are a case of slapping some explosions together, throwing in some Multiplayer maps and putting 'Call of Duty -' in front of whatever is this game's name and out the door it goes.  Then they sit by the register and wait for us, the stupid people, to dish out the money for it.  We do it, even though sometimes we are questioning if this one is going to be any good.
The only reason I still play is because of the people I play with, but it may now be time to catch up on games I missed previously like Batman Origins or Splinter Cell Blacklist.
If you work hard for your money, save some of it and pass on this turkey.  Or, at the very least, wait for the first price drop.  At the rate people are leaving the Multiplayer, you will not have to wait long.

is a sandbox game that seems to draw much of its inspiration as an RPG from the old classic
; additionally, it incorporates elements from strategy and first/third-person combat simulation genres, making a rare combination that's been scarcely seen outside of the sci-fi
series.

's graphics, while a marked improvement over the original
, are certainly not its strong suit. This is not to say the graphics are "bad" but in some cases (campaign map, for example) just above merely functional, although the UI is still rather poor.
The soundtrack isn't bad, although after one hundred or so hours it may grate on your sanity. Sound effects themselves are okay, no real gripes there. The voices, which are mainly only in combat, can be downright hilarious in a way that is almost certainly unintentional.
An absolute delight!
's engine, though certainly glitchy at times, seems surprisingly robust when taking into consideration those of many modern big-name games; hit detection in particular, has proven to be much more accurate than had been anticipated. It's something of an impressive feat to have so many independent actors rendered in combat all at once, although the AI can be rather derpy. The points allocation system supplies a bit more than standard RPG fair but it's hard not to feel a little disappointed at the fact that there's not really any sort of "day-job" skills as a game like this just begs for such things.
There's not really much of a story insomuch as there's lore that the player interacts with to craft their own; it's all very open-ended and harkens back to the golden age of CRPGs wherein players would chart their own goals and not necessarily be bound to a linear path. A downside of this is that players who aren't interested enough to plot a personal course will likely lose interest rather quickly; this is not helped by the rather flat selection of quests and somewhat lacking lore.

I'll be honest, at first glance, this game looks somewhat like a poor man's MMO RPG. But after choosing a class, mastering a skillset, and getting into some fierce online battles, my opinion of the game greatly altered. Simple yet fluid controls allow you to stab, slash, and bludgeon your way to victory in any way you so choose. So jump in. You won't be dissapointed.

Although Mount & Blade: Warband takes place in a fantasy setting, it is worthy of being called the best medieval warfare simulator on the market. Warband is an entire genre of its own, merging a sandbox RPG world with feudal politics and a complex simulation of combat. Miles ahead of its competitors, Warband's single-player mode offers a near infinite amount of replayability, and its online mode further emphasizes the brilliance of its combat system.
Easily a 10/10, Warband is further supplemented by a host of breathtaking mods which can be found at the Taleworlds forums and Mod DB. My personal favourites are:
1. 1257 AD: an incredible historic overhaul which brings Warband into medieval Europe, as well as introduces a host of other improvements
2. The Deluge: a historical overhaul that brings Warband into 17th century Eastern Europe, inspired by Henryk Sienkiewicz's novel.
3. A Clash of Kings: Fantastic overhaul that brings Warband into the world of Game of Thrones.
4. Iron Europe: a multiplayer overhaul that brings players right into the First World War!

I've always been a fan of call of duty, even among a group of friends that hate the franchise.  For some reason I can't stop buying.  Well, now maybe I can.  Not only are this game's graphics, gameplay, gunplay, and lighting completely dissfuntional, but the game just isn't interesting in any way.  They didn't really add anything significant since previous games and they left so very much to be desired.  CoD 4 through Black Ops were all amazing, but I absolutley hated MW3 and Black Ops 2.  However, these games were still able to hold my interest.  Ghosts does not in any way, shape, or form hold my interest.

First impressions were I wanted a refund because I couldn't get the game to run with out lagging so bad I would rage quit. However, after REMOVING old video drivers and installing the newest, then setting the game to run at normal priority I habve played many hours lag free and at the highest settings. My computer is not a late and great. I have an AMD 6 core at 3.0 Mhz and 2 HD-6850's and 6 Gigs ram on Win 7 x64. Not to much above minimum specs.
The Game:
SP - I only have a few hours logged in SP but so far the story line is IMHO pretty decent. I have had no bugs (others have reported bugs) and the missions have gone smoothly other than my own mistakes.
MP - Maps are a variety of CQB and large sniper maps. Have not seen nearly as many hackers as others have been complaining about, but I have seen less than a handful. I am enjoying the maps. I however wish that dedicated servers would be in the next patch, but I doubt we will ever get them.
Kits - Soldier and kit building is far superior to previous titles allowing for full customization of your soldier. The ability to create multiple soldiers and level them up for squad play is interesting and something I am just now starting.
Graphics
Meh. When at full settings the graphics are decent but not worthy of next-gen branding. Destruct
ible enviroments could be described as a very few destructible objects. BF3 even had almost full destructable environments (buildings, etc.) Do not expect this in Ghosts. For a "next-gen" game I expected more, way more...
I'ld give this game 7/10. The gampeplay for me is pretty damn good, but the graphics should be way better.

Call of Duty: Ghosts
Now this game has received a lot of hate. Even from me as I was one of the lucky buyers do be locked out because of a RAM restriction that would not let you play. Infinity Ward took there so called next gen game too serious. After a huge outcry of unhappy costumers and thousands of people wanting there money back they finally gave up and took the restriction out with a patch.
The game is clearly not next gen and we were also lied about getting dedicated servers. Overall the release of the game was a mess.
Now for the Single-player. (SPOILER ALERT ) DON'T READ IF YOU HAVEN'T PLAYED THE CAMPAIGN
I have to say that I enjoyed this game very much for its story. At last we don't have a Russian or Middle East enemy or main villain. This game is set in an alternate timeline that has nothing to do with Modern Warfare or Black ops. This time the threat is from South America that joined forces and overcomes the world. I enjoyed this a lot since I speak Spanish and could understand all the stuff enemies talk about and scream when the fighting begins. The campaign is not the longest but it took me over 10 hours since I went and looked for all the secrets and also made it my mission to get all the achievements. It has some really nice missions not seen in a Call of Duty game. Underwater, in Space, and the use of a German Shepard. The game does look great and might appear next gen ,but that debatable. The overall story just sucked me in and I didn't have that feeling with Black Ops 2 and Modern Warfare 3. Since this time its just from 1 point of view the story stayed interesting.
The music is OK and the sound of guns are also a bit better that BO2. Overall I enjoyed this game very much and give it a personal 8 out of 10.
The Multiplayer.
Now this part has its ups and downs. No its not Battlefield its still Call of Duty. Fast run and gun action like we all love it. The maps are huge compared to the tennis court maps of MW3 and BO2. These maps actually change and move around. The gamplay is practically the same as any COD Multiplayer. New guns , new perks, new costumisation. They actually let you use a woman now for the Multiplayer. The games can be from great to unplayable. No dedicated servers!!! So sometimes the game can be smooth as silk or lag horrible. IW has not patched this game against hackers. So be aware! I play a lot against bots, that is a nice way to learn the maps and play against non cheaters I give the Multiplayer a 6 out of 10.
Co Op Modes.
Now this is what I loved the most In Ghost.
There is a really great amount of modes. From survival modes to squad against squad. Fight against hordes of infected soldiers in co op.
And the one that is my favorite. Extinction!! Yes its finally something else than zombies! This is an entire little story we you play solo or with friends fighting your way trough an invasion of aliens. its not just level after level its an entire little campaign were you have to get from a landing site to the core of the invasion. Its awesome and its nice to fight something different than Nazi Zombies.
I give this part of the game a 9 out of 10.
If you like Call of Duty you will like this game(or hate). If you are new to the series I recommend Call of Duty 4:Modern Warfare which is still the best in my opinion.
Overall the rating for Ghost from me is a 7.5
Wait until it goes on sale for at least half price ... then you'll get some value for your spend ... overall, disappointing.
Speaking purely from a multiplayer perspective, feel free to just ignore this and buy Battlefield 4 instead.

First off, this game is HEAVILY pay to win!
With that said, the gameplay is fun, the controls are responsive and the assault team / generals system works well. That's about all the good stuff I have to say about this game.
Everything that can be bought in game (and I mean EVERYTHING) is absurdly expensive, most of the maps are god awful, the battles are majorly unbalanced and I have noticed the odd issue with net code (almost as bad as it is in Battlefield 4, but not quite).
So, imagine this. You join a battle, but the enemy team has tanks. Well you can just get your own tank right? Nope, once unlocking that it costs over 20k credits to get the basic tank, and that doesn't even have a cannon. So, just give your soldier an AT weapon? Nope, again, it costs a ridiculous amount of credits.
So quite often you end up going against heavy armour and cant do anything else about it. Sure you get the odd AT weapon that spawns on the map, but they spawn in the most stupid places, like out in the open for example.
Most of the maps are so open it's not even funny. They all seem to favour either snipers or vehicles, which you'll be grinding for hours and hours before you get either one of them, oh my bad, you can always pay REAL MONEY to get them early.
So if you can get past the crappy maps and the unbalanced teams, there's the people who have actually paid into the game. You then have to deal with people with one shot kill weapons, better vehicles and a certain badge that gives you more HP. There's probably a lot more stuff you can buy to **** over people who aren't dim-witted enough to give this piece of trash they call a game any money, but honestly I gave up at that point.
Conclusion:
Don't bother with this unless you like unbalanced games and having to pay real money to get anywhere or having to pay to have fun. Like BrazillianSoldier said in his review
, buy Rising Storm/Red Orchestra 2. It's very similar to this, only you pay for it once and you have the whole game, no having to deal with and damn pay to win crap.

Well, here we are again: another year, another
, as the saying goes.
This franchise has grown incredibly stale in the past five years or so. Infinity Ward has stuck to the same formula since
, and as a result, almost everything in
feels dated and unimaginative.
Not that some widely acclaimed aspects of said formula needed any change. For instance, the core gameplay mechanics, such as the
itself, still feel slick and polished.
But how do you justify a 50-gigabyte installation size and the “next-gen” marketing this game received, when it looks barely nicer than stuff that was released in 2007? It’s not an ugly-looking game, sure, and the textures do look pretty good, despite what some people may say. But comparisons with
,
and other recent titles are inevitable, and the fact remains that everything else in
, graphics-wise (lighting, particle effects, physics, etc.), is subpar.
I am not one to judge a game solely on its graphical fidelity, however. The problem with
is that, sans the welcome addition of the ability to practice against bots, it has no redeeming qualities to speak of.
The single-player campaign is short, cliché-ridden and does not give the player any freedom. You just follow scripted orders from your “A.I.” companions, moving forward when told to and shooting enemies that pop out of hiding (when told to). It doesn’t help that the story is entirely predictable and that the voice-acting is abysmal (and since we're on the subject of audio, what can I say about the game's single, useless "master volume" slider in the settings menu?).
But most people seem to buy
games for its multiplayer portion. And it too is a colossal failure. Maps are poorly designed and don’t support more than 18 players (most matches have 12 or less players). The matchmaking system is terrible: teams are completely unbalanced more often than not. There are no dedicated servers, despite Mark Rubin’s (Infinity Ward’s Executive Producer) promises prior to the game’s release. Teamwork is non-existent, as people just run in circles and shoot each other in the back to get the best possible kill-to-death ratio and unlock ridiculous, balance-breaking “killstreak” bonuses.

The "new" Extinction Mode is not even worth discussing. It is basically an uninspired rehash of Treyarch's far superior "Zombies" horde-mode (from
and the
series).
To top it all,
suffers from a myriad of technical issues, such as glitches, crashes and framerate drops. And as a sign of Infinity Ward's everlasting "love" for the PC audience, there is no field-of-view slider of any kind, and a single slider for audio. Individual sliders for music, sound effects and voice communication would be too much to ask, apparently.
The bottom line: don’t buy it.

A bunch of pretentious 20-somethings go on a vacation to do "cool" stuff before suddenly getting captured by slavers on a South Pacific Island they had the misfortune of skydiving onto. Your character escapes and then goes off to try to free the rest of your merry band of friends.
Since I'm already here, I'm going to start with story. Frankly, I found it to be the weakest part of the entire game. Having had basically no interaction with these people I am trying to save, I find it hard to care about them. I know the player character cares about them, but I, the player, have no reasons of my own. The other characters are a mixed bag of competence (Dennis, Sam), bleh (Citra, Volker), and above average (Jason, Vaas, Buck). And the only reason I put Buck up there is that he was the only villain that made me geniunely want to kill him. Sadly the game didnt let me choose how... :(
So some poor character development in some areas, and then the plot makes some very abrupt shifts that made me either go "WTF" or just lose understanding of events. Partcularly at the game's ending missions and the final encounter with Vaas. They ended so quickly and rushed onto the next plot point that I was left scratching my head wondering if I had missed something. There are a number of story areas they could have done much better, but those two for sure.
And if it wasn't for the gameplay, I'd probably throw this game off a bridge for making character/plot mistakes like that.
But FC3 has gameplay, and much of it is pretty cool. One of the few open world sandboxes that feels truly "alive" as I came across countless unscripted encounters. Animals kill eachother, animals kill people, and... people kill other people quite alot. Being something of an animal lover (or at least someone who finds hurting animals distasteful), I was rather disturbed by the amount of animal killing that went on in this game. It made me sad to shoot playful dogs, beautiful tigers, or huggly bears throughout my entire time playing this. In fact, unless it was absolutely necessary ('this one is gonna kill me!' or 'I need animal stuffs to make this upgrade') I tried my best to leave the critters alone.
There are also alot of different weapons, and you can carry 4 at a time when fully upgraded. You can also customize those weapons quite a bit to fit with your particular style. This ensures that you are able to play in the sandbox however you so choose. Do you prefer to go "native" with just a bow and a knife? Or to load up on silenced weaponry and take out entire outposts without them ever knowing you were there? Or are you the sort of person that handles life's problems with automatic weapons, flamethrowers, and rocket launchers? All of those will work, though sneakiness gives you more XP, as usual. Still, I had great fun playing like I was some kind of special forces commando, just as I did when I stormed in and either set everything on fire or just blew it up. Usually both.
Anyway, its a big open world place with lots of stuff to mess with. Plenty to occupy ones time for a few dozen hours if not more. Fans of big sandbox games should feel right at home here. Sadly, I think the devs might have spent too much time getting their bears to be menacing and huggly, and too little time on developing characters and making a less failure of an ending.
So... Yey for gameplay funtimes and sandbox adventures, but boo for story and (most) characters. Sadly I can only say "yes" or "no" on Steam rather than "Maybe."
I'm going to choose yes because whatever failures the plot has is outweighed by the fact that this game allows me to just run around the jungles sniping people at one place and completely burning out the next. Yay!

I wasn't impressed.
The graphics are very nice, and the game runs fairly smoothly even with high detail settings, the sounds are good and technically everything is top notch. It's just that the game is boring. The plot is the most typical boilerplate horror movie plot ever, I.E. a bunch of rich kids are on a holiday (probably paid by their dads) doing skydiving and all kinds of expensive stuff somewhere in Pacific, when they get kidnapped by a bunch of homicidal baddies. One of those kids breaks out, and starts a war against the captors in attempt to free the others.
The game has it's moments, but most of the time it just feels a bit pointless somehow. Since I coulnd't really relate at all to the bunch of priviliged, well off boys and girls, I couldn't form any emotional attachment to them. The island itseld is quite big and pretty, but although you can theoretically spend hours and hours just exploring it, why would you? There's nothing interesting there to be found, all you can ever hope to find are those crates with a little money in them. You can use the money to buy guns, but again it feels pointless since you only really NEED the gun that you had in the beginning... And besides, climbing the radio towers, which there are plenty of and which reveal the map, gives you free weapons, so you don't really need to use money on them unless you want to.
All in all, it's on ok game, I spent 30hrs on it and completed the storyline, but it definitely wasn't anything special. The plot is very predictable and offers no real surprises, and the free world is really nothing but a backdrop for it. I paid a fiver  for the game, and I suggest you, dear reader, don't pay any more than that since it's just not worth it.

is a sandbox game that seems to draw much of its inspiration as an RPG from the old classic
; additionally, it incorporates elements from strategy and first/third-person combat simulation genres, making a rare combination that's been scarcely seen outside of the sci-fi
series.

's graphics, while a marked improvement over the original
, are certainly not its strong suit. This is not to say the graphics are "bad" but in some cases (campaign map, for example) just above merely functional, although the UI is still rather poor.
The soundtrack isn't bad, although after one hundred or so hours it may grate on your sanity. Sound effects themselves are okay, no real gripes there. The voices, which are mainly only in combat, can be downright hilarious in a way that is almost certainly unintentional.
An absolute delight!
's engine, though certainly glitchy at times, seems surprisingly robust when taking into consideration those of many modern big-name games; hit detection in particular, has proven to be much more accurate than had been anticipated. It's something of an impressive feat to have so many independent actors rendered in combat all at once, although the AI can be rather derpy. The points allocation system supplies a bit more than standard RPG fair but it's hard not to feel a little disappointed at the fact that there's not really any sort of "day-job" skills as a game like this just begs for such things.
There's not really much of a story insomuch as there's lore that the player interacts with to craft their own; it's all very open-ended and harkens back to the golden age of CRPGs wherein players would chart their own goals and not necessarily be bound to a linear path. A downside of this is that players who aren't interested enough to plot a personal course will likely lose interest rather quickly; this is not helped by the rather flat selection of quests and somewhat lacking lore.

I know to most people this game looks like♥♥♥♥♥♥ with dated graphics and silly looking combat, but there's a reason this is one of my most played games on steam. You're thrust into a fictional but realistic medieval world and you're allowed to do pretty much whatever you want, be it raiding villages or pledging your allegiance to one of the land's kingdoms. Eventually you can attempt to become a lord of one of the kingdoms and even carve out your own new kingdom somewhere in the world. There are even disgraced princes and princesses who's causes you can aid. You do all of these things by leveling up your own character RPG style as well as recruiting kingdom specific units into your army to form your own "war band." There are also special or "hero" individuals you can add who you level up much like yourself in an RPG way, allowing you to create specialists in your contingent.
Admittedly, the diplomacy and actual interaction with kingdoms can be somewhat bare bones, which is remedied by the Diplomacy Mod, but the core gameplay is solid. The combat is deep, requiring you to block and attack in all 4 directions. However, sometimes the game is punishingly difficult, especialy when you get defeated with low amounts of troops. You can be caught in a non stop cycle of trying to recruit new guys and getting defeated again, and trying to get new guys and getting defeated again.... and so on so on. If you keep with it long enough you eventually get enough dudes to take on entire kingdoms. You can even appoint your own lords and gift them lands and♥♥♥♥♥♥
In addition to this, I highly recommend the Napoleonic Wars DLC, which is only multiplayer. Just imagine fighting in the time of Muskets, where guns take forever to reload, and are wildly inaccurate. Players form into lines, and shoot at the enemy with awful guns, as well as manning and shooting awful artillery weapons, and engage in brutal hand to hand combat. Some clans on the game even have creepily efficient line formation and order, even incorporating color bearers (flag carrier) and music players to keep everyone in order (The music also gives passive buffs like reduced reload speed). It's really something amazing to watch up to 200 players (holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ form up lines and take positions shooting at each other in unison while cannons thunder into ranks of soldiers (often killing groups of ten with a well placed shot) and calvary charging the flanks of infantry. It feels like a scripted movie sequence more than anything else.
Buy this game, it is really fun if you can forgive the dated visuals and sometimes tedious gameplay. I'm surprised by how much I like it.

A great entry to the Call of Duty series.  Updated graphics, an improved sound engine, reworked character creation,  larger maps,  and a return to old school gameplay make this title a winner.
The graphics have seen some pretty serious improvements, especially in single player.  They're not the earth shattering improvements that many expected with the announcement of a "new engine" but obvious improvements nonetheless.  Better lighting engine, improved particles, tessellation, sub-d enhancements that are especially evident in character models all bring something more to the table.  Ignore those who claim that the engine has remained unchanged.  They literally have no idea what they're talking about.
The sound engine has especially been upgraded.  Enemy footsteps are clear as a bell, without any sort of enhancements.  With just about any headset, it's easy to tell when a heavy-footed enemy is sprinting towards your location.  More experienced players will crouch walk or use dead silence to approach undetected.  This effect is really enhanced when the amplify perk is equipped.
Character creation has been completely retooled.  Everything is customizable from gender, race, uniforms, patches, headgear, you name it.  Along with this the new perk system is much more dynamic than previous entries in the series.  Gone are the days of 3 (comparatively) powerful perks, and in their place are a multitude of perks that while alone do less, but when combined offer countless permutations.
A welcome change, or rather a welcome return for the Call of Duty series.  Much less emphasis on run'n'gun and more emphasis on  tactical game play on much larger maps.  Gone is the Treyarch 3 route map making paradigm, and in it's place is a multitude of flanking routes on large, much more open maps.  Fans of lightweight SMG play are likely to be disappointed, but fans of just about everything else will be thrilled to death.
What makes this game really shine though is the return of gun play.  Killstreaks have been seriously nerfed across the board. Rather than the killer airs support that has marked the series since MW2, this game offers lethal kill streaks more along the lines of the Cobra or Hind from MW1.  While they still get a few kills, they're not same rewards as in later games.  Explosives are less powerful, with absolutely no way to replenish during a life.  Instead, this game has returned to gun play, and not pray and spray SMG or shotgun play, but a return of the assault rifle as the dominant weapon, with plenty of room for snipers and marksman rifles as well.  Those looking for cheap exploits like the grenade launcher + OMA from MW2 should look elsewhere.

When I first played Call of Duty: Ghosts on release day I was very dissapointed. The online was plagued by frame-rate stuttering  and other problems. Since then, however, the game has been updated and most of the framereate issues have been esolved. Unfortunately, the online play is still plagued by lag and other network issues.
Further, the "innovations" that were promised are either so negligible that they are pointless, or they damage the online play. For example, one of the kill streaks gives you a dog as your companion who rushes players and kills them. Unfortunately, these dogs rule the gameplay for the most part and you will find yourself dying by dogs way too frequently.
While camping has always plagued FPSs, COD: Ghosts brings it to a new level; Where in past games campers were usually easy to detect, the new enviroments in this new installment are seemingly designed with camping in mind. There are bushes, coves, cubbies, windows, holes, and sniper roosts to an absurd level. To make matters worse, Ghosts even goes as far as to offer dedicated campers ghilie suits to better camp out. To compound all of the above, silencers' usual negative consequences have been removed which has caused the prolieration of their use. First of all i'd like to remind you that this is an unfinished game, and some features may be changed before i get around to updating this.
Hero's and generals is by far one of the best WW2 FPS's ive played. The guns feel good, no weapon is inherently overpowered and the action is almost always there. this is a great F2P if your willing to sink hours into a good FPS WW2 game.
Unfortunatly this is where most of Hero's and Generals upsides stop. whilst the gameplay feels good, the other aspects of the game deeply inhibit the rest of the gameplay. Whilst i have not been able to fully go into the whole "general" part of the game due to me being unable to spend large amount of hours and unwillingness to pay for currency(Gold) i still get the gist. you as a general pay with warfunds(or Gold) to get an assault team, up to a max of five, after this you assign them to battles and allow players of those types to play in those battles, you then get warfunds to spend on other assault teams. whilst this sounds like a great way to simulate how supply and demand worked in the war, its does impact gameplay itself. as you get further into the game, you may find yourself being overrun by tanks, bombers with your team having nothing but infantry or even yourself steamrolling the other team with tanks and such whilst they have noting but infantry, and what this does is make the game feel unbalanced, almost pay to win, why? because the winning side solely depends on who spent more on their assault teams and less about where their placed and when.
They also have a medal system of which is a great idea, but done a little wrong.
ribbons are earned by doing even the most mundane things, running, sprinting, shooting someone with a particular gun all earn points towards specific medals, and in turn give you xp towards ranks aswell as perks and better weapons/guns this gives you goals outside of the main game and is great. but here's where it goes wrong, even some basic items like Anti-Tank weapons are kept from new users behind this medal system and although they tried to aleviate this with certain features (free AT single fire rockets at spawn) it simply does not help. you will still be rolled over by those people who paid to ride the best tanks. this could also stem from the fact that every weapon, wether or not you have aquired the medal for it can be bought with Gold.
In summary, at this moment it feels incredibly pay-to-win, the developers seemed to have built the monetisation of the game over it instead of beside it as key gameplay elements are blocked to new comers and even some who are mid way into the game by pay walls, not to say that you cant get to those elements, but the amount of sheer effort to get to these elements will definatly impact your enjoyment of the game. but even after saying all this i will still recommend this game, i enjoy Hero's and General's and i will most definatly keep playing (if not fustrated at times) despite all the money related flaws i see this as a great WW2 FPS the gameplay is fenominal, each battle you either play as a team or lose, complete strangers giving you cover fire as you capture an enemy radio station or stratigising with people on how best to take out that sniping tank is a great feeling, and as far as ive played there is no better game to expierince this kind of gameplay.

The game currently is not working as intended by the developers. If you're trying to play the generals portion of the game many of the campaign map lines are broken meaning you cannot move troops between many of the cities. Right now the city of Den Haag which has two lines reaching the UK is currently only working one way and that is the allied lines. The germans cannot cross the english channel at all that way. More and more of these lines are breaking everyday and making the war on the Julius server longer and longer to the point that its just a big stalemate now. The developers have yet to make a statement on this massive game breaking bug.
There is also very few active participants in the war itself. There is probably less then 1000 active players using the actual normal missions and the rest are just playing through training missions. You can turn off training missions through the settings and it gives a much better picture of the game.
Many of players are unable to purchase gold from within the game itself forcing them to either wait for this bug to be fixed or to go through at the games website to make a purchase but then being unable to use there steam wallet cards for purchases through steam. The overlay also does not work for many players that play the game through steam.
The game also has some very interesting bugs. The game has some very bad hit detection issues not registering shots but seeing bloodsplatter from the players model. Riding a bicycle and then getting off of it then getting launched into the air and falling to your death which appears to be a bug that has existed even before steam has been release by doing some research on the main game forums. Driving vehicle like APC and tanks and having them flip over simple objects in the game. So far my favorite one is having my tank flip over from running into a bicycle.
The movement in the game itself is very stiff. You cannot move from a prone position to a crouching position and vice versa making it sometimes very difficult to protect yourself from enemy fire. You have to first expose yourself by standing up and then going into the crouched or prone position leaving yourself open to enemy fire while doing this movement.
The game also only in total has 5 maps made for the FPS portion of it. Those are the church map, train map, airfield map which are all assault and defend missions then there are the skirmish maps which is the forest map and the barn map. This is all the maps they have for the game. The church and train maps have very noticeable choke points that make it very difficult most of the time for assaulting team to win without tanks.
The game has a lot of potential but I cannot recommend the game because of the above points and do hope that the game improves by the time it is released with all of these issues being fixed.

I really like Far Cry 3 for the world, the gameplay mechanics and the very fun missions.
Roaming around these beautiful islands is truly an amazing experience, and it often feels more like an adventure game than an action game.
However Far Cry 3 has a few flaws that bothered me, for one the Dubstep music that plays during the action, was really not a good choice for the setting. Maybe it was supposed to reflect the character's youth and style, but I didn't appreciate it.
And the second thing are the characters, especially Jason's friends, who I just could not believe in. Although they tried to depict human emotions, everyone's purpose really seemed to be to push the story and the events forward. The only exception being Vaas, who not only makes up for all the remaining characters, but also ends up making the game itself something unique and entertaining.
The last big flaw that bugged me, were the amount of collectibles to pick up in the game. Being a completionist, I just feel compelled to go and grab the little diamond boxes that appear on my radar, but there are hundreds of them absolutely everywhere, and it ends up feeling like a really annoying grind.
It's true that some of them were placed in hidden areas, which made me actually visit and explore the game, but there were simply too many in the end.
Aside from those 3 little gripes I have with Far Cry 3, I absolutely loved it.

Feminism is a collection of movements and ideologies that share a common goal: to define, establish, and achieve equal political, economic, cultural, personal, and social rights for women.[1][2] This includes seeking to establish equal opportunities for women in education and employment.
A feminist generally self-defines as advocating for or supporting the rights and equality of women.[3]
Feminist theory, which emerged from feminist movements, aims to understand the nature of gender inequality by examining women's social roles and lived experience; it has developed theories in a variety of disciplines in order to respond to issues such as the social construction of sex and gender.[4][5] Some forms of feminism have been criticized for taking into account only white, middle-class, educated perspectives. This led to the creation of ethnically specific or multiculturalist forms of feminism.[6]
Feminist movements have and continue to campaign for many women's rights, including the right to vote, to hold public office, to work, to fair wages or equal pay, to own property, to education, to enter contracts, to have equal rights within marriage, and to have maternity leave. Feminists have also worked to promote bodily autonomy and integrity, and to protect women and girls from♥♥♥♥♥♥ sexual harassment, and domestic violence.[7]
Feminist campaigns are generally considered to be main force behind major historical societal changes, particularly in the West, where they are near-universally credited with having achieved women's suffrage, gender neutrality in English, equal pay for women, reproductive rights for women (including access to contraceptives and abortion), and the right to enter into contracts and own property.[8]
Feminist advocacy is mainly focused on women's rights, but author bell hooks, among others, argue for the necessity for it to include men's liberation, because men are also harmed by traditional gender roles.[9]

History
Feminist Suffrage Parade in New York City, 6 May 1912
Main article: History of feminism
See also: Protofeminism
Charles Fourier, a Utopian Socialist and French philosopher, is credited with having coined the word "feminism" in 1837.[10] The words "feminism" and "feminist" first appeared in France and the Netherlands in 1872,[11] Great Britain in the 1890s, and the United States in 1910,[12][13] and the Oxford English Dictionary lists 1852 as the year of the first appearance of "feminist"[3] and 1895 for "feminism".[14] Depending on historical moment, culture and country, feminists around the world have had different causes and goals. Most western feminist historians assert that all movements that work to obtain women's rights should be considered feminist movements, even when they did not (or do not) apply the term to themselves.[15][16][17][18][19][20] Other historians assert that the term should be limited to the modern feminist movement and its descendants. Those historians use the label "protofeminist" to describe earlier movements.[21]
The history of the modern western feminist movements is divided into three "waves".[22][23] Each wave dealt with different aspects of the same feminist issues. The first wave comprised women's suffrage movements of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, promoting women's right to vote. The second wave was associated with the ideas and actions of the women's liberation movement beginning in the 1960s. The second wave campaigned for legal and social equality for women. The third wave is a continuation of, and a reaction to, the perceived failures of second-wave feminism, beginning in the 1990s.[24]
Nineteenth and early twentieth centuries
Main article: First-wave feminism
First-wave feminism was a period of activity during the nineteenth century and early twentieth century. In the UK and US, it focused on the promotion of equal contract, marriage, parenting, and property rights for women. By the end of the nineteenth century, activism focused primarily on gaining political power, particularly the right of women's suffrage, though some feminists were active in campaigning for women's sexual, reproductive, and economic rights as well.[25]
Women's suffrage began in Britain's Australasian colonies at the close of the 19th century, with the self-governing colonies of New Zealand granting women the right to vote in 1893 and South Australia granting female suffrage (the right to vote and stand for parliamentary office) in 1895. This was followed by Australia granting female suffrage in 1902.[26][27]
After selling her home, Emmeline Pankhurst, pictured in New York City in 1913, travelled constantly, giving speeches throughout Britain and the United States.
In the Netherlands, Wilhelmina Drucker (1847-1925) fought successfully for the vote and equal rights for women through political and feminist organisations she founded.
In Britain the Suffragettes and the Suffragists campaigned for the women's vote, and in 1918 the Representation of the People Act was passed granting the vote to women over the age of 30 who owned houses. Warning: If you're sensative to criticism while a game in in early access/beta, then do not read please.
This game is a massive wreck. It takes a simple concept (arcade shooter in WW2) and manages to implement it in such a way that it is just barely fun because of not only the piles of glitches, problems and bad decisions but also terrible game design choices and systems.
The money is grindy to get and many players never realize this. Your level determines your money and it's set per-mission. As a result getting money is VERY time consuming. Near max-rank I was making just under 2k per match and my rifle (scoped sniper) cost 240k+. This is disgusting, especially considering how much the pre-requisite rifle cost and how useless it was (80k, and is easily outmatched at medium/medium long ranges by SMGs and semi-automatic rifles).
If you get ANY kind of upgrades to your weapons they degrade and must be repaired at EXTREME cost. Any ammunition changes need to be paid for, which is also expensive. It is impossible to improve a gun or even carry anti-tank weaponry AND save up for upgraded weapons/parts because of the ridiculous expenses pushed on the player. Why? Because the gold price equivelent (paid for with CASH) is incredibly small so it's trying to force-encourage spending through not comfort or convenience but PAIN.
Making this worse? The unspoken dynamic of the game is that Infantry take out planes, infantry and objectives, tanks take out infantry (with a tank destroyer for other tanks), and planes take out tanks and other planes. You CAN go anti-tank as a soldier but it makes you near useless in matches and is a long grind with a huge expense waiting for you.
Every single match is made up of squads that are provided via generals side, and with tons of people buying and leveling squads you're bound to get shoved into tiny newbie squads which disallow vehicles, or limit your class, or worse you're on a team with 3 basic squads whereas the enemy has PLANES AND TANKS.
The chat system is text only, and only works in about 3/4 of the matches or less (it was worse but at some point got slightly better).
Ingame you'll find yourself TKing friendlies unexpectedly because of unusual setup, but no worry, while it prompts them to report you for TK or damage it does nothing but play an unfriendly sound to you. Great. If you're going anti-tank like me, expect to rack up the TKs because other players love to dry hump tanks when desperate to kill them. They don't come to the conclusion that they have no effective weaponry  and try to find it, they just...who knows.
The match setups are pretty terrible too, because of map design and the copied mechanic of capturing bases.
Finally progressing in the game is painful because it's set in stone nearly. You will literally progress on average based on the number of rounds you enter more reliably than how you perform.
I wanted to like this game so much, and I played it for so long, even spending money on it to support devs and TRY to make it more enjoyable, but as a programmer the more I played the more angry I got at how lazy or incompetent most of the flaws were.
What's worse is I recall seeing on their forums somewhere that they were bragging or that they had some kind of anti-cheat built in. Thinking on this further, the game is broken beyond any kind of defense and they had spent time with an anti-cheat? For what purpose? Because they wanted to accept payment. They wanted to start an income stream on their busted game.
Finally, so if you put your head down and try to enjoy the game, you can for a while. Seriously. But what drew the straw for me was that as a sniper I could SEE how many shots were phantom hits (blood spray but no damage) and this was infuriating. Their servers and hit detection system is terrible. As a result I MUST say. If you are going to play the game, by the time you finish the tutorial you'll be offered the chance to use the submachine gun. USE IT. Because of the brokenness of the game the machine guns in the game are KING.
Those with grenades make you practically the most flexible player in the game.
You'll murder ruthlessly up close, frustrate snipers trying to hit you and not while spraying pure death at them.
I made a sniper and submachinegun user simultaneously on US then on Germany, and both times my SMG builds were flying through ranks and rarely dying whereas my sniper builds (when I have played sniper since Team Fortress Classic back in the late 90's) would suffer based on mechanics alone.
