Mount and Blade: Warband is personally one of my favorite games.
Yes, despite it's obvious low-budget production, it's still one of the best games I've played, especially for those into the Action genre, but want important RTS and RPG elements.
You also gotta pay respect to the developers, Taleworlds. They didn't have much money when they started out, ( actually they almost had none ) and they started in a garage for the first game, but it slowly upgraded into this glorious masterpiece. Mount and Blade: Warband is a great game because it has a level of depth and complexity that is further developed by it's design.
The combat is one of the best things about Mount and Blade: Warband, because it promotes skill, it promotes variation, and it promotes seperate playstyles. Do you like spears, swords, or what? You can literally pick from lots of different weapons, and these weapons are just copy/paste reskins. They all have another depth to that as well. Weapons do various types of damage and effects. Blunt weapons, for example, will knock enemies out in singleplayer, allow you to sell the enemy after battle to a slave trader. So you can make some money. Piercing damage weapons allows you to penetrate armor, and cutting weapons allow you to chop light armored enemies in half. You can see on the weapon's stat page what kind of stats it has. It may be a faster, but shorter weapon, or a longer and slower weapon.
You may ask 'Why do I want a blunt weapon in multiplayer?' Well, for 1 reason, you can knock down people with it. As in, take them to the ground, where you can beat them silly.
There are also weapons that 'aren't balanced'. This means, you can stun the enemy if they decided to block you, and if your weapon is heavier.
Personally, I like the default spear. It's weak, shorter than other polearms, and not as fast as some. However, I very much enjoy the weapon because it fits my playstyle. It's a flexible weapon, one that can perform in all situations, and perform exceptionally well in open fields and against cavalry.
The multiplayer for Mount and Blade: Warband is also very good. It has the standard TDM, FFA, and all sorts of things, but it also has Duel and Siege. You can duel other players in a match of skill of the blade, or you could play in large battle sieges. Some servers allow for 64v64 player sieges, which is VERY fun to play. The sieges are exactly how you would see castle defence/offense. Archers firing down to the besiegers, crossbowmen firing up to soften the defence, infantry fighting it out on the walls in a tense close quarters melee battle, and warriors emerging from the siege towers.
The Singleplayer for Mount and Blade: Warband, is less about skill, and far more about being much, much smarter. You start off has a foreigner, with different stats and starting equipment, depending on the choices you make. You can also be a male or female, which DOES change which options you have available to you. You can start as a male noble, and have an easier start, as you will have most things you need, such as extra gold, renown ( for getting lords to recognize you ) and a banner ( for looking cool ). It's not like there isn't a challenge. You can start as a commoner female for a harder path if you want. The challenges are sexist, by the way, so don't get upset over nothing. If you still do, get out. Now. Anyways, if you are a female, you may have an alternate way of rising to power.
As a male, you do the generic stuff. You gain renown, become a vassal ( or become another... )
You court a lady you like, and battle for women and fight for their honor in tournaments.
As a female, it is much different. You can talk to lords, some may even already like you, others may insult you for being a woman. You can use this to your advantage. A woman in Calradia can manipulate the balance of power by marrying into a stronger/wealthier family and in turn, using him as a means to rise into power.
As for the other things in the singleplayer, there's many viable playstyles. You don't HAVE to participate in combat 24/7. Maybe you can if you want to. You can be a trader, who buys and sells and owns businesses throughout the land. You can be the plain old adventurer, doing quests for rewards, or you could be a slaver, knocking the enemy out, and selling them to the highest bitter. Of course, there are multiple playstyles available, as I said. My personal favorite is the 'Arena Hero/Tournament Champion' type style. I gain money from fighting in the arena to fund my troops, and I use my troops to help fight bandits, and fight deserters.
As you get further into the singleplayer, you will eventually become a vassal. You can manage fiefs, basically plot of lands, and tax them accordingly, managing the economic state of your area by helping the place out. Towns and Villages will have different types of things to do.
In towns, you will find that there is much to do. You can go to the inn, look for recruits, ask fellow travellers about things, find slavers, book merchants, and companions.
( Companions are like the player, you can customize them and level them up. )
There are also many merchants in town, where you can buy armor, weapons, mounts, and supplies.
In villages, you can recruit peasants of the faction you are at. So if you go into faction A's village, you will recruit faction A's peasants. If another faction takes over those will still be Faction A's peasants.
Also, you will need to manage morale. Being constantly defeated, being forced to surrender, leaving troops to die while you escape... Those will hurt morale. ( Low morale = Deserters )
And yes, you can be beaten. There are no checkpoints. If you fail, you must suffer the consequences of your actions. But, in Calradia you don't die. That doesn't make you special though. No one else really dies, other than the generic soldier. You and every other lord are against each other, friendly or not. Like a particular lady? Better make sure Count Gutlans doesn't sweep her off her feet first. Maybe you'll have to duel him so Gutlans won't see her again.
But let's say you get captured before you can get to Gutlans. You were defeated by bandits and captured. You didn't get to escape for a long, long time. The lady you like is now going to marry him. You've failed in your goal to marry her, and do you know why? It was your fault. Every action in Mount and Blade has a consequence, so making choices are important.
Mount and Blade: Warband's singleplayer is an open-world sandbox. If you want, you can be an adventurer all the way until there is only one kingdom left. Yup, that's perfectly fine. There is no forced objective. You, as the player, are able to decide what you want to do, and when you want to do it. And of course, how you want to do it.
Do you know if you're a top-notch fighter? Think you can take on everyone alone with your boys? If you can do it, go ahead. It's entirely possible to have a team of ultimate fighters against hordes of men.
Mount and Blade: Warband's greatest strength is the use of it's module system. This allows for VERY easy mod use, you just put your mods into 'Modules' and just open the launcher, BAM. It's there. That's all you had to do.
Warband's modding community has developed some incredible mods, mods which improve the game tenfold, mods which completely change the genre of the game, and mods which completely change the way the game is played in and out of itself. They aren't tiny mods that change 1 or 2 things, but legitmately, they are mods that are on par with other triple A titles themselves.

If you'd like a realistic game, where leadership wins, stay away. The AI is like a Zerg. They'll rush you, or take your orders a bit too literally.
However, it is a good arcade slasher in single player mode. Difficulty settings can be tampered with rather extensively, allowing you to create whatever challenge you'd like. Too hard, or too easy? Change it whenever.
Multiplayer is also a rather interesting endeavor, though it may be a bit discouraging to the newer players. To put it lightly, it is a bit tricky to get used to the much more different pace than in singleplayer.
And the mods. Dear god, there are many interesting ones out there. Starting from the general improvements that the Diplomacy mod brings (a must-have for all players playing singleplayer) to the online campaign of the cRPG mod, there is a lot of extra content just waiting to be experienced.
It is a fun game. I'd say it definitely was worth getting it. Whether you want to be a simple mercenary, or rise to the challenge of becoming king. Or maybe you want to partake in grand multiplayer battles? The choice is yours to make.

Mount and Blade: Warband is personally one of my favorite games.
Yes, despite it's obvious low-budget production, it's still one of the best games I've played, especially for those into the Action genre, but want important RTS and RPG elements.
You also gotta pay respect to the developers, Taleworlds. They didn't have much money when they started out, ( actually they almost had none ) and they started in a garage for the first game, but it slowly upgraded into this glorious masterpiece. Mount and Blade: Warband is a great game because it has a level of depth and complexity that is further developed by it's design.
The combat is one of the best things about Mount and Blade: Warband, because it promotes skill, it promotes variation, and it promotes seperate playstyles. Do you like spears, swords, or what? You can literally pick from lots of different weapons, and these weapons are just copy/paste reskins. They all have another depth to that as well. Weapons do various types of damage and effects. Blunt weapons, for example, will knock enemies out in singleplayer, allow you to sell the enemy after battle to a slave trader. So you can make some money. Piercing damage weapons allows you to penetrate armor, and cutting weapons allow you to chop light armored enemies in half. You can see on the weapon's stat page what kind of stats it has. It may be a faster, but shorter weapon, or a longer and slower weapon.
You may ask 'Why do I want a blunt weapon in multiplayer?' Well, for 1 reason, you can knock down people with it. As in, take them to the ground, where you can beat them silly.
There are also weapons that 'aren't balanced'. This means, you can stun the enemy if they decided to block you, and if your weapon is heavier.
Personally, I like the default spear. It's weak, shorter than other polearms, and not as fast as some. However, I very much enjoy the weapon because it fits my playstyle. It's a flexible weapon, one that can perform in all situations, and perform exceptionally well in open fields and against cavalry.
The multiplayer for Mount and Blade: Warband is also very good. It has the standard TDM, FFA, and all sorts of things, but it also has Duel and Siege. You can duel other players in a match of skill of the blade, or you could play in large battle sieges. Some servers allow for 64v64 player sieges, which is VERY fun to play. The sieges are exactly how you would see castle defence/offense. Archers firing down to the besiegers, crossbowmen firing up to soften the defence, infantry fighting it out on the walls in a tense close quarters melee battle, and warriors emerging from the siege towers.
The Singleplayer for Mount and Blade: Warband, is less about skill, and far more about being much, much smarter. You start off has a foreigner, with different stats and starting equipment, depending on the choices you make. You can also be a male or female, which DOES change which options you have available to you. You can start as a male noble, and have an easier start, as you will have most things you need, such as extra gold, renown ( for getting lords to recognize you ) and a banner ( for looking cool ). It's not like there isn't a challenge. You can start as a commoner female for a harder path if you want. The challenges are sexist, by the way, so don't get upset over nothing. If you still do, get out. Now. Anyways, if you are a female, you may have an alternate way of rising to power.
As a male, you do the generic stuff. You gain renown, become a vassal ( or become another... )
You court a lady you like, and battle for women and fight for their honor in tournaments.
As a female, it is much different. You can talk to lords, some may even already like you, others may insult you for being a woman. You can use this to your advantage. A woman in Calradia can manipulate the balance of power by marrying into a stronger/wealthier family and in turn, using him as a means to rise into power.
As for the other things in the singleplayer, there's many viable playstyles. You don't HAVE to participate in combat 24/7. Maybe you can if you want to. You can be a trader, who buys and sells and owns businesses throughout the land. You can be the plain old adventurer, doing quests for rewards, or you could be a slaver, knocking the enemy out, and selling them to the highest bitter. Of course, there are multiple playstyles available, as I said. My personal favorite is the 'Arena Hero/Tournament Champion' type style. I gain money from fighting in the arena to fund my troops, and I use my troops to help fight bandits, and fight deserters.
As you get further into the singleplayer, you will eventually become a vassal. You can manage fiefs, basically plot of lands, and tax them accordingly, managing the economic state of your area by helping the place out. Towns and Villages will have different types of things to do.
In towns, you will find that there is much to do. You can go to the inn, look for recruits, ask fellow travellers about things, find slavers, book merchants, and companions.
( Companions are like the player, you can customize them and level them up. )
There are also many merchants in town, where you can buy armor, weapons, mounts, and supplies.
In villages, you can recruit peasants of the faction you are at. So if you go into faction A's village, you will recruit faction A's peasants. If another faction takes over those will still be Faction A's peasants.
Also, you will need to manage morale. Being constantly defeated, being forced to surrender, leaving troops to die while you escape... Those will hurt morale. ( Low morale = Deserters )
And yes, you can be beaten. There are no checkpoints. If you fail, you must suffer the consequences of your actions. But, in Calradia you don't die. That doesn't make you special though. No one else really dies, other than the generic soldier. You and every other lord are against each other, friendly or not. Like a particular lady? Better make sure Count Gutlans doesn't sweep her off her feet first. Maybe you'll have to duel him so Gutlans won't see her again.
But let's say you get captured before you can get to Gutlans. You were defeated by bandits and captured. You didn't get to escape for a long, long time. The lady you like is now going to marry him. You've failed in your goal to marry her, and do you know why? It was your fault. Every action in Mount and Blade has a consequence, so making choices are important.
Mount and Blade: Warband's singleplayer is an open-world sandbox. If you want, you can be an adventurer all the way until there is only one kingdom left. Yup, that's perfectly fine. There is no forced objective. You, as the player, are able to decide what you want to do, and when you want to do it. And of course, how you want to do it.
Do you know if you're a top-notch fighter? Think you can take on everyone alone with your boys? If you can do it, go ahead. It's entirely possible to have a team of ultimate fighters against hordes of men.
Mount and Blade: Warband's greatest strength is the use of it's module system. This allows for VERY easy mod use, you just put your mods into 'Modules' and just open the launcher, BAM. It's there. That's all you had to do.
Warband's modding community has developed some incredible mods, mods which improve the game tenfold, mods which completely change the genre of the game, and mods which completely change the way the game is played in and out of itself. They aren't tiny mods that change 1 or 2 things, but legitmately, they are mods that are on par with other triple A titles themselves.

If you'd like a realistic game, where leadership wins, stay away. The AI is like a Zerg. They'll rush you, or take your orders a bit too literally.
However, it is a good arcade slasher in single player mode. Difficulty settings can be tampered with rather extensively, allowing you to create whatever challenge you'd like. Too hard, or too easy? Change it whenever.
Multiplayer is also a rather interesting endeavor, though it may be a bit discouraging to the newer players. To put it lightly, it is a bit tricky to get used to the much more different pace than in singleplayer.
And the mods. Dear god, there are many interesting ones out there. Starting from the general improvements that the Diplomacy mod brings (a must-have for all players playing singleplayer) to the online campaign of the cRPG mod, there is a lot of extra content just waiting to be experienced.
It is a fun game. I'd say it definitely was worth getting it. Whether you want to be a simple mercenary, or rise to the challenge of becoming king. Or maybe you want to partake in grand multiplayer battles? The choice is yours to make.

Being this is soley my opinion from playing, It's an alright game for being free, it is fun at first cause its something new but I find that at its current state of alpha its not balanced at all. It falls hard into the "PAY TO WIN" model of business which for me is a huge turn away, You earn currency to buy new weapons and upgrades for them such as (ammo types, barrels, sights, triggers, etc.) BUT I find that you earn maybe in a very good game 3-4K credits on a average game it is 1-2K. Now you can buy premium to get boost's to EXP and Credits and such but I find that if you try to be a free player you are going to be grinding a VERY long time to get anything. Average upgrade is 15-20K credits for one upgrade, the better ones are about 30-60K for an upgrade on a weapon and considering you average 1-4K credits a game....do the math. Now the "balanced" state it is in right now it's basically if you are infantry use an SMG if you fly a plane fly a bomber and if you are a tank driver, well drive a tank. Any 3 of those roles and you really can't not win and it is frustrating. Especially the fact a SMG seem's in my time played to be more accurate and more damage even at long ranges compaired to a rifle and that makes no sense. Again that is just in my experience's. To some it may hold its value but to me it just get's bland after a few days there is not a whole lot to hold my interest. It does have realistic physics with bullet drop so you do have to compensate which is very cool same with vehicle weapons. All in all check it out and find out if it is for you, the current business model and the way its balanced right now is not for my taste so I must pass on it for now.

This is taken from the script of my unpublished Call of Duty Ghosts review.
************
Call of Duty Ghosts! Don’t f*cking buy it!!
*End of review*
No, no, lets just continue.
Call of Duty Ghosts was made by a collaboration of developers, and it shows. You have Infinity Ward, Raven Software and Neversoft, whom made Tony Hawk Pro Skater and Guitar Hero. What a f*cking jump shift!
And what I mean by “and it shows”, is that is feels, *pause* Schizophrenic.
The graphics are bland and look like last gen with makeup. The gameplay hasn’t changed, same old cod... ish…
*Multiplayer*
The multiplayer is nothing exceptionally new or ground breaking, some new modes are fun but its all a big lump of grey mess, WELP I could wrap it up just there but theres more to cover (not really).
The multiplayer is made by Raven Software, and they did an “ok” job overall… yeah, continue!
New modes are added but some are more noteworthy than others, such as Cranked, Hunted and that dogtag mode that revive your teammates.
Cranked goes like this, kill an enemy a timer goes down from thirty, get another kill and it resets back to thirty again, don’t kill someone in the aforementioned thirty seconds and you explode. Hunted is a mode where you start off with a pistol and sortof have to work your way up, by collecting weapons caches. And that dogtag mode that revives your teammates goes pretty much like that, friendly down? Pick up his dogtag and he’s revived! Simple enough.
They have also added a new AI squad feature but I didn’t really care much for that, so f*ck it, another thing is a player vs bots mode survival style also put into the mix, mhm its alright.
*Graphics?*
Ok, now we can move on to the biggest aspect of this game, its awesome NextGen graphical fidelity and the LACK OF IT! Sure they’ve added new features like tessellation, a nifty subdividing technique, Nvidia Physx support apparently, godrays, but its all just, I don’t know, “meh”?!
I saw a comment that stated this perfectly. “It looks like LastGen, but with some makeup”, yupp pretty much! But the more I play the awesome title of yore, I see that they are catching up with Crysis of all games, in the looks department that is. I don’t know, they both are colourfull titles (would you believe) and features a lot of green. From a consumers standpoint it would be brushed off as looking seriously like LastGen. It doesn’t deserve that, but it is true, to a degree.
*Extinction mode*
Neversoft developed a new take on the Call of Duty Zombies, by implementing aliens instead. This is actually a fun addition. The Aliens move and feel alien like, they jump around, climb on walls and feels more in place than the whole zombie craze that the past Call of Duty games capitalized on.
*Optimization*
The game suffers from massive lag issues on the PC, both netcode issues and optimization issues. Totalbiscuit talked about the poor performance on two F*cking Titans! He had to disable MultiGPU for the game to run better, but even then it ran like crap.
By looking online I found some fixes to the performance. CTRL+Alt+Delete, goto Task Manager and set the games priority to Normal instead of High. Now the game will run better, but not as smooth as it should. In said Task Manager you will also find the game only using about 2Gb or RAM! The requirements for the game to run, to actually launch, you need 6Gb of RAM! WTF?!
Not only that but to fix the high ping issues, I had to configure the games config file. SHOULD NOT HAVE TO!!!
But, I digress, as I play this game more and more, it does start to become enjoyable. Granted I had to crank up the FOV to 80 or more so I wouldn’t’ suffer from headaches and motion sickness. There’s now an FOV slider, not in the game originally, but its there now. Only goes up to 80 though.
*Wrapping up*
Score wise, it is a 7 out of 10, just because the game grew on me and I found some modes fun to play. But it’s not worth the full 60 Euros on steam, or $60 if you’re fat and stupid. Its probably better on consoles, but since I mostly play on my AWESOME GAMING RIG, I had some issues (some, haha), but with them gone, it’s actually a fun game, *pause* overall.
Oh and if you’re wondering how its singleplayer goes? Hhaaha, don’t even…
************
Luckily, most if not all issues has been adressed in the next title; Advanced Warfare. All but the dedicated servers...

**Dont be fooled by my game hours, I was playing H&G way before it came out on Steam.**
First off H&G takess a whole new approach to modern WW2 gaming. In H&G not only can you fight the war among the infantry but you can eventualy drive armor and also pilot aircraft (granted the aircraft gameplay is still lacking alot).
As for graphics and ground action I rate H&G at a solid 9 Graphically and 8 FPS Gameplay.
The gameplay on the ground whether in a tank or on foot is amazing. If your looking for the feel of ww2 - running into battle from tree trunk to tree trunk or covering open fields with you squad (all human players) then this is for you.
At the same time you can still take on the challanging role of the lone wolf sniper prowling from the forest or hill top picking off targets. The game can be played effectively however you appraoch it.
Also, H&G offers a unique look at the Generals aspect of the war. When your not in cambat you can view a map of Europe that shows exactly how the war is going on either side. From this map you can move units to specific locations where players (Heroes) will fight as your units.
Overall I give H&G a 8.5 and look foward to future updates! Hope you enjoyed!

Call of Duty: Black Ops II was a refreshing splash of new in a stale and stagnant series. A near-future setting, futuristic weapons, decent maps and a fun and interesting Pick 10 system combined to create a game that I lost over a hundred hours in. Something that absolutely made this experience is that Black Ops II's PC port was handled MARVELOUSLY. Treyarch did an excellent job of porting it, with an FOV slider up to 90 FOV, decent-good textures, and tight controls.
Call of Duty: Ghosts, is objectively inferior in a number of ways. The FOV is hardlocked at 65,  menus are insanely slow, people are having trouble running the game at 60 on a GTX TITAN, they've removed Theatre Mode, and, most important of all, the game feels absolutely horrible. In BO2, if you were being shot at, you had a chance to turn around, or outmaneuver your opponent, and shoot back to get a fair fight. In Ghosts, you are downed almost immediately after your opponent starts firing.
Throughout all this, Ghosts still manages to have SOME decent ideas. The gun sounds are just as good as in Black Ops II, the maps are the biggest in the series (for better or worse), and there are some interesting gamemodes that help shake things up.
For the love of Zeus, do not buy this game. I thought that the PC port would be decent-good; but this port is honestly WORSE than Modern Warfare 3's. In fact, when Black Ops II goes on sale for thirty dollars, you go ahead and buy it. Seriously, it's a good game. If you ever do get it, send me a message. I'll play some games with you and try to get the shame of spending sixty dollars on this absolute trash. Don't make the same mistake I did.

Great game! Spend endless hours exploring and adventuring over the war-torn world of Calradia. Choose to join a faction, become a mercenary, or unite the land under one banner, Your banner. Though at times it may seem tedious, or even hard, being able to mout the fastest horse and wear the best armour  to tank through the enemy ranks is one of the greatest glories of gaming.
Multiplayer in this game is... interesting to say the least. Band together with other soldiers in "Battle", "Team deathmatch", and "Seige" modes to crush your enemy into a pulp. If being a lone wolf is your thing, "Deathmatch" mode gives you the opportunity to show your melee skills (Darn archers) as the greatest there is. However, be ye warned! The multiplayer community is not for those with quick temper or weak constitution; this is because, in short, the majority of players you will meet are rude and will insult you for nearly anything. Racism abounds here.
The Napoleonic Wars DLC is, in a word, wonderful. This expansion is solely multiplayer, which is rather disappointing, but makes up for it in its vibrant community. Choose from five different factions each with historical units that fought during the age of Napoleon's conquests. The game modes are the same as Native, but the battles are truley a sight to behold. Able to support over two-hundred real time players, soldiers can coordinate attacks and defenses to foil the plans of the opposing team.
I heartily recommend that joining a Regiment brings out the full potential of this DLC. A regiment is a group of players that fight together as a team, oftentimes communicating through teamspeak programs. Playing in a regiment has been one of the best experiences in this game for me, and a great host of others.
Mods for this game are many; some good, others not so good. I have to say I have two favorites, one singleplayer and the other multiplayer. "1257 AD" is a great sp mod, overhauling the world map to that of Europe. There are many more nations to join than Native, and a larger selection of units. The best MP mod (In my opinion at least!) is North and South, which transforms the Napoleonic Dlc into that of the American Civil War. There are many, many more mods, but I have not the space here to catalog them all, so go out there and look for them!
All in all, I give this game a 7/10 for the Sp experience, and a 8/10 for Mp.

Easily one of my favorite games of all time.
Most other games this age are already down to $20, however the singleplayer is a lot longer than most other action/shooter games, making it well worth the price.
Amazing singleplayer. Capturing outposts is probably the best part. There are over 30 spread over the massive map. The main story has some pretty good action too. Plus there is hunting, racing, and assassination side missions and a lot of other things that are a lot of fun.
Co-op has some serious issues. When the match tries to launch it almost always crashes or freezes when loading. Due to this you wont be able to find players unless you are playing with friends. When it works it is decent but doesnt have the openness that makes far cry great. Update: co-op has been working better lately.
The multiplayer is actually pretty good, but a little generic. Doesn't have enough players to reach its full potential though.
Both the co-op and multiplayer are pretty basic, but the singleplayer makes up for it. You of course have the story and outposts, but there is also tons of ruins and caves to be explored for relics and loot, side missions, trials, races, dlc missions, and even knife throwing and poker.
An average playthrough of the singleplayer will take you roughly 30 hours, doing the main storyline capturing all the outposts and doing most of the side missions.
The story really tries to be great and in some ways it is but also is a little flat. You and your friends are having the time of your life until getting caught by slavers on a remote island. You escape and have to save your friends and liberate the natives from the pirates in the process.
Very good, open gameplay. Most situations you can choose to attack however you like. Climb any mountain for a good vantage point with a sniper rifle, use stealth with a bow and using knife takedowns, attack head on with an lmg, or charge in with a truck with c4 planted on it.
The co-op and multiplayer are pretty fun with friends but doesnt have a lot of substance.
Good graphics, very good considering the scale of the game.
Maybe not as smooth walking around a small area and shooting a few people as call of duty, but all in all the physics are a lot better than just about any other game. Driving really feels good. Good fire physics, you can light large areas of brush with a flamethrower.
Works good for the most part. Can easily play it on max setting with my laptop, core i7 4810mq @ 2.80 GHz (turbo to 3.80 GHz) 12gbs ram and gtx870m 3gbs dedicated. Haven't had any notable issues or bugs.
Sound is good but maybe a little rough here and there.
Nothing majorly wrong with it but it does have the usual trees growing through rocks and animals spawning inside stuff.
The vast landscape gives you a good immersive feel but could be better if they didn't have so much of the same plants making it all feel the same.
Objectives are pretty basic. Pretty much go fight through these people and do (insert objective here). Some are a little more in depth.
No problems with knowing where to go or what to do. The story line is linear and very easy to follow.
Unparalleled world. Massive world with large mountains, caves, ruins, shanty towns, vast foliage, ocean, and tons of wildlife to try and kill you. Although most of the landscape has the same trees and plants so a lot of it looks the same.
The characters are interesting. The antagonists really make you want to kill them. All the characters are just a little thin but still good.
The menus are pretty poor. Pulling up your map is really slow. All other menus are in the escape menu which is pretty slow and not that great to navigate. Plus there's Uplay which is horrible.
Mostly standard controls. Not my favorite layout but close enough I didn't feel the need to change anything.
As much freedom as you could ask for. You can ignor your current mission to go off capturing outpost, doing side mission, or just go for a nature hike.
The story itself is very linear. Only choice in the game is the ending and what happens after.
Four difficulty setting so good for most any skill level. Average control options.
Sometimes feels like they resticked what you can do at the beginning instead of allowing you to do more later on.
Has plenty of weapons. Handguns, SMGs, assault rifles, shotguns, LMGs, sniper rifles, launchers, explosives, and specials. Over 30 total, though some feel similar.
Most weapons can be modded. Higher level guns can have up to 3 mods. Mods incude extended mags, silencers, and several types of sights, though most guns are limited on which mods are available. Almost all weapons can be painted.
For the most part the ai is fairly intelegent. Considering what they have to do in an open world unrelated to a story, it's very good. Though this causes a few quirks.
Only came out at the end of 2012 and there isn't any notable aging to the game. Not lacking anything that newer games might have.
The story doesnt give incentive replay it, but since you can whatever you like however you like, the rest of the game has a lot of replay value.
For such a long game the balance between length and action is very good. You can go straight to the next mission, rush through a few outposts, or take your time doing everything at your own pace.
If you were to just walk up with an assault rifle everytime it would probably get very repetitive, but change up your approach everytime and it won't be much at all.
It has some good aspects and a few poor ones when it comes to how realistic it is. Even compared to other games the amount of people you are able to kill is a little ridiculous. It has some supernatural elements which isn't bad but they are a little lame and seem to be inspired by acid trips. Other than that it's actually got good physics and overall better than most games.
The downloadable content is all pretty mediocre. A few independent short story missions that are okay, some co-op and multiplayer content, and a few other things that are all insignificant.
50 achievements but only on Uplay not Steam, and 6 are for co-op making them near impossible. The rest of the achievements are great. Good amount and some challenging but nothing too hard.
Doesn't have Steam badges/trading cards.
Far Cry 2 was a good game, however has aged a lot and lacked in a few aspects. Far Cry 3 did a great job at improving and made a very well rounded, good performing game.
Bottom line is that no other game is very much like Far Cry. Maybe slightly similar to games like Just Cause or some RPGs and it may have some Tomb Raider elements but not enough that its overall gameplay is at all the same as anything else.

Great game! Spend endless hours exploring and adventuring over the war-torn world of Calradia. Choose to join a faction, become a mercenary, or unite the land under one banner, Your banner. Though at times it may seem tedious, or even hard, being able to mout the fastest horse and wear the best armour  to tank through the enemy ranks is one of the greatest glories of gaming.
Multiplayer in this game is... interesting to say the least. Band together with other soldiers in "Battle", "Team deathmatch", and "Seige" modes to crush your enemy into a pulp. If being a lone wolf is your thing, "Deathmatch" mode gives you the opportunity to show your melee skills (Darn archers) as the greatest there is. However, be ye warned! The multiplayer community is not for those with quick temper or weak constitution; this is because, in short, the majority of players you will meet are rude and will insult you for nearly anything. Racism abounds here.
The Napoleonic Wars DLC is, in a word, wonderful. This expansion is solely multiplayer, which is rather disappointing, but makes up for it in its vibrant community. Choose from five different factions each with historical units that fought during the age of Napoleon's conquests. The game modes are the same as Native, but the battles are truley a sight to behold. Able to support over two-hundred real time players, soldiers can coordinate attacks and defenses to foil the plans of the opposing team.
I heartily recommend that joining a Regiment brings out the full potential of this DLC. A regiment is a group of players that fight together as a team, oftentimes communicating through teamspeak programs. Playing in a regiment has been one of the best experiences in this game for me, and a great host of others.
Mods for this game are many; some good, others not so good. I have to say I have two favorites, one singleplayer and the other multiplayer. "1257 AD" is a great sp mod, overhauling the world map to that of Europe. There are many more nations to join than Native, and a larger selection of units. The best MP mod (In my opinion at least!) is North and South, which transforms the Napoleonic Dlc into that of the American Civil War. There are many, many more mods, but I have not the space here to catalog them all, so go out there and look for them!
All in all, I give this game a 7/10 for the Sp experience, and a 8/10 for Mp.

After two years of off and on playing, only to completely start over a month ago, I've finally beat Far Cry 3. First off I have to say that Ubisoft deserves yet another round of applause for yet another amazing game. From beginning to end, I was ♥♥♥♥ing hooked. This game has everything, amazing albeit over the top story, game play is fluid and extremely entertaining, the map is relatively huge and freedom to roam it is unhindered, and probably my favorite part is the characters... both protagonist and antagonists are so well played that they can make you love and hate them with deep passion.
As for the story, as I said, it's over the top believing that bratty college kids could learn to adapt to a survival situation so quickly, with the added fact that both north and south Rook Island is chalk full of dangers. Literally even the birds want to kill you. But the metamorphosis from wimpy kid to full blown Rakyat warrior is amazing and fun nonetheless. With the range of weapons, any play style can be found and is throughly enjoyable. Personally my favorite is the recurve bow and the knife, nothing like scouting out a camp, taking out the snipers with the bow then sinking your knife into every guard you come across (only to have the Rakyat come in afterwards and proclaim "who's the man! Me!"... blow it out your♥♥♥♥♥pal...).
Game play is very fluid and easy to get into, the hardest part is mastering timing jumps (especially when climbing a tower to unlock a section of map, or trying to do the "death from above" takedown only to land inches away from the target and be met with gunfire to your face). Crafting upgrades via animal skin is both a welcoming experience but quickly becomes tedious. Especially when you have to collect shark skins and get attacked from behind while collecting. And those god damned komodo dragons...
The map is pretty huge and it's northern section is completely unlocked, but to make it visible from the map you have to climb several towers and remove a blocking device that Vaas and Hoyts guys have placed at the top to... I guess block communication? Either way, that's always a fun task and is rewarded with a section of map being revealed and a gun being unlocked for free at local stores. There's also dozens of side missions you can partake in, some of which are linked online (which is dead right now) in the form of leader boards. Missions aside, there are also tons of little caves and stuff to explore both on the surface, underground, and under water.
And finally, the characters is what sold the game for me. Right off you meet your first long running enemy, Vaas Montenegro. He's a slim, slightly unopposing guy visually but the way he talks and carries himself (which apparently is mostly represented by the guy who plays him in real life) sells the character. And he is BAT♥♥♥♥♥♥INSANE!! You go through three quarters of the game escaping him, getting "killed" by him, and trying to kill him. Each and every encounter with him is easily remembered cause the guy is just that awesome. He's the kind of enemy you literally love to hate. And killing him (not really a spoiler as its obvious if you beat the game) was immensely satisfyingly... but I felt sad because he quickly became one of my favorite video game characters of all time. I won't go into great detail of the main villian, Hoyt, as his character is talked about very little up until the last quarter, you just know he's pulling the strings, but that last quarter makes you really hate the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of him and the "boss fight" was very pleasing. The main character of the game, Jason Brody is also a really likeable character. He's your average rich kid, fresh from college. He's cocky, adventurous, and basically lives a charmed life up until he and his friends get captured when they skydive onto Rook Island. You spend the entire game learning to survive, kill or be killed, getting help from the natives, all while searching for your friends. Jason's transformation from rich kid trying to save his friends to bad♥♥♥♥♥warrior is one of the best stories I've ever had the pleasure to partake in.
All in all the game is amazing, all of the aforementioned plus amazing music and comical quotes during game play from the characters definitely puts this in my top 10 best games of all time.
In summary:
Game play - 9/10
Story - 10/10
Learning Curve - 9/10
Replayability - 4/10
Addendum - Replayability set at 4 out of 10 because once you beat the game, and it's amazing story, the side missions seem trivial.
EPic

All in all it's a solid shooter with terrible balance problems, bad servers and a punishing f2p credit system.

Saying this, I feel that saying 'thank you' for this great system makes me feel at home to a realistic world war two game. Not every solidier is going to have a anti-tank gun. Not every solidier is going to have a MP40 or Browning Machine Gun. This game replicates the real tactical load outs of german and american units from real life. Majority of men in the western front during world war two of germany had Gewhers or K98ks, while the MP40 for was officers only. Only SS units carrying StGs 44s at the time. Same goes for american units who have M1 Garands and grease guns compared to Thompson.
Overall, I think the pay system in this game has a great impact on gameplay, allowing for a realistic feel for players like myself.

Played with an I5-3570K, 8GB DDR3 and GTX660 2GB DDR5.
Realising it is still in Beta AND free to play.
Pros:
It is a really nice game. It combines large scale warfare with infantry, tanks and aircraft into big and compact maps. The surroundings are great, you got your large cities, small farms, bushes, trees, everything for anyone. Next to that, you can choose from several branches of the militairy (either US or German). The General aspect of the game is nice as well, you win some, you get great pay, you lose? You need to rebuy the loses. Just like in real life. Battles are easy once you get ridd of the waiting line. Capturing points is nicely done, stick to the radio, not 100 metres from it. The idea you get a salary, based on your level, is a nice touch as well. Even if you have a really hard time, you still get something for simply finishing the battle. Aiming and walking around, using a tank or aircraft, seems to be working fine. Could use a little tweaking, but works good as far as i could test and see. Guns are realistic, you cant grab your SMG and shoot 500 meters accurate. Guns look great, animations are nice and sound seems to be ok. Skill is also needed to do things, aiming takes skill, taking a carefull shot takes skill, capping points without being seen requires skill. Its not a rampaging run around shooter, which i like.
Cons: (considering its a beta)
The game lacks a decent (basic) chat system. Switching channels does not work and voice chat seems to either not work or is extremly lagging. Sometimes chat does not work at all. Everything, from upgrading to switching classes, costs a lot of money and since there is no way to "test" your purchase or switching a branche, you are doubting a lot if you should purchase or switch. The tutorial lacks "explaining" why you should do certain things or why not. (adding to that, there is a bunch of text and pictures online, but some of us want a interactive tutorial). It seems that Pay to Win (P2W) is also a big part of the game, as getting upgrade the normal way, cost a lot of money. And 1 thing about the grenade throwing system.. This part, could be totally me.. But i dont want to hold down my mouse for 2/3 seconds to toss a grenade, sometimes i just want to drop and run.. 1 Simple click, not a whole cooking time everytime i want to do a quick nade in a room.
Things i would like to see in the future:
A decent chat system. Chat to all, chat to team, chat to squad. Simple.. And a voicechat would be great as well. More guns with diffrent modifications. More servers for less waiting and lagg. An interactive tutorial to explain all aspects of the game, take us through all the branches of the militairy, there specialties, pro's and cons of the branche and ofcourse, how to become a good player. Switch currency system, it is just too expensive to get basics like AT gear. Keep the "real" goodies up in price, but make the basic guns a bit more cheaper.
To sum things up:
If you are trigger happy, and want to play a realistic shooter, in a WW2 theme, and dont mind waiting for a server every once in a while. Go ahead and get it. Understand it is a Beta. But.. It is free to play. If the game is completly polished, it would be a great game i would pay actual money for.

I really enjoyed this game on the PS3.  I was really excited to see it on a steam sale and purchased it.  The first problem I ran into was the UPLAY crash.  When I would click on Far Cry 3 on my games list, it would boot to the UPLAY, crash and not allow me to play the game.
I did find a work around for this problem.  The work around that worked for me is to:
Right Click on Far Cry 3 in your games list, go to properties, then click on Browse Local Content, then right click on the  Far Cry 3 exe file and Run as Administrator (C:\Program Files\Steam\SteamApps\common\Far Cry 3\bin).  Then, UPLAY opened up successfully.
I personally think that you should be able to play the game without the UPLAY junk interferring with the experience.  The game itself I recommend highly, but, the UPLAY crap needs to be fixed pronto.

One of my favorite games of all time.  However, there are some very major flaws which really ruin the experience.  As many others have mentioned you need Uplay to run this game which is total bull****.  Although its gotten better since the game was released, Uplay frequently needs to update forcing you to wait 5 minutes every time you launch the game.  This platform is absolute garbage.  Unfortunately, I don't see this going away for FC4.
The game also frequently disconnects from the UPlay server so if you need to access your skills and crafting and it will try to reconnect every time you access the menu forcing you to sit and wait for 30 seconds until it times out.  Some really weird in-game glitches too.  Many saving and loading issues causing you to lose progress.  In game map acts weird and will sometime not allow you to scroll around.  I started a game on Master (Very Hard) and a number of times the game would just reset it back to default Medium difficulty (which is waaay too easy).  Weird FOV which reduces during cutscenes, flying and driving.
All of these issues only really become an annoyance much later in the game though and don't really matter too much because the gameplay is absolutely amazing.  Conquering enemy bases without being spotted is absolutely the funnest part of the game.  I smile every time when I stab an enemy in the back and then take his knife and throw it at the guy that's standing nearby.  The game gives you the option of resetting the enemy bases once you've conquered all of them and re-doing everything with all of your skills (sort of like NewGame+) which I also strongly recommend.
Your character is a totaly lame dudebro and I wish you had the option to shoot all his friends in the face instead of having to rescue them.  Unskippable cutscenes are really a pain at times.  That being said, this game does have a few really memorable characters and best antagonists I've seen in a long time.
MP and CO-OP feel tacked on.  CO-OP is an on rails shooter separate from the main free roam game.  They really missed the opportunity to make this game amazing by allowing you to free roam with a friend.  I guess they are making up for this in FC4.  MP is fun for 5 minutes but nothing really exceptional.
All in all, I would recommend this game to anyone.  Strongly recommend that you pick this up and play it before FC4.

Imagine a hybrid of Medieval: Total War and Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, and then throw in massive sandbox and RPG elements into the mix. In Warband you take the role of.. well, honestly, whomever you want to be.
Do you want to gather up your army and roll around the map killing bandits or burninating the peasants? Or would you rather pledge yourself to one of the many kingdoms and become a lord?
Maybe you'd prefer to aid one of the pretenders onto the throne in a grand coup, or even go entirely independant and forge your own glorious empire?
All of this and more is possible in warband, but the really interesting thing is how the game actually plays. Initially you cruise around a campaign map, in the style of older RPGs. However, when you enter a battle, the fun begins. Yes, you have your own army, and you can give them tactical orders, much like Total War. The unique thing here is that you don't take the role of some sort of omnipotent flying general; you are in the battle itself, in a 1st person perspective.
Combat itself is fairly satisfying- attacks are made by left clicking, with the direction of the swing determined by your mouse movement. Likewise, parrying is directional, and requires fairly precise timing. Enemies can be caught offguard with a swift kick, but bear in mind that this will also leave you vulnerable for a short time. Advanced players can also feint, changing the direction of the swing at the last second.
However, it isn't all hitting peasants with swords. The variety of weapons available is massive and includes: swords, axes, clubs, warhammers, knives, halbards, polearms, spears, lances, javelins, bows, crossbows, throwing knives, throwing axes, and more. Of all the different combat styles, I found lancing and horse archery the most satisfying. Lancing as heavy cavalry is huge fun- get up some speed and charge at a knot of infantry and you become and unstoppable juggernaut, skewering foes like so many kebabs. Horse archery is probably the most difficult playstyle, but also the most rewarding- travelling at speed on a horse affects different weapons signifcantly- it'll impart momentum to melee swings, allowing you to lop off heads with axes as you charge, and projectiles will also inherit your velocity. As such, arrows won't go where you expect them to, until you get used it it.
Graphically, the game isn't brilliant, but it's functional. There are numerous graphics enhancing mods around that help with this. Speaking of the mods, the modding scene for this is fairly massive, and there are some mods and modpacks around that really change the game. The best of these is probably the Floris pack, however, I've had issues running it with the steam version.
tl;dr: very much worth buying, but only if you're prepared to sink a lot of time into it

So, this game is pretty fun. Don't have much experience in it, but I suppose I can at least tell some new/curious players what the start of the game is like. In the start, you're gonna have just some standard infantry battles. Rifleman versus Rifleman in three-point capture-and-hold maps. Nothing too serious.
Once you reach a certain rank, you'll be given access to the rest of the game (so to speak). This includes the opportunity for larger conflicts that copy straight from Frontlines: Fuel of War's style of point-to-point capture system, while also retaining the ability to have smaller "skirmishes" with just rifleman. Pretty nice selection to choose from, I won't deny that.
Here's the problem, however: If you play as the Americans, you automatically lose. German armor, infantry, and aircraft are all superior at this point in the game's development. In those big matches I talked about? You'll generally be a standard rifleman, wielding an M1 Garand and going up against things like Panzer I's and Panzer 38t's. No anti-tank weapons for you, except for a single panzerfaust that is in the base spawning location. Germans seem to love abusing their armor. They get more of it, more often, and Americans seem to get nothing but infantry.
On top of this, I've noticed that their airforce is pretty sub-par as well. They get the P-38 Lightning, which is a great aircraft... but it was not designed as a fighter-bomber. You can get outflown and outgunned by the BF-109 E-3 model that the Germans currently get, and they'll shoot you down in a matter of seconds. In exchange, the P-38 has one extra bomb to use before it has to reload. Not really worth it, if they can just keep you grounded.
What's worse, is the fact that the American's ground infantry is even worse than the German. The Germans get a Machinepistol early on that can easily shred any infantry it comes across, and their standard rifle (Gewehr 43) seems to have a faster fire-rate and more accuracy than the M1 Garand.
So... yeah. My review for this game? Great idea, horrible balancing, and terribly easy to see that they went for the Pay-to-win moral of "pay us, and we'll unlock weapons for you that give you a huge advantage". Would be an excellent game if they skipped over paying "gold" for better equipment.

Far Cry 3 is a good game. Is it a great one? No, not really.
Far Cry 3 is a solid open world shooter, very solid. Gunplay is satisfying and rewarding, the combat is challenging at times, and it can support a variety of play styles. I spent time equally as a bow wielding, back stabbing ninja, long range sniper, and run and gun rambo type and all worked very well. The island is beautiful and great to explore, its truly a fantastic setting for the game. The upgrade system for both your own skills and weapons is nicely done and I felt a good sense of progression.
The game is very repetive however outside of the main story line. Find and enemy base, clean them out, move onto the next one. Climb a tower (jumping puzzle), rip out a circut board, move on to the next. Outside of the main storyline the game is very dull and repetitive, mostly. The animal hunts were interesting, and some of the challenges were engaging, but in the context of the overall game outside the main story there was little to do. As with many of these games I largely ignored the main story line for quite some time, exploring and leveling up and while the locales were beautiful, I was doing the same thing all the time.
The mainstory line, while it does give you some interesting missions (burning the fields remains one of my favorite missions in any game) the story that holds the entire game's plot together is largely nonsense. The only explanation by the middle of the second act is that the PC is an immortal godlike figure. The game also Peters out by the end of the second act and staggers into a make work third act after all the emotional tension and drive is yanked from the story.
As a final bit of insult, all the Boss kills are trippy and supremely unrewarding QTE's.
If you can pick this game up for cheap do it. The island is beautiful and fun to indulge in for a while.

The game is like Skyrim but with guns and alot more stability and a slightly, SLIGHTLY more believable vainlla story. The biggest thing this game has going for it is the freedom of choice in most areas regarding how to tackle an objective as well as some suprisingly well done story sequences which truly breathe some life into the supporting characters. While the entire idea of "a weak willed American boy comes to the mysterious island nation, gets tatoos and is suddenly superman" seems about as far fetched as the entire premise of skyrim, the supporting characters are all very believable and work wonders towards helping the player ignore the badly casted voice of the main characer.
One of the downfalls of the game, again much like Skyrim, is that once you understand the core mechanics and systems, the overall challenge and replayability of the game fades away quickly. At it's core, FarCry is a game that likes to hold your hand and make things even easier than they need to be with target marking to let you see through walls and a near infinite supply of med kits if you learn how to craft for yourself.
All that aside, the world of the game is well realized and quite entertaining for romping around and causing destruction.

A decent FPS by today's standards. The story is fairly linear, to say the least. The much publicized antagonist Vaas isn't actually showcased that much, only appearing in a few cutscenes before being long forgotten by the second half of the game. Not really a bad thing, since this gives way for further delving into new scenery when the game later branches out into another part, allowing for different new enemies and paving the way for other interesting characters.
The open world of Rook Island is a large place to explore, though it's mostly repetitive in environment and landscape, even on the South Island. On a good note, the world is realistically put together and scaled in size. Possibly, it may very well be just as large as a real-life tropical island. Collectibles are spread across the entire islands, but the myriad of treasure chests scattered literally everywhere you go can be a game-breaker, and slight annoyance. With so many laying about, I could say the game is literally throwing money at you till the point where it is common to run out of things to buy at the store, leaving you full of unused cash and having to tolerate the incessant "Your wallet is full" messages that will be popping up constantly. But a minor downsight to the game nonetheless.

For gameplay: the enemy AI is rather impressive and well-done, with reactionary actions like knowing when to take cover and losing sight of you. They can also be pretty dumb at times, whether acting logically or not.
Weapons are, unfortunately, quite unbalanced, where the simple order of having guns later in the game being in every way superior to the earlier guns. This makes your choice of weapons pretty much straightforward. I'd rather prefer the wep stats spread out across the chart to give more chances for decision-making but that's my take.
Some weps...or gear, are pretty useless as well, such as the repair tool that was so useful in Far Cry 2 has become a complete unnecessity and "specials" like the bow and flamethrower don't really have much benefits apart from being unique. The bow, especially, is essentially a pointless waste, given a silenced sniper rifle already does the same job better. Seriously, why does everyone love the bow as much? There's
greater about it.
Overall the game is pretty much a stripped down version of its predecessor, improving in some ways, lacking in others;
with its silly implementations like being able to heal yourself literally anywhere with a magical green syringe, enemies being marked for you and loot chests and plant herbs lying everywhere you go.
Ubisoft clearly "casualized" it for the masses, removing the hardcore features from its predecessors while at least retaining its core features. This, at the cost of the game being too easy in comparison.
And so the verdict... this game mostly great in quality, despite poor game design choices dragging it down, I'd say it's still worth the play.

This is the game I've always wanted without knowing it existed. The perfect combination of RPG and strategy. Leading a faction, but still being the actual person and not some godly personification of a nation. You can't just control all your armies and cities, you are like an actual medieval Lord - you have to trust some of the tasks on your vassals and friends. And the battles are fun! RPGs are mostly incapable of simulating real battles, while strategy games cannot give you the perspective of the individual soldier in the army. M&B gives you both - and it's incredibly fun to dash into battle leading an army of knights with your sword drawn and a battle cry on the lips. The graphics are not amazing, but the light effects make for really great battle scenes. Also the database concept lacks a few features (separation of title and name etc.), but it's still a fun feudal simulator.

1. oyun efsaneydi. Ama 2. oyunda yapımcı değişmişti, fikir güzeldi ama oyun kanser edici derecedeydi. Resmen fenalık geçirtmişti. Bir FPS oyununu yarıda bırakıp sildiğimi hatırlamam ama FC2'yi silmiştim. Bu yüzden Farcry 3'e şüphe ile yaklaştım uzunca zaman. En sonunda Steam'in yaz indirimlerinde o kadar ucuzlamışken bir şans vereyim dedim ve aldım. ama içimdeki şüpheler devam ettiği için aylarca kurmadım bile. Sonunda oyunu kurdum ve oynadım, sonuç mu? Bu oyun olmuşş... Bazı sahneler var ki sırf o ortama girmek o sahneyi görmek için bile alınır oyun.
Bir kere yaşayan ada olayını bu sefer becermişler. Hikaye de 2. oyundakinin aksine gayet ne olduğu belli olarak ilerliyor. Bir çok plot twist var hikaye de ama hikayeden kopmuyorsunuz. İkinci oyunda en büyük eksikliklerden birisi buydu bence. Hikaye içine çekemiyordu. Senarist kafasında güzel bir hikaye kurmuş ama yazıya dökerken bunu becerememiş gibi bir hal vardı.
Silah çeşidi biraz daha fazla olabilir miş ama yine de gayet yeterli idi. Yay ile oynamak cidden zevkli oluyor. Bıçak komboları da çok iyi düşünülmüş ve uygulanmış bir sistemdi. Gizlilik çok iyi kotarılmış. Mekanlar ve manzaralar 10 numara. Özellikle yer altında geçen birkaç bölüm var ki efsane.
Ana karakterin seslendirilmiş olması hoşum gitti. Karakterin yaşadıkları ile birlikte kişiliğinin değişimi, olaylara verdiği tepkiler, kendikendine konuşmaları vs çok yerinde ve kaliteli olmuş. Hikayedeki yan karakterler de gayet başarılı.
Aksiyon ve düşman çeşitliliği de yeterli seviyede. Düşmanların yapay zekaları da gayet başarılı sayılır.
Grafik kalitesi zaten çok iyi.
Oyun hertürlü parasını hak eden bir oyun.
10 üzaerinden 8.5 veriyorum ben.
0.5 puanı bir çok önemli sahneyi oyun çıkmadan önce fragmanlarda gösterip heyecanı çalan yapımcılardan dolayı kırıyorum. 1 puan da bir oyunun efsane olmasına sebebiyet verecek olan o sihirli dokunuş, kendini diğer oyunlardan ayıran o farklılığın olmamasından kırıyorum.

This game has some really good elements, but it has some significant up-front issues they need to sort out. First, the multiplayer is still quite buggy. Server issues, as well as client issues. These aren't so much gameplay issues as they are issues with getting the client started (why does it start in windowed mode half the time, full screen the other half the time? why does it get stuck in a loop when trying to join a campaign?), and the most major issue - the long time it takes to sit in a queue to get into a game.
The game is still pretty new, so they really should have more slots for new players (Tier 1) to allow people to get in the game and build up to Tier 2. But it takes 15-20 minutes to get into a slot if you are a new player just trying out the game.
That's not an ideal experience to create if you are trying to get people interested in your new game. If they fix that, this will be a lot better. I still recommend it, despite the flaws, but I hope they fix these problems.

H&G is a fun,
, WWII first person shooter, with a little hint of real time strategy. I have been playing for quite a while, and have seen many changes, most of them for the better…
Yes, you can spend real money in the game to advance yourself quickly. As I see it though, this is how they make money on a free game, and I do not believe the advancements drastically alter the individual’s gameplay experience.
on anything in-game and find no need to. Yes, it does take some time to expand your characters horizons, but I have enjoyed every minute of it. This game is
for those individuals who do not want to put in the effort of playing toward, what sometimes can be, distant goals.
Graphically the game is far from being a Frostbite engine game (i.e. Battlefield, Mirror’s Edge), but even as a staunch advocate of good graphics, I have found myself still enjoying it. Of course, there are some odd visuals sometimes, but they have made radical improvements thus far, and I am eager to see what comes next.
Because you are literally conquering Europe, one city at a time, I can easily see them expanding to new factions, making a plethora of new maps (one for each battle), and adding a ton of new vehicles and weapons. Based on how they have set this up, they could be expanding this game for years to come!
I have not invested too much time or effort into the RTS (or Generals) part of the game, but it is largely simplistic. Eventually you can afford “armies” which are the equivalent of “lives” or “spawns” in the FPS part of the game. Therefore, if I move a mobile infantry army to a battlefield, and join that battle (the FPS game), my team will now be able to use my mobile infantry jeeps/trucks. If your team fails to supply these resources to your team, it can be a catastrophe on the battlefield.
One of my biggest annoyances about H&G is the abundance of ignorance on the battlefield. The American side, of which I only play, seems to have quite a lot of noobs. Sadly, this is partially the fault of the developers; due to the lack of instruction/clarity…much has to be learned on your own (this is getting better though). For the most part, the German side seems to be filled with veterans, they know how to work as a team, they know where to be and when, and they seem to have each other’s backs. This is proven time & time again on the battlefield. Very often, the Americans loose the war. This only adds to the poor morale of the American side, and hikes the morale of the German side. Either the Americans drop the game for a while, or they switch to the German side. So then the Americans see an influx of noobs, and the Germans, with high morale, eagerly feed real cash into the game, making it even harder for the Americans to catch up.

I'll be honest and admit I really disliked much (but not all) the story and most of the characters, but I am still able to enjoy the game because the gameplay is really good. It's just fun game to play. I liked the climbing radio towers to unlock parts of the map and capturing outpost mechanics and I enjoyed the leveling/perk and crafting systems. It's just so much fun to grab a few weapons, jump in a vehicle and go massacre the closest enemy garrison and capture their outpost.
The game doesn't seem to try to force you into a certain combat style, either. You can pick off enemies one by one from long range with a sniper rifle (or a bow), sneak around on foot and do the same with melee weapons, run in guns blazing and just blow everyone away with sheer firepower (although this probably isn't most wise option) or use a combination of all three to accomplish your goals. The variety of weapons is wide, they are all fun to use and, if I remember correctly, they are all moddable (with the exception of some unique variants).

H&G is a fun,
, WWII first person shooter, with a little hint of real time strategy. I have been playing for quite a while, and have seen many changes, most of them for the better…
Yes, you can spend real money in the game to advance yourself quickly. As I see it though, this is how they make money on a free game, and I do not believe the advancements drastically alter the individual’s gameplay experience.
on anything in-game and find no need to. Yes, it does take some time to expand your characters horizons, but I have enjoyed every minute of it. This game is
for those individuals who do not want to put in the effort of playing toward, what sometimes can be, distant goals.
Graphically the game is far from being a Frostbite engine game (i.e. Battlefield, Mirror’s Edge), but even as a staunch advocate of good graphics, I have found myself still enjoying it. Of course, there are some odd visuals sometimes, but they have made radical improvements thus far, and I am eager to see what comes next.
Because you are literally conquering Europe, one city at a time, I can easily see them expanding to new factions, making a plethora of new maps (one for each battle), and adding a ton of new vehicles and weapons. Based on how they have set this up, they could be expanding this game for years to come!
I have not invested too much time or effort into the RTS (or Generals) part of the game, but it is largely simplistic. Eventually you can afford “armies” which are the equivalent of “lives” or “spawns” in the FPS part of the game. Therefore, if I move a mobile infantry army to a battlefield, and join that battle (the FPS game), my team will now be able to use my mobile infantry jeeps/trucks. If your team fails to supply these resources to your team, it can be a catastrophe on the battlefield.
One of my biggest annoyances about H&G is the abundance of ignorance on the battlefield. The American side, of which I only play, seems to have quite a lot of noobs. Sadly, this is partially the fault of the developers; due to the lack of instruction/clarity…much has to be learned on your own (this is getting better though). For the most part, the German side seems to be filled with veterans, they know how to work as a team, they know where to be and when, and they seem to have each other’s backs. This is proven time & time again on the battlefield. Very often, the Americans loose the war. This only adds to the poor morale of the American side, and hikes the morale of the German side. Either the Americans drop the game for a while, or they switch to the German side. So then the Americans see an influx of noobs, and the Germans, with high morale, eagerly feed real cash into the game, making it even harder for the Americans to catch up.

Well, where to start. To put it simply, I rented Far Cry 3 on the Ps3 a little while after it came out. After it's release, weeks went by, as I heard more and more about Far Cry 3. Nothing was spoiled, but I heard so many good things about it. At the time, I really didn't have the money, so I decided to rent the game, like I use to do back in the day.
After picking up the game, I was able to play through about half of it, before needing to take it back. However, around Christmas, my parents got me Far Cry 3 on the Ps3 and I was able to finish my adventure.
About six months after that, I saw the Deluxe Edition of Far Cry 3 on sale on Steam, and picked it up. Then things became really good.
Every game genre gets hate by some people. Mainly because of opinions, which is okay. There are genre' I don't like, and others I do. However, the main thing I see about Far Cry 3 in reviews that give it a low score is.....Uplay. Why, oh why must you give the
a bad score because it uses Uplay? I understand, it's annyoing at times, especially needing to run it through two different clients, but to give the game itself a bad score because it uses Uplay, is very unfair. I have never had any problems running Far Cry 3 through both Steam & Uplay. Basically, when it says someone is playing Far Cry 3 on Steam, they actually have their Uplay open, as the game itself doesn't need to be running to say you're actually in-game.
Not to mention, Far Cry 3 has crafting in it, along with survival tactics. Someone went as far to report the game for being a Minecraft clone because of it.
Far Cry 3 is an
,
,
game. With a very in depth story. Good and memorable characters. Amazing world, and game mechanics.
The game takes you in the shoes of "Jason Brody", a rich kid who takes a vaction to an island with a group of friends. Before having enough time to enjoy themselves, Jason and his friends find themselves captured by pirates ruled by "Vass". It's Jason's job to break out of the slave camp and get his friends back. Having never shot or killed anyone, it is up to you to learn how to take down your foe using a wide variety of weapons. Using drugs made off of plants from the jungle, and working alongside people like Denis. Can you make it happen?
Far Cry 3 allows you to form your story. Everyone's playthrough will be different.
The world of Far Cry 3. The world is massive. In my Just Cause 2 review, I talked about the world being massive, but mostly empty. Here, the world is not only massive, it isn't empty. Everywhere there is something to collect, capture, destroy, hide from, or
from. The world is split between two islands, which take part at different sections of the story. Each lush with plains, jungle's , a lot of killer animals, green, some more green, beautiful oceans and caves. Far Cry 3 is a graphically intense looking game. The views are just amazing. The world is populated by loot, like weapons, money, and relics. There are also deadly animals, like the Tiger, or Cassowary. Not only that, pirates, who only mean to kill you.
Far Cry 3 does it nicely, where the whole game isn't out to kill you. The pirates will get into fights with the natives. Angry animals will attack civilians, and pirates. You could sit at a far, watching through the scope of a sniper rifle, as a Tiger slips through the enemy defense and takes down a group.
Thrown about this world are these plants. These plants can be used to craft drugs to help you with many things. Like detecting animals, or increasing maximum health, etc. Along with crafting drugs, you can also craft other items. Like wallets to carry more money, weapon holsters to carry more weapons, or munitions pouch to carry more grenades. One thing that's strange about this is the fact that you must skin animals to craft these. However, for one thing you might need 2 Tiger skin, and the next, 1 Deer skin, see my problem with this?
Scatered around the world are
or "outposts" that are controlled by the pirates. You can take these down by killing all pirates on the inside. By capturing one of these strongholds, it makes the territory around you safe, and creates a fast travel system. Now, how you approach these strongholds to take them down is all up to you. You have full freedom to do what you want. You could run right in with heavy machine guns blazing it out. You sit from a far with a sniper rifle and pick them off. You could sneak in, perform takedowns and use a stealth recurve bow. Or you could lure an animal into the base. There are so many things you could do.
To take down these strongholds, you need weapons, right? Worry no more. The weapons provided in Far Cry 3 consist of pistols, SMG's, Assault rifles, snipers, shotguns, HMG's, flare gun's, flame throwers, and way more.
Now, while on a mission, though they provide a good story, you are restricted most of the time. Meaning you can't really approach the way you may want to.
Alongside the main story, you of course have side missions. These are of two types, but work and are fun. The first of them being the Hunter missions. Where you take out an animal for various reasons. The second being the Wanted Dead missions, where it is your job to take down a baddie with your knife/machete.
You also earn XP for getting kills and completing missions. XP will gain you skill points, which then lead to you choosing a skill you'd like. One problem with this system is, you don't have access to all the skills until you get futher into the story. As the skills move on, they get kind of more useless. However that's just my opinion.
If there is really anything else I don't care about in this game, it's that the second half falls short of the first half. It doesn't really keep the hype going, it kind of dies down.
I'd like to post this here. Far Cry 3 is so far my most favorite single player experience of all time. The story was great, the gameplay was great. The soundtrack is amazing, and brings man tears. This was one of the best things I have ever played. Now a days, I use a hardcore mod. Mods are available for Far Cry 3 that can fix things, or make the game more realistic and hard. Now, obviously Far Cry 3 being my favorite, I cannot wait for the release of Far Cry 4 which only comes in a couple weeks. I cannot WAIT.
Far Cry 3 is a great game that is well worth the time. For the story, the world, and the gameplay. Every piece of this game is full of greatness. You ability to do what you want beings a new level to video games. We need more, like this.
