!!!!!THIS REVIEW IS KIND OF LONG AND I RAMBLE ON A BIT SO BEWARE!!!!!
Right first thing I want to praise this game for is the excellent console port. It's one of the best ported games out there. It's one of a couple of examples of a port done right. And it's by Ubisoft so that's saying something.
Anyway about the game. Now I have never played a Far Cry game before so this was my first entry into the franchise. It's an FPS (Obviously) and it's an open world game with some RPG elements to it. Sounds good? Well read on..........
Story 8/10
Now I loved the story here. A very interesting experience to say the least. You play as rich kid Jason Brody and you, your two brothers and a couple of others are on a sort of gap year-ish holiday thingy to a place called Rook Island. Doesn't sound too good until you meet who I think is one of the best villians of all time: Your best buddy Vaas Montenegro. (Obvious sarcasm is obvious)
Now I won't spoil his character in this review as you need to play it to experience it but he is one of the best villians I have had the privilege of killing in a video game. He is that much of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And his character is executed perfectly.
Now the others, i'm not too sure. Jason's friends and brothers are not that fleshed out to be honest. They are just there for the sake of having people to care about which I don't. I couldnt care less about Jason's friends. They should be freaking out right? But in fact they are more calm than they should be. Too calm. This is why the 8/10. And this is one of my main gripes with the game.
There are many other interesting and colourful characters in the game who you will meet along the way. Of course there is Vaas but others like Dr. Erndheart and Bucky are really interesting people to meet and you just want to know more about them.
Another gripe is the fact that Vaas is not the main villian. The main villian is some Aussie guy called Hoyt and he is barely even there in the first like 10-15 hours of the game. I will not even attempt to understand why Ubisoft did this and doing so will probably result in me busting a vein in my temple.
Gameplay 9.5/10
Now the gameplay is where this title is near perfect. You have a perfect open world free roam game here. My main dislikes about it are really silly nitpicks which may or may not bother you. But good points about it far outweigh the bad. It's like the difference between earth and sky.
So you are fully introduced into the free roaming after some back story and a pretty good introduction to the basic mechanics of the game. And from here you can advance in the main story or either go and explore some. You have your generic bad guys all over the place of course.
But my favourite thing about the gameplay was the hunting and crafting system. Nicely fleshed out, nice upgrades and later on it's a real challenge when you have to craft some of the more advanced stuff and you have to kill a really rare and tough variant of the other animals on the island. It's hard.
You have a great number of vehicles to pilot, a favourite of mine being the hang glider (Is it a vehicle? :D). You have your cars, boats, trucks and quad bikes. The sort of stuff you would expect from a game like this.
Combat is great with a very wide variety of weapons. From you bog standard assault rifles to flamethrowers and silenced snipers. They are all very balanced and ammo isn't readily available. Enemies drop either assault rifle bullets or shotgun shells and sometimes they will drop other ammo but drops are few and far between.
There is also a mechanic where Jason can pick up various herbs and plants to augment his abilities and enhance them. But  only found myself using the enhanced perception one where you see enemies through walls and stuff for a short amount of time and I sometimes used health ones but the default healing animation is better in my opinion. Just take cover and heal.
Another great thing is that this game actually gives you the option of stealth. You can go Rambo style into enemy camps or you can sneak in and stab everyone to death, hide their bodies and avoid triggering the alarm (at which point reinforcements will be called if you do).
To sum up, it's very near flawless and it is immensely satisfying.
Graphics 9.7/10
Now graphics are the real strong point of this game. You find yourself in a beautiful jungle environment with a lot of options to tweak to make it right for you. Absolutely stunning graphics. Little to no complaint here. Character models are also highly detailed and high res. There is some pop in for me but very rare. It is a demanding game so if you want high settings then you must have a pretty good rig. Recommended requirements are not good enough to run at max.
Verdict 9.5/10

***Get it cheap and play for gameplay, not the story. Kill pirates and be happy***
You play as Jason, a member of a pack of spoiled rich kids trapped on an island after parachuting down to it only to be captured by pirates. The game is mainly killing said pirates, saving your friends and trying to get off the island.
Shooting pirates is defintely the most... and pretty much only really fun thing in the game. Sneaking up on an encampment and trying to sneakily kill of the pirates without being seen is fun. The stealth mechanic works well (although sometimes enemies can see corpses that they should not be able to see). Overall the enemy AI is pretty good and the guns handle well.
Unfortunately you are doing it in a fairly dead world mostly inhabited by people you can't talk to... and if you can you usually wish you couldn't since most of side-quests seem to be fetch quests or kill x animals. Clearing an encampment does change who patrols the area, but that seems to be the extent you can affect the island. Likewise, opening up communications just means you get more weapons for free. There are animals and pirates out in the world the world is pretty... but that does not make it feel alive. There is very little character to the island or the people there and therefore it is hard to care.
The same story has the same problem with mostly unlikeable characters and poorly developed villains. Your only interaction with them is as they talk to you after capturing you for the 51th time. The main story line does give some missions that are somewhat fun (the ones that are pretty much specially designed encampment missions), but it is also mired in QTE's and tower segments. They also provide the only real challange in the game since they force you into fighting in the open and you sometimes have characters with you that are not allowed to die. Otherwise the game is very very easy, even on the highest setting. Actually, the only thing the higher setting seemed to do that I could tell was to add more enemies, make animals more powerful and speed up reinforcements. Which of course makes stealth even more important.
Overall I enjoyed the gameplay and I would still recommend the game based on that. The boring character's and lackluster life of the island did take away some of the enjoyment though.

Far Cry 3 Is an awesome and immersive single player open-world experience. At first it seems a bit overwhelming that there are so many things to do on two large islands. Soon after it becomes second nature once you learn skills and crafting. I liked the whole hunt and survive kind of aspect a lot more than just the cliche urban gangster.
The game looks amazing no matter where you are, which makes adventuring through the tropical foliage even more amusing. It starts to get easy once you're halfway through the game, but once you go to Hoyt's island the difficulty ramps up a bit more, and tests your skills once again. The side missions aren't too bad either, and the roles that you have to fufill when liberating the island pose a nice challenge when you don't feel like doing a story mission.

Which brings me to one of the few things that I dislike about this game. It doesn't let you save during your story mission, so I had to do around 3 missions twice in a row since this game was prone to crashing on my system. Some other minor bugs/problems are that if you use a custom control scheme you might have to switch back to default since the "mash" buttons aren't maped with certain layouts. Another is that you have to be spot on with doing climbing or looting since the areas of interaction with those are smaller.

These minor flaws aside, It is a very enjoyable experience being the biggest badass on the island. Every weapon is fun to use, and there's enough diversity in the enemies to keep you on your toes with strategy. The stealth combat is also fun and rewarding. The skill tree will make you want to play more, then feel satisfied after you link together takedowns and throw knifes at unsuspecting enemies. Hunting is also a plus for me, since It's also a necessity for being able to have a larger inventory. The XP system still makes you work for building up your skills and strategies instead of letting you unlock everything after you get a few points. Transportation around the island is awesome as well, flying, ziplining, boating, buggy or ATV racing, won't make you bored when you're trying to reach your destination. The AI in the game isn't the greatest but that's okay since It can either work hilariously in your favor or it can make you create awesome combos for your own ameusment. Hard mode is what I felt most comfortable on, which presented easy battles roaming through the island but made me have to use better tactics and crafting for story missions.
The storyline didn't disapoint me either, It was easy to follow along and had nice twists in it. It just seems awkward that Jason is able to escape death so many times, he just seems like the luckiest man on earth. The personas of the characters were amusing and did make me laugh at points. The personalities of the villans made me dislike them quickly as well. This made it so that you felt more like Jason himself, and wanted revenge on all the tyrants of the islands. It's a tough fight, but if you enjoy the game as well as I did, you'll find yourself playing at least a full 24 hours of the storyline. I shouldn't have a problem going for 100% in the post-game either!
Minus the bugs and small mistakes that Ubisoft has made with the game, I give it a stable 9 out of 10. It looks great, is a very tactical yet amusing FPS, and has a unique story/survival aspect to it that makes it a real keeper. For re-playability purposes, just join with a friend and do the CO-OP missions if you don't want to do all the secrets or side quests after the story. There's almost always something fun to do in Far Cry 3, and I'm glad I've got to enjoy it.

Welcome to the Rook Archipelago; Where you'll be in danger 90% of the time! (NOTE: Haven't tried Multiplayer/Co-op since I'm not sure if they are worth it, or if they are still active anyways. The review is based on the single-player campaign).
You are Jason Brody. Trapped on an island (later two islands) in Southeast Asia by skydiving there while on vacation, you increase your skill set, shoot enemies and animals, and become a Rakyat warrior to save your friends from Hoyt's and Vaas's slave trade and get off the island. The game is fun as hell, allowing you to run across the island(s) as you increase your artilery from a simple handgun to a bow and arrow to a rocket launcher, among other weapons you can either purchase or unlock as you play throughout the game. You can also hunt animals to upgrade your weapon holsters and better arrow quivers via crafting with animals hides from tigers, bears, tapir, deer, and so on. You can also unlock a variety of skills to use, such as extended health, improved aiming accuracy, and faster reload times among others; these skills are represented by tattoos on your left arm, so the more skills you unlock, the more tattoos you have. The game also looks beautiful as well, though less so for me considering I'm playing it on old hardware (not that archaic, just from 2007). Regardless, the lush greenery and tropical scenery still looked great while playing the game, though I'd recommend you to upgrade to newer computer hardware for better-looking graphics. When playing through a mission, you are free to enter any part of an enemy outpost from any side you want, and either stelathfully take out pirates one by one, go in with guns-ablazing, or a little of both; the way you choose to play the game is up to you entirely. Though there are some missions that require you to go in one specific entrance and come out one specific exit, but the mission area you are playing is still allows you to play non-linearly. The characters are also interesting to learn about, including Dennis, Citra, Vaas, Liza, Sam, etc., but the voice cast wasn't as appealing to me; however, Vaas was one of the characters that stood out to me, thanks to his uniquely insane (see what I did there?) personality, his over-the-top behavior, and his calm attitude, making him a very memorable antagonist overall. Last but not least, the soundtrack was great to listen to, from exploring the island to cutscenes; although I was forced to mute the music and increase the volume so I could hear the characters talking, since I had this weird audio problem that turned down the character's voices to extremely low, and I'm not sure why it did (probably because of my old computer, but I don't know for sure). My favorite song to listen to was the main theme during the end credits; oh man I could listen to that all day.
To sum up (and add in other points):
Pros:
+Beautiful Graphics
+Interesting Characters
+Weapon Variety
+Good Controls
+Nonlinear Gameplay
+Great Soundtrack
+Using drugs as enhancements
+Vaas' badassery as the secondary antagonist
Cons:
-Main Antagonist isn't as interesting as Vaas
-Voicework was meh except for a few characters including Vaas
-Using drugs as enhancements
-Audio problem via voices from characters was EXTREMELY low during cutscenes. Now sure if this was just my problem (considering I'm not using an up-to-date computer) or if others have experienced this problem.
Overal Score: 9/10

Moral of the story is that you should never accidentally skydive onto a tropical island filled with pirates that'll sell you into slavery, dangerous wildlife that'll attempt you to eat you alive, and drugs. On second thought, just don't accidentally skydive onto a tropical island, period.

"Addicting as hell." I sat around for about thirty minutes thinking up a good intro but thats all I got. The Mount & Blade franchise is basically what happens when you become a unit on the battlefield of a Total War game. Once you have created your character you are dropped into a country of warring factions with no goal or itinerary. So what does that mean? It means you pick a side or become a rogue sovereign yourself and mount your trusty stead and ride around recruiting an army smacking all who oppose you with all sorts of pointy, blunt, or sharp weapons at your disposal. Sure the graphics aren't pretty and the AI has the enemy running at each other blindly but surprisingly hacking up hundreds of mindless rabble, collecting loot, leveling up, and conquering cities, just doesn't get old. Warband at the time of writing this is the optimal version with many mods (such as the fantastic "Blood & Steel" mod) available as well as an intresting multiplayer mode.

Honestly this may easily be the best videogame ever made. While it may not sport much in the way of cutting-edge graphics, the deep combat system that relies on skill coupled with the excellent role-playing and strategy elements of the single player campaign make for an amazing base experience. Add to that a HUGE assortment of fan-made single player and multiplayer mods (such as Mount & Musket, cRPG, and many more!) and you have an infinitely replayable, deep, engrossing adventure in melee action combat.

Far Cry 3 is a really good game, but my feelings about it are complicated.
I don't write about this game as passionately as I do about Outlast, or Mass Effect, or Arkham Asylum, or Bioshock Infinite. Those games left me with an adrenaline rush due to their excellent executions, novelty, and fodder for narrative analysis.
Far Cry 3 is cool as all Hell, though. You leap over rocks to drive a knife into a pirate's chest (there's seriously a semi-scripted move for that). You sneak through the bushes only to ambush a baddie with your machete and pull the pin on his grenade before kicking him into his imminently exploded colleagues. Your character's a badass, and thanks to this game's mastery of mechanics, you are too.
It's also beautiful, even in 2014. So there's that.
The narrative is where my thoughts are complicated, and it's ultimately what stymies my would-be adrenaline rush. The characters are fascinating: Jason is an unseasoned ♥♥♥♥♥ who discovers himself as he tames his own id (arguably too quickly), Vaas is a genuinely scary psychopath, Buck will make you sick, and Hoyt is the disgusting sort of ego maniac that you can't wait to end in the final act. Characterisation is where this game's narrative is at it's brightest.
The plot progresses in an extremely disjointed fashion, however, and that's were my problem with the game lies. I believe this is because the story is an allegory, not meant to be taken literally. However, that disjointedness makes all of the metaphor really pretentious--the writers wanted to display their creative prowess and neglected to worry about blending it into a clear storyline. You'll teleport around the island as if you had blacked out, but you had no reason to black out in the first place and you won't know how anyone found you to rescue you. You'll hallucinate and see foreshadowy images in the water. You'll be stabbed in the heart, only to wake up in a temple on the other side of the world without a scratch on you. Supporting characters are inexplicably your key to success, willing to help you and total strangers, all at the same time. The allegory is very insightful. Growing up entails mastery of the id: we must acknowledge and embrace it without succumbing entirely to its allure. The story would have been more impactful, though, if the literal progression of events made sense.
I recommend it, though. Insanely satisfying mechanics, beautiful visuals, and outstanding characters overcome a pretentiously told story.

The game is okay, with a relatively large world, plenty to do, and scenery to appreciate.  The main story is your basic Far Cry story: you were vacationing, now you've been forcibly transformed into a killing machine.  You level up by tattooing yourself, with "perks" (gaining new abilities like takedowns and being able to cook grenades, and passive abilities like more health and better healing) and you can level through doing practically anything.  The gameplay is pretty fun, but for the most part enemies are dumb (avoiding cover and running right at you) and pretty easy to kill early-on.
However, it's also a console port, with lots of technical problems associated with it.  Even with a GTX 770 (which can run Metro: Last Light on ultra with zero framerate problems) I cannot run this game on ultra.  Why?  Because it's unoptimized.  Especially on some of the more hectic parts of the campaign where there are lots of things happening.  Even on LOW, I barely manage to reach a semi-stable 60 FPS.  There is a FoV slider and plenty of options to tweak, but they don't really seem to do much of anything.  After some testing, this is because I was running the game on DX11.  Running the game on DX9 gives me a much better framerate on ultra.  Again, it's a console port.
On top of that, you have to deal with Ubisoft's inevitable Uplay nonsense.  This program interferes with Steam's own Gameoverlay.exe program, which allows you to talk to your friends.  Meaning that when/if you get a message, you have to minimize the game, respond, then re-enter the game and re-maximize it (oh, and it enters windowed mode whenever you minimize.  You can quickly go back to fullscreen with alt + enter, though).
Oh, also, a lot of the screenshots in the store page are what you would call "bullshots."  Pre-rendered lies.  The game does look good, but while you're hangliding or wingsuit flying, you'll really notice how painted on a lot of the foliage is when you notice it's flat.

One of the all time classic games. With shockingly poor graphics for the age and very basic sound quality, this game doesn't seem like it'd be a winner. But it's incredibly deep considering the rather simple interface, allowing for a decently wide array of content to explore.
The combat system shines. Mounted combat, including couching a lance make the biggest frustration in the game NOT finding a constant string of fights. It's a gloriously simple mechanic to learn, but rewards skill and timing the more effort you put into it. Easy to learn, difficult to master.
The range of fighting types is amazing. Spear combat is often overlooked (ie Skyrim) but in M&B it's here in all it's glory. Horse archery, heavy cav charges, mowing down peasants with a mace while you look down from your mighty war steed.
On the fly unit orders are quick and effective. Lead your troops from the front or roam the rear lines barking orders and overseeing the battle from on high.
Companions and leveling them offers immersion in character back stories and in-fighting. When companions sometimes leave your employ, you feel their loss.
The content is far deeper than expected from an indie title. Fight as a merc, swear fealty, rebel and put yourself on the throne. But add in personal relationships, courting the ladies, hosting feasts, trading between cities, doing quests for lords and guild masters, fighting in tournaments, and more....and this game packed with content even though much of what you do is watch a tiny horse move around the world map.
Modding is a big part of M&B. There are some amazing mods out there. Floris is huge but upgrades every aspect of the game. Gekokujo is a wonderful Samurai era version. LOTR, and GoT are both represented as well.
Just get this game. You will not be disappointed.

One of the all time classic games. With shockingly poor graphics for the age and very basic sound quality, this game doesn't seem like it'd be a winner. But it's incredibly deep considering the rather simple interface, allowing for a decently wide array of content to explore.
The combat system shines. Mounted combat, including couching a lance make the biggest frustration in the game NOT finding a constant string of fights. It's a gloriously simple mechanic to learn, but rewards skill and timing the more effort you put into it. Easy to learn, difficult to master.
The range of fighting types is amazing. Spear combat is often overlooked (ie Skyrim) but in M&B it's here in all it's glory. Horse archery, heavy cav charges, mowing down peasants with a mace while you look down from your mighty war steed.
On the fly unit orders are quick and effective. Lead your troops from the front or roam the rear lines barking orders and overseeing the battle from on high.
Companions and leveling them offers immersion in character back stories and in-fighting. When companions sometimes leave your employ, you feel their loss.
The content is far deeper than expected from an indie title. Fight as a merc, swear fealty, rebel and put yourself on the throne. But add in personal relationships, courting the ladies, hosting feasts, trading between cities, doing quests for lords and guild masters, fighting in tournaments, and more....and this game packed with content even though much of what you do is watch a tiny horse move around the world map.
Modding is a big part of M&B. There are some amazing mods out there. Floris is huge but upgrades every aspect of the game. Gekokujo is a wonderful Samurai era version. LOTR, and GoT are both represented as well.
Just get this game. You will not be disappointed.

Overall Far Cry 3 is a very solid First Person Shooter game. It has a very intense story that makes you want to finish the game from start to end without stopping. To note this is the first Far Cry game I have FINISHED. I could never finish the previous Far Cry games for many reasons. That being said this game in the series was very enjoyable to me. As you can see the game took me no more than 13ish hours to beat, doing some side missions and other little challenges in the game. It is a fairly easy game to get through compared to the other Far Cry games. One gameplay mechanic I really enjoyed was the stealth. It was top notch fun sneaking around taking people down with brutal machete kills. The skill system works very well with the game too. I never once felt underpowered in fact the way the game progresses you feel weak at the beginning, but towards the end of the game you are a bonafide killing machine. The story like I said was very entertaining, playing out like a classic hollywood revenge film. You play as Jason Brody a man who decides to go on a getaway vacation to a mysterious island. Things go south and your friends get captured, leaving it up to you to save them. The game has great character development showing how Jason must learn to adapt to the situation at hand and become a ruthless killer in order to save his friends. The game does feature 2 different endings each one being very different from the other. The endings were the only thing that made the game a little negative for me. Without spoiling much one of the endings is very empty meaning it feels as if it was rushed and things needed to be futher explained. Other than that it is a great single player experience. I have yet to play multiplayer. As far as technical aspects the game ran very smoothly never dropping its frame rate or crashing. I had a good experience with UPlay too. This is definitely the right step in the Far Cry series and I am now looking forward to Far Cry 4.
9/10- TLDR Great game with awesome gameplay mechanics and a solid story. Looking forward to Far Cry 4!

Do you remember Skyrim? Well, this is Skyrim with guns. Now how awesome is that?! Picked it up at the summer sale and it was well worth the 5€ I paid. I would give up to 30€ for this game, as it's not brand new, but it feels like it is. Now that's for the price, about the actuall game I have to say this: Really nice gameplay, feels realistic, top graphics, runs very smoothly maxed out (EVGA GTX 770 ACX SC, Intel core i5-4670K 3.40GHz), all maps are very well made (singleplayer, co-op...) which shows here: I once drove into a hole while being chased and I thought I was done for as I couldn't get out and I ran out of ammo. But than I swam underwater (there was a pit) and I found an underground cave that lead me straight through a hill and I came out on a road. The AI doesn't seem to have any major problems, but it sometimes acts silly. exp.: Two enemies saw me, but they were on the other side of the river (it was like 4-5 meters wide) so they kept shouthing at me things like: "I'll get you!", "I see you!" and stuff, but didn't fire any shots. I don't think I was out of their range, couse there was like 8-10 meters beetween us. It's also very well voice acted and I LOVE the way driving feels. Also very rich map with many little secrets, hunting areas and side-missions. So my final verdict on Far Cry 3 is 9/10, a great game. Can't wait to see more of the Far Cry 4 footage and what it has to offer.

When I picked this game up in the sales for a few pounds, there was no way I expected it to be as brilliant as it actually is. Farcry3 follows Jason, a slightly wimpy American teenager who gets into trouble with some bad guys on an island. In essence, they kidnap some of his friends and he goes to get them back. Firstly, let's get the characters out of the way. Lots of people hate Jason and his friends, and although they are very 1 dimensional, I have to say I grew fond of Jason. His transition from cowardly white boy to tattooed warrior was a great development throughout the game. The other characters are brilliant; The unstable and unpredictable Vaas, in particular, I absolutely adored. And Sam. BLITZKRIIIIEG! I love the fact that you hear them referring to you as 'Snow White' as your legendary status increases, it makes you feel like a badass.
The game is just so much fun! I felt genuine fear as I ran and hid behind bushes from the enemies, having heard their trucks driving closer and closer. I nearly had a heart attack the first time a tiger jumped on me, and laughed out loud as a herd of cows chased me. I adored having to go to certain areas on the island to hunt for different animals to make things. The skill development trees are great, and the skills built up perfectly in sync with the difficulty progression of the game. The open world feature is brilliant - it makes the game less linear and a lot more interesting. I absolutely loved the idea of having to turn on the pylons to unlock sections of the map, and the turquoise water, sandy beaches and lush tropical vegetation make the game look stunning.
The tasks are varied and a lot of them are so much
(the drug fields task was probaby my favourite task in any game, ever). From having to drive a quad bike against the clock, to sneaking into camps to take things, to shooting a gun and making everything explode from a helicopter, to torturing somebody, the tasks are endlessly entertaining. At no point in this game did I think 'oh great, another one of
tasks'. And that's another thing: you have a lot of choice. No, you don't have to keep taking out all the enemy camps, you can sneak around them. No, you don't have to do lots of vehicle driving if you don't want to. Aside from the main storyline, you can play the game how the hell you want.
The difficulty increases throughout the game so perfectly, you have to take your hat off to Ubisoft. Towards the end, the tasks got really quite demanding, and there were several instances where I 'ragequitted' and sulked for half an hour, before having to go back for more punishment. And to me, that is the sign of an incredible game - I had to finish it, I needed to know what happened. The storyline is probably the best storyline I have seen in a game for a long time, it flows well and you genuinely care about what happens.
Of course, there are a few bugs and general irritants in the game. The enemies are very 1 dimensional and often a bit daft, as Jason's friends are. Some of the later tasks are ridiculously difficult (constantly spawning enemies). Having to pat down dead bodies to steal stuff means you'e continuously having to hold E, and the character feels a little bit clunky when you're climbing around. Having said that, these are very minor issues that took absolutely nothing out of the game, I'm just trying to balance it out a bit.
I wish I could go back to the time before I played FarCry3 and start all over again. I absolutely recommend this game, and for the sale price of less than £5 you would be absolutely crazy not to have this on your list.

Great game!
9/10 in the BlacKy scale.
* Story starts great (no spoiler): A group of rich kids went for a vacation on an exotic island (or a group of islands if u'd like) to have fun, but then gets kidnapped by pirates. You free yourself and get help from local villagers to free your friends and take the kidnappers down.
* Island looks amazing. Overall graphics is very up to date.
* Exploring the island is very fun (whoever liked Red Faction Guerrilla's enviroment will like this aswell). Many side quests to do. Having a bunch of items to find (just like the classic hidden boxes from the GTA series). Driving a vehicle makes you feel as you're inside the game. You can actually feel bumps on the road.
* The wildlife is very nice. Many exotic animals to encounter. Animal's AI is well done overall.
* The more you advance in the game, enemies get thougher.
* Customizable weapons. Need i say more?
* Co-op is pretty fun when its not crashing.
* You get to cheat on your gf with an amazonian nympho.
* Story ends bad, in my opinion: I'll do my best not to spoil - When having the chance to get out of the island with all your friends, you take the other option, revenge, staying behind and killing those who have kidnapped you and your friends.
* Enemies AI is a bit poor. They sometimes suspect that something is wrong but they dont tend to do much about it, even if they're defending an outpost, etc.
* I've found all the syringes except health syringes to be unnecessary to use. No need to dive too much underwater so water syringe is irrelevant. The camera's ability to tag enemies and animals makes the hunter syringe to be irrelevant aswell. You can extinguish fire when you're on fire so fireproof syringes are, again, irrelevant.
* Your health is too OP. You can make up to 10 health packs while also carrying impossible amount of crafting materials to make even more health syringes if you'll need to use later. After getting enough progressed in the game, you have constantly infinite amount of health which makes everything boring and less exciting.
* The skill tree isn't as good as other games, E.G Borderlands franchise. You will eventually unlock all the skills in the game, which makes it unnecessary to think 'which skill am i going to unlock next?'. Some of the skills have absolutely no value in the game so you may think that even if you have free skill points to spare, you wouldn't pick that specific skill.
* While the crafting option itself is very well made. Everything craftable in the game gets unlocked after ~50% of game time (finishing the north island), so you wont be needing to kill animals for hides at the second island at all if you have explored the first island effectively enough.
* Activating radio towers makes the game very easy. Too easy i might say. Weapons will become free in weapon shops, ammo gets very cheap, and you get the sense that money isnt a factor anymore. If you like a bit of a challenge, dont do what i did, which was unlocking most of the radio towers before making the quests. Try exploring everything at once:
- Do a few missions.
- Do a few side missions.
- Explore the island as you can: Find some artifacts / SD cards / letters / etc.
- Unlock some radio towers and outposts.
- Repeat
* uPlay - Sadly this game runs by uPlay, which means constantly-crashing servers in multiplayer and co-op, no Steam achievements, and no real option to search for specific servers like in normal Valve servers via Steam.
Multiplayer and co-op have no skill filter. A level 1 noob will often join a group of level 75's (highest level).

There is two Mount & Blade games. There's the first game that's named only Mount & Blade but you'll want to pick up Mount & Blade: Warbands because Warbands have all the features the original game had including new animations and new items. Also note that the video below is Warbands footage.
Mount & Blade was developed by the Turkish TaleWorlds and published by Paradox Interactive who are also known for publishing titles such as Magicka, Galactic Civilizations II and Lead and Gold: Gangs of the Wild West. Mount & Blade is primarily a medieval sandbox game / RPG.
You start the game as a foreigner in Calderia and when you arrive you get attacked by a single thug in the middle of the street. A lonely merchant hears the commotion and suggests that you take care of it. This is meant only as an tutorial and you can refuse him in order to set your sights on bigger fish. You might be thinking why I'm calling this game a sandbox for then? Well, firstly you can more or less fill any role you might desire. Do you want to be a peaceful trader and create an economic empire? Yes, you can do that. Do you want to be a raging warlord in the service of a king, you can do that too. You can even become King yourself and hand out fiefs to your vassals which will attempt to protect them for you and gather armies in your name. Or you could just run a mercenary company in order to keep your freedom.
Lords, ladies, kings and death
In Calderia you got strict classes in society. Firstly you have the Nobles of Calderia, they will mostly wage war with each other but will work together and against the player depending on whenever they trust the player or not. In the case of war the King will elect a Marshal that will lead the nobles during a war campaign. When they manage to capture cities and castles the Nobles will start to vouch for people who should be awarded these prizes. Since fiefs gives a weekly income to the lords they will not back down from receiving one if they can help it. The player can really try the game of politics and persuade the nobles to "vote" for him so that the king will decide to award the fiefs to the player. The player can get the respect from other lords by doing favors for them or participating in battle with them. The marshal will be especially grateful for the people that answers to the call of battle and will most likely be one of the key contacts the player will have.
And here is where Mount & Blade shines: It's the politics system! You will be challenged throughout the entire game because the Calderians are very stubborn and old fashioned. The game will try to gather the lord (which are often spread out over the land) by hosting feasts in various places. There you can "court" ladies of the realm and possibly get a bride one beautiful day. The lords will also be good associates that will gladly help the player in the player's pursuits. The NPCs are somewhat flexible in this regard but
The game does have it's faults though. The AI of the opponents are somewhat weak and the controls feels a bit clunky. The characters in this game are very stiff and it will very few times be worth the effort of jumping (unless you're on a horse) and you will often curse the sluggish movement speed the characters have. The animations for attacking are uncomfortable and it's somewhat hard to aim thrusts. The bots doesn't seem to have that problem though and will pretty easily pull off quick and well aimed thrusts and chops at the player.
Multiplayer
The multiplayer in Mount & Blade: Warbands isn't perfect but it's very solid. You pick a gameplay mode: Conquest, Capture the Flag, Duels, Sieges, Deathmatches, you name it. And when you're in the game you pick a faction, a general class (Footman, Archer, Cavalry) and then you customize your gear. You don't have access to the entire arsenal of weapons but you have to earn it by killing opponents. The system rewards skilled players by making them harder to beat next time they spawn. Multiplayer in Mount & Blade is really difficult though and expect to fork out just as much time as learning how to play Team Fortress 2 at least. Some servers disables automatic parrying and enables friendly fire which beginners really suffers from but on the other hand, it does counter spamming 2 handed swings and blocking monsters pretty well. It will also make fights look more like a medieval fight would look like and could encourage teamwork (but it doesn't like all other multiplayer games).
The power of mods
But the best part is coming now: Mount & Blade uses python code and is pretty easy to script (not as easy as it could have been though) and right now many dozens of different mods have been released for the game. Some are historical simulations, others are just enhancements to the gameplay, others still change the game so it takes place in different settings like Star Wars and the Stone Ages. Sadly, some of the mods are somewhat amateurish. The Stone Age mod for example could use some work. But other mods like the Blood and Steel are very well made and additively entertaining to play.
Final Verdict
If I were to rate the game solely on it's vanilla game and single-player only I would rate it 4/6 as a good game but thanks to the vast majority of mods and the inclusion of multiplayer this game deserves as much as 5/6, if the animations were a lot smoother and the controls wasn't that clunky the game would have been entitled a perfect score of 6/6 but sadly, there's some thing not even the mighty force of modders can solve. Also, if it could have incorporated some sort of co-op it would also have deserved the highest score...

Sandbox games are hard to come by these days. Every title seems to offer players little choice in the actions they can take, leading them down a pre-planned and predictable path. But, who can blame them. Games these days are like the movie industry. Small, contained pieces of entertainment, offered in bite sized chunks for impatient young adults. At least we have the Mount&Blade series to pave the way for those who prefer a little more choice.
Set in a fictional kingdom of Caldaria that resembles central Europe during the 11th Century, Mount&Blade: Warband is a pure sandbox experience. You start of as a humble being, with little more than a crossbow strapped to your back. As you progress however, you gather followers, meet Lords and enter conflicts of factions, eventually even able to become King of Caldaria... if you choose to. That is the beauty of Warband, you can do whatever you like, the choice is entirely in your hands.

Mount & Blade is a rather unique title. Honestly, while it's not a great game, the experience is not replicated by any other game around.
The mounted combat system is wonderful. Only the Assassin's Creed series comes close. The storyline is very light, nearly nonexistant. You create your own background from a small number of mixable options, and are thrust out onto a world map with only the clothing on your back and (maybe) a swaybacked horse. After that, it's all up to IMAGINATION.
And modding, oh my goodness. The whole reason the games made it to fruition was the vibrant modding community that sprang up around the game during it's development. Sadly, the fact that Warband came out as a standalone game instead of an expansion splintered the community between the two games.
Warband is the better game, but both games ultimately depend on the modding community. If you're willing to hunt for the mods required to bring out the amazing parts of this game, it's worth a try.

Mount & Blade: Warband is probably the most glorious indie computer game ever made.  I know, I know, that sounds like a ridiculous over-the-top statement that you have become accustomed to when dealing with me; but hear me out.  Mount & Blade: Warband features mounted combat – a strange omission from almost any action game ever, and get this – it does it so well that this simple mechanic alone makes it worth the $30 of admission.  On top of this Mount & Blade adds decent graphics, a crude but effective inventory system, varied if dull NPCs, and an addictive if unrefined level up mechanic.  It has a few rough points, but the downsides pale in comparison to the addictiveness of the RPG elements and the joy of combat.  Also, it has multiplayer, only versus and not co-op campaign, but enough for some of my friends to churn out 100+ hours of this gem.
Haven't seen another game do melee combat nearly as well as this.  Also a pretty fun expansive world to roam around in.

Mount & Blade Warband is not what you expect just viewing images of the game, Warband is a deep and complex strategy game, infused with first/third person RPG elements along with political debates. The game blends so many different types of game elements sometimes its hard to define exactly what Warband is. From a band of mercenaries to a powerful king, the game not only throws out strategic problems, it also throws political challenges, all while you are able to cleave a path through your enemies. The multiplayer is what you would expect from such a game, spawning and cleaving other enemies through death matches or castle sieges. The game is complex, and not for everyone, but for what its worth and how much you get out of it, its worth trying, though, unforgiving in the beginning, sticking with the game is rewarding. Mount & Blade deserves more recommendations and with a helpful community, and plenty of mods for the game, even the original version can be played for hours on end.

This is the first Far Cry game I have played, and I am sure that I will be playing many more after this great game. This is undeniably one of the best open-world FPS games that you can get.
What makes this game so wonderful is that it is undeniably entertaining, yet it exhibits this high quality throughout the 20-30 hour main game.  The graphics are beautiful, the sound design is great, and the voice acting is top-notch. However, the best parts of the game are both the story and the gameplay. You play as Jason Brody, and after you and your friends get captured by pirates, you escape and you have to rescue the others. It sounds "generic", but as you go along in the story you notice it is not.  The best aspect of the story is easily one of the main villains, Vaas. Vaas is a sadistic person, and the most memorable parts of the game happen when he is included in different scenes. The gameplay is really fun too because of the open-world you have. Personally, I consider it a mixture between Ubisoft's own  Assassin's Creed and Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption, except on an island and in a First-Person Shooter format. I say this because the influences of radio towers (viewpoints) and hunting animals to achieve certain things in the game are there. Levelling up to achieve skills are here as well.
Overall, there is plenty to do in this game. The single-player lasts for at least 20 hours. Plus, there are little distractions of multiplayer and co-op, if you're lucky to find a game in those. The single-player alone is worth it though. Get this game.

Mount & Blade: Warband is probably the most glorious indie computer game ever made.  I know, I know, that sounds like a ridiculous over-the-top statement that you have become accustomed to when dealing with me; but hear me out.  Mount & Blade: Warband features mounted combat – a strange omission from almost any action game ever, and get this – it does it so well that this simple mechanic alone makes it worth the $30 of admission.  On top of this Mount & Blade adds decent graphics, a crude but effective inventory system, varied if dull NPCs, and an addictive if unrefined level up mechanic.  It has a few rough points, but the downsides pale in comparison to the addictiveness of the RPG elements and the joy of combat.  Also, it has multiplayer, only versus and not co-op campaign, but enough for some of my friends to churn out 100+ hours of this gem.
Haven't seen another game do melee combat nearly as well as this.  Also a pretty fun expansive world to roam around in.

Far Cry 3 is an awesome game to play only once and only for the story. The many additional missions and things to do that are not related to the story are extremely repetitive and only mildly interesting (usually involve going to kill something and then returning; Key word: Repetitive). The guns that are available are alright but there is a lack of customization options and some of the ones available for multiple weapons DO NOT match which means that you can not have a matching loadout (so no same skins for all of your weapons). The game's highest point (plot) slowly degrades since the protagonist begins to be ridiculous about certain things (I won't spoil anything but the plot does degrade imo). There are nearly no players online (incase you want to play multiplayer) and often, the matchmaking will glitch and a bunch of players will be stuck in a lobby indefinitely (until someone in Ubi fixes it, I guess). The whole "stuck in lobby" thing would not be a problem if you could just leave and join a different one, but for some odd reason, when this glitch happens, the matchmaking will keep inserting your account into the glitched lobby (lasted for one hour for me, once). Other than this, the multiplayer is actually quite fun. By the way, a UPlay account is required (Ubisoft's steam-thing), so you will be launching UPlay from Steam before being able to play. Lots of people have a  problem with UPlay, but imo it is not really a problem since it launches on its own and launches the game on its own. All you do is close it after you finish playing. The stealth in this game is very well done, and is very fun (just have to be patient). It DOES get ridiculous, however, since your character becomes seriously OP with all of the skills that you would get. If you play on the hardest difficulty, the OP-ness won't be an issue. Also, the economics system is useless once you obtain all craftable upgrades so some of the perks become useless as well. Money making is not even an issue since you can eliminate the need to purchase weapons altogether by completing some side-missions (which are ridiculously easy, again, I won't spoil what you have to do to get free weapons, but its easy as pie). Also, DO NOT think that this is "Skyrim with guns" because it is not. Skyrim has LOADS of stuff to do and the vast majority of them are interesting while FC3's things to do are painfully limited and not interesting at all. Let's just say that there is a reason that the game is rated an 8/10 rather than anything higher (which is still very good). But it does not live up to the expectations that you percieve to exist. At least, that is what a couple of my friends and myself where thinking about the game. We had more fun playing online, and even that only lasted for about a week.

This game is an absolute masterpiece, and in this review, I'm gonna stick by Yahtzee's rule of: "A game must be able to stand on singleplayer alone." and, wow, this game really does stand out. The summary of this is that you (the protagonist) and your friends has been kidnapped by pirates and you've escaped. The rest of the game you are trying to get them back.
Venturing throughout the game, you battle amongst different species of animals, depending on the food chain. This includes sharks, snakes, komodo dragons, crocodiles, tigers, panthers, and bears. Majority of a lot of the predators on the island include intense quicktime events when they attack by suprise. One sticking out would be a crocodile attack. If you fail to complete the quicktime event, the animal kills you. If you finish it, you either kill the animal, or damage it. You need to also kill animals to craft larger objects (bigger bandolier, more space in wallet). A situation which I found hilarious was where I was hunting for tapir to gather their pelt. I was interrupted by a tiger, who literally left my health at the lowest point. To which I retreat to the river where I was instantly attacked by a crocodile. The game realistically shows all the different situations in the jungle and proves Vaas as he said: "if the jungle doesn't eat you up alive, I will.".
Going onto characters, Vaas is one of the best villians I have ever had the pleasure of laying my eyes against. True fact, Vaas wasn't even supposed to be in the game, Michael Mondo's(Vaas' voice actor) audition pleased Ubisoft so much, that they decided to create the character Vaas for him. As you saw the summary above, which is quite bland, Vaas introduces the story of insanity. To which it makes you think, what if all of this isn't happening and you're sedated or on drugs? What if this is all a dream? I may be sounding completly irrelevant and random, but the theme of insanity really does make you wonder what is actually going on throughout. Not to mention there are even more villians than Vaas.
While you battle pirates and animals, you have a wide range of weapons to choose from. There are RPGs, bows, SMGs, rifles, shotguns, flamethrowers, flare guns and machetes. Not to mention you get to customize your weapons, for instance, you can add a red dot sight to your bow to help accuracy or add a extended mag to your rifle to stop running out of ammo quicker.
Your character also gets tattoos from the Rakyat which improve your fighting and stealth skills. The tattoos you get to pick from are the heron, the shark and the spider. Tattoos that would be an example would be moving faster while crouching, the throwing knife takedown and the added health bars.
If you are thinking "tl;dr", then my summary of this review is that this game is one of my favorites I have ever played along with other great games like Red Dead Redemption, Skyrim, and Fallout. There are a few problems with the UPlay, which ruins it a bit. But all in all, a great game.
10/10 GG Ubisoft.

So you've played every popular multiplayer FPS under the sun and are looking to ditch the guns in favor of something a bit more personal.   Well, this is the game for you.  Pick up your favorite melee weapon and get up close to your enemy so you can see that look on his face just before you stab him in it.
A good analogy for how multiplayer works in this game is Counterstrike without the guns.  You start each round with a set amount of cash and some free equipment and then pick and choose between your nation's weapons/armor of choice and then take to the field and try not to get yourself killed while hopefully taking a few of the enemy out along the way.  In addition to excellent infantry related combat, archery, cavalry and horse-archery are all represented as well if being a ground pounder isn't your thing.
Also, although the multiplayer is a real blast, the game also features a great sandbox-style (think Sid Meier's Pirates) singleplayer game where you start off as a lowly peasant and work your way up to leading huge armies and ruling your own kingdom. There is no linear storyline or hand-holding you here, the game is what you make of it. If you've ever wondered what it would be like to play a general from the Total War series from a first or third person perspective, this game will somewhat give you that experience. If you have a high-end gaming rig, you can set the battle size up to like 500+ units on screen at once (with a small third-party tool).
The game's graphics aren't on the cutting edge of current technology, but they allow for huge battles.  Where the game really shines is in its combat.  It's one of the few games I've ever seen where you control your attack/block directions.  Watching 2 pro's go at it is akin to watching a well coreographed movie fight.
I cannot recommend this game enough. You just don't see GOOD medieval combat anywhere really. This isn't some button hammering console combat game. Check out the demo!

There will come a time when you are unsure of the outcome of a fight. Perhaps it is due to numbers, or troop strength, but you will doubt if you can win or not. In that moment you will have to choose, flee, or crank up your favorite metal music and just make it happen.
Those that bring it to the enemy against overwhelming odds with Fear Factory blaring will find glory.
You will find glory.

Decided to update this review after I went through a phase of having absolutely no internet for nearly three weeks. It does things to a man, luckily for me my drive to do crazy was driven back by (not a wise choice of words, I'm aware) by this here game that I had installed prior to going through that so called 'phase'.
Anyway, down to the actual evaluation. Turns out, given its release it's pretty easy going on the eyes, as in, the graphics are spot on. The next thing one notices in such a game are, obviously, the guns you get to handle. A rather small arsenal to choose from. Only 34 guns in the game in total. But the way you get to access them or finally get your hands on to them, I believe that should make it worth the effort.
The vast choices and open world at your disposal make the game full of stuff to do long after you're done with the story. Although, pro tip; don't wait around for the story to end. Turns out you'd appreciate the things you unlock doing the misc. tasks prior to engaging in the main story. I tried the non pro way once. And then decided to finish the game once again, doing it this new way I call 'pro way' and it made the game a breeze. Only challenge I faced was because of the higher difficulty setting I put it on.
If you're into crafting and therefore improving things by hunting and gathering crap spread across the gaming world, then you'd find this game your type as well. I'm personally really not into that at all. I usually prefer having better things awarded progressively by doing boring repititve tasks. (or so I think I do??)
There's a huge, important, and carefully planned out stress on stealth in this game. One of the things that really attract my kind. I like it done in the dark with no witnesses, no survivors ;)

But all of the sudden my fate turns near as the car stops and I hear the men shouting of the dead bodies. I then stand and kill the driver and his passenger with my AK-47 and take the car onward to get to the radio tower, but along the way I have to kill the engine and duck into some bushes... Released in December 2012, Far Cry 3 was Ubisoft's flagship 2012 title, besides the ill-fated Assassin's Creed 3. Hype for this game was (and still is; at least until Far Cry 4 is released) monumental. Surprisingly, in a rare phenomenon for modern video games, the hype actually paid off. It actually was good enough to be deserving of its fame and proved itself to be an incredibly legit modern shooter. (No, you ingrate, Far Cry 3 isn't "Skyrim with guns".)
Far Cry 3's primary basis is that it's an open-world FPS with survival and exploration elements. The basic idea is that you're put in a large, dangerous jungle island and left up to your own devices to survive and thrive. Among the game's core gameplay, the player is given a variety of activities to do to increase their standing on the island, including hunting, harvesting plants (I fucҝing love drugs!), climbing large radio towers to increase map completion, assaulting strongholds owned by the enemy to decrease their presence on the map, and of course completing main story missions to advance through the game's central story mode. The story missions occasionally provide new mechanics or gimmicks (like the wingsuit or the vehicle turret sections) within them to give the player motivation to progress through them. These fundamental activities are necessarily varied to give the player a good amount of choice in what they want to do, without ever letting them get bored or tired of the game.
Far Cry 3 has an immense amount of content. And I mean immense. Like 30 square kilometres, 20 radio towers, 40 strongholds, and dozens of animal species immense. And that's without mentioning the miscellaneous side content such as the knife throwing or racing minigames, and the abundance of side-missions, plus all the collectibles scattered all over the map. In fact, I believe that all the content in Far Cry 3 is the game's biggest weakness despite being one of its biggest qualities. I have never, not once, actually legitimately complained about a game having "too much" content before. Far Cry 3 is the one game though that I actually had that opinion on. Regardless, the game's excessive amount of content and things to do isn't likely to bother you nearly as much if you aren't a legitimate completionist in video games, so take that complaint with a grain of salt. 100%ing Far Cry 3 is a great accomplishment though. If you actually have the fortitude to completely 100% this game, that's quite impressive. Good job you sack of ѕhit.
Aside from the large amount of playtime and content present in the game, the core gameplay is pretty normal for a modern first person shooter. Now I'm not trying to say that FC3 is generic or boring or anything, but it isn't a modern shooter that plays very differently from the "norm". That said, the player character moves relatively slowly (faster than in something like Halo, though) but can sprint and use vehicles. The player's health regenerates slowly but the regeneration is limited to about one block of health (can be increased through some perks). There's also an experience/levelup system like in a lot of multiplayer games nowadays, with three perk trees available, each specializing in a different aspect of gameplay (stealth, gunplay, survivability, etc). The guns all control fairly well and feel like they pack sufficient punch, but weapon balance is pretty poor if the game is left unmodded. Early game weapons are phased out fairly early in the game by weapons which are arbitrarily more powerful regardless of any notion of ballistics or sense, with more expensive weapons somehow providing stronger bullets to fill your enemies with. The player also has the choice for bringing along specialized or unique weapons with them, such as a bow (which can be upgraded to fire flaming or explosive arrows), a flamethrower, a welder to repair vehicles with, or various types of explosive launchers.
Storyline-wise, FC3 is about a group of college students, the player character being one of them, which get trapped on the tropical island they went to as a vacation destination by an army of pirates, interested in looting the island and killing all of its inhabitants. Jason Brody, the main character, is a particularly insufferable white college kid, consistently complaining about his situation and just overall acting like a bіtch whenever the opportunity prevents itself. In his credit however, he eventually toughens up as the story progresses. After escaping from the pirate camp at the very beginning of the game (in what is a very linear and awful tutorial section) the player is found in the river by a member of a nearby tribal village. Here begins the main goal of the first part of the game: removing the invading island from the pirates and granting control back to the tribal inhabitants. Among the overarching mission to wage war against the pirates, the player also reunites with their kidnapped friends, and clashes with the leader of the pirates, the enigmatic (and also fucҝing crazy) Vaas. He may wear makeup, but he's also likely to murder your whole family, so in a way, this character is a lot like the Joker. Probably explains why people like him so much. The game's story contains quite a few impressive set pieces and plot twists, so even if FC3's story isn't quite among the cream of the crop of video game storylines, it's still entertaining at worst, and worth playing through at least once (it does have different endings, after all).
In the element of graphics, Far Cry 3 is very impressive both artistically and technologically. FC3's setting and artstyle are competent at presenting a believable jungle to the player, making the game quite immersive, especially given the extremely large amount of flora and fauna present in the game. Architecturally, the game's islands are divided between more industrial, modernized towns and buildings, usually attributed to the invaders/pirates, and a more ancient tribal aesthetic given to the Rakyat tribe that the player deals with at various points in the story. There's also scattered WW2-era wrecks across the map, adding some backstory to the islands, and a few Chinese-inspired temples buried deep within the mountains, which the player eventually visits in the story missions.
FC3 is also well above-average in its graphics, essentially being one of the best looking modern video games up to this point. Of course, the fidelity of the game's graphics also demands much from the systems of players. On top of that, it's also a console port, and Ubisoft have a well-known infamy for making especially bad porting jobs. Still though, Far Cry 3 is playable, and performs very decently if you have a well-built modern gaming computer. Either that, or you can grit your teeth and go play it on a console. You probably shouldn't, though. It is a shooter and all. Anyway, graphics-wise, the only real problems I have with this game is that enabling ambient occlusion adds a noticeable black outline to every object rendered, and you need to edit the game's .ini file to disable AO. Using the in-game anti-aliasing effect is also extremely detrimental to performance, so using AA built into your hardware is recommended. In fact, I managed to rack up a hilarious constant frame rate of about 8 FPS when I turned the in-game AA to 8x and AA on my GPU to 16x on my old GPU. Other than that, all the effects work well enough and there aren't too many porting/performance issues that affect the game otherwise.
Overall, Far Cry 3 is a solid experience, and I suggest playing it even if you don't have a strong interest in the first person shooter genre, as it presents an example of a well-done modern-day video game that has relatively little hand-holding and doesn't gear itself towards people that don't play video games.
Also, it's fun as fucҝ to play with a machine gun and an explosive bow and pretend you're Rambo.

Hmmm...Game Of The Year 2012? Yeah, I'm 2 years behind on this game and i cant believe i let this one slide me by. Let me start by saying it's refreshing to meet a game where it's strongest point is singleplayer, usually current games stash all of their real content into multiplayer then hack on some half-witted single player just to have it there.
First off, just to get it out of the way, you have to deal with the horrible abomination that we all call Uplay...I'm glad i could finally play the game in offline mode, but still, it's a dumb program in the way of your gaming experience. There were also alot of server issues galore when i tried and i have yet to be able to play a single CO-OP game. so as of this review, ive stuck to singleplayer.
Most people pass this off as an average console port, but i don't really think so. as far as graphical options, this game truly delivers. Full DX11 support and even offers a dam FOV slider, when was the last time you saw one of those beautiful things? Mouse smoothing also isn't a problem since you can just turn it off. The amount of sheer detail found in this game is outstanding, but moreover, its consistent. Most games of this scale will throw in the occasional bland texture, but ive yet to see ANY.
I'll start with the story, it is really quite interesting as you progress and experience Jason, a town-raised ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, changing as a person; lowering himself to Vaas's level. Becoming a warrior himself.  Vaas, is very Heath Ledger (joker) like, the way he talks and his fast paced personality. you can clearly see the amount of effort that Micheal Mando (Vaas voice actor) but into him. The game is even matched with little tid bits of "Alice in wonderland" quotes thrown here and there between the chapters, they fit perfectly.
Supporting Far Cry 3's story is a pretty large arsenal of side quests; ranging from hunting special animals to races to mini games. There always seems to be something to do. There is even a very robust crafting system in place, at times it feel very lackluster but as my progress in the game grew deeper, i found myself liking it's simplistic style more and more. Crafting in this game is essential and really makes you want to go hunt or gather ingredients for syringes that besides healing you can grant you some neat abilities (the ability to sense the animals around you or repel predators,etc). Now this is a Free Roam RPG shooter, so as well as crafting and side missions, your hit with 3 character advancement skill trees that as you unlock the skills in them, tattoos appear on your forearm *or tataus like they are called here* i feel the skill system could have been a little better, but i think that was just me remembering FFX oh well.
The huge focus of this game is its amazing amount of freedom in anything and everything you do. Sure there are a couple of story missions that are kind of linear or restrictive, but other than that it's all up to you. Do you like to make a noisy entrance into the enemy base, without knowing where the enemies are, spray-and-praying Call of Duty style? Go ahead.Do you like to stalk your prey and make a plan and try to keep to it as you silently pick them off with your silenced sniper or trusty bow? You can do that. Or maybe baiting your enemies while you sneak into their base, plant amine near every alarm and next time they see you BOOM! Or maybe let that leopard trapped in that cage do the job for you. Done! You have so many options it can be overwhelming at times. Most AAA RPGs that are released now and boast with their freedom of choice don't even come close to this game.
As for the animals, this is where the game does a VERY good job. There are two types of animals: carnivores and herbivores. Predators and prey. Wherever you go chances are you will see leopards chasing deer, tigers hunting buffalos, sharks eating tortoises, bears assaulting villagers etc. It feels very organic, natural and chaotic as well. These animals can make your life very hard - like surveying an enemy outpost only to find yourself attacked by a tiger, thus drawing enemy attention and realizing there are 4 times more enemy troops now. Or making a run for it and having to cross a river only to be assaulted by a crocodile and dragged underwater as soon you dive into the river. Splendid!
well, i think i made you read for quite long enough. all in all i would highly recommend this game, especially if you like first person shooters. im sad to say my review was based only on the singleplayer, but ive heard from many people that Far Cry 3 has a very solid multiplayer and an extremely fun and engaging CO-OP, matched with a high singleplayer replay value. this is defiantly a game ill be playing a few times over

I will say right now that if you enjoy action shooters, you will most likely enjoy far cry 3! at the time of writing this review, it is during the summer sale. and for the price of only 5€, I'd say its worth it! even at the 20€, its great!
heads up, this is very long, but i tried and cover as much as I could here!
first lets talk about what is good about it!
firstly, most of the optional things you can do in this game are more often than not very useful! hunting animals for their hides? you use it to craft ammo pouches weapon holsters to increase ammo, money and weapons you can carry!
liberating outposts grant massive amounts of XP and gives you a fast travel, aswell as usually unlocking some more side quests to do like hunting animals or killing badguys for money!
finding and climbing up radio towers grants you the ability to fill up your map!
and stealth AKA takedowns generally involving killing enemies with a knife before they know you are there, is highly rewarding if you can pull it off, having large XP boosts for these kills!
that is not to say that gun toting maniak ala CoD super soldier is impossible to play as! you have a large amount of weapons in this game! sniper rifles, rocket launchers, shotguns, assault rifles, pistols, LMGs, SMGs, a flamethrower, a bow and arrow and other goodies!
the islands are huge and a ton of fun to explore! the view you get from some of the high spots is incredible and the jungle feels like it is alive!
many of the characters are very well voice acted like Vaas!
and there are plenty of side-quests you can do!
and now for the things that suck about this game...
firstly, you cant skip the intro!
this is a problem because the intro is roughly 20-30 or so minutes of boring cutscenes and tutorials! this makes starting a new game after your first playthrough rather painful! thankfully, once you finally get to the first required outpost you must take, you're more free to go about your businees!
the cutscenes are not skip-able!
similar to the intro being un-skip-able, there are a good bit of cutscenes through out the game, and they are usually not too short. this can also be a little annoying at times, but that might just be me...
the NPC's that give you sidequest have a terrible voice quality!
I don't know if they just got lazy or cheap, but the NPC's that you talk to to get sidequests have a very low quality of their voice, usually being very low and like the voice actor stood across the room from the mick. this is a minor complaint, but you'll start noticing.
Jason and his friends are boring!
I am not going to lie, when I was restarting the game before writing this review, I could not for the love of my life remember what Jasons name was or what he looked like. I am dead serious! the same goes for his friends, they are boring and forgetable as hell! good thing they are not a big focus of the story or anything! it also feels like every word spoken by Jason is forced out and feels very awkward.
as I mentioned before, the other characters make up for that with good to great voice acting and development! also, Jasons friends dont spend too much time around Jason (thank god).
there is little to do after you finish the main story!
by the time you finish the last story missions, you will most likely have liberated most if not all the outposts, unlocked most if not all the radio towers and gotten most of the crafting done, aswell as reached max level. and after this, there is little left to do... money is no problem, you get so much of it and unlocking radio towers makes them free and when you liberate the outposts, there are little to no more enemies!
you can try some trials of the rakyat challenges or do sidemissions or simply go around and hunt animals, but it quickly loses its interest. this gives the game a low after-game life! its still a lot of fun to replay it a couple of times, but not too much else to do except get the last collectibles and do achievements...
the 3 "boss" battles are extremely disapointing!
there are more or less 4 "bosses" in this game, but I only count 1 as an actual boss, and that one is mostly just something in your head after you drink some freaky potion. the other 3 are main characters, and the only one I can name is Vass because the other 2 would spoil some story for you...
so, how does the life of the great Vaas, the lord and savior of the pirates that took you and your friends prisoner and messed up the island, end? by giving Jason another acid trip, a quick time event knife fight that has a few cool moves and then poof! screen fades to black and they just say "Vaas is dead, yay"! as you might imagine, it is EXTREMELY disapointing! the same goes for the other 2! this badass guy thats been interesting and built up for mutiple in-game hours! wierd acid trip thing and a quick time event with knifes, and POOF! they are dead...
the difficulty is very unbalanced!
what I mean by this is: the game has a major problem keeping its difficulty flow consistent. in the beginning the game is rather difficult or normaly difficulty, depending if you go stealth or guns blazing. then, in the mid part of the game, it is suddenly easy as hell, and taking out an outpost without getting spotted is as easy as blinking! then all of a sudden its really difficult to impossible to sneak something, and very hard even if you go guns blazing! and then its easy again! and this keeps going and going and going. is rather annoying...
with all those bad things, why do I stil vote this up and say its a good game? because it is stil an enjoyable experience! if you like action shooters, with some other things to do than shoot up badguys, you will like this game! it has enough variety, enough action and enough good characters and side stuff to do, that its worth the money right there! hell, just going around the island is great, with the fairly good amount of detail to the wildlife and plants!
I will say this game is very good, despite its ageing! keep in mind that far cry 4 is supposed to come in a couple of months I think, but this is stil great! go ahead and buy it, you will most likely not be disapointed!

It’s easy to see why someone would want to visit Rook Island – it’s a stunning tropical location with plenty of fun activities, scenic views, and history worth discovering. Far Cry 3 disrupts that paradise to challenge your feelings about enjoying violence. Because of lunatics like Hoyt and Vaas, you’ll see beautiful things you never would have. You’ll do terrible things that make you uncomfortable and meet fascinating, disgusting people. You’ll sympathize with Jason Brody’s difficult choices as he turns from vapid young man into a monster.
Far Cry 3 is important for the same reason as Far Cry 2. It’s a shooter that considers shooters thoughtfully, both in the way they’re designed and the way we play them, and then asks us to do the same. Should massacring hundreds be a great way to entertain ourselves? Maybe not. But it is.

I found myself having the same exact experience over and over again with little to engage me to play more.  Nonetheless, a fun AAA title.

So is it good? Yes. Is it great? Well, that depends on what you want. I enjoyed the "story" or rather the awesome characters, acting and voice acting in this game A LOT. It is simply really well made, I cannot remember a "better" antagonist in any recent or even not so recent game that I have played.
The gunplay and graphics are awesome, the game feels very smooth.
But there are downsides. The beautiful landscape is not filled as well as it could be in my opinion. Sidequest and especially collectibles are repetitive and grindy to the point that they are annoying and boring.
Another part of the game - namely liberating outposts - is immense fun, while other freeroaming aspects did not quite entertain me as much. Especially hunting. Fun for a short while, but after that it is just a grind and then it is suddenly useless.
I am not a huge fan of sandbox games and unlike Assassin's Creed with the nice fighting system, there is simply a lack of challenge when shooting the mildly insane AI. What I also missed was decent music. Especially in a caribean setting like this I would like to hear some more reggae outside of missions (don't get me started on the car radios).
All in all I enjoyed this game a lot, but I would suggest focusing on the main story line and stealthily liberating outposts (for fun).
