Far Cry 3 is a game that takes place in Rook Island, which is divided into North Island and South Island. You begin the game as Jason Brody, an American tourist who is vacationing with his friends looking for fun on this tropical paradise. Things go wrong when pirates kidnap them for the purpose of selling them into slavery. You encounter a leader named Vaas Montenegro, who makes life a living hell for you and your friends. Later you’ll run into another nasty guy in the name of Hoyt Volker, who lives in the South Island has more powerful pirates protecting him.
Jason may seem like an ordinary guy, but you can make him quite powerful using the skill tree system. There is plenty to explore, including the plant life, the animal life, and the numerous outposts controlled by the pirates. You will also get to know the Rakyat, the natives of the island and you will learn their traditions as you progress through the story. The story missions are interesting and well-scripted, but the most exciting part of the game is being able to freely explore the island when not working on a story mission. The world has plenty of randomness such as shootouts between the Rakyat and the pirates. Other times you will see animals attacking the Rakyat. On some occasions you will see animals like bears, tigers, and leopards attacking the Rakyat tribe. On other occasions you will see tigers or bears stalking boars. Sometimes the predatory animals will come after you and you will have to kill them in order to survive. Other times you see a pack of dogs with one howling like a wolf. You look around to see if these animals are stalking you.
There can be benefits to killing animals in the game. After killing them you can skin them in order to craft bigger wallets to hold more cash and craft loot rucksacks to carry more leaves and loot recovered from containers and dead bodies. Liberating outposts requires you to kill all pirates guarding them so that they can be your safehouse. The game rewards you more for using stealth than for going all out on a shootout against the pirates. Each outpost contains alarm panels near the flags representing the outposts that pirates can use to call reinforcements should they find you. But you can shoot out the alarm panels to eliminate the possibility of reinforcements. The sniper rifle comes in very handy when trying to liberate outposts. I would shoot a few pirates and find a place to hide by hiding behind rocks and in the foliage. The XP gained from liberating outposts is used to develop Jason in different ways. This is the RPG element of Far Cry 3. There really no wrong skill to learn because all the skills are useful in some way. You can learn to take down an enemy from behind using the brutally effective machete. Then you can learn to take down an enemy by taking one down from behind and throwing the machete immediately to take down a nearby enemy without alerting others. Liberated outposts offer side missions such as assassinations and hunting animals both common and rare. You have to complete assassinations by using your brutal knife, so using any other weapon will result in mission failure. This is in line with Rakyat tradition that you will learn to respect in Rook Island. The hunting of animals requires you to first stop by a site to pick up a weapon designated for hunting the animals. Using any other weapon will result in mission failure. The hunting of rare animals is rather interesting because the skinning of these animals will help you craft larger wallets, larger ammo pouches, larger loot rucksacks, larger syringe kits, etc. So hunting and crafting go hand in hand and will help you throughout your exploration of the island.
Whether you’re hunting, crafting, searching for relics or lost letters from dead WWII Japanese soldiers or progressing through the main story, Far Cry 3 is rarely boring. You can unscramble radio towers throughout the island to make your map clearer to read and to help Rakyat supply lines. As soon as you kill deactivate a radio tower, you will have a supply drop side mission available. Supply drops require you to drop medical supplies within a certain time limit. This type of side mission lets you know how treacherous driving can be in Rook Island. It also can get a little repetitive. In my opinion, the supply drops side missions are the most tedious in the game.
There are many vehicles that you can drive, but driving on the roads can feel a bit awkward. Driving boats and watercraft can be a lot of fun while exploring the gameworld by sea. You can navigate from one place to another by ziplining, which is more fun from a first-person view than I expected. It’s cool to zipline, get to drop down on a pirate, and brutally stab him at the same time. There are hang gliders scattered throughout the island that you can use to reach faraway places or hard to reach areas.
In the original Far Cry you could use binoculars to tag enemies you see in the distance. Far Cry 2 removed that feature to make it more realistic. Far Cry 3 has brought back the ability to tag enemies in the distance, so you will be able to see enemies through walls after tagging them. Weapons would eventually wear down in Far Cry 2, so you had to replace them. In Far Cry 3 weapons never wear down from use and you can upgrade them using the built-in store in each safehouse for a price. Some weapons can be upgraded by using attachments such as a sniper scope, a laser sight, or a silencer. Some weapons can also be customized by painting them in a variety of colors that are available in the built-in store.
The AI in the game is very good, as you will see enemies react to dead bodies. They will automatically go into search mode in an attempt to find you. They will try to flank you if they detect you or they can hide behind objects such as rocks and shacks. They enemies work as a team when trying to find you and kill you.
The graphics of Far Cry 3 have very impressive textures and make Rook Island look alive. The animals are incredibly detailed and so are the skies whether it’s sunny or raining. The details of the faces of the Vaas and Hoyt look amazingly realistic as do the faces of the pirates.
Without trying to spoil the end of the game, I will only say that there are two endings. Each ending leaves you with moral choices to contemplate. The story missions are somewhat linear, but having two possible endings for the game makes it more entertaining.
In my opinion, Far Cry 3 is the best in the Far Cry series. The other two Far Cry games emphasized an open gameworld, but Far Cry 3 is the most open gameworld and the random encounters really help this game. The randomness ensures that the result of approaching an outpost will never be the same each time. You may infiltrate an outpost on your own only to be interrupted by a predatory animal such as a bear, tiger, or leopard. Sometimes, your attempt to liberate an outpost is thwarted by a jeep filled with pirates. Far Cry 3 is a classic action game that I highly recommend to anyone.

Great graphics, gameplay, sound, music, voice acting, and an interesting (if slightly nonsense) story all combine to make Far Cry 3 a truly outstanding game. You get character upgrades, all kinds of movement and travel options, various weapons, stealth, and an open world / sandbox style map to play on. There are various side missions, objectives, hunting, contract kills, strongholds to take over, the list goes on and on.
Why don't I like this game?
1. First off, I dislike stealth gameplay. I don't like to sit there watching patrols looking for the best time to sneak out and do a takedown. I don't like walking around the perimeter of an area trying to find the best approach. The way the game is designed, however, rewards you for doing things without being detected. In fact, some missions actually require you to do them this way.
2. I also don't like the hunting, which is pretty much a necessity if you want any storage upgrades. Need to be able to carry more guns or ammo? You better hunt boars, sharks, deer, etc. But when you do, you have to skin them, which includes a fully animated knife going through the carcass along with a squelchy sound and your character going "Eww!" which is exactly what I'm doing.
3. Also, the game doesn't easily let you switch back and forth between mouse/keyboard for shooting, and gamepad for driving. You have to go into the options every time you want to switch from one to the other. It's a minor gripe, but it's just another reminder that we're dealing with an obvious console port.
4. I'm not a huge fan of first-person games featuring a male protagonist, with no customization. I prefer being able to choose my character's gender, what he/she wears, and how he/she responds in conversations. In a market crowded by dudebro first person shooters, Farcry 3 sits comfortably, pandering to its target audience.
5. Then finally, there's the abomination that is uPlay. Sorry, Farcry 3, you're just not good enough to put up with uPlay's sh*t.
I imagine I'll probably pick it up and try to play it some more, eventually, but it's pretty low on my list. I'm glad I got it on sale for super cheap. It's an excellent game, for sure, no doubt about it! It's just not to my tastes, not for me. It wasn't designed with people like me in mind. It's like meat to a vegetarian - someone else's food, and that's fine, but it's not mine.

I reposed big hopes in FC3, but this game simply sucks coconuts.
FC3 is a beautiful game of course, it's big and shiny and could be fun...at first sight. After 20h of gameplay i know that this game ain't for me. Far Cry 3 is a bonfire of schizopfrenia! You got it all: lots of shooting,  sneaking and adventuring. Sounds good? Not at all.
Propotions just ain't right. Sometimes FC3 is a hardcore FPS, but sometimes it becomes more like Splinter Cell, or sightseeing adventure close to the newest Tomb Raider. As i said before graphics with subtle cell-shading is great, shooting mechanics is great also... But hey. what else? Nothing really. This game is boring. Sneaking is poor brother of hardcore games like old Thief, or SC, but it is also irritating and you can't just ignore those sequences.
What about adventuring and sightseeing? At the begining it's fun, but after few hours it become unwanted necessity. You want to play an addictive adventure, Indiana Jones-style game? Play Tomb Raider! You want game with lots of "sneaky-tricky" things? Play old Thief! Or maybe you love elements of cRPG? Play a real cRPG game like Skyrim for example.
There are too many ingredients in this game and they are NOT yummy. After few hours of gameplay the taste become bitter, sometimes even intolerable.
Of course you can try FC3 and maybe you'll love it, but be aware of what i wrote earlier. This game sucks entire farm of rotten coconuts, be aware!
PROS:
- graphics,the island i beautifull
- Vaas and his sister
- voice acting and motion capture
- shooting
- cRPG elements
CONS:
- coconuts;-)
- this game is badly balanced
- irritating sneaking sequences
- boring sightseeing
- problematic weapon choice
- no respectable motivation system
- boredom!

This is one of my favorite games. It has a great story which sees a thrill seeker family and friends holiday take a dark turn for the worse. Very good voice acting and some memorable characters. Despite all the hours I've put in I have still only explored about just under half of the island. That does not include all its secrets and side missions either. That should give you can idea of the scale of things. The island really is massive and looks beautiful and scenic. Shame its so dangerous. Survival plays a big part in this game as you learn to live of the land and craft various tools and equipment. Thankfully as you discover key locations the map gives you the option to fast travel. That said with the numerous modes of transport scattered around the island you can still zip around whether its by 4 wheel, boat or in the sky. As you progress across the island new weapons become available as do missions and characters. You literally get transformed from a spoilt rich kid into a one man killing machine.
I am impressed with how well optimised the game is, as with a bit of tweaking I have managed to get it running at a decent fps even on my low spec rig. I am also playing FC2 which is the subject for another review but what I will say is that the story and gameplay is similar but not identical enough for me to feel like I'm playing a cloned sequel. If you can't run FC3 then definetly give FC2 a go. Roll on the release of FC4.

A heart-wrenching tale of an ordinary young adult set to save his friends from the horrible wrath of two druglord madmen, Far Cry 3 is more than just a "shoot-anyone-who-stand-in-your-way" game. It's a journey that combines fast-paced cinematic gameplay elements with stealth and advanced combat mechanics. Its skill tree and item tiers keep you playing for hours on end, and its surprising replayability will keep you coming back for more and more.
It's quite honestly, to me at least, one of the best games ever made. Not many titles can effectively blend smooth and fun gameplay mechanics, gorgeous graphics, and a heart-touching story like Far Cry 3 does. What is even more surprising is that it's made by Ubisoft.
To sum things up, I'll just say that this game is worth being launched through Uplay.

I start from good side: Far Cry 3 is a complete adventure at some tropical islands, where you have to (and have might to) overcome cluster♥♥♥♥, and take a life under control. Dream of so many people. Great story plot, quite comparable with Cameron's "Avatar" movie.
As a game, first-player-view shooter with some "gaining new abilities with experience" (RPG-elements)... It looks good, it allows to move as you please on large and full of life archipelago, and, most needed, it allows you to shoot people (and other things) when and how you want to - which is much clever, than usual "narrow corridor bang-bang run" ala Call of Duty series.
As an inheritor of Far Cry 2, it washed away bigger part of boredom, reason, why so many people turned predecessor down. Far Cry 3 is an open-world game, where you may actually like sub-quests and spend "a little more" time than you have to beat story line.
But... there are cons part.
First of all, oh precious realism, makers of Far Cry 3 most definetely casted it away. Some American boy found himself trigger-happy - that is one thing. But, that boy, cutting throats and sneaking to clear an avanpost silently all by himself... "Ne veriy" (Don't believe it) - Stanislavsky would say. Secondly, I don't like Jason Brody (protagonist) for one bit. Not a golden boy from prologue, not a rambo-like gut-cutter he evolved. All that story 'bout "insanity" make me sick. So, if I'd believe my "nature instincts", like game asks me to at start, I'd through it away. It's way Hollywood-and-plush, "Hunger games" on good bones of "Battle Royale".
For game itself (gameplay process). It looks nice, but Just Cause 2 (released 3 years ago) looks greater and sharper, in terms of visual quality. As for game balance, in sandbox conditions - they have to lock key characters in buildings and scripts. Othervise, everyone will end up killed by varans and cassowary.
About rambo-ing. Sure, I can silently clean an outpost, spend time to look for patrol routine, calculate lines-of-sight for every soldier on it... But why do that? Without any reconnaissance I can rush forward, and kill all of them (armed with AK's, SVD's and probably some machine-guns and RPG-7) face-to-face, with my machete and shotgun. On hardiest setting possible. On quarter or less time than silent approach. Talking 'bout realism again.
Finally, for comparison with Far Cry 2, I'd say, yeah, they cut boring parts with respawnable avanposts, replace some of "dogs of war" realistic stuff with more hollywood-like decorations, very dramatic, of course, but edged teeth of action-stuff-fans up to zero.
There are other lesser flaws, like stupid bow and driving-worse-than-in-farcry2, but I don't want to dig deeper.
Overall, game is big, sometimes even fun and clever, game have catchy moments, but even then it has that "seen it before" scratch of second-hand cloth. Definetely NOT a must-buy. Take it at some discount, if you up to FPS games and don't fall to all that marketing crap already - or don't bother at all, it's not all that good. Total mark - 6,66/10
PS: multiplayer and co-op features could have been a bigger win, but they are too glitchy, too narrow-viewed. Look at Battlefield, for much better online experience.

I love this game, I really, really do.
You might be wondering then, why, why is this guy recommending it when you have this feeling he's about to go off on it?
Because I AM.
Far Cry 3 is truly a graphical masterpiece, and I feel I can say that, I have multiple self-built systems that can play ANYTHING, and my Steam library alone will show you the scope of what I own and play, FC3 is truly a graphical masterpiece. Redundant, yo.
However.
uPlay is forced upon you, you can't play the game unless you agree to it's terms, and this, for MANY reasons, is a very bad thing. uPlay is a very invasive program, it tracks what you do, and I don't mean just your game hours and achievements, it tracks every move you make. Even when it's suposedly closed and no longer running. You read that right. In order to shut it down, you have to go through a bundle of Windows hoops I won't bother to go in to, because most wouldn't understand it unless I write out a schematic for it, and that's just not fair to you. It also collects system information from you, without asking for your approval. uPlay is also UbiSoft's copy-right protection system, which is really pointless and redundant, after all, was Steam not contracted by UbiSoft for that very reason?
Indeed.
In addition, the uPlay platform is extremely unstable, you will often find when you exit the game that it has crashed, and you were never even notified. This, of course, is if it didn't cause FC3 to crash, along with it, It happens. A LOT, generally during fast travel times, or when selling animal skins at the various stores.
Along with all this, FC3 has so much non-essential crap in it, missions that have absolutely NOTHING to do with the story. More, it's supposed to be an open world game, that's blasted and trumpeted in so many places, but the reality is far different. You're told to explore, but, when you DO, you're constantly told you'll fail a mission for leaving the boundaries.
Wait, what? Exactly.
That's not open world.
The game mechanics, which so many say are so great, are in fact NOT GREAT. You're constantly trying to loot bodies, but it's  hella hard to get the game to LET you do that, often when trying to loot, you end up switching weapons with the corpse instead. It's FAR easier to pick up guns than to loot your kills, which is idiotic, as every gun is available in the stores, but the loot is NOT. Ayup. 'Zackly. More, there are too MANY guns, way too many guns, it's like being led into a coffee shop, and being told there are 3,000,000 varieties to choose from, so, have fun with that, don't OD on the caffiene! Unless you really, really just feel like it, you won't use but a very small fraction of those guns. The constant upgrades in ways to kill is, at the least, extremely difficult, for instance, chained takedowns, you have to react in a literal nanosecond to be able to consistently do these, it's virtually impossible to do, because of the, you guess it, game mechanics. For Assassins Creed, they work, but NOT in a "modern" game like FC3, where tactics have evolved a great deal, and the AI is much smarter. You end up with half your skill tree being utterly pointless, and useless. You have to HOLD down your heal key to get healed, and for some reason, that made sense to them. And that's IF the game even responds when you do it, for some reason, there's a delay in all syringe actions. It can be, hek, it IS constantly rather costly. You get killed while desperately trying to heal yourself. :|
Skill trees aren't supposed to be useless. See?
Some of the Paths of the Hunter missions are needed, it's how you get the leather you need to make your gear, but, once all your gear is made, they keep throwing the missions out there. Absolutely pointless.
The actual story telling, along with the plot and storyline itself, gets unbelievably confusing, it in fact becomes unbelievable. The only good acting in the game is Vaas, possibly Dr. Earnhardt. The other main characters, along with the side characters, are completely unbelievable, not to mention unconvincing, and any other word that goes along with it.
The Metascore for FC3 is 88, the game when it game out cost 59.99USD. The reality is that the game shouldn't have been more than it is NOW, at 29.99USD, and it's Metascore was either paid for by UbiSoft, or based almsot completely on the graphical achievement. The real score should've been a flat 70, at best. Which is truly sad.
It had the potential to be so much MORE.
Also, the constantly being notified about EVERY LITTLE THING is extraordinarily distracting, and that idiotic balloon popping up every few secons about SOMETHING, usually POINTLESS, has gotten me killed more times than I can count.
ALL OF THAT ASIDE, I truly love this game, in many respects more than FC2, which I felt DIDN'T get a high enough Metascore. Funny, that. FC2 a lot of the time felt boring to me, FC3, even with all the idiotic weirdness, has yet to leave me feeling bored. I was even telling my wife just yesterday, that even with all the issues I have with the game, I obviously love it, because I'm playing the hell out of it. It's beautiful to behold, it's fun to play, IF, and I stress IF, you can look past everything I've mentioned and just love the GAME for the GAME.
I can, and I do.
It's fun, it's beautiful, it's immersive, and it's even, to a degree, addictive, IN SPITE OF ALL THE PROBLEMS.
Imagine what FC3 COULD have been, did it NOT have all the problems that it does.
It would have truly been a game for the ages.
But, even at it's absolute worst, it's better than every single Call of Duty game ever made.
Maybe that's why it's Meascore is so high? : D

When are words not enough to describe how amazing a game is? When you experience something so great, so beautifully crafted, with so much attention to detail that you find it hard to find a word, or words that perfectly reflect what you have just experienced. With Far Cry 3, I find myself in a state of awe, struggling to best define this masterpiece.
Far Cry 3 is in all sense of the word, remarkable. It has an amazing story, a beautifull location to explore, tons of missions, side quests and activities to do, and even racing. Although some of the aforementioned activities are optional, you will feel like the game experience won't be complete unless you engage in them, and they are quite rewarding and most importantly, a whole lot of fun.
You play as Jason Brody, a regular guy on vacation with two of his brothers, his girlfriend and some friends. The vacation however quickly turns into a nightmare, forcing Jason to do things he never thought possible, gathering strenght and courage with the help of a local tribe, the Rakyat in order to free your friends and liberate the island from drug dealing pirates, and a human trafficking organization.
Rook Island, where the game takes place is not only beautifull, it is also a very dangerous place. From pirates to privateers, to the local fauna, this place feels alive to the point of making you getting lost in it. You are not playing a game, you are fighting for survival. The animals in the game act realistically, and attack you, and can greatly affect the outcome of battles versus your enemies as well. You will need to hunt some of these beasts to craft inventory items, which will let you carry more weapons and ammo for example. Expect to find Bears, Tigers, Komodo dragons and even crocodiles on your journey. Flora also has an important role. You can craft syringes to aid you on your quests, and in order to do so you need to gather plants of several kinds, allowing you to create some really helpfull items. It is very believable and incredibly realistic, in this aspect I have never encountered a game that makes you feel that what you are experiencing on screen could easily be a real life situation.
It is a violent game, gritty at times, and that contributes a lot to the feeling and believability throughout the experience. Characters will swear and have no problem in handling situations in the most violent of ways possible. Unlike Far Cry 2, the characters in this game are memorable, which makes you care about what happens to them in the game. Be warned that this game messes with your sense of morality, some choices you will need to make will leave you in shock.
This game requires Uplay, and some people have a problem with it, for whatever reason. In my experience I have had no problem with it, and even though it shouldn't be necessary to play it, it is not a hassle to deal with. If you are not playing this masterpiece because of this, and you are a steam user, it is utterly hypocritical of you since Uplay is the same kind of DRM as Steam is. Don't let Uplay stop you from experiencing one of the best games ever made, and in my opinion, the best sandbox FPS ever created.

Oddly enough I'm going to give this a no. Skyrim-esque exploration? Check. Stunning visuals? Check. Vaguely-discernable plot in an open-world game? Check.
Where this game falls down is more what I've played than what the game does wrong. An avid fan of the entire STALKER franchise, Skyrim and a couple of others, this game doesn't quite live up to its predecessors. The inventory mangement is crap first of all, and the crafting menu isn't great either. The most problematic gripe though is the FEEL of the game. Bear with me.
STALKER is a really tough open world post-apocalyptic adventure/thriller, where every avenue of approach is open, not only in terms of combat but player customisation. Far Cry 3 feels like a toned down version of STALKER/Skyrim, where players who are more fond of the traditional shooter genre can foray into more unknown territory, with exploration and crafting, but still only a couple of weapons. The world is beautiful, and the exploring is fun but ultimately its still about the shooting, unlike STALKER or Skyrim. The lack of a proper inventory is where this really falls down. Searching a corpse consists of the character just patting them down, and saying it gives you x dollars or x item.
Its probably great for shooter fans, but for players that consider themselves seasoned in SURVIVAL, as per the other two mentioned games, I'd suggest staying away.
tl;dr: basically a really good shooter that tries to market itself as an open-world fps, when in actual fact its just loads of empty space and bushes to cut.

The sandbox world has just about everything you could ask for. The only thing I can think of that is missing is an actual volcano, otherwise the two islands that make up this game's playable area are everything you'd expect on a tropical island. The addition of wildlife in this game adds such an aspect of realism, I found myself stalking a tiger just to watch him take down a deer or goat. This addition also adds a new type of terror/suspense to the game. There is nothing like quickly trying to escape a firefight that you plundered into, running through the jungle and finally escaping your assailants, just to be mauled and pummeled by a tiger. While the resilience and toughness of some of the animals detracts from realism, it certainly adds to the anxiety.
The firefights, especially towards the beginning are very intense. Until you unlock enough of the "skills" to boost your health bars and make body armor more effective, only a couple of bullets will drop you on the intermediate setting. However this is followed by most of the enemies being easily eliminated by a small string of fire to center mass. What is different for this game is the implementation of cover. While the system is a little rough around the edges, it does allow you to hide behind cover and then peek out and fire rounds off at hostiles.
The challenge in this game comes mostly from the improved use of enemy AI. While they are still not brilliant, they do notice sounds and are spooked by finding their buddy lying dead on the ground. The enemy itself will work together to suppress and kill you, as well as take cover to hide from your fire. The confrontations with some of the islands predators is also challenging, as well as occasionally terrifying, though the idea of a shark attack bothers me anyways. The enemies are also specialized, making some of them quite difficult to kill and makes plotting strikes against enemy establishments require careful and thorough planning.
The game overall is worth every penny just for the single player. The addition to weapon customizations and the improved system controls, should also make this an interesting and likely worthy multiplayer. This game has a few small quirks, and no one should expect a Shakespeare story, but you should expect hours of thrills and plenty of enjoyment.

Far Cry 3 is, quite frankly, one of the best games I've played. The unusual plot, beautiful setting and graphics, and great gameplay make this game one you shouldn't miss. While the plot can be predictable at times, following a few standard clichés, it is still intersting enough to be enjoyable throughout the game. The large assortment of weapons, and ability to heavily customize them, means that there are many diffrent play styles. Whether you want to snipe silently from afar, or rush in with a shotgun, this game will equip you with the right tools to do so. The beautiful graphics in this game can also not be overlooked, as I have spent a lot of time simply admiring the landscape. Once you've beaten the story, there isn't much to do, however there are online co-op and PvP modes that allow you to continue enjoying, even after you're done the story. Overall, Far Cry 3 is an amazing game, completely worth picking up whenever you can.

This game...go ahead and schedule yourself out about 3 days to just sit in front of your screen and play. The story is amazing. The character of Vaas especially...dude. So incredibly real and hate inducing. You honestly feel like he's talking through the screen straight to you. You can go anywhere and approach your missions from so many angles. Wanna use your bow? Silent kill from afar. Stealth? Silent takedown time. Not in the mood for patience? Run in guns blazing. Feel like luring some bad guys down the way straight into some mines? That's your prerogative. I struggle to think of anything bad to say about it. The only thing I could say, and this is nitpicking, the radio towers are too easy. You don't have to think at all to reach the top.

Get Far Cry 2 instead.
All the negative reviews I've seen are towards the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ nature of Uplay, which never gave me any trouble and was not a problem at all for me. Let's get to the real reason why Far Cry 3 sucks.
This game is scripted nonsense. With an open world that is literally the same green jungle all the way through, missions that force you into doing what the damn script tells you to do and shooting mechanics that just feel downright floaty. This game throws player agency out of the window in favour of explosions and trying to insult the player by giving them a pat on the back for the most simple tasks. Overall, the game's blurb of "Create your own adventure" is frankly laughable. I had more fun completing the side missions which actually give you a bit of freedom rather than telling you to do exactly what the game wants you to.
It feels like the mechanics were designed by a different team to the actual missions. You have stealth and many ways to play, but the game will force you to either take a stealthy or loud approach quite often. Why? Who knows. It doesn't benefit the game in any way and all they would need to do to make this a game I'd reccomend is stop pulling on the reins and let you complete missions your own way like you could in Far Cry 2!
Visually, it's impressive but lacking variety. Sure it's colourful, but you'll see the exact same sights throughout. Grass, trees, a shanty town, that one bit that looks kind of impressive that's scripted into the game. More care and effort has been put into the visual fidelity of the game than anything else.
So Far Cry 3 is a flashy waste of potential, with levels of player agency comparable to the last CoD game that came out. It looks pretty though, I guess.

Whether you play for headshots, backstabs, gibbs or great stories, Far Cry 3 in particular provides a visceral experience for any player.
Action FPS players will enjoy the outright havoc you can create on defended camps of pirates/mercenaries, loading yourself up with explosives and flame-throwers, not to mention flare-gunning gentleman to make your own screaming party-starter. This is balanced though with the option of stealthier play, going for a special-ops approach by sniping rim targets before dispatching with silenced SMG's, or perhaps opting for the full commando approach of bow and blade for silent and endlessly satisfying close up take-downs.
When it does come to the combat, this is what makes the game shine; the freedom of choice and random environmental events that can make any replay completely individual. You can experiment with techniques and combinations that suit you and the situation until you hit your sweet spot, which for me is dispatching entire battalions without any of them seeing me coming, basically being Batman with camo paint.
In regards to the adventure and story of the game, it's well written, thought provoking and at times legitimately scary in regards to the greatest evil out there; Ourselves. Delving into some beautiful psychological territory and being able to successfully portray their mentalities is what makes the characters of this game so engrossing and real. The character of Vaas is honestly the best portrayed character's i've encountered so far, the voice actor is brilliant, the animation and mannerisms support him so well you can't help but love him...you know, as much as you can love that sort of person.
Admittedly the QTE's do cut into the freedom of the gameplay when it comes to 'boss fights' but it does allow for expression of the protagonist...it wouldn't be as insightful if you just popped them off from 100 yards and had a monologue explain how you felt about it. So as much as I don't like QTE's, these seem pretty  justified.
Next is the environment, which is another of this game's strong points in all honestly. The 'world' is not vast but it isn't small either, and it really depends on how you choose to tackle it. Fast travel points allow you to quickly cross the map but you will miss out on all that randomly generated wildlife and firefighting, so depending on if you want to burn through the missions or really get right into the jungle, you're play-through will be quite different. I've included crafting, hunting and platforming missions in this section just to separate it from combat and narrative; the crafting is pretty fantastic, in that it's firstly a sort of tutorial for dealing with enemies without the risk of ranged damage, but if you are foolish enough to let most predators get close, especially in the early game, you're not going to live very long. This is so much more exciting than shooting at glorified paddlepop sticks and having a voice-over pat you incessantly for performing actions a child could accomplish. On the other point, platforming in this game can be repetitive at times but it's still always exciting, the slip and panic animations when you just make a ledge often causes a tight gripping of the mouse in response. The rewards at the end of these episodes are often worthwhile and you'll rarely feel cheated for that 5 minutes of leaping, ducking, climbing and diving.
Possibly the biggest letdown to this game would be the multiplayer aspect. The lobbying can be aggravating and there isn't a large enough population on the servers to justify it being anywhere on par to other AAA FPS games. The Co-Op can be really fun and adds a whole new story to the world of FarCry, but as with the game as a whole, you'll need a PC that can handle it's graphic demands.
Overall this game is a truly visceral and engaging experience if you can take on the character, if you can step into his shoes and let yourself live his story, you're gonna have a fantastic time. Be warned it's not for the fragile, there's a lot of gore, some nudity, drug references and references to social issues that you might not agree with, but they are used to engage and expand the characters for the most part.
Game in a line:
Wouldn't recommend to time-poor gamers, best played in-depth and with a willingness to be absorbed, after which will be a game nigh unforgettable.

What Far Cry 2 should have been.  All of the broken mechanics from 2 have been replaced with a very Assassins Creed like exploration/progression system.  I'm not a big AC fan, but I have to say that particular gameplay template worked well for Far Cry.
The world feels very alive with wildlife everywhere, and hunting gives you plenty of reason to explore the islands.  Stealth is actually possible now.  Plenty of weapon mods to spend your money on.  The skill system makes engaging enemies worthwhile.  Graphics are gorgeous and make excellent use of PC hardware.
Story is corny and over the top, but that doesn't really matter where you're spending most of the time running around stabbing tigers. Some of the characters are entertaining, but most are too forcefully in your face and trying too hard to make an impression to be interesting.  A few main story missions were good, most were too hand holdy for my taste, but when the game allows you to tackle objectives in whatever style you want you can generate some rewarding moments for yourself.

Pirates, mercenaries, tigers, komodo ankle-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, sharks, crazy birds and heavily armoured opponents, there is not enough adjectives to discribe the joy that can be had on these islands. This is probably the best AAA-game I have tried, and I don't normally like shooters that much. I don't mean it is the best game I have tried, but the whole experience, game mechanics end overall quality is really top notch. Very impressive.
What is great about the game?
Graphics are outstanding - The game looks and feels great even if you have to reduce the quality. Voice acting and sound in general is superb. Acting and motion capture is also very well done. Immersion is outstanding - Moving around feels fantastic, all vehicles are fun. Gunning and fighting is very well done. Interaction with people and cutscenes don't break immersion.
Game is long, but involving the whole way. The game manages well to not be frustrating. The world you are in feels alive, and you really enjoy exploring the island(s). The world "happens" by itself without your input. AI is good and some antagonists are fantastic. World and gameplay is very open, giving you lots of ways to play your own way. Story goes quite deep.
What is not so great?
Well, you need a really good machine to run it well. There is a lot of "in and out" with the menus and maps which breaks immersion. Messages and hints are too many and too frequent. (Farcry 2 had it nailed down, not breaking immersion at all.) Some skills you can aquire are quite useless. Kind of annoyed with the whole "saving rich spoiled kids"-thing.
In many ways, Far Cry 3 is superior to Far Cry 2. It is better paced, has a better story, it is less frustrating, AI is better. But in some ways, I see them as different games. Far Cry 3 is more of a dream and a fantasy, "a game", while Far Cry 2 feels more realistic. Far Cry 2 is not as "gamey" and "Hollywood-ized" either, and is more immersive. It actually still looks fantastic and does not require as much computer power as Far Cry 3. I still recommend you try Far Cry 2 considering it is quite cheap. But do not expect a similar experience to Far Cry 3 at all. Far Cry 2 needs much more patience and has many annoying flaws, still being quite a gem.
The deeper message in Far Cry 3 is quite nice, and makes you think about your actions in the game-world. The game hints at times that you are actually in a game, a dream, a fantasy. I really like this idea, it makes you more aware of yourself, in and out of the game.
There is a lot do in this game. I just finished the campaign, and did not try co-op and multiplayer which I have heard is quite nice. I took over most bases and all radio towers, but I skipped quite a few side missions, still playing this game for well over 40 hours.
But when you have finished the main story you can go back to the island if you wish to explore more, as there is a lot to find. You can also create your own maps with a really nice map editor. So there is lots to do well worth your money even at full price. I also highly recommend Farcry 3 Blood Dragon for a great spin-off with lots of humor but with the same great mechanics.

"Skyrim with Guns" they call it. And how freaking right they are! With this being released just at the end of the year 2012 it easily makes for one of the best games of the year. Having played only Far Cry 2 in the past and having somewhat enjoyed some elements of the game but never actually got round to finishing it, I was in for a ride with Far Cry 3. The main selling point for me to picking up this title was Vaas. Plain and Simple. I loved Michael Mando's role as Vaas, It was absolutely fantastic! When I saw the Character Vaas, I knew this was a game I had to get in on despite my lack of interest from the previous Far Cry games. I absolutely loved every encounter with Vaas and easily one my favorite Antagonist's to date!
Let's crack in with the detail. You play as Jason Brody. You, Your Brothers and some Friends go on a vacation in Bangkok as celebration of your Brother Riley as he obtained his Pilot License. Celebration is cut short after a Skydiving trip after having land upon a Pirate Island. You and your group get captured by the Pirate Lord known as Vaas, a Secondary Antagonist to this story. Shortly after your escape, you are aware of what goes on within the Huge open world known as Rook Islands. Slavery. Your friends have been taken captive and only you can save them against Tyranny of Slavery. You must adapt to your new surroundings or be consumed by them.
How open world is Rook Islands you may ask? VERY open! The map is huge! Tons of exploration as you wonder through the Island discovering Historic Relics, gazing at Ancient tombs, Shrines and even weapons! Rook Islands is certainly a stunning place to be. With the vast amounts of exploration you will want to be doing deep in the Jungle you are going to be wanting to get around as running simply isnt fast enough to get from point A to B. There are various ways to get around Rook Island. Ground Vechiles consist of Jeeps, Quad Bikes and even Dune Buggies! With Aquatic transportation simply boats or Jet Ski's to get around, though preferably boats. Specially if your hunting a certain predator out in those waters...
And last but not least is Air, no not Helicopters or planes but Hang Gliders! What a way to get from Point A to B... Glide to your destination and enjoy the sight bestowed upon you! Ubisoft truly went to town with the detail in Far Cry 3's enviroment and certainly wanted us to enjoy it, with the time spent in the Jungle hunting or in the air gliding across the Island, its hard not to appreciate Rook Islands Beauty and Ubisoft's hard work.
Throughout your journey ahead you will require upgrades to make Jason a more efficient Warrior. This is where the Hunting kicks into play. While exploring the Jungle you will be sure to discover plenty of wild animals that you can kill and skin so you can craft new equipment such Weapon Holsters, Increased Lootpacks, Syringe Pouches etc. A very nice feature and certinaly one I enjoyed. Prowling through the jungle with my Sniper Rifle taking out wild beasts before being bested by a Tiger. Dang! Be aware of your surroundings, The hunter is also the Hunted.
While exploring the Jungle you will come across Plants you can harvest for which you can make Syringes with to enhance Jason.  Syringes of the likes of Fireproof and the Ability to see Enemies through walls. Given that they are a timed effect but still useful. I havent crafted them all however the more creativity you have with Far Cry 3, the much better experience you will have.
Throughout the game as you hunt, complete missions, discover viewpoints (Towers that expand the view of your map, similar to those of seen in AC series) you will earn Experience. The experience will reward you Skill points in which you can use to unlock new talents in three categories. The Heron, Shark and Spider. You are not devoted to one category, you can spend your points across all three Specializations. As you begin to build up your new found traits you will begin to build up whats called "Tatau". Symbolized on your Left arm, this Tattoo represents a Warrior from the Rakyat tribe in which you aid against Vaas and his Pirates. As you progress through the game and spend more well earned skill points, the tattoo will begin to expand along your arm.
With alot of the single player aspects, what else is there to do other than explore and discover the collectibles of Rook Island? Far Cry 3 also packs in a multiplayer to boot, personally I have no interest in the multiplayer as I'm interested in the Single player mainly however it may be something to be explored in time of writing of this review however nice to see they had time to implement this in along side their Epic campaign. However it doesnt stop there! Oh no! They went even further and added a Co-op Story mode, seperate to the story of single player mode might I add! The story of the Co-op mode is set a few months prior to the story of the single player campaign and revolves around four characters, scammed out of their money by the pirates and they won't rest easy about it! Again having not played this side just yet, its still nice to see another addition to the package! More content!!!
Having spent 25hours to finish the Single Player Campaign alone while doing some hunting, side objectives and sightseeing I still have yet much to accompish. Discovering all the relics, completing the rest of the side missions and fully upgrading my arsenal whether it be my weapons or simply hunting related gear. Theres still much left after your done in Far Cry 3 and then if your curious enough to try out the multiplayer or Co-op mode that will earn you even more hours upon your gametime. Far Cry 3 is worth your time and money! I would give this game a 9/10. A must buy, The single player alone was worth it for me but yet much more to be done with this title!

Far Cry 3 definitely had some good things going for it, but it still was not without its faults.  Combat was fun, stealth play was done well enough for those that enjoy it, and I loved the open world.  Oh, and of course, the RPG elements were a welcome addition, even though choice is limited to unlock order and I reached the level cap well before the end of the game.  Unfortunately, enemy A.I. was mediocre, and when it came to stealth, enemies seemed either virturally blind or able to see through cover, depending on their type (pirates (red) v. privateers (yellow)).  Oh, and the boss fights kind of sucked.  My biggest complaint, however, would be that the game had a lot of filler content (Trials of the Rakyat, Tower Unlocks, Outpost Cleared, Supply Drops, Path of the Hunter Missions, Wanted Dead Missions, Letters Found, and Relics Found).  It was fun at first, but by about half way through, I was just doing that stuff to get the unlocks & experience (and because I'm kind of OCD about that kind of stuff).  It just started to get old by the time you've hunted down the 120th relic or did the 23rd Path of the Hunter.  I guess that's better than a short game or an empty world, but I would have like to have seen more variety with this content -well, assuming it was done well, of course; most of the side missions, were already rather forgettable.  Story missions, on the other hand, were varied and quite fun.
Overall, I'd recommend the game, especially if you can pick it up for cheap during a sale.  Combat is satisfying, the story missions are fun, and unlocking new weapons and abilities changes things up and helps to make you feel like a badass.  The a.i. could have been better and the filler content gets a little old after a while, but then again, you can always do as little or as much as you like.  I also had a few other minor gripes (like the ease at which to take fall damage, crappy inventory system, many npc's looking the same, etcetera), but I don't think they detract enough from the game to warrant getting into.  7 out of 10 stars.

This game is one of the true cases of real freedom. Not just because it's open world. Not just because ther's lots of things to shoot. And not just because if you get bored you can hurl yourself off a cliff. No, the devs of this game really went the extra mile.
For example, the hunting. Yes, you can slowly sneak up on deer before blasting it with a shotgun (if you're boring), or you can grab a flamethrower and molotov cocktails, light a section of forest on fire, and when a bear or pig runs past you trying to escape, you can stab it multiple times in the back.
Also, there's a lot of side quests. From finding a missing suicidal teen to seeing how many komodo dragons you can kill with one clip of pistol ammo, there's always something to keep you busy. Also, certain non-essential tasks can help you in the long run. Sure, it may seem boring to climb various towers to reactivate old cell phone beacons, but it'll all pay off when the air fills with smoke and you can still see every one of the dudes you are about to terminate.
Which brings me, yes, to the combat. The combat in this game is fantastic, and filled with variety. You can rip a dude's neck out and leave him out to be discovered by already terrified pirates; you can lure over a pack of wild dogs and let Mother Nature do the work. Hell, you can just run up to a guy and beat him over and over with a blowtorch, until he either dies of trauma or lights on fire.
A personal favourite of mine was to kill a helicopter pilot while he hovered over an enemy outpost, causing the vehicle to spiral out of control, crushing both the pirates and presumably two or three tigers.
Overall, this game gets a solid plus. It's Rambo, Terminator and Tomb Raider squished into one, and I love it.
God help me, I love it.

Far cry 3 is a very good game in general and you can visibly see all the good game design decisions.

However, while I don't want to spoil the ending too much, it's one of the only parts where the game lets itself down.
The final mission of the game is split two ways - Flying from the enemy base in a helicopter to 'Ride of the valkyries' in an epic mounted turret section- then going through some boring tibal love drama nonsence. Then you pick if you want to be with your friends and escape or with Citra- the tribe leader. Its a sort of moral choice sequence with no moral choice. The 'friend end' is the only real end as the other one just ruins most of the stories believeability.

Far Cry 3 was an interesting experience. The core game mechanics were very fun and responsive but the problem of the game turned out to be the story. The game went the usual GTA sandbox route where you can just roam the game world doing various activities or engage in the story missions. Those story missions just weren’t very fun. The thing is that instead of building over the existing fun gameplay they seemed to constantly take away from it by constraining the ways the player could play the missions and filling them with quick time events. To top it all off the characters and script of the game were just ridiculously clichéd and uninspired outside of barely few fun exceptions. Even the missions themselves quickly boiled down to just following markers and watching cutscenes. The main character in particular was just not convincing at all and made me question if anyone in Ubisoft knew anything about human beings. As I said the core game mechanics were very good (if you don’t count the driving sections) and at best made me think of games like Fallout 3 and Just Cause 2. Lastly, I need to point out that people making Far Cry games seem to have an endless fascination with tropics and paradise islands. I happen to hate them. Here’s for hoping that the next Far Cry game will take place in some sort of Twin Peaks inspired setting.

Far Cry 3 is an all around awesome, worthwhile experience.
SINGLE PLAYER:
The single player is the meat of the game, and it's a blast. The story is all-around enjoyable, despite a few hiccups, and it really helps to show you the full extents of what you can do in the game. For me personally, though, I enjoyed the free roam more. The island is beautiful, and the vegetation is lush. There is a nice amount of weapons, attachments and paint jobs to keep you interested. Once a weapon has been used, you can equip it for free at any vending machine in the game, which really allows you to try new things on the fly. Besides the standard weapons (Assault Rifles, SMGs, LMGs, Sniper Rifles & Shotguns), there are also a variety of unique weapons, including a flare gun, flamethrower and recurve bow, all of which help keep the game fresh. The hunting/crafting system could be a bit more fleshed out, as you will likely be nearly done crafting before even reaching the second island, and after crafting is done there is not much incentive to hunt. The core of the game, however, are the outposts. The outposts are definitely the most enjoyable part, and also allow you to really use all the weapons and equipment in interesting ways. As the outposts grow more and more complex the challenge becomes greater and greater to succesfully capture one, and the reward is always worth it. On a side note, the takedown system is also amazingly executed. It distances itself from the type of knifing prevalent in Call of Duty, and changes it up so that when you are within range (close range) it will go into a  little locked animation for the kill. It doesn't make the melee overpowered, but it makes for some awesome kills, especially when you jump off a ledge and land on an enemy.
MULTIPLAYER:
It may not be the focus of the game, but it is well done. A variety of interesting maps and fresh new modes (Firestorm and Transmission come to mind), it's a lot of fun. The unlock system works well, and there's also something called decoding -- after finishing a co-op chapter/multiplayer match, you can find encrypted data. After spending time putting it through a decoder (it decodes in the background) it can give you XP or Weapon Mods. Weapon Mods increase one aspect of a gun by a lot, while having some type of drawback. My only complaint with multiplayer is that higher end data sources take a fair bit of time to decode, with the biggest (Hard Drive) taking a solid 8 hours. This has been helped, though, by speed boosts. After you finish decoding something, you can usually send a speed boost to a friend of yours (no use to you). If you have lots of friends, you should receive lots of speed boosts which can make the waiting time much more bearable.
Overall: Great game. Awesome single player, and fresh new multiplayer as well, Far Cry 3 gets a solid 9/10.

Far Cry 3 is a game that is stimultaneously dark and shocking and yet attempts and suceeds to be amusing and humorous (even light-hearted at times).
It's a FPS sandbox game with some stunning graphics and amazing design. A huge upgrade from Far Cry 2 allowing players to fast travel but those that which to explore every single valley and cave will not be disappointed with the rewards.
The interface is easy to use and somewhat limiting at times the inventory can be a pain but it is a good balance between realism and fantasy, carry all the weapons in the world is ridiculous but only have 1 or 2 would be lame so it makes the player want to achieve crafting in order to carry more loot & weapons. All the weapons can be customized which is very nice.
The crafting is extremely simple yet works for what is needed. Hunting animals is a mixed bag some things are easy while others are quite tough (hunting a Shark with a bow for instance!).
The storyline is a dark one and attempts to showcase the "lucifier journey" doing bad things for all the "right" reasons. The ending does suck BUT... it's the journey that really kept bringing me back (almost 50 hours into just one play through).
The sound design is excellent the only fault is the car radios have the most horrible music on them. Otherwise cocking of a gun's bolt, the sound of brass ejecting, the cries of your enemies, the roar of creatures attacking, the underwater sound effects, just perfect.
The game has some really amazing qualities, particularly the feeling of helplessness at times. First time you get attacked by a shark or croc you may♥♥♥♥♥♥yourself. The soldiers can use tactics that turns you from a Rambo-wannabe into a corpse. The game can be completed either via stealth, Rambo or a balance. Some missions require one absolute over the other but that's all part of the game and makes it challenging.
Overall I do reccommend the game but be ready for some confronting scenes (not just gore), the ending is very lacking and the boss fights are unfortunately quick-time events but all the NPCs are very well done, excellent voice acting and you'll either like them and love to hate them. Hope you enjoy!

The best Far Cry game so far, combines the open world gameplay of Far Cry 2 with the tropical setting of Far Cry 1, and adds new mechanics such as crafting, hunting and levelling up to adquire new skills. The graphics are pretty decent and easy to max up even with a mid end computer. The AI is a little static sometimes and the sidequests are generally uninspired and ridiculous, otherwise there's a lot of fun to be had and a lot to explore.
The game borrows some mechanics from Assassin's Creed such as clearing enemy bases to reduce influence, viewpoints in the form of radio towers and assassination missions which must be performed with a knife.
The story is what you could expect from a class B action movie, which is made enjoyable by some excentric characters such as Vaas, but the rest is pretty forgettable and cheesy.
85/100

The definition of insanity: playing the much maligned Far Cry 2 and expecting a different result in its sequel.  As the late (RIP, breh) under-the-rader YouTube reviewer 'antiosocialfatman' put it, Far Cry 2 took the worst part about MMOs and put them in a single player game.  And while MMOs at least had some form of character progression, FC2 only had the diamond-for-guns exchange mechanic.  Ubisoft tries to rectify this somewhat with the introduction of 'talent trees' but, unfortunately the vast majority of these are either barely noticeable or total overkill (as if there's a shortage of animal skins or cash).  The 'open world' is undermined by the fact that 'loot' is merely a proxy for money.  There's no hand placed secret weapons or interesting locales/scenarios to explore-- it's an endless string of rote checkpoint clears, hunting missions, and various mini-games.  The gunplay is servicable but there are better FPS out there.  The story goes from laughably unplasuible to totally off the deep end midway through the game.  Topping it off is the inability (despite numerous attempts at ini/config tweaking) to turn off the obnoxious post processing that blurs, whitewashes, and BLOOMifies what would otherwise be visually impressive landscapes.

This review is purely opinion so please take it with a grain of salt.
The gameplay is a lot of fun and I love how being a First Person Shooter, it stays in First Person the entire time.  Unlike Halo or borderlands, it stays First Person even when you get into a vehicle, sometimes making it a bit hard to drive, which I like it.  Cutscenes, you stay in your first person point of view.
The gunplay is good, I don't feel like I am wasting bullets, except against heavies, those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s are tough.
You can buy guns or you can unlock the map and earn them all for free saving your money for upgrades.
I. Love. The. Bow.
makes me feel like rambo.
this game even has a flare gun which are always fun but it's yellow, not orange like most are. ya not a real complaint, just an asthetic personal point of view.
If you're looking for a good First Person Shooter with a sandbox world and level up abilites this game is exactly what you want.  It's worth snatching up on a sale. (and i say on a sale because steam has taught me to wait a year unless I reeaalllly reeaaaallllllllyyy want to play it, and get it 75% off.)
As for the story and characters?
I have learned I rather do not like the main character, at all.  I don't hate him completely but he's gotten on my nerves.  You run around blowing people up, whooping and holering sometimes about how fun a grenade launcher or a flamethrower is, and I agree.
but you can skin a thousand and one animals, and EVERY, SINGLE, TIME, he whines about how gross it is.
-.-
And other things here and there just bug me about him.
The only honestly likeable characters die, (some good guys some bad guys) and it bugs me the same as some a little bit that the cover guy isn't the main villian.
As for the story, it's not terrible, but personally I'm not all for it.  Sometimes dumb descisions are made but I won't fault that entirely, we're on the outside and people on the outside always see the stupid mistakes.  when you're in the heat of conflict you don't think straight and mistakes always happen, but sometimes they leade to AWESOME characters dieing. T_T
The ending is the ONLY descision you get to make and it's a dumb one. I won't say what happens but SPOILERS, the choice is kill your friends who you spent The Entire First Half Of The Game SAVING, or do the smart thing and don't.  trust me, pick the spare your friends option, Citra isn't worth it.
Overal, gameplay superb, story lacking unless you like messed up stories, then the overall game is great.

The main problem is, boss battles that should be adrenaline-pumped shoot-em-ups end up being ridiculous QTE (that's Quick Time Events, for the blissfully unfamiliar), where you're following on-screen prompts to click/press buttons at the right times. I still have been unable to finish coop, because on those occassions I try to connect, the servers are often down, or buggy and not working.
In summary, get this game on sale, and play single-player.  Pretend the boss fights were cool, and move on.  Probably the last Ubi title I buy.  Oh, and UPlay is required, and it is ridiculous.

After completing Far Cry 3 on normal difficulty, I am now playing through once more on the hardest difficulty and am trying to complete all of the missions this time. I usually don't play through a game twice, but this game is worth it. There are so many things I like about this game, where to start...
Open World: Far Cry 3 offers a massive, beautiful open world and allows the player to choose one's pace. You can explore the island, do missions, build up skills, build up gear, and follow the story all on your own time. The world is full of goodies like treasures, relics, wildlife (useful and some dangerous), plants, missions, vehicles, and more.
Story: A very simplistic summary would be that you play as a guy who was on a nice trip with his brothers and friends, but then things go downhill and you wakeup in a cage with your brother. You must then escape and save your friends all while building new skills and learning about the island. Of course, it is a rather intricate and enticing storyline that keeps you on the edge of your seat, especially when things heat up.
Gameplay: Unlike most first person shooters, there are so many ways you can choose to play. You can do the traditional guns-a-blazin, you can be like Hitman and stealth your way through, you can be like James Bond and use your surroundings to unleash hell on your enemies, or you can do what I did which is all of the above.
Characters: I thought the characters were very well done. One of the main antagonists in the game, Vaas, is personally my favorite video game villain I have encountered. A very interesting character indeed, though I won't say more than that, you will have to play it and find out for yourself. Besides Vaas, the other characters were also very well designed.
Weapons: This game has a weapon for everyone. Pistols, SMGs, LMGs, Snipers, Assault Riffles, Flame Thrower, RPG, Grenade Launcher, Bow, Flare Gun, Explosives, etc. When your weapon holster is maxed out you can carry four weapons. They are all very well balanced, nothing is too underpowered and nothing too overpowered. Very well done.
Vehicles: A fair variety of vehicles. Everything you would expect on an island like the one in Far Cry 3. Once again, nothing is too under or overpowered when it comes to vehicles. My favorite would have to be the glider, quite unique and very fun to use.
I could go on, but I'll just add one more thing because I think it was incorporated quite well. There are a few instances throughout the game where you are giving some type of drug that sends your character on hallucinogenic, soul searching journeys. They were quite entertaining and really added to the whole storyline. This is definitely a stoner-friendly game, however I haven't smoked while playing (yet anyway), though it would be fun.
Overall I would give this a 95/100. Not a perfect game, but very captivating. I'm also not a big fan of the Uplay launcher, but my rating didn't reflect on the launcher, just the single player game.

Amazing open world first person shooter with survival elements implemented.
The vegetation is dense and well-detailed. The vehicles are varied and feel satisfying to drive.
The Co-op multiplayer, however, is completely different to the hunting-survival-like single player.
Co-op gameplay reminds me of Left 4 Dead (but without the zombies). You and 3 friends run and gun your way through set paths blasting and shooting absolutely everything in your way. There are even mini-games where you compete against your friends to get the most points.
It's a bit different from the single player, and can provide a breath of fresh air if you are bored of sneaking around in the bushes stalking a tiger in order to craft a larger wallet or whatever.
The Versus multiplayer is like any other first person multiplayer game- not much to say here apart from there are some playlists which include custom maps made by the community which is a nice addition. (did I forget to mention there's a level editor included with the game?!)
Overall, a brilliant game that can fill all your first-person shooter desires.
There are some mods online which can tweak your single-player experience to make it more realistic and emphasise the survival aspect of the game, as well as make the weapons more realistic (ie: more deadly).

I bought Far Cry 3 to got a good fps experience out of it. You don't see many of them these days. Back in the day FarCry 1 was a fps player´s dream with a lot of challenging shooter action. Well... Far Cry 3 is a very different game compared to it´s predecessors.
Far Cry 3 is less of an fps game and more of a casual story game with stealthy experience gathering and item upgrade hoarding.  You start with only 1 weapon slot and you must find animals in order to craft more. The joke about this is that the game itself is ridicilously easy even on the most difficult setting. Sure you will have problems with your starting pistol, but after you get famas and mp5 with silencer (which is after 2 hours tops), the game turns into a cakewalk.
The story line was good enough, but you are just a mindless spectator in it. There are also loads of unskippable cutscenes, where you can't do anything but turn your head and press mandatory buttons in order to get forward. You naturally don't have a say on how things proceed. Music and voice acting are mostly good. The main protagonis, Vaas, can even be commended.
To sum it up, Far Cry 3 is a great casual (fps)-game, but if you want a challenging fps in your hands, this one will feel lacking in a lot of ways.

Farcry 3 does a lot of things right and a few things wrong.
Let's start with the positives.  The sandbox open world is absolutely beautiful.  It's massive, it's lush, and you'll always see the islanders out and about doing things so it really gives the world a sense of life.  Out of curiousity, I turned my graphics settings down to low and the game still looked pretty damn good.   I wasn't much of a fan of the music in the game, as most of it was very basic beats, but the ambient noises are excellent and you'll always have that paranoid feeling when you hear that tiger growl off in the distance, not knowing whether it's coming after you or just passing by.
Now the negatives.  The side missions can be quite repetitive.  They fall into the formula of "Go hunt this animal or Kill this guy with a knife or deliver these supplies before the time runs out."  It was hard for me not to get bored at times doing the side missions, because I've already done some redition of previously.  The main campaign was pretty good.  Not excellent, not just okay, but somewhere in between.  The story has a lot to be desired but luckily it's held up by an excellent voice actor cast.
The crafting and skill system is pretty cool.  My only complaint is I had a tendancy to have all my skills filled before the next set would open up, which is dependent on your main story progression.  So there would be times where I would have 3-4 skill ponts I couldn't use because the additional skills were still locked because I hadn't made it that far in the story yet.
The game has a few quirks, but overall was a very enjoyable experience.  If your a completionist, then there are tons and tons of things for you to collect and complete.  Playing just through the main story took me somewhere along the lines of 18(ish) hours, but if you strive to do everything, I would be surprised if you could easily get 35+ hours of gameplay.  I recommend Far Cry 3 who like first person shooters and sandbox worlds.  There is tons for you to explore and story will keep you interested(just perhaps not on the edge of your seat).

Far Cry 3 is far and beyond the best game of the franchise.
No mutant baboons, like Far Cry.  No horrible repetition, respawning checkpoints, and weapons that degrade faster than an ice cube on a hot summers day.  Far Cry 3 gets it right.
This game has a lot of variety, and a rather compelling story.  The character progression keeps the game interesting, making you want to look for every side quest and hidden item hidden across the massive two islands.  Unlocking new ways to takedown badguys brings such enjoyment - like pulling the pin on a badguy's handgrenade before kicking him toward his mates, and watching them all blow to bits.
Crafting and hunting quests bring something new to the game, but a sore point is inventory management.  Sadly there's no quick way to dump some of the things you pick up.  And, when you end up with 90 items that you've got to double click, delete, yes I really want to, enter...  just to remove a 'broken pair of glasses' worth $10 - it gets old quickly.

Reaching the southern island is great in that it unlocks the wing suit making island traversing quck and fun.  The downside to it is that...

you will no longer be dealing with one of the most charismatic badguys of all time.

Lots of replayability here, and well worth the funds.

Cisse Cameron, who starred alongside Reb Brown driving floor cleaners in
like they were futuristic cars, has rather famously said that she hasn’t seen the episode of
lampooning the movie, because what everybody missed was that the movie was
meant to make fun of sci-fi cliches to begin with.
has nothing to do with
but Cameron’s statement certainly does.
casts the player in the role of Jason Brody, a middle-class white college kid without a direction in life who finds himself in a place where the usual trappings of civilization are irrelevant, and he must very quickly learn to survive by any means necessary and deal with the psychological consequences of doing so.
This is the basic setup for the game, but unfortunately, it falters in never going beyond the basic. Jason needed a lot more character development, especially in the first 1/4th of the game, for his story to be sold well, and it just doesn’t happen. It's still a white-dude-power-fantasy. The plot is way too truncated to effectively sell its ideas. It’s also unintentionally racist, with a black man spouting spiritual nonsense as soon as Jason escapes the pirate camp and sending him off to be the local natives’ savour. He is, of course, immediately effective in hunting and killing, limited only by how much he can carry, which in turn is limited by how far along in the crafting system the player has progressed. A simple touch like seeing the Rakyat trying to push forward into pirate-controlled areas independant of what Jason was doing could have alleviated this considerably.
The game leaps from here into what is supposed to be Jason’s ability to cope with everything going on while trying to save his friends and family from being sold into sex slavery, but the game does not
any of it. With the opening act so short and non-eventful, it’s simply another white dude being an unstoppable FPS protagonist, and this irrevocably harms the game’s attempt to examine “what shooting does to us in a videogame.”
This isn’t to say the writing is a complete failure; many scenes stand out, particularly the scene where Jason finds his younger brother as well as the fact that one of Jason’s friends has
sold to someone and sexually abused by the time Jason finds him (the latter, however, is hurt by anemic scripting.) Citra’s sex appeal is portrayed as disturbing if not outright inappropriate. Vaas steals the show whenever he shows up, although Vaas also exits the plot
too soon in what I like to call Bioshock Syndrome: the emotional climax of the game comes too early and the rest is filled with a much less interesting antagonist. The fact that a lot of these scenes are memorable and effectively chilling for their implications makes the ultimate failure to sell Jason as a dudebro who is torn down and rebuilt by his experiences all the more disappointing.

This will sound familiar to anyone who’s played
Casey Hudson wanted

manages to sell the ideas Yohalem was going for as a mere side-effect of not screwing up the things

Excellent shooter on almost every front.  This game brings strong mechanics, polished visuals, and satisfying gunplay to the table, along with one of the best villains you'll encounter in any game on the market.  Never dull, never a shortage of things to do, you can spend 30+ hours in its single player open world alone, and it also includes co-op and multiplayer for players who are interested in that kind of thing.  The only obvious shortcoming I found in it was somewhat inferior audio engineering, but the rest of the game is so well put together that it's easily excusable.  The game provides enormous amounts of new content for people who like to rush stories, plenty of toys for those that like to mess with its sandbox, and lots of objectives to satisfy completionists. In Far Cry 3 I had the best gaming experience in years..I spent my first 4-5 hours just hunting, exploring and wondering how beautiful and realistic this world is.
I was totally immersed and never want to get out of the jungle. I really think this is the strongest point of the game - what you see, is what you get: wild animals with realistic behavior , realistic nature and weather with gorgeous environments, lots of NPC in real villages and tribes and the list can go on and on..
Exploring the entire open-world map is a feast while using all the vehicles in game is great fun, and the word that defines best the feeling is FREEDOM. There's a lot of collectibles and hidden stuff , superb animations and POV action, the crafting is very rewarding and necessary to progress.
The story was also quite captivating , for me, dealing with Vaas was one of the most intense gaming experience I had in a long time, and I recommend playing this game if only just for the sake of him.
The multiplayer and co-op modes are nice addition to the already long campaign (at least 20 hours, mine took 30) , and you level-up pretty quick (especially in co-op). I played about 15 hours of multiplayer and I'm already level 45..I was surprised to see that it's fast-paced and you can have a lot of fun, even though sometimes the lobby breaks for hours, you can try it and it will last you for a while until you get bored..
Yet another complete AAA game from Ubi, and hope to see this fantastic franchise rise through the skies in a Far Cry 4 realistic experience.
