Far Cry 3 takes the best of both FC1 and 2, adds some hallucinogenic drugs to the mix and shakes violently into a volatile, rainbow coloured goo.
And what makes the game? Vaas. The glint in his eyes, the smirk as if it's all a big joke you've failed to get, the way he talks...you know from the get go this is one insane ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The disappointing thing is, Vaas is the main baddie of the game for 2/3 of the game, when the stage is set up for going after his boss, Hoyt. And if you feel Vaas looks dangerous, wait till you see Hoyt. Colder, more calculating, Hoyt is Ras Al Ghul to Vaas' Joker to your Batman. But as dangerous as Hoyt is, he's nowhere near as disturbingly enticing or charismatic as Vaas.
The story goes, you're a privileged American youth by the name of Jason Brody, having an awesome vacation on some tropical islands with your two brothers, your brother's girlfriend, your girlfriend, and three more friends, two of which happen to be a couple. A real Brody Bunch, so to speak.
You skydive into an island and then it all goes south: you're taken hostage by modern pirates lead by Vaas, to be ransomed and/or sold into slavery. You escape and are taken in by Dennis, a social reject who found his place on the island among the Rakyat, a tribe of native warriors who seem keen to welcome outsiders in their inner circle, lead by the subtly crazy Citra.
Thus begins a tale of rescuing your friends one by one, while at the same time doing a bit of background soul searching and discovering your true self as a born warrior, supported by a cast of really well voiced and animated characters, like the aforementioned bunch, the villains (including Buck, who likes to f...) and supporting characters such as
Dr. Earnhardt. The tale takes you places, progressing at an interesting pace for the most part with minor twists and turns and even a couple of big ones, even making you do things you really didn't think you'd have to do. Subjects such as violence, drugs, change, relationships, power, even♥♥♥♥♥♥ nothing seems to be off limits. It all results in a positively ♥♥♥♥ed up choice at the end, which can be very hard depending on how invested you are in the story by the time you have to make it. The main story, however, cinematic as it may be, is merely the tip of the iceberg.
The island feels huge, and having all this environment and not filling it with stuff to do would be a real shame. Good thing they didn't pass by the opportunity, then. Let's attempt to explain how this works (a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of info incoming).
*Most of the things you do in the game (including killing enemies impressively , ie, stealthily or instantly) will give you an amount of xp. Each time you level up, you'll have the choice of spending a skill point on your mystical tatau (a fancy tattoo given to you by the Rakyat) to gain new abilities or enhance existing ones. The path of the Heron focuses on range and mobility, the path of the Shark (bizzarely) focuses on healing and destruction and the path of the Spider focuses on stealth and trade. The tattoo will be visibly changing on your character as you level up.
*The game has a relatively simple but effective crafting mechanic that allows you to craft medicine, combat, hunting or exploration-boosting drugs or containers.
*This is achieved by collecting Yellow, Crimson, White, Green or Amber leaves for the drugs and medicine, and skinning the animals you kill for their leather for the containers.
*Each container requires specific materials, so you can't just be killing boars at the beginning area and you'll be set. You want to be carrying 4 weapons at the same time? You want to have a larger ammo capacity? You want to have a larger rucksack? Hunt, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!
*The island(s) is(are) peppered with towns and camps, some controlled by the Rakyat, some by the pirates, some independent.
* The island is unofficially divided into regions depending on the radius around  pirate or Rakyat controlled camps.
*Rakyat regions offer relative safety from pirate patrols and roamers, as well as shops to sell loot or buy/acquire the impressive arsenal you'll be carrying around, which is also customisable with scopes, silencers and even paint jobs.
*Pirate regions have regular hostile patrols and roamers but, once the main camp is neutralized, it will become a Rakyat region. Once taken, this will also unlock Wanted quests and/or Hunter quests.
*Wanted quests will require that you kill your target with a knife, which depending on their posse might require some really creative stealth.
*Hunter quests require you complete a hunt with a specific weapon, and later ones will have you hunt the rare animals that are required for the top-tier containers.
*The map is obscured by sabotaged radio towers, which you'll have to climb in a display of daredevil platforming to get back online. Each radio tower fixed will, on top of revealing part of the map, permanently unlock a couple of weapons at the shops for free instead of having to buy them.
*The islands have a healthy dose of minor quests (old lady and the plane crash, shudder), as well as races and supply runs (glorified races).
*There's a whole lot of relics scattered around the islands for you to find, as well as pirate memory cards, as well as letters from the Japanese soldiers stationed there during WW2. These are, of course, just collectibles, but at least one skill will need 5 relics found to become obtainable.
*The game boasts an impressive array of weapons, from pistols to heavy machineguns, from flare guns to flamethrowers, from the silent bow and its special arrows (incendiary or explosive) to the acetyline torch required to fix damaged vehicles. Oh, and also a lot of vehicles. And ziplines. And gliders. And later on, even a wingsuit.
*The whole island reacts dynamically, sometimes to your favor, sometimes not so much. Start a fire, and it might spread towards an outpost and create enough chaos so you can take advantage of the situation. Release a predatory animal in captivity, and it will attack whatever is close to it. Shoot a tire of a patrolling jeep, and it might veer of course and down a cliff. Then again, it might just all go♥♥♥♥♥♥up.
Be warned, this will squeeze everything it possibly can out of your graphics card. But, oh me oh my, it's definitely worth it. The island, characters, foliage, wildlife and effects are so beautifully rendered they will leave you gasping at the screen. The indoor environments seem to detract from the overall wow factor, but then again, you won't be spending that much time indoors.
The audio also surprised me: crisp and clear, you can actually tell what's going on in the general area just by listening closely. Is that a firefight I hear way off in the distance? Sure enough, it is. Was that a low growl? Sure enough HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥A LEOPARD ARGHLLLghglhlhlhl! No sound is just filler here and it all serves a purpose, from the tiniest sound effect to the mostly pitch-perfect voice acting. Music only kicks in at specific bits to enhance that cinematic feel, and it works beautifully. Keep your ears pricked for "Ride of the Valkyries".
All in all, Far Cry 3 is the shining jewel in the franchise, and one of the few sequels that managed to surpass every single game in the series before them in every single aspect. Do not pass it by.

Much better than Far Cry 2. This was a pretty good shooter all around, guns sounded great and the bigger and more powerful guns had a satisfying feel to them. The survival aspect was done nicely, you can use pretty much everything in your environment to craft useful support items or gear which you can upgrade over time. For example, you can upgrade your holsters with animal hides to increase the number of guns you can carry at once. One big improvement over Far Cry 2 is that there is tons to do in the game becides the main quest. Far Cry 2 sported a large open world map, but had very little to do in between missions. This one has camps you can take over, kill missions, hunting missions, challanges, and collectable items that encourage exploration. It also has a fairly interesting plot that keeps you engaged and has some pretty cool characters you meet throughout. I highly recommend this one, especially if Far Cry 2 left a bad taste in your mouth.

Far cry is a great first person free roaming game which is non-linear, meaning you can choose to do what you want within the game.  You can choose to hunt animals for skins to upgrade your equipment, hunt for collectibles, win races, conquer outposts controlled by pirates and so on.
The actual story missions could be little less linear and more varied but it does the job. It has some memorable characters in it (Vaas, Bambi, Sam Becker, Hoyt)
The co-op missions are a lot of fun, my problems with it is the public co-op, and the fact that you cannot choose the map you want to play unless you're the host, which doesn't happen often.  This leaves you to be slotted into a map which you might not want to play because you've played it too much or you would like get the achievement for completing another map.
By the way, you do not get the acheivement for a map if you entered the map half way through a session - you must start from scratch. Another issue with entering a session midway through is you have to wait until the other players reach the next checkpoint to actually start playing which can take a long time on some maps and difficulties.
This can all be avoided if you can organize private games using private co-op with your friends.
Multi-player is the same old stuff really. It's not bad, but if you were honestly going to play a multiplayer fps, there are better ones out there.
I came to this game from the position of never having played a game in this series before; so if you're in the same boat you wont be disappointed.
Far Cry 3 is an awesome game with amazing graphics and a decent story-line.

You've been captured by pirates, and it's up to you, Jason Brody, to rescue your friends and get the hell off the island. As action heroes go, Brody is an unlikely one. While Far Cry and Far Cry 2's protagonists had military or mercenary backgrounds, which at least explained their ability to reload an assault rifle in three seconds, you're just an over-privileged Californian bro in his early twenties stuck in a nightmare situation.
Far Cry 3 is one of the best open world games ever.

Far Cry 3, for me, is what Far Cry 2 should have been. In its predecessor the game lacked a proper story and also the game was very difficult. I remember the creators explaining it with the story, i.e. in order to really grasp the reality of the harsh African environment the game had to be hard even on a normal difficulty level.
Far Cry 3 finally has a story and a more interesting protagonist. Also, the antagonist is memorable - his attitude, the voice acting, everything related to his personality stands out. The game gradually gets more difficult and you have a sense of progress here - there are no respawning enemies at the outposts any more: once you capture an outpost the local natives will take full control over it. They later on send patrols to further explore the island so it is now common to see them fighting with the enemies. I liked this approach as you could truly feel you were part of a story here and the fate of an entire people was dependent upon you. Oh, you want to clear an outpost in a much better way? (e.g. following the stealth approach) No worries, the game lets you reset all outposts so that you can complete these again earning some extra achievements.
Proper fauna was also missing in the predecessor. Here you have all kinds of animals you can hunt. Hunting is important as by obtaining the skin / hide of your prey you can apply upgrades to your gear. You can have greater pouches to have more money with you or store more ammunition. I liked how you can even pick up herbs so that you can craft syringes that grant you an extra ability for a short period of time to make battles easier.
And of course we have an enormous amount of collectible items scattered throughout the island. They are atop mountains or deep within in hidden caves. You need to swim in from the outside only to suddenly be attacked by a crocodile.
Far Cry 3 is an exceptionally good game. If you don't mind signing up for UPlay (achievements are logged via that instead of Steam) you should not have a problem with this game. It is beautiful, it is entertaining, it has a good story and an amazing wildlife (e.g. a tiger can easily attack a deer in front of your eyes). And what's more in order to gather all collectibles and complete all side missions the game will hold you captive for at least 50 hours. And this is only the single player campaign as you still have coop mission and multiplayer.

A very good sandbox FPS, although with some detracting elements in my personal opinion. The islands are pretty damn well made and there has been time and effort spent in building a believable backstory, history and culture for the Rook Islands.
The game running and shooting mechanics are also pretty good, where you won't instantly shoot if you are running and switching between weapons feels believable, along with the sliding mechanics which are worth a mention. There are also a nice amount of weapons to choose and unlock from. The enemies are also nice and varied and can pose a challenge if you stay exposed too  much.
The story itself is not bad, but maybe it is me, I just felt I expected what would happen before they happened and found most story elements too predictable. Another thing which actually ended up bugging me is that throughout my game session I probably killed enough tigers to have reduced the overall worldwide tiger population by a wide percentage margin. Tigers, leopards and bears you encounter should in my opinion have been more rarer. And bull-sharks are ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, I happily rammed them with my jet skis whenever I could.
I also feel the Skills system was very redundant in many places, with abilities that were hardly useful, but also some which should have been unlockable earlier (You unlock your skills three times throughout the story, having one set of skills available in beginning, another set further in and then last set of skills a good way into the game).
I would still recommend the game, as it is quite fun and if you spot it at bargain price, get it. I would advice though that while it is Steam, it will start up Uplay, but not been that much a hassle really.

The game itself is pretty fun. Good voice over acting. The main character's fight within himself is pretty fun to watch despite the annoying "I don't have the power" and "I'm not strong enough" cheesiness at the beginning. What killed me with the game is the bugginess. When you are on a story mission, you can't save at all. I restarted the first part of the game three times because I didn't have a full 45 minutes to get to the point where the story was done and it would save, so I would have to start all over again and listen to the same story again. Then, if you alt tab out of it, it goes into windowed mode and you have to go back to options to change it. There are virtually 0 sound options to turn up cinema, voices vs sound effects. The sound is really an issue because on two separate computers, I've had a wireless headset battery die, and the game will not output sound again without closing down.. which is a problem if you’re in the middle of a story since you can't save. Additionally, sometimes if you open it up and it crashes, steam will think it is still open and not let you open again. To top it all off, it's on Uplay. If you've ever dealt with Uplay and the issues that come with going from Steam to Uplay, you won't want to do it again.
The game would have been lots of fun and if you don't run into bugs, I bet it is. I've ran it on two separate computers with decent builds and encountered bugs on both. There are a lot of YouTube videos out there for fixing sound issues and save issues, but it's just not worth putting any more time into the game. The lack of ability to save whenever I want in a story campaign and bugs causing me to repeat stories, made me uninstall.

Far Cry 3 definitely sets new standards in terms of story narration and atmosphere. Still I have several points, which led me to not recommending this game, after having finished it.
In the first 15 hours I was hooked and really enjoyed the game, liked the story missions, the whole drug experiences, the fluid animations, graphics style and gameplay. I even liked the grinding for better gear.
What was annoying from the very beginning is the horrible crafting and item management menu. In Farcry 2 they managed it to keep the game completely immersive and in FC3 this feeling is destroyed everytime you craft a syringe or look at the map while driving when you switch to the cumbersome menu. After the mentioned 15 hours mark, the gameplay became very stale. It's nice to have a sandbox game where you can do so many things, but 90% of these things are irrelevant like playing poker, throwing knives, looking for letters from WW2 or completing side quests. Actually this game is completely linear while being a sandbox game, which makes all freedom pointless. You can never make a decision which actually influences the story. It is not that I don't like linear games, I really enjoyed Max Payne 3, which is almost ridiculously linear. FC3 is not really focused onto the story and character development over the whole game and i found it very tiring to complete it. I also didn't like the boss fights, the mostly great story missions peaked into. Just a bunch of quick time events embedded in a virtual LSD trip, which were not really challenging.
If I had only played the first 15hours I would have given it a 9 or 10, but in the end I wouldn't give more than a 6. It's definitely worth to have a look at it, but it's not worth to put 30hours in to see a pointless ending.

CYNDERBLOCK's Far Cry 3 Review
One way that I have heard Far Cry 3 described is Skyrim with guns. While Far Cry 3 hosts a beautiful open world jungle, Skyrim with guns doesn't quite do this game justice.
Graphics 10/10
If you have a video card powerful enough to play this game on high/ultra, I recommend you do. This game is stunning from the water to how the jungle plants move and feel as you move through the world. Plants will move and sway as you move through them, hightening your emersion.
Music/Soundtrack 7/10
Some of the more "native" music was nice to listen to at times but overall it wasn't anything that made you just stop and listen to the in-game music for an extended period of time.
Cinematics 8/10
All of the cinematics (if you can call them that) take place in first person so you always feel a part of what is happening around you. This can sometimes really excel the experience as something life threatening is happening but others times you feel like something else could be going on in the scene but you can't see all of it because your view is restricted. This is all part of the first person experience however.
Story 6/10
Content 10/10
This game will not leave you bored. From main/side quests, radio towers, outposts to retake, mini-games, collectables to find and more, you will not be left asking what is there to do.
Controls 9/10
On mouse and keyboard the game feels very smooth. You don't get the feeling like on some PC games that it was designed for a controller and M/K was just an after thought.
Gameplay 8/10
Far Cry 3 feels like your standard modern FPS. I felt crafting was too streamlined with only needing the plants/skins and no other components to make syringed and bags.
Multiplayer 8/10
Co-op missions are tons of fun and a welcome addition. Player vs player multiplayer has some interesting things that make it unique but nothing that I felt will keep your coming back for more on a long term bases.
Final Verdict 8.25/10
Far Cry 3 is a great game that would have been worth every penny of it's original purchase price and was a downright steal when I got on Steam sale. I look forward to the next installment of the Far Cry series and hope they add more gameplay features (better crafting) and have a better story.

I have really mixed feelings about this game. On one hand, the production value is amazing. It reeks of money. On the other, its pretty dull and offensive.  You are given a very large beautiful environment but not too many things to do.
Missions:
Hunting - go to an area and kill an animal with a specific weapon
Racing - race against the clock on a vehicle.
Medic - pretty much racing
Bounty - find a target and kill them
Unlock safehouse - take out a camp of dudes (you'll be doing this a loooot)
Story missions - fighting
The combat is a nice mix of stealth and actual gunplay, it feels very satisfying sneaking around and taking dudes out one by one with only a knife. You can also tag enemies with your binoculars so you can keep an eye on them on your radar and when they're behind walls, a bit like the Arkham games.
The problems:
The game gets tedious after a while. I'm the kind of person who feels obligated to finish after investing so many hours though, so I'll see it through to the end. Unlocking safehouses loses its appeal. The racing and medic missions feel kind of pointless and hunting also loses its appeal after a while.  Now, I'm willing to a slog through a less than spectacular gameplay experience if there is a great story pulling me a long, but in this game, that is not the case.  The writing is ♥♥♥♥ING TERRIBLE. It's also a pretty racist game.  It's a white savior story of a bunch of spoiled rich white kids treating other cultures as novelties.  They get kidnapped (and they deserve it) and the protagonist Jason has to become the savior of all the island's natives (because them colored folks are too weak to save themselves). It's atrocious and takes itself so goddamn seriously while being atrocious.

Fantastic game. So many great factors. Predators in the wild will sometimes inadvertently help you by jumping out from the jungle to attack enemies... or sometimes mess up your stealthy masterplan and cause you to alert the enemy to your presence when you're shooting a tiger in the face to get it off you, crocodiles blend in with the shallow water -- there's just so much. Hunting animals allows for upgrades, and picking up plants allows you to craft temporary buffs.
The world is beautifully fleshed out and if you spend time doing the side quests/activities/item searching (there's a lot), you'll get a lot out of this game...
Take the island over by climbing towers for map vision, and take out enemy camps for control.
Many vehicles, flight suit, parachute -- there are plenty of ways to get around the jungle. Gain experience and build your tattoo (skill tree) for more efficient gameplay. The game also maintains a level of realism to try and keep you immersed in the atmosphere (switching around menus is a minor gripe, and not a major issue when you consider Far Cry 2 used in game menus)). -- The game does have a some cool "Max Payne" hallucination sequences using drugs as the machina. Also the game has some pretty cool temples which made me feel like Indiana Jones at times.
So many weapons (which feel good to use), good AI, good difficulty, good story, good characters... a great all around game.
I do recommend... you need to experience it for yourself since there's so much I left out. Although the game is fantastic, I'll say I hated the quick-time-event boss fights, but again, it's ignorable when you look at the game as a whole.
Moments that stand out: setting a dock on fire by flamethrower-ing an enemy, then low on health needing to retreat from enemy fire... I go to jump into the water and notice 2 sharks circling.
Not many games can scare/startle me anymore, but this game made me jump a couple of times (running away from angry cougar only to have a crocodile grab me in shallow water).
Do get this game, worth every penny for entertainment value -- especially next time it's on sale.

I'd like to start with the good stuff. And there's a lot of it! Up until now the strong suit of this franchise wasn't the story or voice acting, but rather the immersive open world gameplay and the excellent realism. That's why it was an incredibly pleasant surprise to find out Far Cry 3 managed to produce one of the best story lines and character builds I've recently seen, while at the same time keeping those features we loved so much in the previous games. I could actually feel Vaas's psychotic rage and couldn't wait to discover what was to come in the next main story mission. On the other hand, the islands are full with side quests and activities that can keep you distracted for hours. Needless to say, the graphics, animations and the actual sceneries in this game are just beautiful. I couldn't enjoy them fully though, because I played on my laptop and I have a relatively small screen and weak GPU. Still, I could run it fine at high settings with reasonable framerate and get really gorgeous visuals. Weapon variety is pretty wide and everything is customizable. The AI is really well done. Enemies will run for cover and try to flank you when you are detected. They will also estimate the direction from which a shot came when trying to find you, so if you want to snipe them off one by one, you should behave like a real sniper and change position after a shot or two.
And now for the only drawback I found in the game. If you want to only play the single player campaign, this will not affect you at all. However, if you try to do any public co-op or multiplayer, you will probably be as disappointed as me. Multiplayer just doesn't work 80% of the time. It either getsyou stuck in an empty lobby, or makes every player's name invisible to the rest, or it gets stuck on the loading screen. I am trying to play this from the UK and am having great difficulty. I don't know if they are planning to patch this soon or if it's just a temporary server problem, but it is really annoying that I can't play, because it seems so much fun from the few games I've managed to get into so far. I've been stuck in the lobby with lots of players and they are experiencing the same thing. Hope it gets fixed soon.
So if you like an excellent open world, story based single player experience with breathtaking visuals, you should definitely pick this up! It now gets good discounts, because it's been a while since the release, so you can probably get it for 1/4 of the price during a sale. On the other hand, if you want to have an enjoyable multiplayer experience, you should probably wait and see if they come up with a fix for the issues first.

I grew to love this game. The gameplay, to be precise. I couldn't really care less about the spoiled white boy protagonist aside from the fact that he's me in the game, so the story sort of... got in the way, at times. Held me back from gaining skills due to encounter-locks versus XP lock outs, that sort of thing. It's the exploration of Far Cry 3 that really appealed to me: the exploration of two beautiful islands with lots of violent potential. I went totally Indiana Jones in this game and loved it.
The variety of enemy takedowns possible with the use of stealth and position appealled to me. They feel fluid, gritty, intense. The game features some kill-challenges that require you to take out the target with a knife among a bunch of bodyguards, which only helped encourage getting more proficient with the takedown system. The reward for successful takedowns was many times more experience than a simple gunshot frag.
The vehicles are all fun to use, the more off-road, the more scenic the game becomes. I rode a jetski through a mangrove river, a buggy from the top of a mountain ridge down to the beach, and would off-road Jeeps just for the experience of it. There is also a wingsuit in the second-half of the story that allows gliding and parachuting. That was awesome!
The downside of the game really isn't anything major, but a variety of minor niggling things. They reoccur frequently but are easy to dismiss.
*I play using a keyboard and mouse, but the game constrained my assignable hotkey choices to just two number keys, 7 and 8. This meant breaking up gameplay, usually when under fire, to access the menu to get to items that could have easily been assignable using other keys. That disrupted many instances after long periods of seamless gameplay.
*I'm unsure why the game required me to be standing directly on top of and looking at the many useable items in order to interface with them, but that plus having to hold the use key down was annoying.
*Such beautiful island design. I really liked the mountain cliffs! I wanted to scale them free-hand, but sadly could not. Many times an ascent did look like it was possible, and perhaps half of it was, before hitting a wall... the only way up is the way that the developer gave you, most of the time. Just follow the continuous grassy patches, and you can ascend.
*At times I had completely no idea how to spend money, and my limited inventory was full and needed to be sold off. My ammo was maxed out, my armor was 100%. All of the guns available for sale were already owned. The solution presented itself in an odd way: purchasing extraneous weapon attachments and vanity color schemes for weapons.
Bottom line, this game is worthy of thunderous revelry because of its mechanics and is only held back from vaster glory because it felt like a constrained port with some oddish design decisions to me.

Ok, so i finished the main story line...Here are my thoughts.
Overall I can give this game a 5/10. (Thankfully bough ti ton sale at 75% off so not too grumpy about it!)
The game starts off with an explosion of what promises to be a fantastic, story-driven, epic adventure. For the first few minutes of the game I actually really enjoyed myself, it was obviously a very linear tutorial lesson but still good none the less. Sadly not long after this the story begins to veer off in an uncontrollable spiral of random "Let's see what kind of ♥♥♥♥ing absolute nonsense we can place here and try and force it into the plot!" shenanigans. I would honestly compare the way this story barrels towards some form of closure to the train wreck that was the last Indiana Jones film, which is incredibly frustrating given the potential of this type of story. By the end, you feel no real connection to the characters in the game. The only exception being one of the bad guys you are out to kill in the game, Vaas(sp?) is probably the strongest personality in this game and he is a disposable character...this makes no sense to me.
Enough with the story that has more holes in it than a block of swiss cheese, on to the visuals. Here is where the game earns it's highest rating from me, at a staggering 7/10. Most everything is very pretty to look at, especially the water and the foliage. Some of the props however are so glaringly not completed it almost pisses you off. Ever seen the inside of a Japanese Zero's cockpit? Don't expect to see it here either, they apparently ran out of funding so it looks like it was made from rock and the pilots needed no guages...or controls...or a seat. I could go on and on with these but it wasn't game breaking, just a tad bit distracting at times.
Sound? It had it. Actually a part of the game that I truly enjoyed and I wish they had more of these kind of events, involved burning some weed fields with a flamethrower with a fantastic dubstep song to go along with the whole experience. It all tied together really well and the music made it just that much more satisfying frying stuff with a flamethrower.
There are a few things that really killed the game to the point that I don't think I can bring myself to play back through it again. The typical collision issues are a big one. Some fences I could plow right through, only to be stopped by a 2 foot tall palm leaf sticking out of the ground...seems legit right? The terribad terrain "Steepness" issues were also incredibly frustrating. I know the character you play isn't a Navy Seal or anything, but not being able to run up a slightly steep hill at all makes for an incredibly annoying run anywhere. And to clarify, by slightly steep I mean literally a child could walk up some of the places this guy can't sprint up.
Enemy AI? *laugh* This is another game that falls into the category of "Increased Challenge = More Mindless Waves Of NPC fodder." Seriously what is the though process here? You are halfway through the main story and the only thing that changes from mission to mission is the ridiculously high number of screaming mad weirdos you have to take out. This excess holds true to every mission in the game that I have seen, inclucing all of the optional side missions.
TL;DR
Pros:
-It's decently pretty for a game nowadays
-It has sound
-The story starts of with incredible promise
Cons:
-Collision/Balance issues out the wazoo
-AI isn't great (they just charge at you, that's it...even the snipers)
-Story starts strong, makes you want to care about the actors. Ends with a fizzle.

Far cry 3's best moments are also some of my best moments in gaming, I'll leave my love for this game aside and try be fair evaluating it's aspects.
First of all, you can feel the Far cry 2 engine here, similar animations and gunplay, but its definitley improved.
Graphics are pretty, shaders could have been a little less saturated for a more realistic look, but its an art direction choice, still beautiful anyway! I found a few bugs, objects revealing geometry, shadows loading in a weird way and black textures appearing on roads whenever I was nearby, It breaks immersion but don't compromise the fun.
Gameplay is fluid, animations are well made, guns feel powerful and there are plenty to choose from your loadout, you can craft boosts from herbs you harvest in the jungle, use a bow that add's a Hunter feel that we all love, and take a stealthy approach if that's your thing, that was something I wasn't sure it would work out well but It did, I finished the game using the knife and bow mostly.
Performance is pretty fair, the game runs well if you have a good machine and still pretty even on medium specs, I played this with an GTS450 on medium and then maxed out with a 650ti Boost, running with 40fps most of the time.
Story and characters are quite memorable, did I ever tell you the definition of good character design? you got it.
After you finish the story you still have activities to complete, hunt & assassination missions, outposts to clear,  towers to climb and work your magic to unlock new weapons, it's a very rewarding game and it has lore on every item you acquire. I still have to try the co-op, if you're reading this maybe we should give it a try!?

+ Stealth is an option
+ Replay value
+ Burning weed with Skrillex™

Almost every mission and sidequest is fun. Some games pad themselves out with pointless and boring collectibles, but Far Cry 3 is nearly the opposite. I gladly hunted down animals for more crafting materials, and loved assassinating local warlords. Parts of the story are ridiculous if not just poorly-written, and the story peaks partway through. That doesn't matter - Far Cry 3 is fantastic.
Graphically, it's beautiful. I love seeing a blue sky and a lush jungle as opposed to a grey post-apocalyptic landscape.
Games that do the same thing as Far Cry 3 (crafting better weapons by killing enemy creatures, climbing to the top of towers to get a better map, taking over strongholds) may feel stale after playing this game. Or if you play those other games first, Far Cry 3's sidequests may feel stale.

So, just finished this game and I gotta say...I enjoyed it. (Edit: I did NOT play online, so my review is specifically for single player.)
Before I say anything though, this is from Ubisoft....which means you'll need to install Uplay beforehand. It installs automatically when you install Far Cry 3. Not only that, there are no Steam achievements - only Uplay achievements. I will at least add, that certain achievements will give you "Uplay points" that let you "buy" certain DLC for the game, like a special gun or music, etc. There's this one "DLC" called "TESTING UNIT"......Don't get it. Save your Uplay points, because it's literally just you shooting a few dogs and then running out of a poison gas-filled area. When I finished it I was pretty disappointed. Very short and very *shrugs*. Didn't even get a reward for it (I think you get exp though. So if you don't care about Uplay or any other Ubisoft PC games, go ahead, I guess.)
Graphics were awesome (even on low-mid settings, since my gaming laptop is a bit outdated). The stunning vistas seriously made me stop what I was doing and look around in awe. Beautiful, beautiful stuff.
Gameplay was excellent. Sneaking around and stabbing multiple enemies before using your last enemy's grenade to kill a group of unsuspecting enemies in front of you is just...a sight to behold. Gunplay was also very well done, though I tended to stay very sneaky - both because you were heavily rewarded with sneak-kills as well as I didn't want to kill my framerate with too many explosions (Even though said explosions were awesome.)
Enemy AI, however... a hit and miss. Sometimes they were smart and were able to weed me out of my hiding spots while other times they seemed far too easily distracted. Animal AI however, was much better. I think the more aggressive animals though should've been a bit more random with their agro. Tigers, pumas, bears (oh my) just instantly went after you - in RL I doubt they'd do that.
Controls were good. I used keyboard+mouse and had no real trouble. I think I really should've rebinded the "item" keys somewhere else though, since 6, 7, and 8 number keys are a bit rare for me to use in most games. But that was just my problem.
Storyline was very well done. Quite a few twists and turns. The main character's voice really felt like he was just some guy that got dropped into hell. Part of me didn't like it because I wasn't used to hearing my main character's voice so "innocent". That's not a bad mark, however.
Crafting system was interesting, but flawed in my opinion. It didn't take a whole hell of alot of time to craft - everything -. I was probably mid way through the game by the time I had everything I could craft other than a few items that needed me to kill rare animals from particular Hunt missions.
The levelling system is pretty good as well. You have multiple trees you can go through, and you're able to eventually max them all. The problem though lies in what I had stated earlier - you get far more points being sneaky than going Rambo. Though I understand that reasoning, it kind of stops the Rambo players from enjoying themselves. Seriously - a sneak kill can give 5x more exp than a normal one. Liberating a camp undetected gives you 1550 exp while going in guns blazing (which can actually be harder in some areas) nets you only a quarter of that. I was at max level by the middle of the game.
The UI in this game is...not good. It feels as if it was tacked on, and I found myself crashing once in awhile while buying or selling items. Very aggravating. Luckily there are autosaves every time you go anywhere. The menu simply takes you far too out of the game. Why cover up the beautiful scenery whenever I want to pause the game? Definitely a bad move.
Missions were very cool. Side missions didn't even get monotonous - though Hunt = kill certain animals with certain weapons and the bounty hunting quests = kill a particular enemy with a knife, you were given almost full range on how to go about these missions. I never felt like I didn't want to do something......other than when I had to dive deep, deep into the ocean to grab a relic (one of the many collectibles in the game). Sharks....yeesh.
Overall, it's a ton of fun even with the stilted exp rates, UI elements, and the forced Uplay. If you like open world and FPS games, get this one.

This game is really good.
Far Cry 3 is open, original and plays beautifully. The story is pretty good and personally, I liked the insanity theme, in spite of it only being present on fixed moments in the game. Besides the story, the game is also quite unlinear most of the time. You are able to take over enemy outposts scattered over the game word and that can be done in from any direction. What is really good too, is the fact that this game adds a lot to Far Cry 2, which was already a great game back in the day. A lot of pleasant features are present, such as weapon customization, a wingsuit and good graphics. The main villain is written quite well but ( SPOILER: halfway through the game he is switched out for a slightly less impressive, but still nice different antagonist END OF SPOILER).
It is also nice that, unlike Far Cry 2, which usually placed unrealistic cliffs next to the road to prevent you from cutting through the map, this game is truly unlinear. There are no unrealistic obstacles anywhere so you can go pretty much everywhere in a straight line.
One important issue that I have is the difficulty, in that it is way too low for my taste. I was able to play the game on maximum difficulty with only some places near the end where I died a lot, and generally speaking I'm not THAT good at FPS'es.
I tried the multiplayer as well. It is simple, but quite satisfying to play. I would not let it influence your choice: to buy or not buy, that is a question that only the single player may answer, as the multiplayer is quite empty at the time of writing.
The difficulty aside, this game has nearly everthing you can wish from a first person shooter: Nice graphics, good story, unlinear environments and a fair amount of variety.

This is actually an open world RPG pretending to be a shooter.  Lots to explore and find and an overall good pace.  Maybe a touch long (took me over 60 hours to complete), but then again, I completed *everything*  so YMMV.
Cool weapons to suit different styles of play, and while many of the skills were quite useful several were a bit lacking although .  There were a few elements that peaked-out way too early for me.  There was a somewhat interesting crafting element, but that finished up around two thirds of the way through the game.  I maxed-out my characters skills about three quarters of the way through.
There isn't enough to spend your money on either.  Later in the game, you almost always have maximum money and have really nothing further on which to spend it.
A few times, the game really put you on rails and there was a bit of an idiot plot at times (as in the lead character had to make idiotic choices to move the plot forward), but overall it wasn't bad.  More off-putting to me were the occassional dream sequences or scripted fights where you had to click a button or hit a particular key at an indicated time.   Those took me out of the immersion of  the game.
Overall, 8/10

FC3 is an absolutly gorgeous game, the world looks and feels amazing, the weapons are solid and the flamethrower is a joy! The mechanics are sound, the guns handle well, there are lots of them and each has their strength and weaknesses.  The game is a stunning sandbox and does an impressive job creating a balance between exploration and goal setting, combining a simple crafting system that allows you to hunt down various animals to craft better gear while having you hunt down towers and new enemies in order to unlock new weapons.
In addition, the islands are dotted with enemy bases, making the surrounding areas dangerous with respawning enemies until the bases are destroyed.  The game also allows players to handle situation steathily (a very rewarding approach) or the gung-ho approach, both different and each has their own rewards.
Add in a bazillion pickups such as money, ammo, collectables and drivable vehicles(Cars, trucks, boats, handgliders etc) and there is no shortage of things to do.
And then there is the main campaign/story.  Personally it is great and when looking at it from the perspective of the character you play makes it all the better.  I cannot elaborate more on why without spoiling so the best way is to see for yourself.  All I can say is, have an open mind and put yourself in the mindset of the character you play.
The only negatives I can think of are the fact that once a base has been neutralised all the enemies in that region dissapear leading to a lack of action ones large swaths of territory have been cleared.  That being said, bases can be "reactivated" if your trigger finger is getting itchy.
Also, the money/purchase system is not well thought out as most weapons can be unlocked and made available for free.  Not a huge issue however.
Lastly, the game suffers somewhat from a lack of replayability.  Once you have played the game once, done the main quest, cleared the island and gotten all the collectibles (straightforward to do in a single playthrough) there is little to keep you coming back unless you want to try a different approach (direct vs stealth).  Then again, it is always a joy to revist this beautiful world from time to time.

First thing I want to say is that I have a lot more playtime on this game then what steam is showing. For whatever reason steam doesn't record my hours played on occasion.
That said let's talk aboot the game. I loved it. I always had a place in my heart for FPS games and open world games and this brings both together in a splendid manner. The gameplay is great and involving and the best thing is you choose how to play it. You get to choose how to do things and what to do first. You could, like me, spend the first 10 or so hours just roaming the world, hunting and crafting and killing things galore. Or you could focus on the story and do side activities when resources are needed as the game becomes more difficult. The weapons aren't anything crazily innovative or creative but all of them feel different and with the addition of customization of these weapons, both functions and painjobs make using them a real joy. The silent and deadly bow, the large, heavy and noisy shotgun, the revolver you keep as a last resort, and the sniper to snipe the stragglers.
If you haven't noticed I really like this game. Another reason being the story. While most people on the internet, mainly reviewers had some weirdly harsh things to say about the story it's pretty good and the story missions themselves are rather enjoyable to play. The characters are usually well developed and they have realistic dialogue for the most part.
While there are a few downsides, most of which minor, I still recommend this game to anyone that likes guns, open world gaming, or strategic thinking(especially on the harder difficulties) this game might be for you, so why not have a play?

This is one of the best single player fps games I have ever played. The combat feels great and exploring the gorgeous island is extremely satisifying.
There is plenty to do with the rpg-ish elements and the crafting system. However; you can completely ignore that aspect of the game if you wish and just focus on shooting/knifing people. Ironically, melee combat is very satisfying and the game is designed such that it encourages you to plan your attack so that you sneak up on enemies and take them out.
The gameplay itself reflects the open and explorable island. You can choose to arm yourself with explosives and charge in to fights gun blazing, sneakily take out your enemies without alerting them with your knife, or any other strategy of your choice.
The only negative thing I have to say about this game is that Vaas (the villain) doesn't have a greater presence in the game. Seriously, his character is just awsome, in every sense of the word.

Remove the grapple from Just Cause 2, switch the viewpoint to first-person, and add in some (slightly awkward) crafting, better AI, and a whole big pile of stealth opportunities, and you've got Far Cry 3. It's not particularly original, and the story is even annoying (I disliked the protagonist from the start, and nothing changed that), but it's a huge, interesting and beautiful open world where exploration alone (especially on a hang glider) is a delight. That's what makes the game worthwhile.
There are a lot of other things to do, of course. Hunting and crafting are welcome additions, though they are rather awkwardly implemented; syringes in particular are a pain to craft and use, though an important part of the game. There are a lot more collectables which are thankfully well-implemented. (You can buy maps of where they are, but even with these some of them are a welcome challenge to get. I do wish they'd delayed making the maps available until much later in the game, though.)
The main thing the game drops from Far Cry 2 (besides a significantly better story) is the unrelenting pressure of enemies everywhere. If you're tired of them re-manning checkpoints just a few (in-game) hours after you've wiped them out, simply go capture the nearest outpost (admittedly a very enjoyable activity itself) and the problem is gone for good. In the second half of the game, not even this is necessary in most areas, since you quickly get a disguise that keeps you from being attacked regardless.
Add to this the easy availability of overpowered weapons, and the game really does become too easy, unless you deliberately play it for difficulty. I'm trying a playthrough now where I unlock neither outposts nor even radio towers (leaving me without a map and a much more limited minimap). For all its faults, that the game gives you the flexibility to do this is what gives it the potential for a lot more investment than a single playthrough.

In Far Cry 3 you play as Jason Brody, a kind of a spoiled brat who, along with his friends are vacationning on Rook islands somewhere in the Pacific. Things take a turn for the worst when the whole gang is kidnaped by pirates and are held as ransom. You manage to escape, and from there the adventure will include tattoos, hunting, saving your friends, reconquering the island from the pirates and ascend the ranks of the local Maori tribe.
The story is paper thin. FC3 doesn't make the case for first person narratives. After countless pirate kills Brody was still disgusted by skinning an animal or felt horrified by something he kinda did dozens of times before. This wasn't enough to disconnect from the game but it definitely was enough to establish a distance and render to nil any emotionnal involvement.
On the flip side though, the game introduce Vaas, the main antagonist, and he is awesomely written and acted. I would've loved to see him fully developped but alas it wasn't the case. Boy, talk about missed opportunity.
-FC3 has RPG elements, you gain experience from completing main and secondary missions, liberating outposts, finding lost artifacts and so on. The skill tree is divided into three categories that improves hunting, combat, health and survival.
-You have various vehicule at your disposal to get you around. They all handle pretty much the same way except for land vehicules which had a rough edge I liked. Being Far Cry you can also hop onto a glider and there are also ziplines that brings speed to the gameplay.
-I found the main missions to be a lot of fun, they are intense and varied. The same can't be said for optionnal ones. Ranging from menial to plain dull, ythey can all be skipped without generating any meaningful impact on your playthrough.
-There are also diversions such as races, hunting and assassination, but they are not that thrilling at all.
-In order to get around you have to be able to see the map and you can do so by activating radio towers scattered across the map. Once you do, a portion of the map will be visible and unlock more missions and diversions. The pirates have many outpost and liberating them will lessened their foothold and open the territory to friendlies and civilian alike.
Combat is fast and fun. You have many type of weapons available, each containing several weapons. There are also unique weapons that can be earned by completing missions, discovering items or simply advancing through the game.
Though not explicitely said stealth play is THE way to go. For instance liberating an outpost undetected grants you three times the experience points and takedowns are part of the core mechanics of the game.
Takedown are quasi quick time events that lets you insta-kill an enemy. Simply approach one undetected, push the prompt button and watch. The basic takedown is a stab but skill points can let you buy several other type of takedowns such as from below, from above and the ability to chain them.
The basic takedown is savage and thrilling and offer an additionnal strategic option to combat, but I can't help but feeling that this mechanic would've been right at home in a 3rd person action game but feels clunky in a FPS.
Returning from FC2, wildfire play an important part in the game. It can cutoff enemies, set them on fire but can turn on you in a pinch.
Wild and plant life plays a HUGE role in FC3, you can hunt the former and gather the latter. Upon progressing in the game you will unlock recipes. They can be crafted with the proper amount of plant samples and will grant you temporary effects.
You can also hunt the wildlife to gather their hide. These will upgrade your equipment so that you can carry more weapons and ammo and a bigger inventory. Wildlife is quite diverse as there are boars, antilopes, tigers and pack of wild dogs just to name a few.
If there is one aspect the Ubisoft nailed it is this one. Not only does wildlife adds realism to the setting but also makes it completely alive and unpredictable. One of the nicest moments in my playthrough was when I was slowly approaching an outpost, then in walks a tiger who proceded to maul all pirates in the camp and liberating it in the process!
Here comes the negative stuff. Actually it can all be summed up in two words : hand holding.
I set my game to hard expecting a challenge. The hard setting in FC3 is the equivalent of easy or normal in most other games, depending on how hardcore of a gamer you are. Let me put it this way, my health is gone and getting another bullet doesn't kill me.
Next there is money. Very soon in the game you will be chin-deep in money, it is everywhere. Most actions that you do lets you earn money on top of finding it all over the place. If a torrent of money wasn't enough as you activate radio towers the merchants will give you their weapons for free! Needless to say that the economy in FC3 is quite underwhelming.
I mentionned loot, but there is no item system in FC3, the myriad of items found totally meaningless except to be sold in the store. Too bad as it could have become the basis for some barter system that would have been interesting.
Hunting and crafting is amazing but by the 1/5 of my playthrough I had all the upgrades I could have and there is no other incentive for hunting except maybe to sell hides. As for crafting, well, you can't walk ten steps without stumbling on a plant. They appear on the minimap and shimmer in your field of view, just in case you missed it.
Here you are, in this big sandbox game and exploration is neither encouraged nor rewarded. Looking for a tiger skin? No problem, just open the map and find the area with a big fat tiger stencil on it, then travel to that area and you will find one in no time.  Looking for a plant to craft a syringe? Just walk in a straight line and you will find one eventually. There are over a dozen recipes that can be made but only three are helpful and the others are completely useless. Why would I need a syringe that would let me soak damage when the game encourages me to play stealthy?
There are also loot and collectibles, namely statues and letters. All of them appear on the minimap when you get in their vicinity but you can also buy maps that will reveal their locations. Aside from the achievementsthere is no incentive to collect any of them as they will only give you more money. Let's not talk about loot crates, they are countless, and only serves to give even
money!
Last but not least, FC3 works with a checkpoint system. There is actually  1, yes only 1, save slot, and saving will only save your progress. If you quit and restart the game you will spawn next to the closest radio tower or outpost from your save point. If you want to reload your game try a different strategy be ready to make your way back first. In this day and age this kind of save system is inexcusable.
:
-Wildlife dynamic is so well done that it raises industry standard
-Pleasing visuals
-Main missions are a blast
-A good chunk of achievements feels like achievements
:
-Open world game that doesn't encourage or reward exploration
-In-game economy is a joke
-Not very challenging
-Bland story and dialogue

I just can't put this game down. It is just too immensely rich and fun to play. There is always a cave you haven't explored, a secret you didn't find, a nice place you didn't see, a way of fighting you didn't try before... Rook Island always makes you come back for more.
Gameplay--- I have to place this statement in a proper context though. My first playthrough on the vanilla version of the game only lasted about 25 hours, full of high-tempo combat, mad driving, killing pirates by the dozens, completing missions in a hush-hush way. This is because the original game can feel a little FPS-mainstream (damn you, COD, for what you have done to the genre). The emphasis is a little too much on the action, and less on the open world and side missions, as is the case with Far Cry 2. However, where game-dev's fail in order to satisfy the producers and the company, the game community comes to the rescue. With proper modding (Ziggys Mod!), this game becomes what it had to be all along. The pace is slowed down, the difficulty has gone way up, making run-and-gun console-type approaches impossible. Instead, you have to resort to guerilla-warfare and the use of stealth and your natural surroundings. The over-guidance of the vanilla game is gone; you have to rely on your own noodle now. Sometimes you'll be the hunter, sometimes you'll be the prey, and that is what makes this game an exciting experience. Also, you will notice that this game is much richer in content than you noticed at first, since you spend too much time running and gunning in the vanilla version. Now, you can just ignore the missions and go hiking the amazingly beautiful island on your own.
Storyline--- Although I get the feeling that it is a little too cliché-ridden, the storyline is quite decent. No big plot twists or big schemes, but enough to keep the game going, and to give you a sense of urgency. Also, it does a good job in letting you question your morality and sanity by the end of the game, a nice break from the justified-violence themes in other games in the FPS-genre (yep, looking at you, COD). The most credit has to go to the voice-actors, who did an incredible job in giving the characters some depth (Vaas already is a classic).
Technical aspects--- The graphics of this game are just insane (keep your finger on the print-screen button!). Then again, so are the system specs, even for current standards. Bear this in mind when you buy this game!
Multiplayer and coop--- Not really worth the trouble. The multiplayer is COD-clone without depth (sorry for the fanboys that I keep mentioning this franchise in a negative way). The coop, however, is quite fun and easily accesible, since it uses a sort of 4-player drop-in format like L4D. But honestly, who cares? This is the best single-player experience I had!
Conclusion--- Buy it, mod it, fall in love with it. Once you set a foot on Rook Island, you'll never want to leave.

No big plot twists or big schemes, but enough to keep the game going, and to give you a sense of urgency. Also, it does a good job in letting you question your morality and sanity by the end of the game, a nice break from the justified-violence themes in other games in the FPS-genre (yep, looking at you, COD). The most credit has to go to the voice-actors, who did an incredible job in giving the characters some depth (Vaas already is a classic).
Technical aspects--- The graphics of this game are just insane (keep your finger on the print-screen button!). Then again, so are the system specs, even for current standards. Bear this in mind when you buy this game!
Multiplayer and coop--- Not really worth the trouble. The multiplayer is COD-clone without depth (sorry for the fanboys that I keep mentioning this franchise in a negative way). The coop, however, is quite fun and easily accesible, since it uses a sort of 4-player drop-in format like L4D. But honestly, who cares? This is the best single-player experience I had!
Conclusion--- Buy it, mod it, fall in love with it. Once you set a foot on Rook Island, you'll never want to leave.

Disclaimer: This game was my entry to the Far Cry franchise, aside from the demo of the first game, played on Xbox 360, many a year ago. As far as I'm aware, the games are neither connected in any other than tangential way, nor do they reference one another so nothing (story-wise, etc) is lost if you were to do the same.
** This review will be presented in the style of the Compliment Sandwich, where appropriate. **
Gunplay: Solid all around, from sniping to run'n'gun; responsive and otherwise well executed. Relatively small weapon selection, with over-powered "Signature Weapons" outshining everything else; luckily, there is at least one for each category. There is enough variation within the proffered selection of weapons that you should be able to find something you really like, with all the major areas covered I.e. sniper rifles, SMGs, assault rifles, etc.
Island (Terrain): Relatively navigable, and interesting. Some places suffer from an excess of hilly terrain, or escarpments, however, making travel uncomfortable or needlessly complicated to get to some place. But at least it's not Cyrodil, THAT was a nightmare.
Skill Tree: Varied, and well-sorted into its thematic parts. Personally not a huge fan of skill trees, and did not like being locked out of whole swathes until I did X mission when I have 5 skill points sitting there. Skills generally impart mild bonuses, avoiding making you feel over powered and the enemies/hazards trivial.
Combat/Stealth System: Adaptable and flexible, freely able to approach pretty much every encounter as you please if choosing between "guns blazing" and "stab everything silently". The "Heavy Beatdown" skill is nestled far into the skill tree, meaning you may not be able to deal with that LMG-toting guy the way you
want to until later. With the ability to start a fire fight and
, this is what I want from pretty much every open world game, ever. Actually, make that every game, ever, period.
Collectables/Unlocks: Lots of things to collect. Yay. I think. At least you get fancy guns out of it, and without a ton of effort.
Characters: I hate them. All are exceedingly shallow and one-dimensional, their presentation leaving so much to be desired, I'd hardly classify the cast as "characters". None of them are expanded on or explored in any real way. I think Vaas ended up as the most relatable character, just because he shows the most varied sides of himself: insane, psychotic, but probably tragic as well. Even then, he's little more than "insane and murderous pirate leader". Dennis had a bit of almost accidental backstory injected into the game, but it was so random and seemingly irrelevant that it's hard to relate it to anything in the game. Overall, you could say I was pretty disappointed with pretty much all the dialogue and interactions. Jason, in particular, is an overly unsympathetic protagonist. I simply could not relate to him, nor care about his plight, at all.
Story/Setting: Ambiguous Spoilers. Mostly speculative.
Overall: Solid shooter with decent open-world playground and excellent combat/stealth system. Suffers in presentation, to the point of being all but insufferable at several points, such as excessive "controlled helplessness" cutscenes (press [forward] to participate in the cutscene!) and poor characterizations, i.e. unsympathetic protagonist. Great for killing time, and possibly much deeper than it appears, but be ready to cringe at the writing and bang your head against the wall in frustration with the skill system being locked at certain points.
Numerical Score: 7/10 - Enjoyable, for what's there, but no masterpiece. Recommend you buy it on sale, or for not more than $10. Maybe $15 if you really like open world shooters.
Mods: this game is moddable! Check Nexusmods, they have a section for Far Cry 3. Keep in mind, modding in this game generally involves overwriting files, so the degree of customizability will be low.

The theme of a descent into insanity is nothing new to video gaming. But few games manage to properly juxtapose the senseless and euphoric ultraviolence of the standard gaming experience and the psychological decomposition that happens to real people in such situations. Far Cry 3 is one of them.
You are just a regular college student by the name of Jason Brody who's on a tour of east Asia with a few of your upper-crust friends and your two brothers. On a whim, you make an excursion to an all but uncharted island seeking some easy, anarchistic thrills, and quickly find yourself in the lowest pit of hell.
Your friends are taken hostage by drug-farming, slave-trading pirates, from whom you barely escape at a terrible cost. From there, you meet a whole host of world-class characters brought to life by brilliant voice-acting (Vaas and Buck especially) as you fight to survive and manipulate the living, open-world jungle.
There's a small degree of collecting and crafting, but when it comes to upgrading it's very straight-forward. You gain experience from combat (more from stealth takedowns) through an arcade-like point system, and you gain weapons by looting them off dead foes. The combat is fluid and dynamic, as planted explosives, freely roaming animals, random NPC patrols, and your own mistakes can aid or hinder you in your quest to save your friends.
Kills and gunplay are especially satisfying. Melee kills make your heart pound with their hectic but smooth animations and audio, making every strike feel personal. The gun porn is ramped up and though recoil isn't a major concern, the ballistics are very effective, and the animations match the beauty of the open world of the islands.
As you progress the story, however, Jason Brody will have moments of recess where he confides in others who are justly becoming concerned about his having gone tribal. And you might need a little genre awareness to realize that the horrible things you watch your first and even your second major adversaries do are no worse than what you've been wrecking upon their hapless subordinates.
Alongside the main story are some side-quests with a couple more hilarious and unique characters, as well as small missions for hunting, gathering, assassinations, deliveries, and so on. Or, you could just give in to your inner demons and prowl the jungle seeking out the poor souls who wander its depths.

This game offers a beautifully realized tropical paradise warzone for you to chew through as you see fit.  Each enemy outpost is a puzzlebox to be carefully picked apart, or smashed to pieces with explosives and flamethrowers.  Takedowns, special melee kills you can perform on unaware or surprised enemies, make the stealth approach incredibly satisfying, and more advanced variations let you become a god of sudden death, chain-killing, knife-throwing, and 'ha-ha I got your grenade pin'-ing your way through your prey.  Progression feels good and advances at your own pace, and there is nothing stopping you from getting all the upgrades before you are halfway through the game.  It can create a bit of the old ludonarrative dissonance at points, with the story expecting you to have only made so much advancement between missions, but otherwise it is a great system.
For a game with such freedom in how you approach it though, there is frustratingly little you can do to affect how the story plays out.  One example is a cutscene that triggers as you walk through a doorway in a story mission.  A man hiding in the corner knocks you out with the butt of his gun and you are captured by the enemy.  I was playing tactically, so I would clear rooms with a grenade before going in, but the cutscene doorway there was an invisible wall, so the grenade bounced at my feet. I tried a few more ways to clear the room, then ultimately walked through, assault rifle drawn facing the direction I thought the enemy would be, only to be yanked around by the cutscene transition and blindsided from the direction I was covering.  It left a sour taste in my mouth, so I took a break from the story and cleared the rest of the outposts on the first island.  Watching a group of panicked pirates being devoured by a tiger I let loose in their camp really cheered me right back up.
I can't attest to the multiplayer, but the singleplayer is an enjoyable romp, and if you can forgive a few indiscretions on the story's part, you'll have a blast.

What can I say about Far Cry 3?  The game is pretty.  That is the only good thing I have to say about this game.
The following review may contain spoilers!!!  You've been warned!!!
You start Far cry 3 and the first thing you notice is how great everything looks and you think to yourself "This is gonna be great".  Since this is a game that lets you free roam you do the first storyline mission, maybe two and then you just go explore.  The problem with exploring is there really isn't anything to explore.  You have to liberate the radio tower in an area to unlock the map and then you get 2-3 camps to liberate to remove enemy soldiers from the area.  The only other thing to do is find all the collectible crap that might unlock signature weapons but mostly is just there to keep the OCD people playing until they complete 100%.  Everything that was fun or interesting about the game was over by the time I finished the first island.  The second island in the game was not fun at all and contains pretty much every crappy gimmick that has been put into video games in the past decade.  Seriously timed button presses, mini games,  and poorly made rail shooters.  I only completed the storyline missions on the second island just so I could finish the game.  It wasn't fun, interesting, or engaging.  It seems like they knew their game was bad so they decided to make you have to jump through hoops to unlock literally everything in the game.  You have to unlock the map, the weapons, extra weapon slots, extra ammo slots, all the skills, literally everything.  Nothing in this game happens without you performing some kind of grind.  This isn’t fun, what happened to the days when games were fun?

It's hard not to like Far Cry 3. It's by no means great, but it's good. It works. It gives you characters and motivations and an amazing environment to run wild.
The shooting is tight and all of the guns feel like they serve a purpose. There are some balance issues with when some guns unlock: I got a top tier sniper rifle as one of the first unlocks and I never purchased another. And silencers are worth the investment. Being stealthy matters as much or more than just putting lots of big, nasty bullets into bad guys. And while there is a unique pleasure to taking out guards with no one spotting you, forcing a stealth section on us is still bulldroppings.
Uplay is a hassle, though, and the lack of Steam integration sucks. Not that the Crysis series is in better hands.

This game forces one to be swift, stealthy, and cunning. Or have a massive arsenal and a machine gun. Either way you play is sure to be great- and nothing evokes the same sense of panic as hearing a bear growling behind you while sniping out a base.

While many First Person Shooters Don't tend to be anything unique or interesting nowadays, Far Cry 3 manages to feel fresh and it really is a blessing to the genre.
The story in this game isn't going to blow you away, but the characters certainly will. Both the enemies and companions you meet throughout your journey on the island all have amazing personalities and really have lots of life to them.
Never once do they feel bland or annoying and the voice acting is phenominal, Vass especially.
Speaking of Vass, he is now one of my favorite antagonists. His character is performed in such a way that really makes him something special. Seriously, I smiled everytime he opened his mouth. His voice actor delivers his lines so perfectly and with so much emotion that he feels like a real person. A person that is insane and constantly trying to kill you that is.
Far Cry 3 also has exceptional Gameplay as well. All of the guns are a delight to use and they each can be modified to a specific use. For example, My assualt rifle has a silencer and a long-range scope for taking out enemies silently, while my Light-Machinegun has a extended magazine for longer suppresion of enemies before I have to reload. There are just so many oppurtunities for ways to approach enemies. Maybe you want to wipe out an entire camp just by stabbing all of them in the back, or perhaps you want to immediatly rush in there with your vehicle and run over a few people before pulling out a flame-thrower and burning the camp to the ground. The choice is entirely up to you.
The game also has a great sense of progression. You are constantly hunting for wildlife and upgrading your equipment like how many guns you can hold or how many syringes you can have on you. Not to mention hunting for extremely rare animals to use their pelts to make bigger wallets, rucksacks, ammo pouches, etc. Also, as you gain more XP from killing enemies and completing missions, you can upgrade your skills for more take-downs, better weapon handling, acrobatic skills, and more.
That's also not to mention the
amount of side missions, relics to find, places to explore, caves to discover, bases to raid, commanders to assassinate, and so much more. Far Cry 3's island has so much additional stuff to see and explore that isn't in the main campaign that after 25 hours, I still havn't seen every part of the island
All-in-all, Far Cry 3 is an excellent FPS and I highly reccomend to shooter fan out there

Far Cry 3 has by far reigned among my top 5 open world games, every aspect of this game is great; from the story; to the gameplay; the action, world and its mechanics. You are Jason Brody, a young man looking for an adventure while vacationing on a remote island with your closest friends. Yet you get more than what you bargained for, when your group is kidnapped by drug pedaling pirates to be sold to the underground world of slavery.  Now its up to you to save your friends, bring peace back to this once pristine environment, and inspire hope to its native people. As you diverge from your expected path you become a true product of your new environment. You turn from a scared boy, to a ruthless warrior. Though be careful who you trust, for betrayal is lurking around every corner.
This game is like no other, the story missions are long and tough and the side missions are a blast. You must climb to the top of hundred foot radio towers to acquire maps, radar and weapons; liberate pirate outposts; learn the lay of the land; hunt its native creatures, both docile and ferocious; find its most precious and scarce relics; bounty hunt for the islands most wanted; and test your skills through vigorous timed trials. This enormous world has more than enough ways to spend your time. If you feel like taking a break from the fighting, go play some poker, place wagers on your marksmanship, throw knives,  get laid, or race ATVs.
As you delve in to this chaotic world, you find all resources at the palm of your hand. Customize your weapons by adding scopes, extended magazines and suppressors. You can pick someone off from a mile away, shoot them in the back with your bow and arrow, slit someone's throat, or blow it all up! Every desirable weapon is available at your disposal; hand guns, shotguns, assault rifles, SMGs, LMGs, RPGs, C4 explosives, knives, even a f**king flamethrower; everything your twisted heart could desire! The question is, how will you save this world? As a silent assassin, or a gun toting  juggernaut?
Choose who you wish to become by picking skills from three separate skill trees. You can chose to become a stealthy assassin, a long range killer, an unstoppable killing machine or all three.  Will you learn how to shoot from a zip line, or how to silently ambush numerous enemies from atop and below? These skill will also help you become a better hunter-gatherer. Collect indigenous plants to craft potent remedies and abilities or learn to silently hunt a tiger or shark for its hide.
Like any good contemporary game, there is multiplayer along with coop. Fight with or against players across the world to complete objectives, sabotage each other's bases, go on missions, or just shoot each other up in death match. Be careful though, for the losing teams best player is to be made an example of. The winning team can chose to show mercy, or beat him to within an inch of his life.
So mount up! This world cannot be saved without your efforts. Just remember, trust no one. Not even yourself...

A thoroughly enjoyable FPS with some great ideas and a decent story. The weapon and skill progression pacing is very fluid. And naturally the weapon/skillset becomes more fun to use as you progress, with some crazy weapons thrown in near the end. In general, the game is designed so you're never short of content to do. The soundtrack is fun, with a few nice set pieces and even some licensed music to add effect to certain situations.
I found the game a tad repetitive after reaching the southern island, and tasks like climbing radio towers and finding relics etc. became more of a completionists chore rather than anything that adds substance to the gameplay, or giving the feeling of rewarding you for doing so (which it should). Also, try to get all of your extra content done before you liberate all the outposts, otherwise you'll find locating enemies more and more scarce!
The co-op mode I think it's fair to say is one of the most rushed and tacked-on modes I've witnessed in a game. If you play this mode for achievement hunting (for Uplay), then you are best off playing with a friend. The reason for this is because if you make a private online lobby, and become the host, you can change the maps/difficulty as required. But in the online public lobbies, you just get thrown into a random lobby / map / difficulty, and have to take what you're given. The only way to become a host in a public lobby is to stay long enough to see yourself become the leader after other people quit. Or hope all the other lobbies are full and that you get to start your own. Only then can you actually change the map to the one you require for an achievement. Which is quite frankly bizarre.. and goes to show how rushed this portion of the game was. It's also quite a buggy mode in general. So be ready for that. The multiplayer section itself is quite derivative of modern day FPS multiplayer, it doesn't really add much to the table.
The reason you'll want to play this game is for the single player experience, and for that reason alone I would gladly recommend it.

And then I try starting the game from Uplay and I see where it says "Play", but it doesn't look like it is highlighted and not really clickable. In fact, it is not clickable. So then why is it there?
