Or you need even more proof? Go to the store page of Far Cry 3. And check out the negative reviews on this game. They are mostly about UPLAY.
I have found a few solutions for this, and well, some of the suggestions are to remove certain files, install some new driver, go into some folder and change something........uh....I bought the game, and I have to put up with all this garbage? Coming from recently playing Just Cause 2, I didn't expect the length of this campaign. Especially if you take the time to do side quests, DLC missions, and take over all the outposts and radio towers. This game is fantastic. You can run around and go in guns blazing, or you can sneak up and take everyone out quietly with silenced weapons or the bow. However, my favorite way to play is probably by getting to a high place and picking off enemies one by one with a sniper rifle. The campaign in this game is a must.
The co-op is OK. It's not amazing, and I was disappointed that the co-op wasn't really open world like the single player campaign. You can play with up to four people, but you don't get all the abilities you have in the single player. One of the most fun parts of the co-op are the competitions. In each mission there is a part were all players are competing for the highest score. There are jet ski challenges, sniper challenges, bow challenges, RPG challenges, and more.
The multiplayer was surprisingly fun. Most games like this that aren't built with a multiplayer focus are not very good. I find this one to be enjoyable. However, there are only a couple hundred people who play regularly, so you cannot play most game modes.
There are some things in this game that just make you go "What?" Because as realistic as it seems most of the time, sometimes there are just crazy things. I won't tell you any so it's not spoiled, but be prepared for some crazy stuff.

I played the original Far Cry and found it to be a game of lackluster storyline and glorious graphics. I player Far Cry 2 and found it to be annoying, repetitive and boring, yet nice-looking. So that's what I expected from Far Cry 3 as well.
I was wrong.
Far Cry 3 is pretty, that much hasn't changed. In fact the game was so pretty that all the pretty environments, visual effects and bright colours actually made me feel physically ill sometimes, which I guess has to count against the graphics, but other than that Far Cry 3 is a gorgeous game.
However, unliked it's predecessors, Far Cry 3 has an interesting premise, that of young adults captured by pirates and struggling to escape with the assistance of native resistance warriors fighting the pirates. It has cool locations, characters and missions, and most importantly: it has an arc. The protagonist, Jason Brody, changes throughout the game. He grows on you in this weird way, and I found it unusually easy to relate to him.
The voice actors are solid, the game uses original and lifted music effectively and most of the sound effects seem top-notch.
And then there is the positive surprise! While most modern games give you something between 6-10 hours of gameplay, Far Cry 3 got me up to 22 hours, with easily 90% of the side missions untouched and much of the map still left to properly explore. If you are that kind of a person, you can easily get lost in this game and just roam the land, hunting prey, be it man or animal, and taking in the glorious scenery.
I didn't expect to, but I truly recommend this game.
Playtime: 22+ hours (single playthrough)
Ratings (1-10)
Visual: 8
Audio: 9
Story: 8
Gameplay: 9
Overall: 8

Far Cry 3 is a brilliantly executed open-world First Person Adventure. Many call this an FPS, but that’s only a small facet of this game. I enjoyed the first half of the game, but I had to will myself to cross the finish line.  FC3 has many “tacked-on” elements that don’t really add to the experience. It has “crafting” and a “skill tree” that could have easily been absorbed in to the games progression, as neither really changes your game experience beyond expanding your inventory capacity or adding a new way to take out enemies. A decent player will have both maxed out well before the end-game.
The weapon progression was fun; especially the high powered weapons that send enemies flying on impact. The addition of weapon mods was nice, but arbitrary. The mods were only available on the higher tiers of weapons, and limited to an artificial cap. The mod categories are suppression, magazine size, and optics (in some cases you could stack optic choices, like adding night vision to a long range scope); unfortunately the designers chose to artificially limit the number of attachments and only allow them on top tier weapons. The result is a huge number of underused weapons. I might have experimented with more of the lower tier weapons if they were upgradable. This would not have thrown off balance since there was so much redundancy in weapon choices anyway.
The story starts with strong conflict which cements you in to the mythos quickly. I enjoy hardboiled tales as much as the next guy, but there was very little foil to the darkness  and grittyness. For a 40+ hour experience, it would have been nice to have some humor and light hearted content mixed in to the hard hitting main quest. There were some likeable characters along the way – Vass was a good “bad-guy”, Sam was a lot of fun, and the deep cover agent straight out of Miami Vice was a nice touch, but I found I was less interested in the main story and more interested in my own exploration. The number of times I got shot, stabbed, drowned, and “left for dead” started to become an in-joke (they even mention it in the game).
Overall I would lump this game in to the same family as Skyrim or Fallout 3, both of which far eclipse this game in story and progression. The area that Far Cry shines is in the gameplay mechanics, and the interaction with the world. I felt much more in control of my characters physicality which ultimately sustained my intrest allowing me to play through to the end. (The wingsuit is AWESOME!) I really did get the feeling of being a one-man-army action-hero without it feeling like I was dealing with idiotic AI. It’s worth playing and I look forward to seeing how they improve this franchise going forward.

Far Cry 3 provides an epic story about a friendly vacation gone wrong. Jason Brody is your typical youngster who's only care is to party hard, but circumstance force him into a situation where this boy must jump on the fast path to manhood.
The graphics of Far Cry 3 are simply stunning. This latest edition goes back to its original roots of lush island landscapes. The scenery is fantastic. As day changes to night and the rain starts pouring down, it provides a sense of realism that is rarely accomplished in many games today. Characters are amazingly detailed and the interaction with them add to that sense of realism. Vaas and Hoyt are two sick son of a ♥♥♥♥♥es that keep tensions high and continually throw unexpected twists your way. The different variety of vehicles like hang gliders, jet skis, and dune buggies make exploration fun, while sprinting is fast enough that it provides a reasonable alternative to using vehicles at all. The large variety of weapons allow for a full range of games styles, from stealth play to I'm here to blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up. I actually played very stealthily in the early parts of the game as the bow and arrow was probably hands down my favorite overall weapon, but later on I just overpowered my opponents with sheer firepower. I found both methods equally satisfying.
Side missions are initially fun, but ultimately become repetitious after a while because they don't offer enough differences. Liberate enemy camps, expand your overall field of vision by claiming back radio towers, assassinate key figures, and hunt wild game. Hunting and skinning animals is necessary to upgrade your standard equipment. It goes well with the island paradise and doesn't heavily disrupt from the primary story.
Three categories of character skills are available to promote stealth, firepower, and survival. Missions reward stealth gameplay with more XP which I don't necessarily agree with because it tends to steer your gameplay in that direction. I was able to unlock all available skills by the story's end. There's also crafting of drugs using flowers collected which can increase various attributes for a limited time.
I found the menu system to be the weakest part of the game. It feels overly cumbersome since you have to escape out of the game to craft syringes or use skill points. It just doesn't feel like it was integrated well overall.
All-in-all, Far Cry 3 represents a really fun open world first person shooter. Single player is genuinely fun, but I have yet to play the co-op or multiplayer elements.

This game is an exact cross between Far Cry and Far Cry 2. For those that don’t remember, Far Cry was the first game (afaik) which allowed players to hide in shrubs on a massive tropical island with luscious green foliage. It used the first Crytek game engine. In Far Cry 2, you couldn’t really hide in shrubs, instead you were placed on a barren African landscape wearing a straw hat and on safari. This time the Dunia game engine was used which I’d personally say is more than just a heavily modified version of the CryEngine.
Far Cry 3 uses the Dunia Engine 2. What this means is, the gameplay mechanics and overall feel of the game will be more like Far Cry 2. This is particularly noticeable with the shooting mechanics, the openness of the landscapes with trails/tracks/villages/compounds and even the driving of boats and vehicles will feel pretty much the same. Except the only difference is you’re on a luscious island where you have plenty of shrubs to hide in (or burn lol).
What’s different? We get a pretty full on cinematic experience. It almost felt personal with the characters being so close and their faces taking up the entire screen. I thought they all wanted to kiss me. Aside from that, I thought all characters were standup comedians. Vaas in particular, but Buck as well. They have hilariously crazily loveably outrageous personalities.
There is also an XP skill system in place. It didn’t bother me (see my Hitman: Absolution review) but after a year I’m now growing to hate seeing this in games. Not only is it a lame way to track progress, I reckon it damages the RPG genre. But like I said, it wasn’t much of a bother in this game.
Overall Far Cry 3 in my opinion is for those that seek a very slow-paced game where you complete menial tasks on the island, but with the goal of exploration. Having said that, the island is a work of art, very detailed at every place. Not just a piece of terrain where they plopped buildings and 3D models on randomly.
It’s interesting seeing how the land mixes in with the river banks, tree roots, erosion and sediments. Like you’ll see some tin shack on some beach in the middle of nowhere with intricately placed shore rocks, or you may walk through a plain field of grass with some oak-like trees during the night, or a lake in the middle of nowhere, it’s an experience to remember.
I can almost certainly guarantee you that you won’t traverse the same spots on the island more than twice. This can be proven by purchasing maps to display the locations of all the loot chests. There’s a crap load of them! And for about 30 hours I was really nitpicky in the beginning opening those chests.
The game was a bit buggy for me from time to time, but I always seemed to pull out of it without losing too much progress. Like sometimes you can bypass waypoints with ease which will break the mission. I also didn’t like long unnecessary animations like patting corpses for loot. Sometimes the game would just crash when I sell a lot of loot items in the store. I run an AMD 5000+ overclocked to 3GHz and HD6870. This is a pretty old gaming rig and I was able to play on high settings comfortably enough (felt like 25-30 fps when running).
I prefer Far Cry 2, but Far Cry 3 is a very sophisticated game technology-wise. Definitely a step forward that newcomers can jump into without needing to play the predecessors since the stories and characters are all different.
*note this review was cut down from 9000+ words.

Gamers returning to the Far Cry franchise will be releaved to see me write that Far Cry 3 does NOT continue its tradition of having a major glaring flaw.  The first Far Cry game broke the mold with one of the largest maps in a first person shooter at the time; making it standard to have a player travel over a kilometer from one objective to the next by scrambling over mountains, skipping accross oceans, or occasionally taking to the sky.  This was made even more true in Far Cry 2 when the player was tasked to brave a veritable country's worth of sub-Saharan Africa.  Unfortunately both these titles had tremendous flaws.
In Far Cry 2 It was commonplace to have to drive a long way to get to the desired location (think 10 minutes) with very few exceptions or quick travel remedies.  Even with the use of the bus system you were still forced to do many minutes of boring driving on top of that.  While enemies were fun and challenging, and the triage healing brutally visceral, the combat got tired as you passed a checkpoint causing a fight, only to experience the exact same fight at the exact same fully staffed checkpoint 3 minutes later.  This repetition ended up being the majority of the game, and the player was forced to invent their own variety with the arsenal available.  Luckily, the fire weapons caused beautiful chaos with quickly spreading brushfires and the stealth weapons gave you the feeling of a tiger stalking through the grass, though these were largely unexplored in the main story.  On the subject of story, this game suffers from a glitch that basically destroys the story that is supposed to be illuminated through your collection of interview tapes in the second half of the game.  This problem, known as "the Jackal tapes glitch" causes you to get the same tape over and over; if you want the actual story elements, you'll have to go to YouTube.
[Far Cry 1 spoilers]
The first Far Cry introduced you to some of these stealth and distraction elements with your trademark rock.  Without the highly developed combat of Far Cry 2 though, it was criticized for overly keen-eyed enemies who could engage you from hundreds of meters away with laser like precision and calculate your exact position from the flight path of your rock throwing if they were of a certain alert status.  The worst however was yet to come.  The game breaking TriGen (literally mutant monkeys) very well ended the fun in any areas they were at from the moment they arrived.  The developers somehow decided that adding enemies that could leap 10 horizontal meters and kill you in a single blow were a great idea for close quarters indoor battles; when it came to outdoors combat they stole a page from the DOOM Mancubus and gave us gorillas with two rocket launchers grafted onto their arms.  Many players would be well advised to stop this title halfway through.
[/far cry 1 spoilers]
[Crysis spoilers]
This could be further extended to CryTek's other franchise Crysis, as many players will tell you the alien opponents were an unwelcome addition.
[/crysis spoliers]
To my delight Far Cry 3 does NOT continue this trend.  Instead, it takes the best of both worlds and merges them.  With a well integrated stealth system, this game allows you the same feeling of stalking through the grass, marking your targets, and unleashing hell upon them in the method of your choice.  Whether you'd like to bend the forces of nature to your assistance using stealth and cunning, or bring your own hellfire in the form of rockets and lead, you can enjoy the chaos or calculation therein.  You can still cause quite amount of madness with setting brushfires and about halfway through the game you find enemies capable of returning the favor.  The story remains a fairly driving force behind your progress as you feel time is always against you.  More importantly though, it doesn't suffer from the apparent glitches nor destructive elements of its predacessors.  Instead, it adds to its legacy with an even larger map, better rapid travel system, new mediums of locomotion, extra dangers in the form of the island's animal inhabitants, more stealth and subterfuge combat options, tremendously talented voice acting, a well integrated cover system, fascinating dream sequences, and some of the same visceral field medicine we came to love in Far Cry 2.
On the other hand, it does have some faults, first among them being uPlay.  Ubisoft's proprietary digital content delivery system serves as a parallel to Steam.  Unfortunately though, you are forced to use them both when playing through Steam, and therefore are required to maintain two accounts for one game (assuming you desire to play through your Steam account).  This is mostly a frustration and does not greatly effect the game other than in screenshots as the uPlay overlay does not hide itself from screenshots as the Steam overlay does.  The game can also feel a bit unfair as sometime it seems the wildlife will go out of its way to spoil your plans as buffalo trample you to the ground and kill you before you can rise to defend yourself, though this is a rare occurence.  Being such a massive game, it does take a couple graphical and processing short-cuts so you can expect physics not to be present in most of your projectiles, the detail of your surroundings to suddenly phase in after arriving, and tree sprites following you around if you look down during flight.  Though it may not have the famed engine of the Crysis games, it still looks great.
The gamefurther improved by an interesting multiplayer.  While borrowing heavily from the Call of Duty paradigm and suffering from a small player-base and an excess of weapon mods (NOT attachments), the multiplayer is surprisingly fun, especially when it comes to close quarters combat.  Unlike in single player, your multiplayer character feels slow and weighed down, so don't expect the same pulse-pounding pace you had there.  This is made up for though by forcing the player to make wise decisions when advancing around a corner or through a doorway, and much like in real life the simple momentum and violence of your actions can lead you to victory.  It is especially rewarding when you can work your way into the enemy's supply lines and rack up an array of terrifying melee kills with your trusty machete.  Sniping is a challenging affair and in general you either need to use great distance or reflexes to win the day; in this respect it is a bit unrealistic, but is wisely done to make it more fair and fun for everyone.  The unlockable "Team Supports" as the killstreaks are titled, seem a bit underwhelming, and it appears as though the ones the player begins with are really the superior options anyway.  They do however add to objective based combat as effective area denial weapons.  Levelling your character, weapons, and abilities is done through the normal methods, but can be enhanced with the decoding game on browser and mobile platforms that allow you to level more quickly by completeing daily puzzles and events.
Along with all this the game still has a co-operative mode which can mostly be described as a series of single player missions with a very narrow focus meant to be enjoyed among friends.  With few exceptions, this is a very enjoyable experience as well, albeit a fairly short one.  Despite lacking any kind of open world, it does lend itself to VOIP communication fun as you can accomplish what you always wanted to but never could in the the single-player; use a coordinated surprise attack and wipe out an enemy force in seconds, before they even knew what was hitting them.  Far Cry 3's multiplayer provides an often overlooked facet that surprises with an interesting and deep multiplayer experience that will likely leave you wanting more.
All-in-all Far Cry 3 surpasses all of its predaccessors.  If you have any enjoyment of the previous titles, or are a lover of shooters with depth, this game is for you.

When Jason Brody decides it's time to take a vacation, he does what any carefree and mildly successful 25-year-old would do - party in BANGKOK! Besides stretching the US dollar and consuming copious amounts of booze, Jason, his girlfriend, and the rest of his friends are seeking an adventure. That's when they hear from the local DJ about a tropical paradise known as the Rook Islands - a place where you can do anything and everything. On the word of Doug the DJ, whom they've never met and certainly shouldn't trust, they travel to the Rook Islands.. via skydiving..
What Jason and his buddies don't know is that the Rook Islands is anything but utopia. From Chinese Warlords slaughtering each other over treasure to the Japanese Imperial Army turning on itself after World War 2, the Rook Islands have a tendency of inducing insanity and bloodshed. So instead of a partying on a white sandy beach, they're kidnapped by a pirate, Vaas Montenegro, who enjoys repeatedly explaining the definition of insanity to his helpless victims before executing them.
However, Vaas has different plans for Jason and his friends, electing instead to hold them for a hefty ransom due to their presumably wealthy roots. But Jason miraculously escapes and it's now up to him to save his friends - and himself - from hell in paradise.
Over all, i would give this game a 10/10, in my opinion, it is jsut a perfect game.

I didn't have high expectations of FarCry 3 after playing FarCry 2, and FarCry 1's story was a little far fetched for me. I was immediately engaged by the opening scene of FarCry3 and I had to play it a couple of times because of how the save points work. I was mostly engaged by the story, although there are some points you want to go WTF? But there is a really cool scene that blew my mind. While shooting bad guys is pretty repetitive, I had a lot of fun capturing Radio Towers and Bandit camps for the challenge of not being detected. I didn't spend a whole lot of time searching for relics or loot because it would never end, but the game is just gorgeous.
The "upgrades" you can do to yourself are fun and add to the game and most of them I didn't find useless. Another nice feature about the game is the ending. Once you beat the game, you have the option to "leave" or continue on. I opted for continuing on, but all I have left is searching for relics, and there is about 300 in the game. Not really worth the time to me. I don't know about the replayability of the game, but it was worth the discount I paid for it. It's one of three or four games out of 90 or so that I've actually wanted to complete.
I would recommend this game, even at the current regular price, but if you can find it on a discount, even better. I do have one complaint. I would consider my computer hardware to be above the norm, but the game sometimes would run great and then go down to 10 or so FPS, which when doing certain tasks (radio tower medical quests), it would make it extremely challenging. You may find other reviews complaining about how the game is not optimized, and I felt the same pain. Didn't detract from the game, but out of 5 stars, I would give it a 4.5 for this reason. If it ran well 100% of the time, I would have given it a 5.

After spending 90+ hours completing everything there is to do in Far Cry 3, I can safely say I haven't had this much fun in an FPS for a long time. Having the freedom to do practically anything you like, in any order you like, in any style you like, is a refreshing change from the standard-fare modern military shooter. I had so much fun doing things like, when needing a vehicle, popping a jeep driver with my Desert Eagle .50, watching the jeep slide up a hill, flip over a few times, kill the gunner in the roll, and then land perfectly upright on the road in the direction I needed it. Thank you very much!
However, the game does have a few caveats - firstly, it's as buggy as all hell, even today. Crashes to desktop on buying/selling items, restarting mission/quest checkpoints, or just entirely randomly while running around is worryingly common, so save often. I even fell through the ground and out of the world on the wingsuit once.
The UI and save system is also somewhat irksome and could've been implemented better on PC (an unfortunate leftover of the inferior console version), and the cash limitation is absurd - once you've bought all the weapons, upgrades and paint jobs, the only way to spend your wallet is to deliberately burn ammo and get yourself injured to buy armour/medicine. Not a game-breaker by any means, but annoying for a completionist like myself who wants to loot every chest, but can't because of an arbitrary cash limit - it just doesn't need to be there.
Finally, there are one or two poorly-balanced story missions that can be very difficult to complete unless you metagame it and do things like lay mines with advance knowledge of enemy spawn positions (Huntley and the plane repairs, I'm looking at you!). The plot could've done without some of the trippy, mystical stuff as well.
Despite a fair few misgivings, though: overall decent shooting, interesting world, plenty of free-form fun, and some intriguing and dark characters make for an enjoyable game. Just don't expect it to be perfect.

"Do you know the definition of insanity?"
The character 'Vaas' steals the show as the antogonist similarly to how the Joker was the best part of 'The Dark Knight'. A human being that is clearly pure evil and yet, you just can't help but love the character thanks to the actor's performance.
I am very happy to see that more and more games are starting to make open world enviroments that contain unscripted entertainment that increases replayability. Taking over enemy bases can be a unique experince for each player depending on how they approach the situation.
The cons for this game is having a somewhat predictable straight forward plot that is really only appealingbecause of the superb role Vaas and other memorable villains play in it. The difficulty in the game is very easy even on the hardest setting (There is a bug that makes the difficulty reset when closing the game sometimes). There are a few parts in the game where you operate a machine gun while someone drives the vehicle you're on that are a bit broken as the difficulty for those particular
scenes spike drastically and are nearly impossible on the hard difficulty.
There are also a few side missions where you can help some people on the island but they quicly became dull for me as they are usually mundane tasks (go here and go there come back) and rarely offer any interesting insight.
Overall however, this is an excellent game that offers great gameplay in an open world where you can unleash chaos in a variety of ways. The soundtrack to this game is phenomenal. It really captures everything from the themelancholy of the viciousness that transpires on the island with a beautiful soft theme, to an action packed firefight with very energetic dubstep.
Rating
8.9/10

What if I told you about a game that open's up with five privileged white Ivy League party goers sky diving and celebrating on a scenic beach looking for their next big thrill? Documenting their moments how most young people from this generation do, through their Phones and Tablets. Laughing vicariously from shot to shot nothing would be out of place seeing their lives sprawled across a Facebook Profile. Then in the last moment of the opening cinematic the scene is actually shown playing off a smart phone held by hands through a bamboo cage. Far Cry 3 has a memorable opening setting up for a predictable payoff only to push you off the edge and out of your comfort zone by Introducing an unforgetable Villian named Vaas. Far Cry 3 Developed and Published by Ubi Soft tells the story of Jason Brody who's with a group of friends in Bangkok celebrating his younger brother Riley on getting his pilot's license. They decide to take a trip and go sky diving landing on a tropical island somewhere between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Transistion to a smart phone with paused video of the last scene held by hands in the darkness of a camp. This is the first time Vaas makes an apearance and he establishes early on that he runs the island and it's people. He let's Jason and his brother know that they are valuble and will net him a "huge pay off" through ransom. Short tempered and emotionally unstable parallels can be drawn from villians in other media, especially the Joker. The few ecounters you have with him up the ante each time with more sadistic and twisted ways of getting across how much he likes killing.

After Vaas leaves the two in their wooden prison, his older brother unties his own hands and then frees Jason telling him to remain in place as if he were still tied. Calling a guard over he pulls his head in through the bars of the cage and snaps the man's neck taking keys off the body and opening the cage. He proclaims "That is what they teach you in the Army." They sneak around the encampment plotting their escape and poundering where their friends might be. Jason finds a map and a GPS device and while under some wooden structure at the camp his brother looks at the map and begins planning their next move. Then a loud shot is heard, Jason's brother Grant has been shot in the throat and a QTE (quick time event) appears on screen while in the distance you can hear an incoherent rant from Vaas saying "You want to run? You want to run? You want to disrespect me?." Rapidly pressing the button prompt on screen you see Jason putting his hand over the wound trying to stop the blood loss, Grant gasping for air takes his final breaths succumbing to his fatal wound. Vaas mercifully declares "I'm gonna give you 30 seconds and if this jungle doesn't eat you alive I will. Now go." Jason running into the darkness of the Jungle hears Vaas yell "run Forest. Run!" as search lights shine in his direction. He finally makes it to a water fall and has no choice but to jump plunging into the water, floating under the river currents while the introductory credits begin to roll. In the next scene he awakes to a man tattooing his arm who starts telling him about the Rakyat people who live on this Island and the evil pirates under Vaas's control. The tattoo is called a tatau and is only giving to warriors and for each new tatau abilites are giving. Jason is introduced to the village and told he can avenge his brother's death and save his friends if he's willing to fight along side the Rakyat people to defeat Vaas and thus begins Far Cry 3.

Far Cry much like it's last two predecessors is an open world First Person Shooter and is released for Xbox 360, Playstation 3 and PC. It runs on the Dunia Engine 2 which is a heavily modified version of Crytech's Cry engine software. The game itself is very beautiful with beliveable grass and jungle leaves swaying in the breeze to day/night cycles where light fades and cascades based on real time physics. Realtime cutscenes and in game animations are well done with great voice over performances from the main cast. Vaas in particualr who is voiced, motion caputred and model after by Canadian actor Micheal Mando speaks to the quality and care that Ubi Soft managed to achieve. But not all is perfect in this paradise, repatative dialouge from the pirates and fellow villagers becomes noticable later in the game though it does not ruin the experience, a more conversational pallet would have been prefered. Just like many other open world games QA testing can only go so far before a product falls into the hands of gamers. These days it can feel like gamers become the second wave of testers, runing into glitches or wonky physics. Here is no different, I've had menu transitions freeze the game to weird clipping and artifacting of objects. But nothing trully game breaking like save files being corrupted and truth be told these issues seem to appear randomly after hours of play time have been racked up. I played this game on PC so I can't relay any issues specific to the other platforms. Just make sure all your drivers on Windows OS and Graphics card are up to date and you should be good to go.

From the moment you leave the Rakyat village you have access to a large portion of Rook Island to explore and take on side quests. One interesting aspect in the game is activating radio towers which show the towers region on the Map screen along with enemy outposts and the type of animal life that exsits in the area. Not to mention for each radio tower you turn on more weapons become available and certain weapons are offered for free. It adds an incentive to explore much of the island as possible in hopes of aquiring that one expensive weapon at no charge. The early story missions also have you become familiar with the robust crafting system and general gameplay mechanics by having you hunt animals and scavange for certian plants. You can gain experice by killing people, animals, completing quests, liberating pirate outposts and activating radio towers. When the experience bar reaches full you gain 1 skill point which can then be spent on various abilities through 3 skill trees. The Heron, Shark and Spider skill trees differ in what abilities can be learned or skills that can be upgraded, for example the Spider skill tree has many types of stealth takedown moves that can be learned and upgraded from. After confirming your choice, you see Jason's left arm get etched with either a Spider, Shark or Heron tribal tattoo depending on what skill trees where chosen. As the game progreses his arm will get covered in more ink, and at least for me it was a visual reminder of how far I've come and what it means to be a warrior for the Rakyat people.

Crafting is used for upgrading your lootruck sack, weapon holsters, Syringe holster, wallet, certain weapons and to creat Syringes. The Lootruck sack is where your collected plants, animal skins and sellable items looted from chests and dead bodies go. Initally only holding 24 items the game almost compells you to constantly be on the lookout for the ingredients to increase you sack size since most of what you forage will go here. Early on you can only hold one weapon but by skinning the appropriate animals you can increase your holster to hold more weapons which gives you more options in the heat of combat. Same thing for consumable items like grenades, molotovs, C4 and claymore mines all those type of holsters can be upgraded to hold more of each which is exactly what one would want being a lone solider on a hostile Island. Ironically enough the wallet was the least important to upgrade even though I did it and was able to hold more money, I found that by spending time finding radio towers I was able to amas a good sized arsenal pro bono. Syringes are conumable and get injected into Jason's arm. The medical Syringes heal you and combat ones help to do more damage or to increase survivability meanwhil
Sadly Plagued with a couple frustrating bugs and an annoying 3rd party ubisoft program, none the less a great game with a storyline that kept my attention. 7/10

Far Cry 3 is a good game, a great game even. You could even say it's an excellent game. No game is without fault however I'll talk about some of the good things and some of the bad.
First: the guns; the core part of any FPS. They're so fun to use in this game simply because they all feel different and it's very easy to recognize the differences between all the weapons. Stealth is also a big part of the combat, stealth takedowns and silenced weapons eventually become your best friend as rushing in is generally a bad idea (especially once you've reached the later half of the game) even on normal difficulty. Optional objectives are spread throughout the game which include: side quests, hunting challenges, sniper challenges and poker. Most of them are purely optional offering nothing more than something to do while you're playing others are higly incentivized (Radio towers, hunting, liberating camps + supply drops) as they offer XP, money and lead to unlocking better equipment and guns! Getting around isn't that hard either (provided you aren't getting shot at) and you'll find that once you have access to more fast travel points you'll reach your destinations really quickly!
Now I'll touch on the story for a bit before I get to the cons! The story... not so great! That is to say it's not amazing, but it feels a lot like an action movie and those don't really require great stories either! I did find, however, that across the story there were a few memorable characters and sequences that I really liked but the ending leaves a lot to be desired. Also worth noting, several instances of nudity!
And now the final part of this lengthy review, the cons! There were quite a few bugs, mostly visual and none of them game-breaking definitely a slight on the game but they can be over-looked! I found that when I was exploring or hunting for collectibles whenever I had a waypoint on my map there was no clear indication as to whther or not the thing I had waypointed was above me or below me. By the time I realized this this I had usually gone too far off to find the actual path to the thing I was looking for. And finally, the major offender... UPlay! I have nothing against the platform itself but not having it installed prior to playing this game lead to me waiting a good 45 mins before I could actually play the game. It also requires you to be connected to the internet for a enjoyable experience, meaning if you've got a dodgy connection or are simply having issues you should probably just play something else.
To wrap things up, like I said in the beginning, this game's great. If you have any interest in shooters or open world games then you have to give this game a spin, as there's tons to do and you'll probably have a good time doin' it!

Aloha and welcome to my review of Assassi... eeh.... Far Cry 3.
So, this is my first review of a game I bought on Steam and (even after only a ´few minutes´ of playing) I have to admit that this one is interesting in ... many ways.
First of all: The installation kindly offers UPlay - with a sledgehammer, just Ubi´s standard.
The graphics are pretty good, even on my ancient (DX9) PC which doesn´t really go above the minimum requirements.
After 2 crashes right at the beginning of the game, it seems to run very well now (window mode). The AI/animations are ´nice´, though not ´breathtaking´ and the whole scenery and the details in gameplay are implemented delicately. So far I would tend to recommend this game to everyone who likes open world action games, BUT...
...it seems like that one of the developers dropped off with his head on Copy&Paste.
Yes, of course you have to expect some similarities to the Assassin´s Creed games, but this is on the edge of being ridiculous.
Two of the most important things in this game is to capture towers to ´unlock´ and reveal parts of the map and the conquer enemy bases. Does that ring a bell? Yes, you had to ... capture towers to ´unlock´ and reveal parts of the map and the conquer enemy bases in Assassin´s Creed. Oh... and (spoiler spoiler) the storyline tells you to rescue your friends. I think I can remember a game with a similar task. ... Ah, right. Assassin´s Creed by UbiSoft!
Dear developers,
if you copy/paste major parts for an older game of yours, please don´t make it THAT obvious, you make me feel dumb. :/
So: If you haven´t played any AC-game yet or if you would like to have "AC 3 1/2 - Goes modern", this game is for you!
P.S.: I will give a NO on the recommendation just for the "Let´s recycle it and squeeze it out"-spirit.

Got to say Far Cry 3 is a brilliant package. Visually it's one of the most gorgeous games I've played so far. The tropical island is lush, appropriately has wild life here and there but not oversaturating the islands. Shooting and the hide and stabbing work satisfyingly well. Compared to Far Cry 2 the game has much more substance. There's much more to do in the open world and it doesn't feel so empty. Plus the driving, which actually in 3 is much more optional than in 2, has much more weight and is through that more enjoyable. There's a lot of good writing in characters, especially in the "evil" ones. But I suppose like with every open world game there comes the sense of repetition eventually. Focusing doing too many side quests and other side activities might make you a little bored after a while.
I really didn't have any problems technically despite maybe a crash that happened once during the 18-hour playthrough but that's just really minor. If you've got the specs on your machine to run this game and you do enjoy a bit of open world FPS, can't say you're going wrong by buying and playing Far Cry 3. Unlike Far Cry 2 it's totally worth your time. It's a sweet piece of... smooth jungle beauty.

When I say this game has a good story I mean the gameplay flows nicely and the concept of the story is really intresting. But to be completly honest with you this game is a really sad game if you think about it. First off everyone on the island except for the civilians living there has a problem. What was once a peaceful island turned into an absolute power struggle  between three waring factions. Not only that but if you think of it many of these factions were into bad habits such as killing innocent people for money and doing drugs and the worst part is they learned to enjoy it. What's even sadder about this game is "you" as a character also fell responsible for killing people and thourghout the game your chracter starts getting used to it like it's an everday thing. Although, you were trying to save your friends at the end of the game your character comes to realize that he has turned into something that he does not want to be and what he has done on the island will always be in his memory. This is why I find the game sad. One thing I didn't like about the game was the Multiplayer I had many issues with connecting to servers and even if I did get into a server tons of host migration were soon to follow which disrupted the gameplay to a point were the game was unplayable and in my opinion the Far Cry series is more of a single player game rather than a multiplayer game. Eventhough, this was the first Far Cry game I played I can't wait for the next Far Cry to come out and I can't wait to see what it has to offer.

Pros: Fantastic open world, great combat, decent weapon selection, decently competent AI, RPG-like exploratory experience that almost never feels "grindy". Hunting big game is awesome, and actually feels like...hunting. Stealth game play is even solid, which tends to feel gimicky and slapped on in these types of games. Generic missions have enough variety to stay fresh. Although I'm focusing on other aspects of the game, this list can go on and there's no denying that the game play in of itself is stellar.
Cons:  A few annoying features in terms of design (for example, sometimes picking up items is mixed with weapons switch out since they use the same hotkey). Occasionally weird physics can ruin some immersive moments (why is that giant dead bear rolling and bouncing down a realatively flat surface?). Some seemingly easy to add features were completely unavailable (why can I only move bodies on a special kill?  Why not after they have already dropped to the ground?)
Story: 7
While much of the story itself wasn't particularly revolutionary, the fact that simply playing the storyline alone can last over twenty hours without feeling repetitive, grindy, or contrived is a feat unto itself.  The motivation feels vague at times, but the clear conflict between the need for violence to save himself and his friends and the consuming negative nature of said violence becomes starkly clear by the final act.
Mood/Atmosphere - 9
Fantastic jungle renderings, gorgeous mountain ranges, and beautiful lagoons.  The soundtrack compliments the emotion of the landscapes. Certainly a memorable experience.
Graphics - 8
Solid facial and body animations. While the detail itself wasn't the best I've seen, the motion tracking worked well for creating believable body movements, which complemented the acting. Environments looks great , and the weather effects look stunning even on low settings. The grass effects are simple but effective for stealth game play and hiding the animals in the grass.
Sound Design - 7
One of my biggest pet peeves of Farcry 2 was the obnoxious looping soundtrack. Farcry 3's score was substantially stronger, and after the game I found myself relistening to the opening theme days later. The rest of the sound design erred on the side of subtlety, to the point that sometimes I didn't even noticed I had been injured because the character didn't make the usual borderline-sexual grunting noises when hurt.  While maybe detracting from some supposed "realism", it removed a lot of the audio repetitiveness of the last game which for me was a plus.
Acting (special category): 10
Few games deserve this as a category seperate from story, but this is where the game really shines. Particularly in the case of Michael Mando, there are arguably few better performances in gaming history. While the story may not be revolutionary, the implemtation of motion capture and performance certainly plays out in an incredible way.  That alone is enough to carry the game.  As a side note, a live action youtube video series was released with Christopher Mintz Plasse and Michael Mando.  You should check it out, its hilarious.
Should I play this game?
There are few FPS or RPG players who won't enjoy this gaming experience. There's a little bit for everybody, and it's worth the 20 hour play through on the incredible acting and cut scenes alone.

"Did I ever tell you the definition of insanity?"
That haunting quote is delivered by one of the best antagonists I have ever encountered in a video game, Vaas Montenegro the Pirate leader who captures you and your friends and imprisons you on the vast jungle that is the Rook Islands.
The game puts you into a first person perspective of a daredevil college student name Jason Brody and his journey to save his friends; the challenges he faces along the way both physically and mentally.
What I think is brilliant about Jason is he is so relatable: at the start of the game it shows how he is shocked at having to kill somebody to save his own life and how he develops to killing people without even thinking about it and he even refers it to at one point as "winning".
Without spoiling the plot to much I would like to reflect on the quote at the start of this review, it is really applicable to the whole story line Jason being a slave to society and his mental downturn as he attempts to save his friends. The plunge that Jason takes from school boy to warrior is something that very much made this game for me.
The islands that you are on is a vast open Jungle that is just aching to be explored, many different cave systems and old relics from the islands history can be found such as collecting long lost letters from deceased Japanese soldiers way back in the islands history, during WWII or collecting ancient Rakyat relics. Rook islands are themselves a beautiful place, the graphics on this game are outstanding, I was playing this game on almost maximum graphics without anti-aliasing and it still looks gorgeous even when you switch to the low graphics option, just don't expect a difference in weather as I have only ever seen it rain twice which I guess helps with the immersion of a tropical island. The whole islands are accessible to you right after the first mission and you are always given the choice of exploring first and missions later, the later I chose and it has taken me most of my game hours exploring the island which I do not regret.
The island can be quite dangerous, not to mention the vast array of wildlife that you can encounter and the pirate enemies who just want to kill you. There are a range of animals from carnivorous tigers and bears to your average pig and deer. All of these animals can be killed and skinned in order for you to make more pouches to carry new gear.
One of the antagonists of the game that I thought was a selling point to this game was indeed Vaas, who I mentioned right at the start of this review. You would normally expect your average villain to constantly be hurting you and torturing you; not Vaas. I thought Vaas as more as a comedian than the antagonist, his delivery by the brilliant Michael Mando was outstanding, Vaas reflects on the overall theme of this game. Insanity.
The gameplay is also outstanding in this game:
There is quite a factor of stealth in this game, throughout the game there are options to take over outposts which when captured allow you to travel the island safely without encountering enemies such as the pirates. You have a wide range of ways to take over a base for example: you could hang back and scout out the base first and take down each enemy one by one or go in guns blazing shooting everyone on sight with the risk of them calling for back up; there is the alternative of setting many of the animals found on Rook island upon the enemy’s which is always fun.
As with every RPG/FPS there is always a levelling system, in Far Cry 3 this comes in the form of a self-growing tattoo dubbed 'Tatua' by the natives, I think that this is a unique approach to skills in a game as every time you acquire a new skill you gain a new tattoo and by the end of the game you look like a Japanese warrior.
Speaking of which, there is also a mass of weapons to choose from, you can choose from Magnums to SMG's to AK's and even a flamethrower (of which there is a brilliant mission involving burning a certain illegal substance).
Although the quest is quite a short one it is once again reflective of the games theme of insanity, which would have to be my only criticism in this game. If I were to play again and just focus entirely on the quest I could probably get it completed in under a day. But it is the exploring that makes the game interesting because you can acquire items that help you with the main missions.
In conclusion:
This game is a brilliant open world RPG/FPS action game that has a beautiful jungle setting with a short but memorable story the line and more than memorable characters. It has a alternative setting to the usual modern FPS instead of being a trained military soldier you are just a young adult fresh from college. A must by and a gaming experience I will not forget for a long time.

Far Cry 3 is the perfect combination of First Person Shooter in an Open World. Although the vanilla version of the game isn’t quite perfect it is pretty dang close, and Ziggy’s Mod helps fill in the gaps.
Far Cry 3 feels like a FPS. All of the guns and weapons feel and sound like you expect them to. Everything ranging from a bow or silenced rifle to a flamethrower or rpg gives you the ability to go about your business in whatever way you want. But Far Cry 3 is also the most open of open worlds. If you see two “bad guys” walking down the “road” you can leave them be and go around them, or kill them quietly with a silenced weapon, the bow, or your melee knife takedown; or you can pull out your ak47 assault rifle and let the gunshots echo off the hills (they don’t actually echo, but that would be cool). If you do choose to just let the gunfire rip then you will suffer the consequences. Within seconds a car or two with more “bad guys” will come racing up to hunt you down, or some other fellow “bad guys” that were walking on a trail not too far away will come running your way.
This leads to one of my favorite aspects of this game (on the harder difficulties). It doesn’t take much for your character to die. That’s right. You’re not invincible, one headshot can “end the game” so to speak (death in the game doesn’t really penalize you), but it isn’t that hard to kill one of the bad guys either. One well-placed shot will take down 99% of the “bad guys” in the game.
So going back to the previous scenario where you killed two lone “bad guys” in hostile territory, if you aren’t careful then you will get surrounded which is all but a guaranteed death for you. So if you are going to make noise then you have to keep moving, and if you are engaging multiple hostiles then a tactical retreat and circling around will help keep the enemy puzzled when it comes to your location, which gives you the advantage.
Most of the animals in this game can be killed and skinned of their hide, which can then be used in the crafting to increase your storage for weapons and grenades ect ect. For the vanilla version, the crafting was very rudimentary and was extremely easy to get the required skins. In Ziggy’s mod the crafting recipes become way more difficult in the variety of things that need to be collected as well as the sheer number of items that need to be collected. The map also removes the locations of each of the animals. This makes the game a bit harder as well as more time is spent traipsing over the island looking for a specific animal that you know you saw earlier in the game, but you just can’t remember exactly where you were.
Like most FPS games you are pretty much a one man army that can kill waves of enemies without getting a scratch, and if you get a scratch then you can heal yourself during combat without thinking twice. But during the cut scenes you are a person with feelings and vulnerabilities. In Far Cry 3 the main character isn’t a macho man like other games with a special ability or an augmentation that gives him an advantage, he is more of a normal guy (although he does seem to be a bit whinny). A lot of people seem to dislike this about the game saying that he would never be able to do what is done in the game, but I argue that no matter how well trained a single soldier is they wouldn’t be able to take on the odds in Far Cry 3. If you can get passed that point then the story is enjoyable and better than others although it does seem to fit into a cheezy survival flick that you would find on tv in the middle of the day. If you look pass the surface level story of the game then it delves into obsession and insanity. This is something that I think a lot of people have misinterpreted, or perhaps I am the one reading between the lines where nothing was meant to be read.
There are a number of features in the vanilla version of the game that have been changed or eliminated in Ziggy’s mod. Things like being able to highlight the “bad guys” with your binoculars and then be able to see them through walls and behind trees and stuff, or unlocking a weapon to buy for free just by picking one up off of a dead bad guy, or having to hold down the interact button for 2 seconds to do things like loot bodies or open chests or doors. Ziggy’s mod also increases the difficulty of the game as far as the AI goes. For any “hardcore” gamer out there looking for a challenge I would recommend playing Far Cry 3 on the very hard difficulty with the Hardcore version of Ziggy’s mod and go to your game options and turn everything off. (things like detection meter and reticle aiming)
When you die in Far Cry 3 it is because you got overwhelmed. Example: You are getting shot at and loosing health while a rabid dog is attacking your leg, you need to reload and take a health injection as well as just sprint for cover all at the same time, but you can only do one thing at a time. That is when you die in Far Cry 3…
Ziggy’s mod is great for people wanting to play through the game for a second or third time with the additional difficulty. For your first time, I would recommend trying the vanilla version and if there are aspects of the game that you dislike that can be fixed by Ziggy’s mod, then go ahead and get it. There are different versions of Ziggy’s mod difficulty wise so you should be able to fix things that you want without adding too much difficulty although I can’t confirm that. I know for me the long button press to loot a body or open a door was too much. Ziggy’s mod shouldn’t be too hard to find. It is on NexusMods and you will have to manually install it since steam doesn’t have a workshop for it.
As always do some research about the game before buying it. If anybody has any questions feel free to ask, and I apologize for all the English errors.

You play as Jason Brody, who went on vacation with his friends to Rook Islands. However, during the trip you are abducted by modern pirates and are held hostage for ransom money, or to be sold into slavery. You manage to escape and have to save your friends and conquer the islands.
The gameplay is wonderful. It's a smooth, streamlined FPS control scheme with basic controls (WASD, Space to jump, shift to sprint etc.) however it brings plenty of amazing features to the field. Channel your "inner warrior" through the "tatau", a growing skill tree in the form of a dynamic tribal tattoo on your arm. Learn skills to increase your max health, perform great knife takedowns (such as reaching out of the water at a dock and pulling down two enemies, then stabbing them both, all in one "Double Death From Below" takedown.) or recover more materials from plants and animals.
Oh right, I forgot to mention. Plants and animals.
This game has a crafting system. You use plants you find to craft various syringes, from those that can be quickly used to recover health, to those that can grant fire immunity, or increased animal detection. Use animal skins and leather to craft larger weapon pouches to carry up to four weapons at once, a much larger loot sack, a larger flamethrower fuel pouch, and much more.
Aside from completing the story missions (which are long and detailed,) you can choose to do sidequests, which range from meeting side characters and performing tasks for them for money, or taking over radio towers and enemy outposts. Radio towers are scattered across the islands, and are old and rickety. You'll need to maneuver up them with their falling walkways, broken handguards, and dangling ropes. Once you reach the top of one, you can remove the scrambler from it's control box. This does two things; It reveals the surrounding area on your map, and you are also rewarded with a few free weapons from the nearby shop for each tower activated.
The other activity I mentioned was taking over enemy outposts. The pirates have many outposts across the islands which can be identified by their red flags and giant smokestacks. You can approach one, and must take it over by eliminating all of the enemies in it. You can approach this any way you like. Stay on a cliffside nearby and try to snipe them all with a silenced sniper rifle. Sneak into the nearby bushes with a recurve bow and pick them off silently and skillfully. Perhaps you want to run in with a powerful LMG and empty a clip into everyone you see? Or just bring in a handy dandy flamethrower and burn everything and everyone to the ground. However you choose to do it, kill everyone and the outpost is yours, to serve as a shop, safe haven, and fast travel point.
As for the game's AI, it's pretty good, but not the best. It's great in some places, for example, enemies will clearly avoid you if you're wielding a flamethrower, lighting everything up, and try to attack from afar, and unlike Far Cry 2, they'll easily notice if one of their friends drops dead near them at the hands of your bullets. Unfortunately, they aren't too dynamic, and if they see you madly slashing away at their allies with your machete, they'll still stay pretty close and attempt to shoot, ignoring the fact that they're about to be split into two as well.
One of my only jabs on the game is the crafting system is a bit odd if you think about it. Why do I need boar skin to build this specific size wallet? Why wouldn't cassowary leather or pig hide work?
The game itself looks stunning. It's a beautiful tropical paradise (except for the fact that there's pirates that'll sell you into slavery) that has tall mountains, beautiful forests, stunning waterfalls, and all around looks amazing. As long as your PC can handle the "Ultra" graphics setting, you'll definitely consider putting this on a list of most beautiful games. Not only is there the beautiful tranquility of the landscape, but also the chaos can be wonderful. The guns and player models look great and well detailed, and fire looks menacing and natural, burning away trees and grass, and spreading like a normal fire would. The game's facial animation and expression is extremely well done, and you can always see the emotion conveyed in the character's faces.
The game's audio really imerses you in Far Cry 3. There are pretty much sounds for everything, from sliding down a cliff to being mauled by a bear. They are all in great quality, and surround sound immerses you further if you have it. It's such a great moment of terror when you're scoping out an outpost you want to conquer and you hear a very close, very loud growl of a mountain lion. As for the soundtrack, it's one of the best out of any game I've ever played. The game plays intense music that truley fits when you've been discovered by the enemy, and somber piano tunes when the story reaches a tragic point.
, although you can't truly understand how great it is without hearing it in context in the game.
I won't say too much here as to not spoil it, but this game has probably my favorite story of any game ever. Some say it is bad because it's unrealistic, and they aren't wrong about the slight shift from reality. At some parts there are a few questionable moments, such as, "how is this one white boy taking down an entire army of pirates?" although questions like that are asked in many games. However, this doesn't make it any less of a game, it just helps you realize more and more however that you might just really be falling into insanity.
This unfortunately, is where the game falls behind. The multiplayer is bland and is pretty generic. There's nothing WRONG with it necessarily, but there's nothing too good with it either. Any other multiplayer shooter should stand about level with it in terms of multiplayer. Even the co-op compain can seem a bit grindish. This will be a game you'll get and love for a great singleplayer experience, story and gameplay combined. If you mainly like multiplayer games, I'd say keep looking.
Far Cry 3 is a refreshing open world FPS game that brings a great skill system, fantastic crafting, smooth gunplay, and a beautiful world. The game is great to experience on your own and the story will almost certainly not dissapoint, although the game does fall behind if you want a great multiplayer experience.
+   AMAZING STORY
+   FANTASTIC GUNPLAY
+   WELL-REFINED CRAFTING AND SKILLS SYSTEM
+   BEAUTIFUL, EXPANSIVE OPEN WORLD
-    BLAND, LACKING MULTIPLAYER

I stuck it through to the end of the campaign, but this is the first game in a while that I was happy to delete.  This game is a “far cry” from the Trigens that I loved in the original Farcry, and it’s turned me off the series now for good.  There’s a reason why the game is so cheap.
Visuals are incredible.  Sound is awesome.  The characters, voice acting, and animation are top-notch.  At its core, the FPS gameplay is superlative!  This game is BEAUTIFUL and provides movie-quality experience.  The best advice I can give if you already own it but haven’t tried it, is to play it free-form and enjoy the open-world experience.  But if you want a better FPS story experience that looks just as good, try the Crysis titles instead. As for co-op, I didn't try it, but I’m sure it’s good, as the FPS mechanics in this game are very good.
However the campaign content in Farcry3 is so RAW that I cannot in good conscience recommend anyone playing this game.  I like my meat medium-rare, but this one is still on a living animal.  I am VERY concerned that underage people are experiencing it.  Now, don’t peg me off as some religious bible-thumper that is pro-censorship; you should hear me swearing and cursing at slow drivers while I tear down the roads cutting people off in my gas-guzzling tweaked-out car.  In the end, with FarCry 3, I just was not ENTERTAINED by “playing through” the actions you are required to take to progress in the game.
The game is plastered with EXTREME profanity, there was no hope of me playing it with the volume up without offending anybody nearby.   The pirates are constantly swearing at you, taunting you, calling you a mutha*cker, the main character swears as he skins animals or nearly dies, and the cut scenes are so full of offensive language that it seems they had to fill a quota and fill in as many sh!t’s and fu*k’s as they could.
The single-player campaign has you hunting animals (boars, pigs, deer, goats, sharks, komodo dragons, dogs, leopards, tigers, bears) with all sorts of weapons, including bows, shotguns, assault rifles, and flamethrowers.  Yes, there ACTUALLY is a mission that requires you hunt down and kill eight dogs with a flamethrower.  Now, to be fair, they were advertised as “rabid dogs that need to be put down.”  But as I approached with my flamethrower in hand, and walked right up to the pack of 8, not one attacked me.  And as I started to flame them, all they did was run away whining.  NOT a fun gaming experience.  I have a dog, she’s an important member of our family.  THIS was in no way fun.
And then, the premise is, you skin each of the animals.  On the screen, as you do this, you get a gory visual of the main character inserting his knife into the dead animal, ripping the skin off, and putting the lump of flesh into his rucksack (usually with a “f*ck!” while he does it).  This is REQUIRED so that you can “craft” larger containers to carry your crap in.  Otherwise you can only carry one weapon, with little ammo, and very little money.  F@ck, if I want do that crap I will go play deer hunter.  And CRAFTING?  Why, since MineCraft came out, does everyone think they need to have it too?!   If I want to mix sh!t together, I’ll go try to cook something in the kitchen and fail miserably.  Why can’t I just pick up med kits or buy them in stores like all the other FPS games out there?  No, I have to search for green leaves to CRAFT syringes (where does the syringe come from???)
Anyway, back to the story.  It is a mystical tale of human trafficking, drug trade, overcoming all odds, and saving (or betraying) your friends, who are being held hostage on the tropical paradise by pirates.  The bad guy characters are all way too over-the-top insane.  Hilarious at times, mind you, I did laugh, but Vass is simply too much, and he sure screams a lot.  Oh, and did I mention he swears?  Hoyt is a bit better for language, and funny too, but you actually see him for less of the game than Vass.
You spend half of the key plot sequences in (apparently) a drug or mushroom-induced hallucinogenic state, fighting fiery demons with a bow and arrows or knives.  At the end of these sequences, I found out that, apparently, I succeeded in killing the bad guy.  What the hell?  Why can’t I just put a bullet through his head?  Oh, was that a bit too gory for mainstream gaming perhaps?
At various points, the game has you holding space bar down to TORTURE people.  It includes first-person sex scenes with a crazy jungle girl.  There are themes of r@pe (including homosexual – you are asked to pucker up your a$$ up on several occasions).  There are people that are burned to death in cages in movie-like experience.  If I want to see all of that, I’ll fire up an old copy of Amistad.  This is NOT entertaining.
All in all, it’s just too much.  I just want to run and gun and save the hot chick so she can suggestively tell me that I should come over later with a smile and a wink.  Happy ending.
Back to the good in this sh!t sandwich – the guns are done very well, with a good selection and interesting attachment options.  The vehicles in the game are lots of fun, all sorts of road and water craft to try, albeit with some questionable physics.  The islands themselves are beautifully constructed, with beaches, caves, hidden pathways, old temples – everything you loved from Tomb Raider, and more.  The open-world concept is very nice, “freeing” the radio towers is an interesting side quest for the first 10 towers, and then it gets tedious afterwards (though the puzzle aspect of it was fun).  At least it unlocked new guns and opened up your map, otherwise I wouldn’t have bothered.  I have the same feelings about re-taking outposts, it was fun the first 20 times.  However the game requires you to do it in order to open up new “hunter quests” so that you can craft the very best equipment.
By the end of my ~25-hour experience, I simply had enough and powered through the rest of the campaign so I could delete it from my hard drive.  Unfortunately for me, once I start something, I usually have to finish it.  Notice I didn’t have to mention uPlay to complain about this game.  But that part sucks too.
ANYWAY, there was one memorable and awesome part of the game that I want to mention – you are required to take your newfound flamethrower and burn up some drug fields on a plantation to set back the local warlord.  As you arrive at the mission site, the soundtrack switches over to gangsta rap (a good track actually!) while you run and spray all of the drug fields.  It was very well orchestrated and reminded me of the epic fax machine scene in Office Space.  If there’s one reason I’d start up Far Cry 3 again, it would be to do that mission.  If it was available as a separate $2 mission, I’d buy it and play it.
Don’t do it kids, go enjoy real life or a more encouraging game instead of wasting your time with this overly-negative story experience.
EDIT:  Steam Censorship

What a massive game this is. Huge islands to explore with just too many sidequests. You can just run/drive/fly around and do nothing or you can; hunt animals, craft items, free settlements, find relics and other secrets, take over radio towers, do some trials and a whole lot of other activities and (side)quests. It's seemingly endless and completing the entire game will take you probably well over 50 hours. Now that's some value right there.
The graphics are just gorgeous, no matter what settings you use. You can't make this game look bad, you just can't. The animations and models are some of the best I've seen in a game. Wow. The same thing applies to the sounds and voice acting, which is brilliant and truly convincing.
While doing the story and sidequests you'll earn XP to upgrade your skills. There are 3 skilltrees in total and the way you play the game is entirely up to you. The Shark skilltree will let you upgrade your assault and healing skills, while the Heron tree will help you with your sniper skills and speed and finally, the Spider tree will let you focus on your stealth and survival skills. There's no right way to play this. There are many ways to complete an objective. And that's what makes Far Cry 3 fun, but not necessarily unique.
However, there aren't many FPS that give you this much freedom, while telling a realistic, focused, story at the same time. So I take my hat off to Ubisoft for creating this masterpiece. The commercial and critical success for this game is well deserved.
Let this be a lesson - and example - for future first person shooters. Hooray for Far Cry 3 !
Great game, great story. Linear story, yes, but fantastic. This is what FPS games should be like.

Rather than write out a wall of text I'm just going to summarize some things I've noticed in my ~6 hours playing.
FC3 introduces a crafting system that allows you to increase the amount of ammo/guns/items/syringes/etc. you carry. This is done by killing and skinning different animals (of which there are a ton) that roam the island. Different items require a different animal skin, and the amount of the skin needed varies as well. This is better than simply going to a store and purchasing them with money, but it's not very in depth. You could go and farm the animal skins/plants and max out your ammo/guns/syringes within an hour if you really wanted.
The storyline is pretty dumb/ridiculous
The game relies a little too much on stealth. You receive bonus XP for killing enemies with your knife or a "takedown", which inadvertently punishes players who prefer to snipe or run in guns blazing. In addition there is new "assassination" side quest that has you take out someone causing havoc on the island. Unfortunately, you
to use your knife to kill them and they're never alone. So you can gun everyone down and then try to knife them when they're on full alert, or spend 5 minutes silently stalking and knifing everyone.
There's also a new side quest to hunt down and kill animals using a specific weapon. It'd be nice if the assassination quests were like this.
The visuals are gorgeous and the sounds are fantastic.
There is a huge, open world environment to explore.
The game is a little easy because loot chests, animals, and plants are all shown on the map. If you wanted you could go and collect all the loot boxes and sell the items for a ton of money pretty quickly. Syringes are crafted from plants, which there's a small amount of, but they all fall into color categories : green, blue, red, amber, white, etc. All are visible on the minimap. So you if you just care about health syringes, you could easily only pick up the green plants to craft them while avoiding all the other colors of plants shown on the map.
The weapon selection is pretty decent and offers some typical customization options (attachments and skins). No attachments for sniper rifles though.
You have a camera which can mark enemies, so you can watch them on your screen/minimap. It helps to plan an attack for when you want to go stealth. Pretty useful, I use it often.
Overall FC3 is really fun, I find myself playing it for a bit everyday. I have a few gripes, but it really doesn't detract from the game that much. I got it during the Winter sale for $7.49, and I think I've already gotten my money's worth. I wouldn't pay $40 or whatever it is normally, but if you're interested and it goes on sale, I'd recommend picking it up.

Far Cry 3 is a great game that showcases how far video games have come as far as technology goes, but I personally found it uninteresting and unoriginal. It's a great game in its own right, but in my opinion it does little to separate itself from other shooters except being open world, which is not enough to keep my interest.
Don't get me wrong. This is a gorgeous game, with a carefully crafted world, decent storyline, and about everything else you can expect from a triple-A title. The way the game tries to "innovate" is through the addition of RPG-like elements, such as crafting (a process created to encourage players to go out and hunt wild animals or collect random flowers of different colors), stealth (very similar system to any Bethesda game, crouch and hope they don't see you), and skill trees. However, many of these mechanics simply served to irritate me, in a way that is hard to explain unless you have played the game yourself.
In my experience, crafting simply made gameplay tedious for me. I would often find far too many of one kind of plant or creature, but hardly any of another. My inventory quickly became overloaded, yet I hadn't found a single hide of the required type to craft a larger bag with more inventory space. It felt more like a barrier to the gameplay, creating unneeded tasks to fill up gameplay time rather than making the actual experience more interesting.
Stealth (something I am very fond of in my action games) was hampered by the fact that once you silently kill someone, the body becomes unmovable, alerting enemies who discover it to your presence. I later discovered through the internet that there is a perk that allows you to move bodies, but only if you hold down a key as you are killing the enemy, with the corpse becoming once again unmovable after you drop it.
Another thing that bothered me was my inability to "click" with the main character or put myself in his shoes. He (I don't even remember his name) seems like a normal guy, thrown into a situation that is way over his head. I understand that much. What I don't understand that breaks the experience for me is how he suddenly becomes a superhuman army of one, who can suddenly sprint for hours across a jungle, getting shot 5 times, while raining a firey bullet hell on his enemies, but sounding like a whiny kid in all of the cutscenes (ALL OF THEM). He is potrayed as young man, but it feels like he is still in high school. When the player is put in control of him he is suddenly an action hero, complete with sunglasses. I don't buy the "tatoo gives me strength" crap either, because one would hope his voice would be a little less high-pitched if it did. The development team tries to make the hero relateable to by making him seem inexperienced with death (Illustrated in the beginning of the game when
) but then suddenly turns him into a f*cking death-dealing grim reaper of AK-47's with no explanation. (hormones?)
Ubisoft's mandatory Uplay account is also tiresome, forcing you to create yet another email-linked account that allows corporate bodies to send you unwanted spam.
If you enjoy high quality first person shooters but don't care about orginality, then your money is well spent. Far Cry 3 is a very well made game, in a perfect position to show off the revolutions in video game techonology. Don't let me stop you from getting the game, which is worth the money development-wise. However, if you came here looking for innovation or something new, keep looking.

If you play games for the gameplay mechanics, then you might like this game. The FPS mechanics are pretty solid, and the stronghold takeovers were enjoyable. The menus and map take too long to load, though. This is especially noticable when opening the map, which, being an open-world game, I had to reference again and again. I also felt that my character died too easily during the main story on the "Easy" difficulty setting, which became frustrating in the later missions due to the positioning of checkpoints.
If you play games for the storytelling, then you might not like this game unless you like stories geared towards young adult males. I felt that the voice acting was very good. The story was acceptable, but the actual dialog that the voice actors had to speak was often bad. All of the characters annoyed me with the exception of Vaas (who i felt was the best part of this game), Citra and possibly Sam.
The game world looks fantastic. One things that I was pleasantly surprised by is that way that fire spreads. Throw a Molotov in the jungle, and stand back.
The stronghold takeovers were the high point of this game for me, and I put off the main story to do them. After I had finished all of those, however, I felt the urge to uninstall this game a number of times before I had finished the main story.

While Far Cry 3 is a good game it really misses being a great one. It seems like a developer that went through the trouble of created such a detailed world for us to adventure in would at least try to avoid some of the irritating gameplay that troubles most sandboxes.
