If you cannot do more dialog just turn it off after we are so far in the game. Silence would be golden at this point. It is at the worst when you play the poker mini game. Where the other players nag you with their repeatable dialog until you want to scream. No penalty for dying is a big game play mechanics mistake. In a game I could have spent many enjoyable hours, I have spent the usual twenty then the game has turned into work trying to ignore the irritating faults built in to the gameplay. Do not get me wrong this is a must play game for all the game engine break through that are too numerous to mention. But for all their hard work if they would fleshed out some of the irritants that really start showing up from about twenty to sixty hours of gameplay they would have had a masterpiece game. Far Cry 3:
+ Good graphics
+ A nice array of side quests and activities, including assassinations, medical supply drops, hunting tasks, assaulting enemy strongholds and breaking signal jammers on radio towers.
+ Decent storyline
+ Great arsenal of destructive weapons, such as bows and arrows, RPG's, grenades, submachine guns, shotguns, handguns, assault rifles and more!
+ Weapons can be upgraded with silencers, laser dot sights, extended clips or reflex sights, so you can adjust gameplay to your own style.
+ Skills system whereby you learn new abilities each time you level up.
+ Co-op mode for multiplayer.
+ Approximately 70-90 hours of gameplay for completionists.
- Side missions and activities, while numerous, are usually very repetitive. For example, assassinations always involve killing a particular individual using a knife and medical supply drops are always timed 'races' through checkpoints. This didn't impact on my fun but for some people it will, so I've listed it here.
- Many abilities in the leveling system are not very practical, you won't find much application for them in the game world. Some improvements to health and weapon accuracy are useful but others are not. Thus, the skills system is not as good as it could have been.
Overall score: 8/10

After having played the previous Far Cry titles mildly and to some level of discontent, I've come to the third title in the franchise hoping that it takes the open-world formula far enough to stand out amonst the crowd of blockbuster titles waiting to be played in my backlog. I'm very happy to say that despite a few paralyzing bugs that disallowed me from furthering my experience with the game, reformatting my hard drive was totally worth the second half of the game. There isn't anything revolutionary or mind-blowing about Far Cry 3, but Ubisoft keeps all facets of the game's production as tight as possible from it's stellar motion-capturing and voice acting, to the primal soundtrack, and the few but jaw-dropping moments in the plotline. The villians in this game are compelling, and during your killing spree in the tropic island you begin to question your motives and your identity in significant ways.
There may be a chance for me to replay this game with my mind set purely on playing in the sandbox than pushing the plot. A major negative to this game in the context of Ubisoft is that it's exactly like Assassin's Creed but in a different setting, and so Far Cry may beg for a bit more creativity. Regardless of how this game compares to others, there isn't one quite like Far Cry 3, and I highly recommend it for at least one play through.

They will all die for taking my outposts, the pirates are dead men walking and they don't even know it.  Which sounds impressive until I realize I didn't pay enough attention to my surroundings and a goddamn leopard has snuck up and is disemboweling me before I can even put away my binoculars.
The most fun is taking an outpost by shooting the front off a cage and releasing a leopard/tiger/bear and then picking off the pirates as it chews their faces off.  Also starting a nice brush fire is fun - that way I can send a bear or leopard from the forest into the outpost!  I am Jack's faceless death...

This may be long, but there are some things about this game that should be known before someone buys it.  I have no idea why the review says I played it for 1 hour or so as I completed the game and it certainly didn't take an hour.  Thanks UPlay and Steam for their accuracy and well done programs.
The game is actually very, very good for the most part.  It is interesting and very fun to play with some reasonable challenges for an FPS and has some nice RPG elements thrown in to make it a bit more interesting.  The graphics are pretty good.  The NPC AI was actually good for the animals but I am not sure why people (NPCs) were added.  For example, I found a woman crying on the beach and some guy carrying a piece of "I" beam on a road while exploring.  There was no way to interact with them - even just to say "hi" let alone what they were doing or if I could help.  It just seemed sort of stupid to have them in the game if they did nor added nothing to the game.  I also wondered why there were groups of the locals standing in locations just shooting guns in the air.  I typically went towards any gun fire I heard, hoping for a nice fight and earning some skill points, but typically found 3 NPCs shooting guns in the air for no reason and no way to find out why.
Weapons were not over or under powered and accuracy was pretty darn good as I was doing lots of headshots with various weapons from a pretty good distance.
For a FPS, the story wasn't bad, a nice and simple "go kill the bad guys" like it should be - but for the minor RPG aspects it was terrible; clichéd, contrived completely uninteresting and didn't add anything to the game that the simple "go kill the bad guys" didn't already set as a completely adequate game story.
For the most part, the game is quite good and it is well worth buying and playing if you get it on sale for a low, low cost, but I wouldn't pay more than $10.00 for this game - and here's why.  The designers and programmers were lazy or stupid or just didn't care about elements and the game.
Walking along and getting stuck on a slight protrusion on the ground is just bad, lazy programming. I constantly hit this glitch entering the village store and on bridges, stairs, in buildings and caves, etc.  It was just annoying and completely distracting when focused in a fire fight and sneaking/running for cover and getting stuck on a door transom 1/2 inch high or getting stuck on a stone path in a cave while trying to skirt some hazard or manoeuvring to figure out how to get over/around some obstacle.  Same with looting a body or chest - if you are not in the exact, correct spot, you have to adjust left-right-back-forward until you hit the sweet spot to get the signal you can now loot, empty, skin or gather the item in front of you.
The game is advertised as "open world" - it lied.  It isn't open and I constantly ran into a big warning that flashed on the screen that I was leaving the mission area and unless I got back, the mission would fail.  It actually was so linear in places it ruined play.  I want to get to that rock to use my sniper rifle and get a tactical advantage, but I'm 10 feet off the path the game insists I follow so I fail the mission?  Not open world by any definition. Yeah, doing nothing but wandering and exploring is open world, but then it doesn't matter.
Cut scenes.  Other than the first conversation cut scene, none of the others actually added anything to the story, didn't aid in doing anything and were just annoying and frustrating and had enough sway and jerk and tilt to make you seasick.  Did I really need to know that some native was in the USA as a mechanic and got made fun of because of his accent?  I'm not sure what this added or why it was in the game.
Then there was the times you are getting really involved and things were getting really interesting and... the game takes control of your character, then you have control, then the game, then you, then a big white flash and a fade out and you wake up to a cut scene with your character moaning and groaning and gasping for 2-3 minutes and suddenly with a bright white flash you are back in the game.  It was frustrating, stupid and annoying and ruined some of the best parts of the game. Worse, in some cut scenes the way to get through was by button mashing. Really?  I am fighting some NPC/animal and I have to press "E", "C", "mash Space", "Left Mouse", "Right Mouse" then "mash A, A, A" when cued by a big flashing symbol on the screen to successfully win? I missed everything on the screen because I was watching for the cues on what button to mash.  Annoying and stupid.
The Boss fights are incredibly stupid, lame and so wasteful.  You spend time and effort and actually have a ton of fun doing any number of things in the game to build up your character and get skills and abilities and weapons and when you are all prepared for the big Boss fight.... none of it matters.  The stereotyped, native witch with the terrible accent (and she is the ugliest female I have ever seen in a game - and that includes 8-bit games I played years ago) puts you on LSD or some jungle juice drink and you wander through a haze to kill a smoke monster (the easiest Boss I have ever fought-3 arrows to the face and - done) and then you have to stab another stereotyped native with a bad accent holding a magic knife.  No skills needed nor any abilities, just run up to him until the cut scene takes over and you stab him and he dies.  Gee, thanks for making what should be the best and most challenging part of the game just a lame, stupid cut scene.
Do I recommend the game?  Yes, but if you get it for a really low cost and can take the frustrating and poorly done parts in stride.  About 2/3 of the game is hugely fun and offers hours of interesting entertainment fighting, looting, exploring and collecting certain items, so again, I'd buy it if it's less than $10.00.

Far Cry 3 is a delightful and harsh tropical wonderland, crawling with wildlife and threatened by the pirates and drug runners that disrupt its peace. The troubled paradise you explore is colorful and wild, enticing you to investigate its ravines and discover new ways to enjoy the open-world playground sprawling in front of you. This is a game that ignites the desire to complete every last challenge and check out every last icon on your map. You gradually journey across the entirety of two sunny and sinful islands, hunting for rare game, speeding medicine to needy communities, and skinning sharks so that you might craft new wallets with their hides. Far Cry 3 is an excellent game, marred mainly by some irritating design elements and an inconsistent story that often defaults to generic "tribal" cliches to make an impact.
When the story leaves those cliches behind for deeper territory, however, it does manage to communicate ideas of substance. It takes many hours for its themes to come together in a coherent way--yet in certain aspects, the incoherence makes sense. As protagonist Jason Brody, your initial quest to rescue your friends from a chaotic and truly frightful pirate named Vaas turns into a personal journey blurred by drugs, and fueled by the desire to follow a new and exciting spiritual path. Those friends are too shallow for you to care much about them, which keeps the story at arm's length for a good half of the game. But his friends' shallowness ultimately allows Jason to take a guilt-free look inward, as he grows further mesmerized by the customs of the local Rakyat tribe that takes him under its wing. You might see the narrative curveballs coming after a while, but the trippy manner in which certain events unfold effectively blurs the lines between reality and Jason's occasionally drug-addled imagination.
Nonetheless, narrative oddities stand out. Some of Jason's friends are strangely unaffected by the horrors inflicted upon them. The game quickly glosses over an event that would make most of us emotional wrecks, making Jason's proclamations that the issue was harder to deal with than he expected ring hollow. Some moments seem made to be shocking for the sake of shock alone--not because they develop the world or its characters--but Far Cry 3 isn't so much about story as it is about its world, and the ways you exploit it for your own personal enjoyment. Story missions have you navigating caves and holding off enemies in modern shooter fashion, but out in the wild, you have an entire paradise to tame.
And it's that lush and menacing world that makes Far Cry 3 utterly enthralling. The game is big, certainly, but where Far Cry 2 could feel aimless, its sequel feels more focused without ever losing its sandbox appeal. One core activity may sound familiar to returning fans: you shoot up enemy outposts so that you may liberate them, turning them into safe zones where you can load up on ammo and other supplies. These camps also serve as quick-travel points, lessening the tedium of driving from one objective to the next. Early on, freeing an outpost can be remarkably easy: you shoot down a handful of pirates, and the flag is raised declaring the camp as the Rakyat's. Further in, however, you must put Far Cry 3's diverse possibilities to intelligent use.
Best to deactivate the alarm before engaging.
One consideration: you must be aware of an outpost's alarm. Should a pirate trigger it, reinforcements arrive in a matter of seconds, so you might want to sneak in and deactivate the alarm system. Or, you could snipe the individual alarms, though shooting one does not deactivate others. Caged leopards and bears can be freed with a single shot, granting you a temporary ally in your quest for vengeance. Consider using a C4 charge and luring a small group of pirates to an explosive demise, or using a flamethrower to char evil henchmen to a crisp. That same flamethrower can lay waste to vegetation and effectively create moats of fire that can keep combatants at bay. (Well, some combatants, anyway.) Near the end of the game, your foes can put up quite a fight, and be great in number, so Far Cry 3 doesn't just give you the tools to be creative; it ultimately demands you use them to survive.
You don't have to conduct your business so loudly and dramatically, however: Far Cry 3 gives you ample opportunity to be stealthy and sometimes outright requires it. Forced stealth, such as that seen in a later-game mission that fails you the moment you are discovered, isn't that enjoyable. Fortunately, sneaking about is usually a blast, because it pays off in a brutal takedown of your unsuspecting target. Such moments are even greater once you have earned certain powerful abilities, such as the one that allows you to assassinate a pirate and toss a blade into another's skull in a single, effortless move.
Liberating outposts is only one of many activities to pursue in Far Cry 3. To reveal more of the map and gain access to free weapons, you climb radio towers and hack their transmitters. The entire concept is clearly inspired by the Assassin's Creed series, and no wonder, considering both games were created by the same development studio. First-person platforming is a frequent frustration in shooters--but Far Cry 3 makes it a delight. The tower creaks and groans as you climb ladders, make a few well-timed leaps, grasp some ledges, and ultimately arrive at the pinnacle. After you make a few hardware adjustments to the transmitter, the camera zooms to several points of interest, and you can make a breathless descent to the ground via zip line.
On the islands, being a drug dealer has its benefits. A big fancy house is one of them.
There's so much more out there: hunting missions that give you a bow and arrow or a shotgun, perhaps, and send you after rare creatures. You can jump on an ATV or behind the wheel of a truck for a timed medicine run that showcases Far Cry 3's bouncy vehicles--and how they respond authentically to the bumpy terrain. Some challenges compare your performance to other players via the game's online leaderboards; others require you to murder a specific target using your knife. These activities are tied together in smart ways, with one task often leading you to another hunting challenge, a vehicle to race, or even a cave to investigate.
Mix in a vast array of role-playing elements, and you have a fully featured single-player game that lasts upward of 35 hours or more, depending on how much you want to do. Kills earn you experience, which in turn earns you upgrades (such as more health bars) and new skills (kill an enemy from the ledge beneath). Corpses and chests can be looted for cash and saleable items; you then buy new weapons and maps, and can replenish ammo at safe houses. Out in the wild, you collect plant life of various kinds so that you can fill syringes with meds that heal you, make you less vulnerable, or enhance your senses.
Earning XP means gaining cool new skills.
Some of those enhancements make it easier to hunt wildlife, which is not only a fine pastime in itself, but also rewards you with skins and hides, which you cut from their corpses in properly squeamish fashion. Expect your quarry to put up a fight, though; tigers apparently don't enjoy being riddled with bullets and set on fire. Wild animals are more than just targets, however: they are also part of the world's ecology. Leopards attack boars, leaving behind their carcasses for you to loot, and scaring off the remainder of the herd. You might merrily waltz into a run-down shack seeking loot, only to have a couple of Komodo dragons wander in and sink their teeth into you. Such moments lend Far Cry 3 an air of unpredictability; you feel like anything could happen--and that whatever it is, you'll probably end up bleeding from it.

Far Cry 3... Where do I start?
Do I start at the simply horrific performance of this game? Where you notice frame drops from 60 to 21 FPS on even the LOWEST settings when enemies spawn? Do I talk about the pants-on-head-idiotic AI that just stands in your face and still doesn't understand it should shoot you? Do I talk about the simply outragious 'difficulty'?
I guess I'll treat it all starting with the performance.
The performance of this game is simply terrible. The game has seemingly random FPS drops on every single graphical setting. Low, High, Ultra, it doesn't matter, FPS drops will happen. And seeing as I run a 780Ti that should run this game 10x over, that's really unacceptable. I could go on about the graphics and 'performance' forever, but there's more to complain about.
The setting itself, this so called "Rook Island". Ubisoft will have you believe it feels 'super alive and real and everything has it's own life and there's animals'. Jup, there's animals. What do they add? ♥♥♥♥ all. Sure you can hunt a few and craft skins, but hey, you'll do that once to have all the skins you need and you'll never look at them again. As for the pirates and Rakyat that occupy the island, they just sit there. Now and then they go on a patrol, but mostly they just sit in areas waiting for you to come kick their♥♥♥♥♥ These little pirate base raids are fun, but they add oh so little.
Since we're talking about gameplay anyway now, there's so much wrong with that. For example; radio towers. To clear the 'fog' on the map, you climb radio towers all over the place and thus unlock parts of the map once you reach the top. Doing this also gifts you free weapons in stores. This effectively renders money useless. Who in their right mind would buy a gun they can get for free with little extra effort? Stupid design choice, radiotowers should've unlocked guns to be able to buy, not just give them away. Another gameplay mechanic that's just plain stupid is the difficulty. It's truly unbearably easy when you play this game on anything other than the Master difficulty. If you don't, enemies will just pump you full of lead and you'll keep walking and 1 shotting things like the Terminator. You're basically indestructable, unless you're world's biggest retard.
The quests and story are also very strange to say the least. The entire game seems to be centering about this theme; Insanity. Insanity is nearly portraied as being a 'super epic thing' instead of taking it serious. The whole storyline seems like it was written by a few clowns on acid, and doesn't keep me entertained in the slightest.
So overall; you're stuck on an island full of kuh-ra-zy pirates and people, with few really outstanding characters. The island itself feels boring and has a lot of terribly empty places that just seem to serve as a filler to make the island look big, the performance is abysmal and the story is idiotic.
Highly disrecommend.

This game is awesome. The RPG elements unlock new moves instead of generic stat boosts (though a couple of 'skills' are just stat boosts). The ways to move around and kill people are fairly varied; I especially like the slide move, which is triggered by tapping the crouch button while sprinting. The takedowns are also cool, and you get options of what to do after the takedown, such as pulling the pin on the enemy's grenade and kicking his body toward a group of enemies. There are multiple weapons with their own feel; I'm fond of the flamethrower for close range and silenced sniper rifle for long range, but the bow and arrows are also very powerful. Overall gameplay is a lot like Just Cause 2 where you roam around an island paradise Liberating it the American Way by finding installations of 4 to 8 pirates and setting fire to the entire camp. What Far Cry 3 does better is it makes stealth more of an option, and the first person shooter genre has more immersive combat. It doesn't have Just Cause 2's parachute/grappling hook, though, which makes exploration considerably less entertaining. Far Cry 3's story is also pretty cool. Pirates kidnap you and your friends and you gradually go from a terrified product of overindulgent western civilization to a vicious warrior as you fight for survival. This is interlaced with some commentary on the nature of games and the state of the medium.

A beautiful open world, a large number of weapons, a variety of land/sea vehicles, decent enemy AI, the ability to approach targets from any angle and make meaningful tactical choices on how to engage - Far Cry 3 takes all the good stuff from Far Cry 2, gets rid of that game's annoying malaria mechanic, and then adds in some cool new features as well. In addition to the above you can expect to have fire support from friendly-faction AI soldiers, gather plants and hunt animals, use gathered materials to craft new equipment and medicines to expand your capabilities, use experience points to unlock new character skills, and engage in a wider variety of side-quests than in previous iterations.
However, though it gives you plenty of good firefights, open-world exploration, and the kind of free-form mayhem that leads to memorable encounters, the game does miss the mark in a couple key areas:
Number one problem, the story is really bumpy - there are times when you'll think it's perfectly tolerable and then an hour later you'll just want to shout "...what!?" at the screen. It can't decide what sort of tone it wants to present, key characters never really get developed or explored, and the ending is unfortunately a big pile of nonsense. Luckily cutscenes are few and far between so player control is not often taken away, and quick-time events are fairly sparse as well. Still, don't expect to be moved by the events of Far Cry 3 because it seems like the writers forgot what they were doing halfway through.
The other problem I had was with the weapon customization; it's there, but there isn't enough of it. Once you're a few hours into the game you'll realize that (because of a mechanic that progressively unlocks the basic guns for you to have free of charge) the main use for all that money you're collecting is in upgrading your arsenal to tailor it to your playstyle. Unfortunately, many of the weapons don't allow customization at all, and those that do usually allow for two of three main addon types: optics for aim-down-sights firing (you want long or medium range?), silencers for quieter shots (doesn't seem to affect damage or firing characteristics), and extended magazines. These are definitely helpful upgrades, but it would have been nice to see more differentiation, for example - laser sights for increased hip-fire accuracy, underslung grenade launchers for quick explosive attacks, different ammo types like slugs for shotguns (shotgun pellets seem to just disappear at around 10 meters in this game). The system in-game isn't bad, it just leaves you wanting more.
Fundamentally though, the flaws in this game are worth complaining about because they're marring what is otherwise a really solid and fun open-world shooter. This is particularly due to the chaotic 'living' world that the game takes place in. Imagine your stealth attack on a pirate outpost being interrupted by a komodo-dragon charging out of the woods at your intended target, causing all the pirates to go into a frenzied state of alertness. That's just one example of Far Cry's free-form open-world combat in action.  It's far from perfect, but it's definitely capable of providing you with dozens of hours of fun and most-likely some unique scenarios that you won't find in any other game.

Far Cry 3 is by far the best game in the series. It took the harsh tropical environment from the first one and the interactive open-world engine from the second one and created this juggernaut of video game craftsmanship. The story is stunning and believable, pinning you against the most ruthless pirates of the international waters. In order to save your friends, you must master the art of survival and become just as cruel as the pirates you face. Far Cry 3 is nearly identical to Far Cry 2, however the environment in Far Cry 2 was lacking interaction, and stealth is nearly impossible in open African plains. Far Cry 1 had the same environment as Far Cry 3, but the story was nearly non-existant and about half-way through the game, they pin you against giant monsters that can somehow use machine guns? Anyway, Far Cry 3 is an amazing game that I havent ben able to put down since I bought it for $15, which by the way, was definately worth the price.

Racist♥♥♥♥♥video game. Okay, maybe you won't really agree that the game has some race problems like I do, but at the very least, I didn't care at all about the main characters which is kind of a huge issue. I don't mind a heart of darkness retelling, actually in fact I love them, Spec Ops: The Line for instance is an incredible game and does this similar kind of story in all the right ways. Far Cry 3, however, feels like the story and missions were the almgamation of many different studios with different ideas that don't all quite fit, for instance a pretty hefty part of the game is spent trying to find a knife with supernatural like properties but then you never really do anything with it, leading me to think that Far Cry 3 may have at one time had a more realistic supernatual element to it like the Tomb Raider games.
I suppose the shooting was actually quite good but it wasn't that much of an improvement over Far Cry 2, and I did have some fun playing it some of the time, but I just couldn't get invested in the action going on because I didn't care at all about what was going on or what what was happening to the characters. My biggest issue in gameplay is that it never feels rewarding and often feels too much of a chore and I'm someone who grinded like no other in WoW and other games so this was a huge issue for me.
And I guess you could say, "well it isn't about the story it is about exploring around and exploding stuff." Okay sure, I don't agree because I think this game is trying to tonally be a story heavy game, but If I were to accept that I think there is a lot of problems making a game playing a priveleged, wealthy white dude that finds it fun to kill scores of brown people in a developing, war-striffed country and while I did have fun with some of the shooting this was something that I kept thinking of in the back of my mind. It's not that you should have sympathy for the people he is kiling because they are pirates in human trafficing and drug trade. But, it is the fact that it was made by design to have the primary villians be people of color and you can only play as a wealthy, white dude.
I would be okay with racist elements, meaning I would still think they are racist, if the game was still enjoyable and redeamable in other aspects but the other aspects, I thought, were "just okay" making the game not recomendable.
TL:DR It's okay. But, not good enough.

Far Cry 3 is beyond any doubt an amazing game and an experience that mustn't be missed, even with it's flaws.
The graphics, ambience and voice acting are all amazing and makes this game one of the most asthetically pleasing titles in recent years, however as a result Far Cry 3 is pretty demanding in the hardware department. So make sure your gear is up to speed and optimize it for maximum performance.
The gameplay has been referred to in the past as "Skyrim with guns". This is true, Far Cry 3 puts the player in the heart of a tropical paradise plagued with drug-running pirates and gives them the opportunity to go about as they please: Exploring areas, fighting off skirmishes and collecting items. However unlike Skyrim the primary story isn't completely optional, with constant reminders appearing on your screen to go here or do that while out experiencing the island for yourself makes you feel like a dog in an off-lease park; yes you are free in a sense but you're still not in total control of your experience.
To further add the sensation of "freedom with boundaries", Far Cry 3's story is very restrictive in comparison with the exploration. During a mission you are forced to use this one specific weapon, drive this one specific vehicle, do this objective in precisely this particular way, go here within the alloted time; the list goes on. Adding unpredictable restrictions to the story makes the player feel like a ball and chain has been shackled to their ankle, which does no favors to the overall experience of the game. However, when you are allowed to play your way, Far Cry 3 really shines through. Plotting out ambushes on fortified outposts or joyriding across the island running over whatever gets in your way is a blast through-and-through, made even better by a large variety of destructive weaponry ranging from grenade launchers, RPGs and even flamethrowers.
The story of Far Cry 3 is simple, you take on the role of Jason Brody, a rich white boy who loves hair product. While you and your friends are on a drunken binge in exotic places you're all kidnapped by a band of pirates looking to ransom you and then sell you off to slavery. Jason manages to escape and begins his adventure to rescue his friends and kill the bad guy and get the girl. To be frank, the story isn't all that great. Jason Brody and all his friends are shallow and dislikeable, and I'd much rather shoot them all in the mouth than risk my life to save them. In contrast, antagonists in the game are interesting and imaginative and save Far Cry 3's story from being dullard. Vaas Montenegro, the most well established villian is similar to the Joker from Batman: Arkham Asylum, he's psychotic, unpredictable, imaginative and fun to watch.
Far Cry 3's combat is split into two categories: Stealth and shoot-em-up, and both are well-made and flow well into eachother as the situation requires. Jumping into foliage when not in combat makes it so enemies cannot see you, allowing you to plan out your attacks or to play venus fly trap and lure them to you by throwing rocks before jumping out and puncturing them with a knife takedown. The takedowns are a very satisfying insta-kill against unarmored enemies (and can be used against heavy foes later in the game after acquiring a perk) so long as you take them by suprise, and with unlockable perks takedowns become even more versatile and deadly by either pulling the pin off a grenade of the freshly deceased or going for multi chain stabs. On the other side of the combat spectrum the guns and shooting mechanics are satisfying and have a good healthy punch to them.
Unfortunately the combat indulges in one of video game design's bad habits, Quick-Time Events, prominently when fighting carniferous wildlife like aligators and sharks. You're swimming across a river when SURPRISE GATOR SEX comes up, then you're given half a second to mash a specific button before you die. QTEs are a bad mechanic in video games and while they're not too prominent in Far Cry 3 they still feel unecessary on the whole. Finally the worst part of the combat is the battles against the main antagonists like Vaas or Buck, both of them being such hostile albeit savourably enjoyable characters you'd think the fight would be memorable, right? Wrong. When fighting them the game designers decide to put you and your foe into a sort of drug-trip combat sequence that makes no sense and is incongruious to the rest of the game, followed by a series of QTEs taking control away from you for the sake of trying to make the encounter more cinematic. This resulted in final struggles that were disappointing and left a very sour aftertaste.
So in all, Far Cry 3 is a game with flaws, but they don't drag it all the way down. Far Cry 3 is fun, addicting and worth the time (especially if you got it while it's on sale). I suggest you look past it's flaws and let the overall experience take you in.
Also before I close off I need to mention: Far Cry 3 also has an online multiplayer, which only exists for the purpose of having an online multiplayer. It's unimaginative deathmatch and is not anything special.

I rather enjoyed this game, especially considering I purchased it for very little money during the Steam Winter Sale, and I would recommend it to anyone that enjoys both sandboxy exploration coupled with linear story line.  I like how you can, for most of the linear story, go off and explore the game world while completing mini-quests and liberating outposts.  I played this game almost exclusively until I completed the story line, and you get to choose your own ending, though I haven't gone back in to choose the other ending to see if you truly choose or if the game diverts you back to the ending I witnessed.  After you complete the story, you have the option to go back to the island and do more exploration, and if you haven't liberated all the outposts from pirates (modern day pirates, not the arrrrgh matey variety, sorry Cap't Jack), I believe you would be able to continue doing so if you like.
I do not have very much experience with FC3 multiplayer.  I don't know if I was suffering from "you haven't restarted Windows yet today so your PC is slow as hell" lag, or a bandwidth bottleneck somewhere between my computer and the rest of the world, but I found it a bit laggy compared to my current favorite Multiplayer FPS (Battlefield: Bad Company 2).  There are differences to how multiplayer FPS games handle/feel/play, but this seemed like my difficulties were artificial rather than a real lack of ability, I do hold my own pretty well most of the time in other FPS games I've played.  It was a lot less smooth than the single player experience.  As a result, I didn't really play multiplayer FC3 long enough to give any real review beyond this, and I have yet to try Co-Op mode.
If you enjoy single player sandboxy FPS games with a linear story you can follow at your own pace and a huge environment to explore, you will probably love the hell out of this game, and I highly recommend it.  If you're more into miltuplayer, you may want to make sure you have more than 4 gigs of RAM, a better processor than my dual core 3.8ghz, and a current video card with a bit of GRRR in its pants.
I hope this helps.  ;)

Far Cry 3 is wonderful in terms of the environment and graphics (stunning visuals!). There are not many games that have such an enjoyable system of roaming around the map, hunting, driving, swimming, flying etc. The fight is often easy, but fun. The singleplayer experience is quite tense and full of fast-paced action (car chases, bomb escapes, burning houses, helicopter flights, ambushes... a lot of good points). There are even some stealth aspects, you may conquer the outposts in a silent-assassin way and I admit - it gave me a lot of good gameplay experience, especially with later knife skills. Aside from the outposts you'll see it's just a nicely scripted shooter often with no practical use for silent approach :)
So, why do I give it a negative mark? Let me explain in a few points...
If you spend some time on doing side miniquests and hunt, you get really powerful - I quickly got to point when I maxed my skill tree, had bought everything I could and still had overflow of money. Of course, it's up to you how far you go with exploring the map, so let's say it's not a minus, more like neutral remark.
The game has a very dark feeling in it. A lot of despair, loneliness, brutality, often without reason. Sometimes the protagonist make extremely stupid, unbelievable decisions. Your enemies (and some allies...) are psychopatic maniacs. There are a lot of drug themes. I know a lot of these are justified by the plot, but every time I moved a bit forward in game (not counting map exploration), I felt sad and dull. (game music even amplify it) Watch out, if you feel pesimist, probably this game might just make you feel worse...
Whole drug aspect - not only there's too much of it for my taste, I also feel that the game creators took it as a handy shortcut for fixing loose plot points. I don't want to leave spoilers here, so let's just say that replacing a few proper fights with drug induced visions (and then, magically, your character somehow won everything!) is very cheap. You see a problem but don't solve it, just hop into narcotic projection, see some ghosts and delusions, get back to 'real' world and everything is already done. Yay...
Although many parts of the campaign were enjoyable (especially action scenes mentioned before), the ending itself was so disgusting/stupid (I chose "good" ending, "bad" one was even worse) that it totally threw me off this game. Honestly, I haven't played it anymore since I finished the main plot.
Multiplayer - I managed to unlock everything before I finished singleplayer and then, without the feeling of getting rewards, it got very boring. It's not a bad experience, but it's very chaotic, certainly not better than other shooters. There are no dedicated servers, so you have little influence on any technical aspect of the game. Also, expect A LOT of hosting problems, a few host migrations during one match seemed like a standard...
Oh, also the game needs to be played under Uplay - Ubisoft DRM system, which is very inconvenient, much less comfortable than Steam... (a bit ridiculous, that we already have to use two platforms, Steam and Uplay, at once to play a game, who knows how many additional programs we will have to run in future to play one game?)

I'd say this was the best game I played in 2013, but as it came out in 2012, I'm gonna go ahead and say it is one of the best games I've played in 2012 as well as 2012. Great story, great gameplay, great music. All comes together to give you some of the best experiences you'll have in gaming, and I can say that without a doubt. Steal system was excellent too.
Presentation: 10/10 - Nothing that I noticed could have been improved.
Graphics: 10/10 - Even for it's time, this game has outstanding graphics. If you have the rig for it, pump it up to max graphics and you will be in for a ****ing treat.
Sound: 9/10 - The music in this game is fantastic, and there is nothing scarier than trecking through the jungle only to hear a leopard or something of the sort nearby. Some of the weirdest music pieces have been used in some situations, but that adds to the charm. Weird doesn't necessarily = bad, mind you.
Gameplay: 9.5/10 - The shooting, the running, the falling, the swimming, the stealthing, the rock throwing, the bow mechanics, everything. Oh and did I mention you will be able to go cliffjumping?
Lasting Appeal: 9/10 - As far as the multiplayer goes, that left a little to be desired but honestly it was still pretty decent. I had fun for a few hours running around shooting people, similarly to titles like Call of Duty, etc, but with a few twists on the gameplay. If you have a few friends to play with in a deathmatch or even the co-op missions I wasn't honestly very fond of, and you will have yourself some fun times with this game after finishing the story. Hell, you may even want to repeat the story like a lot of my friends have on a higher difficulty. Definitely a lot of replayability here.

At the time of this writing, I have owned Far Cry 3 for a week and have logged almost 30 hours in the single player and co-op, and it is by far one of the most well made and addicting games. The gameplay is nothing groundbreaking mind you, but the way everything is put together makes for an oustanding experience. I wasn't a big fan of the first 2 installments, they just didn't grab me the way that this one has. My only gripe for the single player is looting and skinning animals can be a bit frustrating to line up with to execute the hold E option. Now the co-op is another story, AMAZING!!!! I haven't enjoyed a co-op feature like this in quite some time. Leveling up is relatively quick, getting the phone app in conjunction with the game allows for quicker decoding of items gained at the end of the missions. Basically it is a shooting gallery for up to four friends to go nuts! The mission style reminds me of L4D as there are chapters to each of the missions. During your mission there are some competitive sections such as racing quads to deliver bombs and who can kill the most with a sniper rifle to break up the  pace a little bit which I found fun. All in all, I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys a captivating experience in a LARGE world that isn't as overwhelming as some, and doesn't skimp like others.

The characters in the game are believable and interesting. The game is truly open world, and missions only start once you approach the area. Some parts don't make a lot of sense, such as when you fight Vaas at his camp. But all in all, this game was amazing and would recommend it to anyone who likes first person shooters.

I would like to start by saying that for the price that I purchased this game for ($8), this game is more than worth the purchase. The story is engrossing, the combat mechanics are smooth and varied, and there are distinct nuggets of value within the game. The island is beautiful, the levels of customization for your character are enough to keep you intrigued, and the story will propel you through the game.
That said, the game is certainly not without its flaws. Far Cry 3 has an overarching storyline that loses its focus about 3 quarters way through the game (that is the most I can say without spoiling plot points). The invasion of camps becomes repetitive if you employ the same strategies each and every time. The middle of the game suffers from a lag that makes you wish it would rush along a bit. The textures of the island are rather simple and not very attractive. Facial animations are awkward, even if the voice acting is good. The weather could have more diversity than the occasional rain shower. The game could provide you with more incentive to explore and conquer, in terms of story value.
All that said, I consider my experience with Far Cry 3 to be a positive one. If you happen to see this game on sale, you should strongly consider it, especially if you are in the mood for an action adventure.

I just finished the story and let me just say that this is one of the best games I have ever played so far.
For those of you who want to know the story(in a nutshell):
You are playing as Jason Brody and you and your friends went on a vacation into an island. Next thing you know, you and your friends are now captured by some pirates who inhabit this island. You barely escape the camp and a guy named Dennis saves you and brings you to his place and this is where your story begins. You must now find and rescue your friends at the same time discover the warrior in you as Jason Brody evolves from some college kid into a badass warrior.
The graphics in this game are AMAZING, the island looks gorgeous and full of life. The environment is well detailed and everything just looks like paradise.
As for the gameplay, there are a LOAD of things to do in this game. You'll be finding yourself hunting and skinning animals to upgrade various things like your weapon holsters, bags, wallets and more, going up radio signals and deactivate the breakers to reveal a part of the island, which is a must if you want to get free weapons, liberating camps which have been taken over by pirates to unlock it for fast travel, looking for relics, WW2 letters and other collectibles and completing various quests to prove to the inhabitants that you are a true warrior. There is also an RPG element to the game wherein you get these tattoos called "tatau" everytime you level up and they are unlocked to gain new perks or abilities.
The story is good and the environment really reels you in to get the feel that you're actually there and you get to socialize or interact with the people.
However it also has its downs, one of which is that the environment isn't really that destrcutable. Say for example you set fire to a wooden house, no matter how much you burn it, it will not get destroyed. There are also some abilities which are not that really necessary or you get to use them rarely like shooting from a zipline or taking out enemies from a high place or from underneath. The boss battles are also cut down into quicktime events which isn't much of a problem to me but it might be for others. But these are just minor flaws and they do not hinder you from enjoying the game that much.
Overall, it's a fun game and one of the best there is so pick it up and play it sometime, you won't regret it.
My final verdict for this game is a 8.5/10

I've only had this game for a week. This game is awesome! I'm a little late to the party as this game has been  out for over a year since when I purchased it, but I usually don't buy games at release and like to wait for the to be discounted -- a budget gamer.
Lots of side-quests to do in the game while you complete the main objective so you don't ever get the feeling of just trying to complete task. You can spend lots of time just aimlessly wandering around to take in the surrounding and not feel like you're wasting time. The interaction with various NPC's in the world, whether they're human or animal, is quite incredible. You can watch islanders have a battle with the enemy pirates, or animals attacking humans, or animals preying upon other animals.
The game mechanics work well. Your character moves in a way where you feel like you are actually in the game. The weapon selection system is easy to master in a short time. The vehicle driving system is simple and works great. The progression of upgrading your weaponry and inventory is ingenius! Hunting and scavenging for items to craft into upgrades make you feel very involved in the evolution of your character.
This game is well worth adding to your Steam library if you haven't already purchased it.

Weeks later: So, I still find the game boring as hell. However, a random recollection of a random comment by some game production moggle came to mind: the suggestion that if PC gamers would accept the 720 resolutions, they could guarantee 60 fps. I initially assumed this was a lazy programmer trying to take pot shots at the PC community, as is often the case. However, upon remembering this statement, I was tempted to retry Far Cry 3 in 720p. To my surprise, without even activating the fan on my GPU, I am able to run the game at the highest possible settings with well over 60 fps. Is this good: no. For the fact that, just before I ran this test, I was playing Skyrim, a similar graphical powerhouse at full capacity at 1080p. At 720, yeah it may be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of graphical presentation, but what good is it  to do so only effectively at 720p for most (non Titan and similar high-end) machines; it still looks bad. Especially when a rival and fairly contemporary game runs beautifully at 1080p at 60 fps. So still, don't bother, but if you are compelled and run into issues, try it at 720i or 720p.

Kui sa oled FPS Shooterite fänn, siis tegemist on MUST PLAY mänguga. Imeline graafika, story ja gamepaly on super combo. Täiesti prefektne. Muidugi oli ka paar asja mis häirisid, nimelt oli loot cheste väga palju ja nendest sai vähe kraami. Mõtekam oli sidequeste teha. Ütlen siis ära, mängu lõpus on valik, ehk saad lõpetada mängu kahte erinevat viisi. Mina ise valisin selle "inimlikuma". Selliseid valikuid oleks võinud olla rohkem mängus. Osad cutscened olid minule vastutahtmist. Näiteks ütles karakter, et ta tahab saarele elama jääda, kuigi mulle see üldse ei meeldinud. Kui tagasi tulla story juurde, siis asi on väga deep. Mida kaugemale jõuad, seda rohkem tahad kätte maksta. Selles mängus soovitan palju eeltööd teha enne main questide juurde asumist. Kindlasti oleks vaja võtta kõik radio towerid ja outpostid ära. Mängu alsutades oli plaanis ka kõik relicid, messaged ja memory cardid ära koguda. Hiljem sain aru, et see oli praktiliselt võimatu. Memory cardid (tegin ära) ja messaged olid mõleldavad, aga 120 relici on natuke üle piiri. Lõpetamiseks kulus 25 tundi, mis on open world mängu kohta täiesti paras. Kindlasti kui oleks teinud veel side queste ja chillinud oleks 30 tundi ka ära tulnud. Mängus on ka veits rpg elemente, ehk sul on võimalus enda karakterit leveldada ja asju craftida, et paremini metsikus looduses ja sõjas toime tulla. Kindlasti soovitan mängu, see on igat senti väärt!

This is one of the best games out there. It features a huge open world, tons of content, sharp combat mechanics, a cool story, and lots of things to do. It's really easy just to get lost in it while the hours drift away. I've been playing FPS games since the dawn of time and this is one of the best. It basically throws you on this island and lets you go about it on your own way. Regular missions are linear, but those turn out to be a small fraction of the run time. Everything else - taking over strongholds, completing side activities, hunting for doodads - lets you do it at your own pace. The game works as a combat shooter but definitely leans more towards the stealth side - there's more than a bit of Predator in the way you can sneak through the jungle and then quickly dispatch enemies. It's great.
If I had to make any complaint, it is that the leveling system isn't balanced at all - the game features two large islands but I had most of the upgrades before I even set foot in the second island. People who do a more thorough job of clearing out side missions would likely have them all even before that. There is a possibility this was intentional - the game just gets better the more tools one has at their disposal, and perhaps this was Ubisoft's way of rewarding thorough players. It is still noticeable, though.
In the end, this is just a minor quibble. On the whole, this game is amazing and a must-play for anyone who likes open world games or shooters.

Okay, I'd give this game a 6/10.  The open-world gameplay and combat is solid and it's what I enjoyed the most.  That said, there's no other reason to pick up FC3.  The story is very weak.  The writer has defended it by saying it's a parody.  Just because it's a parody or a commentary does not mean weak writing is excusable.  If anything, a good parody is harder to write.  And it shows.  The story is weak, the character development is predictable or non-existent for anyone other than the protagonist and the endings are lackluster.  This is not a deep game, it is not a well-written game, and it is not a game you should play for the story.  However, if you enjoy killing pirates and open-world exploration and combat that is toned down from TES level, you'll have some fun.  Just don't expect it to get any better than that, it certainly won't blow your mind.

A good entry into the Far Cry series, despite the fact that it has nothing to do with the other entries. And despite the fact that this game, like many others, is slowly becoming more 'cinematized'; that is to say, more cinematics to watch, slight interraction and button pressing during them which constitutes gameplay. But it suceeds in telling the story, so it is what it is.
This entry took the working aspects of the series and took out some of the more annoying elements, but it borrowed heavily from the second entry (like it or not). Things like unlocking weapons in the shops via map objectives and the open world gameplay, for instance, but thankfully they've excluded such things from the second entry like weapon breakdown/deterioration.
Some other positive (or negative) highlights of the series would be the unlockable weapons, crafting recipies, etc. Some are critical (awarded via storyline checkpoints) and some are not, but greatly beneficial (such as almost all of the signature weapons, usually making the store counter-parts look like cheap knockoffs or the extremely powerful serums like Touch of Death). Also, there are a lot of variety in ways to make your way about the island, so there are always ways to get about quickly, either by actual transport or via the waypoint system. But, as a minor side-note, the game's 'driving' mechanics are pretty terrible, requiring either tapping motions or the mindset of a crack-fiend to control the vehicle or it slams into an object or overshoots a turn. Most of the time, I end up walking to avoid frustration. This is one aspect of the game I wish they would have borrowed more heavily from Far Cry 2, as the vehicle operation was far superior in that chapter of the franchise.
All and all, I'd recommend the game. It will occupy your time for a while, its open world format allows you to play your way (such as hammering through the storyline as it goes, or unlocking everything on the island first and then going through story), and the weapons/tactics are workable enough that it doesn't get old quickly. If you like shooters, especially of this kind of format, you'll enjoy Far Cry 3.

I was really looking forward to a CryTek-powered open world shooter.  What I got was a dirty needle and some pig entrails.  This is a disgusting game in more than one way.  Obviously, there's a crafting system that involves gutting and skinning animals that you hunt.  It's gross and I can get past that.  That's not the disgusting that bothers me.  The enemies are pretty rough characters -- drug runners, kidnappers and mercenaries.  Looting them will yield an assortment of colorful vendor fodder like dirty needles, crackpipes and the sort.  This bothers me a bit...but I can get past it.  The game, however, seems to pride itself in what an ugly world and situation it places you in.  Loading screens treat you with random, stream-of-consciousness words, a few of which are obscenities.  Of course the in-game dialog is repleat with obscenities.  I guess you can't have a modern "gritty" game without them.  At this point, I'm swallowing a lot of ugly for the sake of the game play, which holds up pretty well until you start hitting certain progression walls.
Like many games claiming to be open worlds, the world is gradually revealed or unlocked through progression in the story.  Character skills and crafting recipes are similarly locked to your storyline.  In the end, it was these restrictions that put me off to the game entirely.  I hated the storyline for the game's ugliness I described above.  I just didn't want to run through it.  However, with at least half of the game world locked away behind irritating game content, I lost my will to play the game at all.  And cheat codes don't help you much in escort missions in which NPCs will gladly take cover in front of enemy gunfire.
All of that said, I laud CryTek for what they tried to do here -- open world shooting with crafting and skill systems that feel lifted from the latest MMO.  I loved that concept.  I just wish it weren't tied to content that made me feel worse for playing the game.

Ah, Far Cry 3. It's a game that is insanely playable. In it, you play Jason Brody, some well-to-do kid in way over his head. Throughout the story, Jason takes ...oh...several levels of BADASS.
The setting is beautiful and expansive, with plenty to do and keep you busy for a while. The soundtrack is perfect for this game. The controls and stealth system is optimized for it, and the combat is delicious. Also, there's a coherent storyline that pulls you in, with interested villains and protagonists to keep you on track in the storyline at least. Also, it's mostly nonlinear, so you can explore the first island with impunity, only deciding to follow Dennis' orders when you damn well please. Not only will you gain new weapons and items, but you'll also gain several power ups and new ways to murder your fellow man.
I only have two gripes about this game. The first is that the game starts off really, REALLY slow. You feel like you're grinding, trying to gun down that last f'ing deer with an AK-47 in order to build a bag to cart around all the stuff you'll find. That being said, the begining feels really roughshod. You're either carrying too much stuff and are forced to sell it, or you're carrying too much money and are forced to buy things. The other big glaring issue is that you have to install Ubisoft's version of Steam, "UPlay" in order to play the game. Now, Steam is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and doesn't track the game itself when you're playing it, it tracks UPlay for some asinine reason, leading to you being "in game" for several hours after you finish, and keeping Steam from functioning properly. And Uplay will attempt to force Steam to play the game, but Steam won't want to because it says you're already playing it.
Yeah, get back to me when that logic works out.

Pros:
- Vast weapon customization
- Full controller support
- Linear story.
Cons:
- Runs through U-Play
- Finite campaign content.
Although U-Play has been nothing but a terrible client overlay for Far Cry 3, the game has lived up to the promises metacritics have croned about. Far Cry 3 is vibrant and beautiful. It is sneaky and explosive. It is the alpha and the omega of action-based first person open world shooters. That sounds pretty good, doesn't it? Well, you will have to trust my word and experience it yourself as there is nothing more satisfying than driving a speedboat, shooting incendiary arrows, and watching things go boom. Take out drug lords, explore an island of mystery and bring the myriad to justice. The campaign levels run through leveled zones with ammo and grenade depots that allow the player to keep pushing forward and never stop illiciting gunfire. One of my personal favorite experiences in game may be the silent covert assassination of an entire camp with nothing but a bowie knife. Absolutely wonderful game and excited for the next installment by Ubisoft. However, as the game does run through U-Play on PC, I urge consumers to be aware of the inconveniences associated. As for the client, I hope a solid rework the interface and the way the overlay functions while gaming arrives soon.
Bottom Line: Far Cry 3's weapon customization and actionbased gameplay lend it high replay value in the co-op market even though the solo content may be lack luster. Far Cry 3 = 82/100, U-Play Client = 55/100

The game really surprised me. After reading all reviews about it I was a little bit sceptical, but it was a must for me to play it, since I've played two of it's prequels, so I have a nice comparsion.
First Far Cry revolutionized free-roam FPS games. Huge world, astonishing graphics for it's time, that even now, after 8 years, still surprise!
It's sequel was a bit of a... dissapointment. It had much more to see, with beatiful (once again) graphics from UbiSoft, but it was lacking severely on it's plot side, not to mention being a tedious run-and-gun kind of FPS, but it did introduce very clever ideas.
And now you have Far Cry 3. Game, that kinda connects two of it's older brothers, having not a bad plot line, very interesting characters (Vaas is the Heath Ledger of video games), combined with an open world like the one from Far Cry 2, but located in the jungle once again.
Everything comes together right here. You have excellent gunplay, lot's of activities, things to do all over both islands, everything has a purpose, including hunting animals, hunting bad guys, driving around.
Ubi made one big, long and complex game that deserves attention, because everyone can find something interesting in it.
Although it does run into a few problems. First of them is definetly the floaty model of driving the cars. It was already not that great in Far Cry 2, and I feel it was just copied and pasted in Far Cry 3, cars handle almost the same. You can of course take that it's jungle, the terrain is uneven and you can't switch from 1st person view, so let's forgive the game that, it's okay for what it is.
Secondly: the plot lacks sense. It has major twists, that even made me turn it off to soak up what I just heard, which is a huge plus, but because how complex it is it runs into a few logical issues. First of them is the main character. It's very well made in the beggining, you are just a spoiled kid who is on a virgin island on vacation and all of a sudden everything turns into hell. It's greatly shown how you are helpless, you don't know what's going on and people are introducing you slowly, but steadily. It let's you get immersed in the game from the very first seconds... Just to ruin that in the next hour, giving you a rifle and telling you to kill 200 grunts in the nearby outpost. What the f**k?! Seriously? It doesn't make sense, that a young kid, who has never had a gun in his hand is able to kill countless bad guys on his way.
Thirdly, for what it is, Far Cry 3 is a FPS on rails, with an ability to do things your way. You can't influence the world apart from capturing outposts and doing side-quests, all the relevant quests are just to show you a bit more of the story... and it's fine. It's a long game, so with the included multiplayer mode and the free-roam in single it can give you a lot of entertainment.
When I heard the Skrillex's dubstep song while burning down a field of marihuana, the game already got me hooked up. After hearing movie and game refferences, I was almost extatic. When I heard the classical music while flying a helicopter I was all on board.
The game also doesn't give a single f**k about what major rating companies think. People swear all the time, boobs are being shown, there are sex scenes (although without showing bottom parts), drug use and abuse. It's by all means not a game for kids. This game was made for adults, and it's pretty damn good at it.
All in all - it's a must if you are looking for a good, long FPS. With singles I have a problem - will play day and night untill I finish it (much as with books sometimes). It gave me a lot of fun and it was an amazing pick up from the winter Steam sale. Even if you get bored halfway, you can still just do the main missions, and these will keep you entertained for at least 15 hours. And afterwards, you can pick up a co-op game. Your choice.

Though dead bodies don't show injuries and the fire physics have been relaxed a little from FC2, the rest of the game is absolutely stellar. I mean, you unlock all your abilities before the game is over and actually have a  chance to use them! What a concept!
But seriously; get this, it's good.
Just play it.

The first Far Cry game was a classic. The second was fun but seriously flawed. It looks like Ubisoft learned from their mistakes of the second game when then made Far Cry 3. Unfortunately they added new mistakes along the way. But first, the good.
When Far Cry does something right it does it very well. The graphics are beautiful. The islands look amazing. Visually speaking there really isn't anything to complain about. The sound is top notch. The music is some sort of industrial-ish electro thing that has a a real grim and moody feel to it and it just works. The guns all sound great and handle well. The explosions are top notch. Setting off an ammo pile in an enemy base is something to see. Letting someone have it with a flamethrower and then subsequenlty burning the whole base down brings a big smile to your face. Playing the game in Dolby Digital 5.1 surround sound is engaging. Everything works perfectly sound wise. The voice acting is, for the most part, top notch. The player character, Jason Brody, is laughable but the rest if the cast is generally very good. Exploration of the islands is quite fun and you really get a sense of being there. This place is huge. Getting into massive gunfights while taking over a camp is a  blast. Obviously you try to disarm the alarm system and go in with stealth but if that fails you don't really care because the ensuing battle is going to be entertaining as all hell.
But Far Cry 3 suffers from a death of a thousand cuts. A ton of really small stupid issues drag it back down from how great it should have been. Here's a quick run through of these problems.
1. WORST DRIVING CONTROLS EVER. PERIOD. I'm willing to accept some less than stellar driving mechanics since this is a PC and I'm using a keyboard. I don't expect greatness but damn, the driving is such a joke I frequently just get out and walk. It's THAT BAD. No kidding.
2. Characters do werid glitchy things like crying in the floor because something sad has happened and then all of a sudden they stand up and say somthing to me like "thank you" or whatever for completing a mission that helped them and then fall back down and start crying again like nothing happened. WTF?
3. Crafting items. I ended up ignoring most of this stuff. I just didn't care. I did craft the bigger pouches, wallets etc but after that I just ignored it. It was a boring game mechanic. I never bothered to use the leaves to make syringes. I can just buy them anyway or just heal myself. If your loot sack fills up with leaves or skins you can't sell them or even drop them. If you do the game will crash to the desktop. Your best bet is to only collect the hides you need to craft the things you need and then never skin another animal again and never pick up leaves. Unless you love reloading the game after hitting control alt delete that is.
4. For an open world game I was constantly reminded "Do not leave the area! Mission will fail!". Why can't I just go wherever the hell I want? It got annoying being told to stay where you were instead of circling around to a different position. You get immersed into the game only to be ripped back out out of it by some imaginary border line that you better not cross or else!
5. One thing that frequently made me groan was going to the map screen only to have it immediately scroll way off to the side because apparently my mouse was on the edge of the screen? The map screen should have been stationary until I purposefully moved it. It did this all the damn time. It got old.
6. The menu screens could have been a bit more friendly to navigate. Go into a menu and if you want to go back to the top of that menu you have to go to the lower right hand corner of the screen and click back instead of just hitting the category itself again. Why couldn't I just click the category I want and go back to the top of that category? Having to hit the back button repeatedly just felt lazy. Not to mention it's placed in the exact spot of your screen that popups from Steam occur. Several times I needed to click back only to see it was blocked by a Steam message from a friend's game.
7. Notifications. Holy crap does this game have them. In fact the notifications are like Far Cry 3's version of malaria. You will be nagged to death to stop what you're doing and look at your menu screen to read about something or to do a mission that you already know you need to do. You know you need to do it because they've told you 5 times to stop exploring the island and go do the damn mission. I don't mind every item, car, person, etc having some info about it. I'm OK with that. I would stop from time to time and read them. But the relics? Why am I always reminded to check the relics screen whenever I get another one since THERE IS NO INFO ON THEM! They all say the same thing. I don't want to be reminded to go read about something that has nothing to read.
8. NPCs will say the exact same lines over and over and over. "It's all me! It's all me!" Enemies and friends alike never stop saying the exact same thing every time you walk by. The game badly needed more dialog for NPCs. Look at Grand Theft Auto for how to do it right. That's a sandbox game that knows how to do NPC dialog. Just makes lots of it so it feels like a real world with real people. When everyone spouts the same 5 sentences for the whole game it kinda ruins the immersion.
9. Looting people. You hold E to loot people you've killed. Unfortunately you also hold E to drop your weapon and take theirs. You frequently don't want their weapon but get it anyway even though you just wanted to loot their items. This happens frequently enough that you get to the point where you just don't bother looting people any longer. It's not worth dancing around them to find the sweet spot.
10. Trying to do a stealth takedown. You creep up to someone and see the message onscreen to hit F to do a takedown. You hit F and all of a sudden you're no longer in the "sweet spot" and nothing happens. Instead you're just out in the open with your♥♥♥♥♥♥in the wind. The game is very picky about this magical sweet spot to do takedowns, loot people etc.
11. Jumping puzzles. I know some people love them but I say they really have no place in a first person game. The whole jump up the busted tower game mechanic to turn off signal jammers so you can see the map was lame. Jumping puzzles in FPS games generally are annoying and the whole thing just felt like a cheap way to pad out the game and make it longer. The hell with that. Just give us a map and let us fill it in by walking around or something like Fallout. Making precision jumps on towers in first person was not fun. It was a chore.
12. Items you loot or find in chests have no actual use in the game. Their just for selling to get money. If they have no use then why include them? Why not just find money instead? Why do I need to loot a traffic cone? And why any shop buy that from me anyway? Who needs traffic cones on this island? The whole random junk looting just seemed like more padding that really wasn't even needed unless the developers were just trying to be funny.
Having said all that, this game is still very fun. None of the complaints are deal breakers. They're all small things that don't mean much. They only thing that truly sucked was the driving but again, I'm using a keyboard so I can't complain too much. The story was OK but the idea that some rich white kid somehow gets the power to take down a bad guy and help the natives of the island seemed a little off. What does this white kid have that the natives don't? They're the ones giving him this power so, what, they can't wield it correctly? They need super white guy to do it? Seemed a bit goofy but the story was still OK regardless. The bad guy with the mohawk was great. Good voice acting and even the model animation was great.
Far Cry 3 stumbles but still comes out a blast overall. On sale? Get it.

When I first heard that they were making FarCry3, I was naturally very excited, but somewhat dubious too. I'd bought FarCry when it first came out, and played it to completion. I loved the gameplay and the story, and thought it something really special. Then, when I heard of FarCry 2, I rushed out to relive that same magic, but alas, FarCry 2 was nowhere near as 'fun' to play. Granted, it had nice visuals, handled well, but the constant re-spawning check-points and the whole Malaria storyline got really frustrating. I remember, in fact, giving up about half way through - still not having completed it to this day.
Then, I heard about FarCry 3. Again, it seemed to be a story set on an island, open world, with milita style check points, so I was caught in a quandry - would FarCry 3 be like FarCry 2, or would it actually be fun to play? Well, I'm pleased to admit that I took a chance and bought FarCry 3 - and I'm pleased I did.
I was gripped, from the opening cinematic scenes to the end credits, by the compelling story line and excellent handling. Not only that, but having taken over 45 hours to complete the game, I consider FarCry 3 a perfect example of how fun PC gaming can be. The characters have depth, the voice acting is superb, and the story has a plot that makes many a Hollywood movie seem shallow by comparison. Sure, there may be some (very few) linear moments, but that's coupled with a genuinely 'open world' experience, sub-missions, crafting of kit from scavenged items etc. The choice between a stealth kill and the 'all out guns blazing' approach differs in result and reward, and both can be used on every mission.
In closing, I have to admit that it's not often I actually sit and read the end credits of a game, but this one was worthy of my time and attention. It's been a long time since I enjoyed a game this much, and I sincerely look forward to FarCry 4 - Let's hope they build on the sucess of this game, and not fall back on their laurels.

I higly recomend this game if you are a fan of FPS and open world games with RPG elements. The gameplay is smooth and on harder dificulties stealth becomes a much more valuable skill. The story is good, even if it takes itself too seriously at times. The first few tutorial missions are linear, but after that you are free to roam at will. The game sadly lacks many RPG elements and the crafting system is too easy, also the mini-map and flashing objects can really divert from the game. To adress this issues I would highly recommend downloading a compolation mod like "Ziggys mod" available on the Nexus:

Keep in mind the game does not permit multiple mods like Skyrim, only one can be active at a time.
The multiplayer isn't refined quite enough, but isn't bad. It feels like a tropical COD. However you should buy the game for just the single player. The Multiplayer map editor is amazing allowing you to create virtually anything you can imagine. If you can find a good server with custom maps you will be happy to find classic MP maps from games like COD, CS, and a few others.
I would rate Far Cry 3 a 8/10 and a 9/10 while using mods.

I know I heard people talking about this game earlier into the year and I didn't buy into it. I should have. I can't stop playing this game. It's almost completely non-linear allowing you full access to the first island right off the bat. It's far more like an open world RPG then it's former titles, but that doesn't sell it short, only make it batter.

They basically took Far Cry and added elements of survival, a lot like the new Tomb Raider game.  You have to hunt and use skins to unlock a lot of things you usually take for granted in other FPS.  Things like holsters and ammo pouches.  They also took from Assassins Creed in having to climb radio towers to get a vantage point and unlock your map of the area.  Overall this causes you to slow down and enjoy the finer points they went through the trouble of adding into the game.  Hiding and being stealthy are heavily rewarded in this game and the combat is rather challenging from the get go.  Being noisy alerts foes and makes things more difficult.
Overall I'm impressed with what they've done.  I was expecting quite a bit less and picking this up during a sale for $7.50 was well worth the price.  If you see it on sale, I advise you to pick it up as well.
On a side note, I haven't tried the multiplayer yet, but I want to get through more of the single player before I bother with it.  I'll update this review once I have.
