So let me give my overall opinion of this game, and work backwards; It's good. A fun FPS with a fairly decent story and good characters. However, it's by no means perfect. I have a lot of problems with the game that range from glitches, the combat, the story it self, and controls.
-Story
So we enter the shoes of a kid named Jason Brody, a young man who loves living life to the extreme, though things like Sky diving, mountain climbing and surfing. He, his brothers and friends are within the ranks of the biggest stuck-ups in the universe, being incredibly rich to the point of irritation, and being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to the residents of their first vacation spot. However things quickly change when they are told by a DC to go to Rook Island, presumably thinking that there were no rules there.
When they arrive, they are quickly apprehended by a group of pirates lead by Vaas Montenegro. However Jason manages to escape and is picked up by local tribe that quickly assimilates him into their ranks of Warriors, thanks to Citra. He does so with a porous, to save his friends and go home. Though out the game, a Dr. Earnheart watches over the friends of Jason while he goes off to save them.
But nothing is this simple on Rook. Thoughout the course of the story, he slowly goes mad, enjoying the killing, the drugs, the guns. It leads up to him having to make a choice as to weather or not to stay or leave Rook.
I wont explain much else, otherwise spoiling it.
Overall, good story. Rather dumb, channeling Rambo for better or worse, but good.
-Gameplay and Mechanics
I'll go though this from disliked to liked.

First off, who the hell thought it was a good idea to bind the Grenade key to the middle mouse button? Or switch grenades to rolling the mouse wheel? Same thing with the drugs, binded to keys I don't use that often, being way the hell out on 7 and 8. Whatever, I managed to rebind them and move on. No big deal, just a personal bug-bear of mine.
Melee-play. ughhhh....UGGHHHHH *goes to throw self off a tower* It's so ♥♥♥♥ing boring. You push one button to do a quick slash with a machete, it's unfun and a major missed opportunity.
Loot. There is no point to loot in this game, you don't find any interesting weapons, and you can only flog the lot when you get it for money. The colorful dialogue for the stuff is pointless. It would be cool if there was a model of whatever the item is, but there isn't.
Hunting. What a great idea in this game, but wow did it miss some opportunities. After you craft all the items though hunting, there is no point to keep hunting, because you don't eat, don't need new clothing, don't need anything like that. After you get everything, it's down to the shop to flog the lot. I wish there was a better way to go about it, but there isn't, it's just dumb.
The drugs. Right, I tired them just to say "Hey I tried em'" but was not impressed at all. I was expecting to see some trippy♥♥♥♥♥state and beable to see the enemies from the point of view of a bird or something. Instead it just looked like the Sniper ran though smashing Jarate on everyone's heads, and was unimpressed. So while it was toted really well, it was just a boring little gimmick in my mind, and I never used them.
The missions them selves were ♥♥♥♥in' sweet for the most part. Everyone who's played it will know of the Burning Weed level. That♥♥♥♥♥♥was awesome. However, with some missions, you get this sense of it's trying to funnel you from one area to the next. All of them contribe a reason for you to be in a valley of some descriptions, or stuck on a low lying island, or asked to stay in one position and snipe. It's irritating, although the missions are still put together really well. Nothing is over done, or underdone, it's just right.
Driving. Yeah it's all right, coming from a background of racers, the driving is by no means bad and it's nice to drive a sodding truck for once.
The radio towers were defiantly one of the better fetures, but it raised two questions in my mind;
1. How can a radio tower have an effect on a GPS when GPS Units don't use the towers?
2. Why the ♥♥♥♥ can't I get a paper map that has everything on it?
So to 'unlock' parts of the map on GPS, you need to climb up these towers that are scattered all over the island and activate them (?). It's interesting, but with the two questions above it does kind of prove moot. But I do like it, as the towers are varied in the states of decay they lie in, and it makes for a challenge at points to climb the towers.
Gun-play and customization. I suspect this is where a bulk of the budget went, as the guns, while limited are fairly fun to use and sound ♥♥♥♥ing awesome. Except for the .357 and Desert Eagle, I mean Jesus ♥♥♥♥ing Christ. The weapons are all fun to use, and can be used at any point. You don't need to upgrade to a more powerful weapon to fight with, you can just use what you like. That's fairly cool. The customization is really nice, albeit limited. You can give the guns paint jobs and upgrades that add scopes, silencers and extended magazines. Again, multiple misfires here. More items to put on the guns, or a painter to make your own design would of been awesome, but someone failed to bring this up. Explosions are particularly epic, so is using fire to suppress the enemy.
Stealth. This is easily my favorite aspect, as it sheds away everything from the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ economy, the broken loot and hunting system and uses the game's great gun-play and ideas to it's benefit. It's so satisfying to beable to sneak into a base and kill everyone without alerting anyone. Or if you♥♥♥♥♥♥it up, you can still go run and hide before reinforcements show up, then kill them off that way. One problem; The AI is brain dead, and if they can't find you, they go back to their patrols as if nothing happened, even walking across the body. That's forgivable, if a little annoying. Example; I got a stealth kill with a big ♥♥♥♥ off truck, and the guard's friend said "It must've been my imagination" ignoring the now burning truck that slammed into a pole.
Overall the gameplay is good, but man does it miss the target in areas. Definably worth playing, if only for the gun-play and stealth.
-Ghrapics and Performance
This game is beautiful. I love how everything looks, that even though the situation it self is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, it takes place in such a pretty locale that it easies the trauma of the situation. My computer handled it really well, even when things got busy, the frame rate never dropped bellow 30, and remained at a consistent 45-50 FPS at all other times.
It's pretty and runs well. Derp.
-Overall

I recommend it, but just bare in mind, it's really, really basic. There is nothing here that hasn't been done before or better. I recommend it only for the stealth, story and gunplay. Other then that, blehhhh.

Far Cry 3. FAR CRY 3! Ubisoft must be proud of this game. Far Cry 3 takes the open-world action onto a completely new level. You can either spend your time completing missions, overtaking enemy outposts or hunt animals. Hunting animals isn't there just so the jungle feels alive, it actually has a huge purpouse. You can skin animals and craft wallets to store more money, craft better weapon holsters, or craft potions to, for example, see all enemies, all animals, regenerate health etc. Upgrade and customize your weapons exactly the way you want. You can even fight SHARKS in the game, which feels absolutely INSANE.
That was only the Singleplayer. But no. Ubisoft doesn't stop there. Far Cry 3's multiplayer is AMAZING. You can level up, make new weapon loadouts, customize your weapons like in the singleplayer, decode data from flash drives and disks to unlock new weapons modifications. When your team wins a match, the person who has gathered the most experience can either kill the enemy with the most experience with a unique death move, or free him.
This game does everything perfect. I cannot say anything bad about it. Anything.
Final Rating : 10 / 10

Now, the story and the man character are absolutely the games biggest weakness by far. The story is boring and forgettable. The main character/protagonist is just annoying and awkward. Come the white savior and face your insanity through substantial substance abuse.
There are a couple of improvements from the last game, such as no more re-spawning enemies at checkpoints, NO MORE MALARIA SHOTS, more advanced upgrade system, better presented faction war, more meaningful exploration, more open world (instead of labyrinth-like ravines of Far Cry 2), etc.
The story:
You play as a rich white guy who probably never worked a day in his life and who came to the island with his friends and family to relax, jump out of airplanes and be "the king of the world". Short time after you and your buddies get captured and butt♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by a pirate named Vaaaaaaaas. Eventually, after escaping, you find out that you possess magical-primal-instinct-killer-powers which you develop and which enable you to kill pirates, run for miles without stopping, rescue your friends (or whoever is left) and liberate the dark-skinned native population on the island who accept you as one of their own and eventually come to revere your mere presence. Typical White Savior theme, it's kind of sickening. Dances with the Wolves, Avatar, Blood Diamond, The Last Samurai, anyone?
The graphics:
The graphics are okay despite the fact that this is one of the few games to fully utilize quad core processors. The jungle is static: no vegetation moves on the island because there is no wind (except for when it's raining), the waves always move though. . There's some destructibility but not much. The field fires are back though which is good. The drawing distance kind of sucks though, there's this constant distance blur and it gets even worse when you are hand-gliding. It just doesn't look crisp or sharp enough so it kind of hurts your eyes, aesthetically speaking. To add to the injury you sometimes see trees appearing in the distance and you also see massive texture load almost every time you spawn at a safe house. The water is just okaish. If you swim under water and look up you will see this weird pre-rendered texture of the same waves which looks pretty bad. Think of Crysis (5 years ago) and how that game managed to create unique wave patterns distinct from each other.
One thing that does help is the field of view which can be set at 110 degrees. I honestly thought I was playing on a 2560x1600 monitor.
The physics:
The physics are mostly well done. You can't just keep jumping and climbing everything like in Skyrim. And when you fall down the hill or you don't just hover in air, you slide down and hurt yourself. However, at the same time you can jump and infinite amount of time and run and swim for as long as you want – no stamina whatsoever. The climbing is done pretty well.
The gameplay:
it's Consolized somewhat. For instance if you want to sneak up on someone and knife them you could easily do it without breaking a sweat. For one thing, the enemies' field of vision is extremely limited both during the day and night (if I recall, it was much easier to sneak up on enemies in Far Cry 2 especially after you save enough to buy a stealth suit). You can sneak up on them even when they are supposed to be seeing you and the detection indicator won't even go op. Then, when you are about 10 feet away from them you can click the melee button and knife them easily even if they see you for a second, I kid you not. I forget how many outposts I took out just by using my knife. Also, the menus suck. You go into your loot sack and it's cluttered with stuff you collected. It's not organized in any way in case you want to clear up some room. It would help if the yellow leaves and red leaves were actually pained YELLOW and RED on the screen instead of the game indicating they were through text. Same goes for animal skins. Just color them in appropriately, not too hard.
There's also no more quick save, which works in some linear games with the whole checkpoint system but not here. You HAVE to finish missions before you can manually save (by going to your main menu) or your will lose some progress like crafting and collecting items. Not having the ability to quicksave diminishes the RPG quality of this game in some ways. For instance you go on a mission to shoot 5 deer with a specific weapon. You kill 2 and decide to craft something. Then you fail to kill the other 3 because you miss and run out of bullets. Mission failed. Start over, and craft another item AGAIN. Same goes for loot and collecting hard to reach relics. Also, why only 3 save slots? The two previous games had an unlimited amount of save slots. Why? Why can't I save the best moments of the game?
What they also did is replace the hidden diamond briefcases with boxes of loot that are always shown on your mini-map. Why? Same goes for plants that are to be harvested. That simplifies the game in many ways, so you never really end up searching for something because it's always up there on the minimap. Far Cry 2 didn't have this problem (you didn't have a minimap and you had REALLY look for them diamonds using your proximity tracker). However, at the same time you didn't really collect as much stuff in Far Cry 2 as you do here.
The constant notifications in the upper left corner are also annoying. Seriously, I'm trying to explore that part of the island, I KNOW that going to the Medusa ship is the mission objective, yet I am getting that notification a few times every minute and the only way to make it go away is to complete the actual mission.
The enemy tagging via camera is back from the first game. Only this time, once you tag your enemies you can see them through the terrain! How convenient! Just like in Hitman: Absolution.
The safe houses are still here however, now you can buy and sell your gear at any safe house! Why? You don't need to travel to those very few people who trade your diamonds for weapons and upgrades. Also, you can't sleep at safe houses anymore and pick the time of the day that you want to complete your objective. However, that's hardly relevant now since the day/night cycle now entirely depends on how fast you are moving in the world.
Far Cry 2 healing is back!
The skinning of animals isn't really skinning, it's just taking the same chunk of flesh; be it a turtle, a shark, or a giant carnivorous bird.
You also can't see your legs or cast a shadow…figures.
Viewing any foe or animal through optics automatically tags them, enabling you to see them through walls during firefights, thereby taking out lots of challenge out of the game.
Most animals also take several shots to the head to die. WTF?
The game also features a Kill-Zone type of cover system which is welcome in an FPS.
The AI:
95% of all AI's look alike. Most of them wear red for some reason. Quite often they are as dumb as a stick insofar as taking them out by one goes since most of them probably have extreme cases of near-sightedness. However, when they start ganging up on you and start calling in reinforcements then you got to think quick.
-The weapons:
Pretty decent, the kickback is sometimes not enough though, feels too arcadish. There's some customization there and there, like better scope, extending magazine. The constant lack of ammo forces you to savor your shots. Also, I don't like the way new guns become available to you. Basically new weapons get unlocked when you disable radio towers. How is that relevant to you being able to buy new weapons from your safe house lockers now?
Co-Op is fun but lacks replay value since it's basically a skirmish. In some ways it feels more like a competition rather than a cooperative buddy experience.
Multiplayer is pretty solid, I must say. What's annoying though is constantly getting the temporary killer instinct ability and being able to see through walls for some time. I also like how when the team loses, the best player from the team is granted freedom by the victorious team.
All in all,decent game that sucks you in

As with the previous Far Cry games, we have always expected them to be a PC gaming benchmark graphically and this game is no exception. The graphics are excellent, and can bring high end gaming machines to their knees! However, even with a mid range graphics card you could easily manage some playable settings and enjoy the game to the end.
The characters are quite easily the best part of this game. Vaas is possibly the greatest villain ever portrayed in a game, largly down to immaculate voice acting & believable animations. Even the side characters you meet on the way are believable and help immerse you in the story.
Controls are easy to get to grips with whether you use keyboard or control pad. I played through with an Xbox 360 controller and it was an enjoyable experience start to finish. The feeling of the guns is realistic and they feel different whether using a pistol of LMG, the weight and control is spot on.
Overall the game is immaculate and shouldnt be missed. It's a shame the PC multiplayer seemed quiet because I thought it was brilliant, some nice game modes, excellent maps, and the graphics are still on point. Better than the typical CoD games. Did not get a chance to try Co-op but from what i've seen it seems fun.
I would give the game 9/10 for single player alone, could have been 10/10 if the multiplayer had been able to extend my time with this game!

FarCry3 is a good open world game, with decent action and wonderful graphics.
What I enjoyed the most was the story. It is well ochestrated and keeps you motivated to play on, to rescue your friends and leave the islands. The antagonist and your friends are well written characters that keep you tantalized. The cutscenes are great and the voice-actors do a very good job as well.
You can either follow the story straight through, keep a fast pace and enjoy the story like a good action movie or you can slow down and explore the island. Find money, relics and other hidden treasures. Or go hunting and skin animals for crafting materials to upgrade certain inventory items that will help you along your journey. Clear out enemy camps all guns blazing or sneak in and get an XP bonus, your choice. There are plenty of weapons, from knives, bows and pistols, to sub-machineguns and heavy weaponary. All upgradeable and customizable.
The skilltree is ok, but not great. Most of the enhancements are either not worth taking or just for fun.
But by the end of the game you will be fully skilled, if you clear out the camps and do the side-quests.
All in all a enjoyable game that is far better then it's predecessor FarCry2 and tries to tie in with the first FarCry installment.

One of the most amazing First person action shooters I've ever played. With amazing graphics, story telling, and gameplay, Farcry 3 is sure to make your mind explode.
One of the major strong points of the game is the open world feature. This is prominent in all of the Farcry games, but in Far cry 3, the setting, Rook Island, is by far the best. The map is massive, estimated to be 4-5 square miles. It's full of different wildlife, such as sharks, lions, deer, and lizards. The main biome in the map is jungle, but there is also beaches, mountains, and open plains.
Relating to the map, the graphics are fantastic. It is one of the best looking PC games I've seen in awhile. If you see the first screenshot I've posted, the draw distance is very large, and everything looks great at a distance. The character models are also very good. Faces look amazing, and the devs also payed attention to scars, pores, and moles/freckles. The scenery is beautiful, one of the most attracting parts of the game I would have to say. Walking through the forest alone is amazing. It blew my mind.
Apart from visuals, the game also does a very good job with gameplay. All throughout the entire game, you had options, going stealthy or going loud and getting into a big fire fight. The guns in the game are also very balanced as well, each one has it's ups and downs. Sliding is also another cool feature in FC3. Sliding can help you quickly dodge bullets or get into cover to escape enemy vision. Apart from all of that, a new feature in FC3, crafting, is also very cool. Hunting animals will get you hide, which you can turn into a bag to create an extra weapon slot, or extra weapon ammo, or tons of other things. This was one of my favorite features in the game by far.
The core of the game, storytelling, is the most appealing part of the game. The main character's name is Jason Brody. Him and his friends get trapped on an island known by Rook island, which is controlled by drug lord pirates. The main goal of the game is to rescue all of your friends and kill the main antagonist, Vass. You travel to many different parts of the map in search of them, and meet many new people in the process, such as Citra, who is a leader of a clan/tribe/group. A big part of the story is the dynamic characters. For example, the main character, Jason, undergoes so much throughout the entire story. He starts as one person, and ends up as an entirely different person. It's very entertaining to go through these changes with him. I really got attached to him as a character, and was very sad when the game ended. Speaking of the game ending, the while campaign is long, it took me a week of playing 2-3 hours per day to beat it, and I enjoyed every minute.
Another thing I'd like to call out, which isn't very important to the key functions of the game, is the soundtrack. FC3's soundtrack is pure bliss. The music starts playing at the best possible times, and it sounds amazing when it does. The composer/producer, Brian Tyler, did an outstanding job. You can listen to it here:
To conclude, Far Cry 3 is one of the best FPS games I've ever played, with very enjoyable graphics, unique gameplay, and one of the most astounding storylines I've personally ever seen in a game. The game gets a 9.5 out of 10, due to the ending, which is a little rash.

In Far Cry 3 you play a spoilt little rich brat, who drops down the rabbit hole. That is, if you go by the Alice in Wonderland theme that the game is not too subtle about. In more literal terms, he (Jason) drops down onto a tropical island. While on vacation with some equally bratty friends, everyone gets taken captive by a group of local mercenaries who plan to hold them for ransom. You escape, with tragedy along the way, and now have to rescue your friends and let the captors face your wrath. You are set free to roam the island and take on missions that advance the main story, but you can also spend time on a variety of optional side-activities and mini-games.
At first, Jason is pretty helpless and your options to take on enemies are limited. Thankfully, you soon get taken under your wing by the rebels on the island who are at odds with the mercenaries. They set you on your way to fulfill (what they see as) your destiny and become a savior, not just to your friend, but also to the rebels. Oddly, these bands of armed locals hang back and let you do all the dirty work for them. What inspired this faith in the innate capabilities of a city kid, is not clear.
You will be gathering leaves to craft syringes that give you health or tactical advantages. You will also be hunting down the local wildlife to fashion holsters, backpacks, wallets and slings out of their hide. This will allow you to carry more money, weapons and ammunition. It’s just as well that the game plays in first-person perspective, as you must look pretty ridiculous by the end, carrying around an extensive arsenal. If you feel bad about having to hunt and skin virtual animals, just realize that the animals in this game do not like you. If you come too close, they will happily attack you and they can be surprisingly deadly.
You will discover this as you go around liberating the island by taking over the enemy bases strewn about the map. In some of these bases, you will spot caged animals. Shoot the cage, and these are set free. It’s not unusual for a bear or tiger to take out the majority of a base for you while you watch safely from a distance. It defies belief that a bear could shake off multiple people emptying their gun on it, but watching the animal at work can be entertaining. Sometimes you don’t even have to shoot a cage. You may be planning your takedown of the base when an animal just wanders in from the forest and does the dirty work for you.
I found that liberating the bases and climbing various radio-towers to reveal new parts of the map – Assassin’s Creed-style – were the most satisfying (semi-) optional tasks. Even though both become a bit routine by the time you get to the last ones. The towers, in various states of disrepair, challenge you to find the only way to the top, without plummeting to your death. How you approach clearing the bases is entirely up to you. You can sneak in and take enemies on one-by-one, go in guns blazing, or never even set foot in the base. I found that the most effective and fun way to go about it was to lurk on a nearby hill, tag all the enemies by zooming in with my camera, snipe the alarms and then to take everyone out through smart combined application of my upgraded sniper rifle and a rocket launcher. It got a bit repetitious, but that was mostly my own fault. It felt illogical to go for a more risky, time-consuming approach, when this one made it so fast and easy.
It is just as well that the long-distance fighting is fun, because the controls for close combat are a bit irritating. The menu wheel that allows you to switch between weapons  isn’t the most responsive and the action doesn’t stop when you bring it up. So you can end up fumbling with it and dying stupidly. Also an issue is that when playing with an X-Box controller, depending on context, the Y button lets you put yourself out if on fire (this happens more often than you would suspect), ...

Very fun and immersive game, plenty of things to do, lovely environment, great game to play.

For what it tries to be - a game of tactical jungle combat and survival on a beautiful desert island - Far Cry 3 succeeds fantastically. A huge pair of lush islands give a gorgeous backdrop to great open world mechanics: Hunt animals for skins for upgrades, climb and disable radio towers for guns, stakeout and plan assaults on outposts, explore WW2 bunkers or ancient temples, or just quadbike/jetski/wingsuit around. You always feel like you're using your wits to win combat, and have to be aware of your surroundings (and your enemies'). The story's a little too heavy handed, but the main villain is well written and the setpieces in the story are stunning. It's very well polished, and constantly engaging.
One of the best Sandbox FPS games around. Easier than Far Cry 2 for sure, but much more fun overall. I love going stealth and clearing outposts without anyone noticing.

Despite the injection of a heavy dose of console-style action in the storyline missions, Far Cry 3 still delivers the open-world mayhem you would expect from the series. Some of the missions feature silly game mechanics more typical of console games, such as "Mash this button to win" and "Quick, press this button or you'll have to watch the cutscene over again" which feels out of place in a PC shooter, but Ubisoft has gone out of their way to add in FOV controls and other features that you would expect. All-in-all this is a very fun game and I would recommend it.

Some games are exciting for a few hours and then you forget about them forever.  Some games are replayable but because they are so scripted it's more or less the same game every time.  Far Cry 3 overcomes these faults by giving the player the freedom to explore the game world and find treasure, have skirmishes with pirates, increase skills, or simply explore the beautifully crafted landscape.  On top of this freedom is the series of missions you need to complete to finish the game.  These can be done at your own pace and are interesting.  I am currently playing the game for the third time.
If that game has faults they are probably to do with the controls.  It might be just my computer but sometimes I find it difficult to enter doorways or go up stairs.  I need to jiggle the controls back and forth or jump.  I would also like the option to save while in a mission but this is not a major fault.  I just make sure I have time to play before entering a mission area.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes shooters but doesn't like being forced to follow a script all the time.

So, here's my final verdict for Far Cry 3. Well, I'm currently doing my fourth playthrough of the game (been doing every difficulty) And I still enjoy it just as much as when the first time I played it. I guess that tells you a little bit if the gameplay/story is good, if not, let me go deeper into it.
Story:
Without spoiling anything, I'm going to briefly tell you what the game is about. You're jason, some guy who was on a nice trip with his friends until everything went downhill. You find yourself caged with your brother on an island full of crazy pirates.
Then you have Vaas, in my opinion one of the coolest villains ever in video game history. Actually, I'm not gonna tell you anything about him, why don't you just get the game and take a look yourself? Throughout the game, you become more powerful, powerful enough to decide you want to take down the people who run the Islands. Are you able to do so, though? You can only find out yourself. There are 2 different endings.
Gameplay:
Far Cry 3 offers a LOT. It's not your regular shooter, no, It's more like.. Hmm, It's quite hard to say really. On Rook Island, you can find plants, animals and useful gear to upgrade your Jason with. You do this by crafting either ammo pouches, medicine, or useful items that can make hunting a little easier. There's quite a lot of different weapons to find/buy, and they all seem to be pretty damn well done. I didn't find any guns that seem underpowered. A single playthrough of the game should take you well over 20 hours, maybe even 30, if you take your time to explore the amazing landscape and secrets the island has to offer. I don't want to go on too much, so I'm just gonna leave you guys to decide wether or not to get the game. Would I recommend it? YES. Absolutely YES. There's nothing you can go wrong with here. Oh, before I miss it, this game support MODS. If you want more of a challenge, try out Ziggy's Mod. It makes the game a lot more challenging by removing the hud, spotting and free weapons.
My final verdict for Far Cry 3 is a 9/10. Only because it wasn't a perfect game, I still wish the multiplayer could be worked on a bit more, but the 9 goes to the singleplayer alone. Thanks for reading my review, and I hope you'll get your hands on this amazing game. :)

Far Cry 3 is an incredible open world adventure where you can essentially play in any way that suits you. Would you like to run in guns blazing? Fancy a rocket launcher or flame thrower? Or how about wiping out an outpost without anyone knowing your there? Any of these options can be done and are all equally viable ways to accomplish the in game objectives. Within the first thirty minutes I experienced an incredibly emotional and engaging introduction that rivaled all my favorite memories from similar games. Remember the beginning to Half Life 2 or dying in the beginning of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare? Far Cry 3 wipes those experiences under the table and then continues to give you things you never thought possible in a game of this magnitude.  Every drug-laden sequence early in the game makes you feel like first-person shooters have risen to a new level in terms of creative narrative story-telling.
We are presented with a very typical open-world game. We can explore the scenic island, take on a slurry of optional missions, search for a staggering amount of collectibles, or take on the newest gaming cliche: hunting. The exploration feels very reminiscent of Skyrim. The stealth elements are familiar for fans of those genres. There are role playing elements and skill tree upgrades. It’s got a little bit of everything and at first-glance they’re all done well.
Even with a new high-end PC I couldn’t play this game on ultra, but on high Far Cry 3 looks absolutely incredible. Environments are gorgeously rendered allowing the player to immerse in every detail of the beaches and jungle down to single blades of grass. The character models are perfectly motion captured and so well acted that you want to know “Who is this guy playing Vaas?” These elements provide a real emotional connection to what’s happening. From the very start you become completely immersed and invested in your motives, the story, the characters, and the world as a whole.
So what’s the problem? Far Cry 3 is a great game that suffers from the trappings of what makes it a game. The strengths and impact of the opening sequence are quickly diminished when your first few mandatory missions act as tutorials of collecting plants and skinning pigs. With further progression you are inundated with endless optional missions, while entertaining, are irrelevant to the larger story. More may not always be better. And the more you play, you’ll realize: this game is riddled with all the tropes of similar experiences.
You’ll need to escape from a burning building, hunker down for turret sequences, use “stealth” to follow a person in broad daylight, and deal with a car chase where you blow up pursuers with a grenade launcher. Meanwhile, every meandering story mission you go on seems to further remove you from any logical character development. Fighting a giant tribal ink demon in a drug-induced state looks cool, but it’s completely pointless and punctuated by a ridiculous first-person sex scene. There are multiple times in the game that make you question what you’re doing and why, because at a certain point none of it makes sense.
This game would have benefited immensely from a shorter and focused campaign. What should have been a linear and powerful storyline is ruined by padding the game out with irrelevant mechanics and tired plot sequences. There was such amazing potential dealing with concepts of human trafficking and how revenge at any cost can transform an ordinary person.  However, the human drama takes a backseat. We’re left with a game that feels manipulated to meet bullet-points on a marketing checklist and a feeling that we are the lowest common denominator for a target demographic.
A lot can be learned from games like Spec Ops: The Line. What seemed like a formulaic shooter was actually a concise narrative that took risks. It explored and engaged the player with what trauma and death can do to the human psyche.
Far Cry 3 could have easily cut characters like Willis, Citra and Hoyt and focused on the drama with Vaas. The optional missions could have been made available as a narrative hook after the main campaign or online experiences with friends. The problem I have is that mechanically the game is still fun. I can recommend it for those reasons. However, narratively speaking, it had so much potential and in the end I was just disappointed with the entire package.

I wasn't prepared for was how much of an utter disappoint this game was. In my opinion the HUD and terrible plot are MORE than enough to ruin the game, and it baffles me that anyone could even get past these two obstacles to even enjoy the game-play. Thankfully, I had installed a couple of mods to improve game-play (more accurate weapons and improved selection) and remove the HUD completely (the official patch didn't go anywhere near far enough in this regard), so the game I am scoring here is not the game I've been playing for the last three weeks, it's the game I would have been forced to play without the mods.
Seriously, who needs that amount of information flashing and bobbing around on their screen to tell them the SAME thing at least three times? The HUD elements, even with all the customisable ones turned off, turn a potentially enjoyable challenge into a ridiculously easy arcade game, where neither thought, exploration or initiative are required. Objectives tell you to 'find' this or 'locate' that, and yet the whereabouts of every objective, no, every STAGE of every objective, is indicated in three different places, two of which are on your HUD (not including what you can actually see with your eyes!). The AI of the enemies is fantastic, amongst the best I've encountered, but the poor sods don't stand a chance because they're splashed all over your mini-map and appear clearly, even behind objects, with big red icons over their heads.
And then there's the plot and characters. Unfortunately, no one's come up with a mod to make the plot or characters any more interesting, and no amount of HUD removal or weapon modding is going to help me give a damn about any of the characters and what's happening to them. Even your own, annoyingly vocal, character, Jason, is a hateful adolescent (not in years, but in behaviour), and his friends are all stereotyped air-heads with no substance.
I get the feeling there is more to the story than it first appears, and there's some kind of 'Alice in Wonderland' sub-plot going on (I've avoided plot spoilers), and that maybe there will be some kind of Fight Club-style reveal where it turns out Jason is actually Vaas, and vice-versa. But you know what? I just don't care any more. I'm about 8 hours into the game and have deliberately avoided following the story, not only because it's weak and the characters are hateful, but also because it means I'm likely to have to sit through endless boring cut-scenes, or stupid, arcade-style mini-games, or encounter the nemesis of any immersion junkie like myself, the dreaded quick-time event (seriously who actually LIKES quick-time events? Who buys a game and says to themselves, 'oh wow, I hope this game has LOTS of quick-time events). Why can't developers just let us PLAY the game, instead of constantly forcing our actions, or taking away our control all together. Valve and other progressive developers have proved time and again that you can have both a great game and a great immersive experience without compromising your in-game freedom, so why is there still this obsession with trying to turn games into movies?
It's a damn shame, because there are loads of things to love about FarCry 3; the hunting, the expanse of the island, the superb AI, the weapons, the beautiful graphics, the best motion-capture acting in a game (Vaas), but all of that can only last me so long, and I just don't want to be in the shoes of this character any more. I'd rather put Jason's friends out of their misery and explore the island.
With mods, such as the removal of the HUD and the improved weapon selection, I'd give the game a 6 out of 10. A better story would have probably meant an 8 or 9. But the vanilla game deserves nothing more than a 1, because developers need to realise that you just can't treat your audience like imbeciles.

You start of as a young man from California named Jason Brody, who is going on a world wide tour to celebrate his kid brother for getting his pilots licens. Afterwards, Jason and all of his friends are captured and held captive across Rook island. Your mission is to rescue your friends, and return home. In order to achieve this, you take aid from a huge variety of firearms and characters. What you do with these in the meantime, is completely up to you.
This game really delivers and is worthy of the Far Cry title. As long awaited sequel to the success of Far Cry 2, it has updated physics engine, combat engine, AI and all around updated badassness. This game has layed ground to some of the most iconic scenes and characters of the present time. With a large variety of weapons, tactics, side-quests and events, this game is well worth owning, no matter how you get it.
Far Cry 3 also features a four player Co-op mode and a multiplayer mode. In Co-op, Mikhail, Callum, Leonard and Tisha are betrayed by a ship captain, who sells them to pirates, and runs of with their hard earned cash. They fight their way through Rook island in hopes to find the captain and retrieve what is rightfully theirs.
The multiplayer mode features 4 gamemodes, Domination, Team Deathmatch, Firestorm and Transmission. You play as either Pirates, with Vaas as commandeer, or The Rakyat, lead by Citra. With leveling systems and fully customizable loadouts, you can achieve anything you want. As you level up, you gain access to more advanced weaponry. These weapons you can then level up in order to unlock attachments to your weapon. This also applies to Co-op. You can also decode certain disks that you find by completing co-op chapters, or playing multiplayer matches.
Pros:
-Nice storyline
-Variation and much to choose from
-Incredible graphics
Cons:
-Some skills in the Single player skill-tree is practically never used
-People only play Team Deathmatch
-The crafting system is a bit wonky, as you need to search the entire damn island for skins and plants.
Final verdict: 9.5/10

Rook Island, a place of beauty; truly the best aging hardware from 2004 can pump out.
You play Jason Brody, a rich white boy who lands on the previously mentioned Rook Island with the rest of his rich white ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ posse. While you initially cheer Vaas for kidnapping these morons and plugging them with bullets... the horrible truth dawns on you within minutes. You have to save these unlikeable losers!
And there it begins; you go on a quest to kill everyone that doesn't look like you to save your wonderbread crew. [There's no real racism in the game, I just wanted to use "Wonderbread crew" somewhere.]
The villain they built up and even show on the cover of the game, Vaas, has maybe 20 minutes of actual appearance in-game. He's dealt with fairly quickly and thrown to the side, a HUGE disappointment as he is the character that was most interesting.
The game itself is amazing fun. Exploring the islands, sneaking through bushes and picking off pirates with a knife and then dragging them back into the bushes, tossing grenades into a cluster sitting around a campfire,  or even tricking enemies into running into a pack of wild dogs, tigers, or even an angry ol' bear. You can approach any situation with dozens of possibilities, and I'm actually eager to go back in and re-play the game just for the crazy missions/scenarios I can make up on the fly to clear out pirate camps.
I've only scratched the surface of what you can do, and what I've mentioned above is without the ability upgrades you can get. So I recently bought Resident Evil 6 and since the download is so slow I could send my dog run to China, swin across the Pacific ocean and come back, and my download would still be at 50%!
While it's making the download, I figured why not review Far Cry 3, Ubisoft's 2012 best game and one of my personal Games of the Year of 2012 (like I said before I have 4 "winners").
Graphically, the game is stunning, everything is high-res, attention to detail is ludicrously high! The color pallet is incredibly varied! I can actually see greens (true greens, not f*cking brown-grey-ish greens, Skyrim!!!!), the water is actually blue! I was shellshocked the first time I saw it, it's truly amazing and a sight to be seen ASAP!
Story wise is where I can safely say the game shines (since every single side quest is as repetitive as a CoD game. Side quests are basically: kill this super holy♥♥♥♥♥♥huge beast animal! OR it's: This pirate is really badass and only you can save us! Kill him! But with a knife because it's our ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ will-get-you-killed-some-day tradition!),  one of the antagonists (of course, Mr. Insanity himself: Vaas!) is the best villain of all time! Movie-wise, book-wise, game-wise, whatever-wise. Vaas is the perfect Villain I've been expecting to see somewhere for years!! The story tells the personal story of Jason Brody, who is trapped along with his girlfriend, brother and friends in a circle of human traffic, lead by Vaas and other amazingly written villains (not as good as Vaas, but they are still some of the best I've ever seen anywhere!). The story is really good, character development EXISTS! It's amazing! One of the best storylines of all time! Although it's annoying the cliché at the start where Jason is a lonely boy who doesn't know how to do anything and 5 seconds later he's Jason Brody, the son of Rambo + Chuck Norris in the womb of John Connor! It's not very believable, but with that aside, the story is stellar and it's the steal of the show along with the graphics!
Gameplay is pretty standard, you have guns n' sh*t and you have to kill some animals to create bigger bags to create bigger ammo pouches, bigger rucksacks (for loot), bigger wallets (it's pretty obvious...) and carry more guns (up to 4 guns, yes you can carry 4 LMG's if you want to do so). The is an RPG like system where you gain XP for stuff that you do and get skill point with then you spend in 3 different skill trees, which allows you to have more health, takedown heavier enemies (this game has stealth and actually does it WELL! F*ck me finally!), among other amazing traits!
Gunplay is pretty good, guns have a very nice handling and feel. Most of them sound very powerful. However in the demo shown at E3 2011 (I think it was E3 2011, not sure) the guns, like the AK (the one shown) looked and seemed to feel much better in that demo than in the actual game, but those are small complaints since the AK still feels amazing in this version.
SOund design is amazing as well, you can hear jungle noises, tigers roaring, gun fire at the distance. The Island is alive and it's great! It really really is! I love the game and everything about it! The game also has a FULL Co-Op campaign up to 4 players and a FULL Multiplayer component (with perks, attachment for guns, clan support, so much, just so much to cover in this game, you can easily put over 40 hours out of it!)
Get it at any price, even 49,99€ it would still be worth it! On Steam is now 29,99€ buy it now or wait for a sale, you won't regret it (unless you're not a tropical island/FPS fan, but who isn't? Nobody, that's who!) :D

"Far Cry 3."
A review by Richard Valkinsenn.
"Did I ever tell you the definition... of insanity?"
Far Cry 3 stands as one of the go-to games for a rich, open world first-person experience. The game features an excellent campaign with a compelling narrative about a group of reckless vacationers who find themselves stuck on an island with bloodthirsty pirates. Colorful characters litter the experience, from the game's psychotic yet memorable villain to the tribe of modernized warriors living on the island whom the player allies with. Many other memorable characters are also present, and thankfully, the player's interactions with them are never stale or lifeless.
Challenging, deep, and innovative gameplay is on display here, as Far Cry 3 allows players to hunt, kill, buy, and explore their way through an island filled with diverse wildlife, hostile pirates, and ancient secrets. A wide arsenal of weaponry is available to purchase -- or unlock -- and upgrade as desired, though some of the starting weapons don't have as much options available as would be desired. The game also features a story-related perk system that makes all the difference to the player as they progress through the campaign, as the game's opposition will only get tougher as time goes on. There are also pirate camps for the player to raid and destroy and successfully doing so will grant fast-travel points allowing for easier traversal of the island. There are also radio towers to unlock and doing so will reveal sections of the map and grant access to free weapons and equipment.
This game is not without gripes though, as its boss fights end up being unsatisfying quick-time events instead of straight-up fights. Worse, barring spoilers, one of the game's most memorable characters is killed off halfway through the game. His replacement, though also memorable, just doesn't really have anywhere near the same impact as his predecessor did. On the other hand, considering the massive amount of content that Far Cry 3 has to offer, these gripes are minimal at best.
Outside of the campaign, a sidestory co-op mode is also present, supporting up to four players, along with unlockable weapons, gear, and etcetera, but it's only really a distraction, at best. Multiplayer is also present, but let's face it: you're here for the campaign, and for Vaas. The overall multiplayer suite doesn't really offer up much different from other games on the market, anyway, outside of a few quirks.
Bottom line, though: Far Cry 3 is an excellent game worth buying and keeping. It's an engaging, unique, and unforgettable experience worth playing through again and again. Not to mention the fact that it also features one of gaming's best and most memorable villains.
Final Verdict:
I loved it.

FarCry 3 was an amazing open-world FPS that kept you playing to learn the outcome of Jason Brody and his friends and family. The scenery gives you the sense of a tropical island paradise where you can just lay back and forget everything, but the pirates chasing after you and the inner conflict brings you back and shows you the real story of the island.
The story kept you hanging on and eventually letting you determine the fate of you and your friends. The drug trips remind me of Fallout 3's Point Lookout DLC, hallucinations and drug use is all a part of living on the island. And at points, the ending to the hallucinations left you wondering what really went on. It adds to an already amazing story. And in the end, you get to decide what happens. Not to Vass or Hoyt, but to your friends and yourself.
Combat is seamless and taking cover is as easy as crouching, using the aim button to lean over cover. I had played Deus Ex: Human Revolution right before I picked this game up, and unlike Deus Ex, enemies are not impossible to kill, with just a few bullets to the chest. Flame adds a whole other aspect of gunplay. Burning shrubery, grass, and trees can siphon enemies out of hiding spots, as well as block off escape routes.
As I had just finished Deus Ex, I was still in a cautious stealth gameplay mode, and Far Cry 3 did a good job at the aspect as well. By the end of teh game you're able to take out an entire outpost in just a few seconds all the while staying in stealth. Throwing knives from one enemy unit to the other or taking the pistol off of one person and using it to take out the rest of the outpost. Even taking enemies out from above or below silently, adds to the stealth aspect of the game. It's not the most perfected stealth, but it works for the game's purposes.
I didn't really find too many cons to the game. No game-breaking bugs or easily looked over mistakes. I outright had a great time playing this game and nothing broke it. But, there's always people who will have a different opinion.

Not terrible. The base gameplay is pretty fun, but it does feel repetitive after a few hours. By the time I reached the second island I was very ready to just end the game. The difficulty settings are wonky too, as I had no trouble on Master difficulty up until the last two missions.
The story is pretty mediocre. A couple characters stand out, but the rest vary between bland and way overdone. As a side effect, many of the cutscenes are very annoying because of the lack of well done characters.
Mods add a lot of challenge to the game, some adding a more realistic distribution of plants and wildlife around the map, removing the wallhack-esque feature of marking targets (not having it adds a LOT more tension to fights), rebalancing the weapons, rebalancing the shops/economy, etc etc.
Buy FC3 Blood Dragon first since it is a standalone if you're on the fence about this game. If you like Blood Dragon, then try FC3.

Open world FPS with a very tight story, focused on character progression. Many actions not found in a typical shooter sets it apart, something mostly introduced by the second Farcry game which shares a very similar feel. Things like pulling bullets from your arm or setting a dislocation to regain health in the absence of a health kit, or having to clear the chamber of a poorly maintained found-weapon.  The tropical enviroment is also a star of the game, with vistas around every corner. Driving to the top of a cliff and jumping off so you can wing-suit your way into an enemy compound in a valley below is as fun as it sounds.

An absolutely fantastic experience. The developers screamed "Have fun with this great island we created!", and oh, I have had so much fun it is unbelievable. Vaas is probably the best villain in a game this year, on the same level as Comstock and Handsome Jack in my books; he seems like a genuinely crazy person, with full control of his insanity. You really learn to be afraid of him, and he can be truly intimidating, in a different way than most of the modern villains we see in movies and games, respectively. A must-buy for everyone. Just a little notion: I recommend you have at least a GTX 460 or the AMD equivalent, since you will want to experience this game in its (near-)fullest glory; the world does so many wonders to the story, so enjoy it all by having a decent PC! The game is really well optimized as well, so you can pull amazing graphics on older systems as well, so give it a go no matter what! Truly one of my recommendations I can be really happy about.

The Far Cry series has done what so few others have in that each game has redefined our perception of what this franchise is. The first game had you blasting through a Island of Dr. Moreau-inspired landscape, the second brought us back to reality with a hunt for an arms dealer in Africa, and now the third installment aims for a more personal experience while drawing inspiration from films like Taken and Turistas.
In the game you play as an American 20-something year old named Jason Brody who accompanies his two brothers and wealthy friends on vacation in Thailand. Being thrill seekers and adrenaline junkies the group is told about Rook Island where "anything goes" and they decide to blindly sky dive onto it. Shortly after landing the group is taken captive by pirates led by the clearly sadistic and violently insane Vaas who plans to collect a ransom but sell them into slavery anyway. After narrowly escaping, Jason is taken in by the local natives who inpsire him to take the fight to Vaas and save his friends.
The story is beautifully crafted, the characters are vivid (thanks to phenomenal voice acting and animation), and the game's use of insanity as a focal point pays off brilliantly.
Like the previous titles, FC3 drops the player in an open environment that's just as big if not bigger than Skyrim and all of it save a smaller island is available to explore from the get-go. Populating the game world are story missions, side missions, and hidden collectibles and transportation including cars, trucks, boats, ATVs, hang gliders, and jet skis. The combat is exciting and tense and a large arsenal of weapons is at the players' disposal covering handguns, SMGs, assault rifles, LMGs, sniper rifles, shotguns, and even a bow and flamethrower.
While the story missions are always varied and great fun the side missions are repetitive and lack luster after awhile. Tracking down hidden collectibles also becomes a chore pretty quickly as the payoff for doing so is limited. Lastly while the environment looks incredibly appealing it does become stale after awhile in its lack of variety. Additionally, some of the more detail oriented players have noticed that the game world lacks some of the awesome physics and destruction features present in the PC version of Far Cry 2.
Overall though the pros greatly outweigh the cons. Far Cry 3 is a tense and brilliantly designed game that is totally worth picking up. If you're looking for something that seamlessly blends a fantastic narrative and addictive gameplay look no further. Personally I can't wait to see what they do with the next game and how the franchise will redefine itself again.

Far Cry 3 is a first-person shooter action game created by Ubisoft Montreal in 2012.
The player, Jason Brody, skydives with friends and ends up on an island full of pirates and natives called Rakyat that are in conflict . Jason escapes but is unconscious. An inhabitant of the island, a Rakyat called Denis rescues him and performs a tattoo that gives Jason powers. This is the first step on his journey to become a warrior. The game is a sandbox, and the main story is just a little part of it, the player is free to make a huge amount of fun activities. Play racing , throw knives , face challenges, hunt animals , free towers and regain positions held by pirates. The game has the graphic quality of a first person shooter with the freedom of an RPG .
The graphics engine is called Dunia Engine. The graphic quality is very good , similar to Crysis, awesome for being a Sandbox. Far Cry3 was one of the best and most complete games of 2012. Extremely funny and fascinating.
It is a worthy successor to Far Cry , well above the poor Far Cry 2 . A true wonder for lovers of external environments and forests in games.
The game was released for PC , PS3 and XBOX 360. The PC version has superior graphics and a powerful graphics card with DirectX 11 is seriously recommended.

I feel as if a recommendation of this game would make me seem like I am high, much like a lot of the game to be exact, cause EVERYONE says this is a brillient game. Its kind of surreal really, because for a game that recieved such high critical acclaim, and was so popular and FPS like, I actually genuinely liked it as an FPS.
Not because of the RPG mechanics, or the inclusion of crafting, gun variety, character development, decent main story, trippy topics like drug use, and abuse, piracy, and slavery. Well I liked all of those actually, but the shoot-em-up sections were fun. The game managed to keep a consistent tone, and actually develop itself over the course of time, in a meaningful way. It created that open world magic of going out to a location, and taking it down with your acculated ability, and weapons, but this is where is starts to fray.
Because at its core, its an FPS, its no Skyrim with guns, because thats Fallout. FC3 fails not on a fundimental level, but on an auxillery one, whereby, its not fun to explore without a solid objective, or tangible reason to be exploring. The island is just bland, empty really, sure it looks nice, but there is nothing secret to explore that cant be found by buying a loot map from stores. The game turns from that open world fun, to another rather linear progression of "go here, get new gun, do story mission to unblock this set of new skills". The game tries to pace a open world game, and that does not mesh well. As well, it is incredibly easy, and more deaths will be attribute to poor design, rather than lack of character skill, or weapon balence. In other words, there is more of a case of rage quit deaths, than real honourable ones.
Now dont get me wrong, even though I just spent the last 157 words bashing the game, I still think it is brillient. I would recommend it to anyone that wants an easy shooter, that would like to have a rather relaxing and enjoyable experiance like me.

This game is truly demanding of utmost respect in the titles of this decade. It's what I feel is one of the more advanced out there. You have splendid character developement, an intruiging skill system, a lovely arsenal of weapons with customization to enhance performance and it just gets better. The game is beautiful, with almost believable environments. You can hide in the bushes as you'd expect to in real life for stealth. Crafting items is actually useful in this game instead of just for show -- as are the Path of the hunter quests. You'll find that even though this is a beautiful game, it's full of jump tricks. By that I mean, you could be innocently walking around, and hear a soft hiss. Next thing you know, a snake is latched to your arm, or a Komodo Dragon is nomming on your feet. And watch out in the water, sharks or gators do wrestle with you. Enemy AI is fantastic, they're intelligent enough to take cover, and try and lure you out. As for the AI regarding driving, don't try and get a friendly to drive for you -- they're really scary.  All in all, I thought this was one of the best Ubisoft has thrown out there. Don't wait for this crazy island to magically appear, go and get this game. You'll be glad you did. Thanks Ubisoft, you made my day!

What really makes no sense to me about this game is how the hell does Jason learn all of these para-military tactics within a minute, after his armed forces brother dies 5 minutes into the game, when he clearly admits that he has never done anything like this or taken a life before.
However, I somehow still really enjoyed this game. The gameplay behind Farcry 3 is amazing. It's a sandbox sort of game filled with so many hostiles, including animals that you're able to hunt for materials. I like the concept of skinning the animals to further your carrying capacities, however I feel that it could've been a bit better. I really did enjoy the fact that there were multiple vehicles whever you went, such as Jeeps, Quads, MG mounted boats,  Jet skis, and sky gliders. Overall the gameplay is superb, but the main character and his story could've used way more help. Vaas is the only saving grace story-wise.
Also, the CO-OP mode is essentially a Left 4 Dead copy, where there are 4 players connected to one server, and you get swarmed with hordes of enemies while completing petty objectives.
I would've liked to see a better story, but this game easily gets 7/10.

This game can be defined with three words. Open world immersion! Crafting, hunting, exploration, side games, challenges, optional quests, lively characters, and amazing weapon design -- this game has it all! Not many games live up to the given price tag, and this is one of them. I spent fifty hours on my first play though. That is an extensive single player fps.
Cut off the music and turn off all of the "hud" options that can be toggled, (I left the grenade indicator on) and this island will come to life. When hunting, the player will need to stand still and listen for the growls and other noises made by the animals. The items obtained from the wild life give the player options to craft new weapon, ammo, and consumable slots. The open world feel will often send the player face to face with tigers, bears, or enemy patrols when least expecting it.
The ONLY thing I didn't like about the game.... Is the main character! I wanted to smack my guy in the face way to many times =/ But that is a small price to pay for a full and complete game that has been polished into a guided, open world thrill ride that is sure to please. The first time you light an enemy base on fire then slide down a steep mountain side for a quick and slick escape from the guard dogs like a serious BA, just to land on a pack of frickin' grizzly bears -- you'll be hooked!

There are some really annoying QTEs that hurt the cinematic experience, and I had a hard time relating to and caring about the protagonist and his band of friends, but, all in all, it’s a solid game that improves over the 2nd with a better travel system, much better guns/gun play, and far more interesting characters overall.
8.5/10

Far Cry 3: Return of the Mohawk Man is great point and click game that follows the life of infamous Pirate "Bason Jorody" as he goes around Rook Island pillaging corpses and buccaneering new vehicles throughout the game. His adventure ends, however, when the "Mohawk Man" attacks him with his gang of mercenaries and kidnaps what he loves most, along with is friends. Follow Bason as he fights to save POTATO SALAD and makes the necessary sacrifices like murdering all of his friends with an assault rifle and burning orphanages down just to sell the charred corpses to the local Meals On Wheels to keep POTATO SALAD safe. Mohawk Man is just as sinister as he is in "Far Cry 1: Mohawk Man and the Great Wahoo Wave" if not even more so. The voice acting talent is top notch and needs to be just that as Bason devours POTATO SALAD throughout the game. When he spits flecks of POTATO SALAD at the Mohawk Man, you feel like he's spitting flecks of POTATO SALAD at you. Far Cry 3 is better than its predecessors but claiming it's "Elder Scrolls with guns" is hyperbole at BEST. The game has a beautiful world, yet it's shallow and sparse--lacking true believability or detail. This leaves the player feeling empty and unmotivated; having no emotional attachment with the world or its characters--something one wouldn't expect from an open-ended world. Far Cry 3 takes place on an island that consists mostly of wilderness with a few small shanty villages and pirate outposts that you can "liberate". The game has some brief adrenaline-pumping sequences but it is ultimately a generic FPS through and through. Granted, it does have a light mixture of other elements like weapon customization, skill trees, and crafting. However these options don't make combat any less repetitive or the quests any less tedious. The story develops in traditional, albeit questionable ways and side missions and challenges are laughable and boring. I wouldn't recommend this game for $30 (which is what I paid for it). I would wait for a better deal. I know there are people out there who enjoyed Far Cry 3, but I'm not one of them.

FarCry3 takes the general gameplay from FarCry2 and improves it a lot. The savannahs and djungles of Africa has been replaced by an beautiful island paradise much more like the original FarCry. The single player campaign is one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had in a long time. The story is a lot more mature than you expect from most FPS. At it's best it's emotional and makes you take some tough decisions. Ultimately I felt that it didn't quite live up to it's ambitions though.
But the single-player campaign is only the start. FarCry3 has one of the best co-op games I've played. Instead of just re-using the campaign, the co-op mode has four unique characters and story. Think something like Left4Dead but with pirates instead of zombies and you'll get the idea. The co-op mode also loans some features from RPGs, like buffs (shouts and booster shots) and weapon upgrades based on experience points.
There's also a more ordinary multiplayer mode (with some special gameplay quirks).
FarCry3 is well worth the money. It's one of (if not the) best games released 2012 and offers a lot of replayability. Even if you get tired of the single-player campaign, the co-op mode offers a lot of long-lasting fun.

オープンワールドFPSシリーズの大家、Farcryの最新作。前作の課題となっていた煩雑なアンロックミッションはかなり緩和され、また新しい要素として、経験値によるスキルアンロック制を導入されている。舞台となる島の作りこみは極めて美麗かつ秀逸で、散策しがいがあり、シチュエーションが豊富で飽きが来にくい。操作性も良好で、スキルの取得状況によって動作が豊富になっていく点は非常に爽快。以下は欠点。
１：スキルレベルは序盤から中盤にかけては割り振りの多様性があるが、結局のところすべて取得することになるのでそこまで育成の楽しみはない。そのためRPGライクな要素の多くが―クエストやチャレンジ等ー終盤無駄になる、メリットがない。
２：ハンティングの要素についても同様で、初期こそ多様な動物を装備充実のために乱獲する楽しみがあるが、装備は中盤にはほぼ出そろうので、あとは少々めんどくさいオブジェクト程度の価値しかなくなる
３：ストーリーの中だるみがひどい。中盤以降のストーリーが平坦で盛り上がりに欠ける、特に終盤ははっきりいってこれまでの探索すべてをぶち壊しにするくらいの出来。
４：消音装置のついてない武装に存在価値がない。正面からの打ち合いよりもステルスを推奨するのはいいとして、正面から戦うミッションの数がそもそも少ないので必然的にステルス装備で常時過ごすことになる。なのでプレイスタイルが変化せず後半飽きる。
特に３はわりと致命的なレべル。海外レビューはかなりの高水準で、プレイした感じも操作性やシステムについてはおおむね同意できるのだが、自分の動かすキャラクターに愛着が湧かないのは少々、FPS形式のアドベンチャーとしてはつらいところ。伏線の回収し忘れなども多々あり、狂気をテーマにするわりには狂いきれていないのはちょっといただけない。

Tasteless, repetitive, boring, unbalanced, horrible performance, no optimization whatsoever. That's what this game is.
It desperately tries to bring an entire open world where you feel like a survivor in an epic adventure, but in the end it doesn't. No immersion. I don't feel like I'm Jason. The story is not bad, but it's not good either. Nothing new. The main antagonist is the only character with a real personality. And that's not good. It makes me want to lose so he can win.
Let's focus on each point and why it fails:
1. Story: nothing new. Boy goes on adventure, something goes wrong, friends in trouble, must become a hero and save them, join some guys who are against the villain's tirany. It's not bad, but it's not enough.
2. Performance: laggy, choppy, with no optimization, can't play in high graphic settings with more than 30 fps. And even playing in ultra, the graphics are not good enough for what it consumes. So far, a crappy port.
3. Gameplay mechanics: nothing new, and very badly done. Open world, full of enemies, you can hunt, you can do side missions, you can collect things, you can craft. Like any other open world game of this kind. Weapons suck, I can do more damage with an AK47 than with a Magnum revolver. I mean, a magnum has a 6-bullet round and should take 1 shot to kill, but in this game, it takes all 6, even with headshots, versus 1 headshot with the AK47 which can be accomplished fairly easy if you are used to FPS games. Bows? More like freaking machineguns at the speed they shoot. No need to charge your shot, no sir, the arrow will always go fast as a bullet out of the bow, and you don't even need to reload! Incendiary arrows? Way better! Just shoot them 20 times in 10 seconds and burn the whole island to the ground!
4. Interface: crappy. They should've used steamworks instead of uplay for multiplayer, because it is very buggy and difficult to join a lobby. It takes a long while to load because it has to send and receive a lot of data, and it does it slowly.
5. DRM: the worst part. Not only you have to log into Steam to play, but you also have to log into UPlay to launch the game. And the worst of the worst? Manual input of serial keys, without being able to paste it. You have to input it letter by letter - and remember, no scores or capitals, or else it won't work! It took me 3 times to enter it correctly because of this! - to unlock your game and DLC. Why on Earth?
6. Co-op: linear, repetitive, boring.  It can be fun if you play with friends or just want to shoot around people, but just that.
Overall, this game was a disappointment. I don't even want to finish it.

When someone installs a shooter these days, a few things are to be expected: a tired, gray or brown aesthetic with hyper violence, an uninspired cover system, and a poor story about beefy marines (sometimes in space.) Far Cry 3 has none of these things, and boy is it refreshing.
The first thing you'll notice is COLOR. Dear God, remember when shooters had color? The landscapes are a lush green, with hills, mountains, jungles, cliffs, forrests, and beaches as far as the eye can see. The graphics are truly a sight to behold. The character models go for a stylized realism that works very well: the eyes tend to glow, bringing life to even the lowest merc that happens to get the wrong end of your machete. The animals tend to glow a bit too, making most would-be scary ambushes lack that eerieness. Sharks tend to glow in the dark at night, for whatever reason (although the aligators are camoflaged too well; I couldn't even tag them even when I had my scope right on them at times.)
The sound design is sufficient. The music tends to kick in and out at nonsensical times, but what is there is pretty good. That is, the original score, the licenced music seems to be a poorly thought out cash grab simply for advertising purposes. The weapons are well designed and sound great, but feel a little too acrcade-; all but the .50 cal rifle and shotguns feel like your phazers are set to stun. Perhaps this is because there's surprisingly little out of cutscene violence. There's no gibbing, and even a headshot produces only a splash of blood and an action movie stunt-fall. In all honesty, the "viceral" hyper violence is getting old and I didn't miss it for a bit. On the other hand, it may have brought some much needed kick to the gunplay.
The pysics system is hit and miss. Although corpses ragdolls are at an all-time high, when you get fall damage, and how much you get, seem to be entirely arbitrary. Sometimes I can slide down a sheer cliff with no worries, other times I can't make jumps I can in real life without getting my health cut in half. However the arrow physics are to die for. The bow and arrow isn't even a very good weapon, but you'll keep it with you the whole game just because it's so satisfying!
The tatau perk system is rather lazy and leaves very little room for customization. By the end of the game, you'll definitely have all of the perks. And for an open world shooter, the game is surprisingly short. I beat the game and did almost every side quest in under thirty hours; and this was on the harder difficulty setting (which I certainly recommend you playing on if you have ever played a shooter before.)
Lastly, there's the story. Far Cry 3 has recived a lot of press about how good the story is, and this isn't entirely inaccurate. There are a number of very, very, interesting characters (Buck is a legend! Willis and Sam are pretty great too,) but most characters fall horribly flat. Especially the friends of the protagonist; a part of me wished they would just die so I could move on with the game. Jason was a pretty paper-thin character himself, although having a very easily identifiable protagonist works for the alien world of Far Cry 3's warrior culture. However, the main villains are one-dimentional and much of the supporting cast don't even have that (I'm looking at you, Dennis.) Vaas can be described in one word: crazy -- like a bad Heath Ledger in The Dark Knight. Hoyt? A bad Scarface. And the boss fights are all done in a trippy, non-spaciotemporal knife fight demention, which is cool, but it really just boils down to a series of quicktime events. Now that I think about it, very much like DDR with knives. These druged-out segments are some of the best times though, many of them having no enemies what so ever, but the immersion is incredible. You actually feel like a stranger in a strange land, much more so than the very, very, shallow Through the Looking Glass quotes that only seem to break what little tension you would have after a lackluster quicktime event.

Far Cry 3 is two games.
The first 2/3 of it is an open world first person shooter that lets you control the pace. You can go hunting for wild animals, attack enemy bases, and tackle the vast majority of the missions in any way you want, whether that's via stealth or dudebroing it up, or whatever. It really is exceptionally good fun!
The last 1/3 is just... well... it's linear, it's boring, it's Call of Duty-esque gunsplosions, i.e. gameplay is driven by linear environments with checkpoints, and progress is through attrition rather than player ingenuity. All of these are symptoms of a game that has lost its way towards the end, or christ, even had another team entirely working on it.
Sure you *can* still explore the open world in the last third, but the impetus and momentum at this point is on beating the game rather than unlocking♥♥♥♥♥♥ since doing it is for its own sake at that point (earlier on in the game, side missions are to get XP to strengthen your character in order to tackle the tough story missions). The game even acknowledges this by raining ammo packs and body armour down on you at the end of each story mission at this point so you don't have to spend time going to restock.
Couple this with a predictable plot, lame characters and a rather binary sense of morality, and Far Cry 3 is an okay, if not amazing, product. I can recommend it, since I felt compelled to finish it, but be warned: the last third of the game is really lame whereas the first two thirds are really quite good. Just be sure to get the game when it's cheap.

There is a lot to keep you occupied here.
Of course its your open world FPS just like FC2.  Much bigger. Like they said "Skyrim with guns."
Single player sports a kind of RPG system. Taking outposts, defeating enemies, completing missions nets you EXP which gives you points to skill up in your Tattoo Skill Tree.... thingy...
Theres guns to unlock. Challanges to complete like racing boats, ATV's, or combat challanges like how many badies you can take down with a knife in the set ammount of time.
The game is farily flexible on how you tackle certain challanges. You can put a silencer on your weapons and try and take out an outpost without anyone sounding the alarm. And if you're just that damn good at it you might be able to do it without anyone detecting you at all. Want to set the trapped tiger free in the outpost to help you take it down? Can do! Shoot the cage door with a sniper rifle and watch the pirates get torn apart.
There is a fairly fun crafting system in the game. Hunting animals will give you materials to upgrading your weapon holsters, ammo pouches, etc. Spend a lot of time hunting and you'll soon be able to hold many weapons, medical syringes, grenades,etc.
The story is fairly interesting. Nothing that will make you scream "Oh Gawd I must see what happens next!!!" but its enough to keep you going.
One thing about Single Player that ticked me off.... Achievements go thru the Uplay client and not Steam..... I don't like Uplay.... nuff said.
Multiplayer boasts a Co-Op and PVP. Playing either one will help you skill up and unlock more guns, perks Call of Duty style. FC3 does sport more variety with its unlockables in multiplayer however.
Overall its a great game. I actually was interested enough to finish this one... so.. Well done FarCry 3. You officially pleased one of the most demanding gamers on Steam.

After a few hours playing this game, all I can say is : good story, interesting plot. Nice graphics. The games mechanics are fun to play with. BUT there are few things that ruins the pleasure : un(mouse)scrollable menus makes navigation a real pain, the scrollbar is very small. Menus in menus in menus in menus... Ubisoft news, even on in-game menu, no shortcuts to switch from map to crafts to quests or anywhere you want to go when you're on a menu... Environment problems that makes me getting stuck even on wood planks or stairs forces me to jump everywhere, even if the ground /seems/ flat...
The game is worth the time spent on it for its story and environment, but mabe not enough tested on long playing sessions to make it smooth.

All around solid FPS game. This game has a ton of exploration and side missions to keep you very busy. The main story is decent length as well, but coupled with side missions and and certain collectables you could easily be busy past the 20-30 hour mark.
The visuals are probably one of the strongest things driving this game. The world is very detailed, and it looks and actually feels like a real island in the middle of the ocean. The character models are solid, but the environment is where this game really shines. There are a lot of weapons to use and the most fun is probably the bow along with doing takedowns with your machete. Aside from the main story, you can do missions like hunting certain animals, killing a certain pirate and driving medical supplies from point A to point B.
The voice acting was decent, but the pirate Vaas easily takes the crown in that department. I think Ubisoft did a great job with this game and I highly recommend it.
