The scale of Far Cry 3 is enormous, and the game looks amazing. The visuals alone make Far Cry 3 and amazing package, but the gameplay pushes it to another level. The combat is fun, and with so many weapons and attachment options, you can craft your play style to which ever you prefer. The bow is the star of the show, and it is extremely satisfying to lurk around under the jungle canopy, taking pirates out from the bushes, or pulling of a long shot with the bow with the AI none the wiser.
The random animal factor adds even more to the atmosphere of the game. In the early game, animals are terrifying encounters, and a roar in the jungle will have you hiding away. As you progress through the game, animals become less of a threat but they still add tons of random entertainment to the game when they wander into your battles.
The story in the game is adequate enough for those interested, but it never really seems to gain traction. Side quests are dull and seem pointless besides gaining money and experience, but these are never hard to come by. Hunter’s quests are more interesting than the side quests, as are the Wanted Dead quests.
The crafting and leveling system adds a lot to the Far cry series, and hunting down all the animals to increase your storage capacity can leave you side tracked for hours. Crafting most of the upgrades can be done very early in the game, which makes the game feel front heavy and the later game feel like there is very little to do.
Clearing the outposts around the map, and climbing the radio towers can be a lot of fun. Taking down an outpost silently is as exciting as going in guns blazing. Unfortunately, clearing outposts removes the enemy threat from that part of the map entirely and leaves the island feeling dull. It is almost worth leaving most of them alone to keep pirates around to fight when you just feel like messing around, and taking only a few for fast travel purposes and to resupply.
The small time spent with multiplayer was lackluster at best, not really doing anything to set itself apart from the crowd. It's mostly a forgettable addition to the game, and playing against higher leveled players is a chore. Cooperative can be quite fun with friends, but it also seems to be where all the bugs come through. Some bugs can hinder progress completely, while others are annoying at most. Cooperative is nothing special though, consisting of a throw away story and run and gun gameplay.
Far Cry 3 is definitely worth playing for single player alone. The jungle island setting is extremely fun, and just hopping in and causing havoc is the main draw more than the story. Crazy things can happen when pirates, animals and fire mix.

Being that the Farcry franchise has gone a long way to end up giving satisfying sandbox worlds, all with a jungle vibe, the third prodecessor is a definite hit. With added RPG elements known as "Tattoos", players can experience a multitude of playstyles, whether it be the Shark (mid-range fighting), or Spider (silent-killing). With plenty of options such as hunting to upgrade equipment, cutting plants to create syringes to get an edge in combat, or even tackling numerous posts whether stealthily or guns blazing, who could go wrong? Characters such as Vaas, an insane twisted and sadistic drug-lord, or Dennis, a leader of a tribe and follower of Citra, the story's characters certainly deliver and convince. With that, Farcry 3 also free DLC to boot with Co-Op missions and even an extra weapon for keeps.

Farcry 3 is an open-world RPG shooter; and one of the best shooters I've played so far. This game inclines more to a shooter while attempting to balance it's RPG-play. The RPG aspect comes from the customisability of the player's loadout (weapon etc), allowing for the player to take on an objective with his most comfortable style. Although Farcry 3 has a skill tree or "perk" tree that introduces more role-playing elements, the fact that every skill in there can be obtained diminishes the "different player, different stats" element of a RPG. Hence, the game feels more inclined towards a First-person shooter.
The unique thing about this game is the integration of animals into the gameplay. This gives the game a more realistic feel as animals are abound in the wild and they can come as a boon or a bane to anyone. Farcry 3 has effectively brought out this aspect by having animals roam the wild and aiding you while you set up a raid on an enemy camp or create confusion for the player while attempting to raid an enemy camp. Animals in captivity can be used to your advantage against its captors, or while sneaking up from the flanks of an enemy group/convoy/camp, a wild animal attacks you causing your plan to fail. The introduction of wildlife into game also allows for side "quests" such as hunting and also crafting of personal equipment. This aspect gives the game a more varied feel as opposed to traditional FPS.
On the topic of realism, as with many other games, the producers have created the protaganist (the player) as an android running on nuclear power. This could have been improved with the need for sleep (such as a timer which resets upon sleep or penalises players with reduced stats/abilities/actions); that, however, is my own take on how the game could have been made more realistic and may not suit all players out there.
The graphics of the game is comparable to most FPS games out there on the market (2012). Although not top notch for the year, in my opinion, it is very good considering it is an open world game and has many aspects fused into its gameplay.
The actions and shootouts of the game is highly non-linear due to its open world setting. It allows one to play a First-person shooter the likes of Modern Warfare/Black Ops without having a linear flow. This aspect, in my opinion, gives the player a more "on-the-set" feel; where every action that the player makes, leads to something totally different in the reaction of the enemies. I personally went for the long range and stealthy approach, thinning the enemy ranks with hidden sniper fire and then going in "Black Ops" style when the time is right. Other players can choose to go in loud, taking out groups of enemies with RPG or Grenades then finishing the rest with heavy fire. This myriad of interchangeable play style, which differs from player to player, is the game's main plus point - one which will make Farcry 3 suit the many gamers out there.
In all, it is fair to say that this game is a strong contender for the title of FPS or Action/Adventure Game of the Year. It has a heavy FPS aspect while giving the player a role-playing "feel". It is definitely a must-try game for those die-hard FPS fans who want to experience something different from the linear FPS games.

JIST: Far Cry 3 is an open world FPS action adventure game. The story is forgettable, with interesting villians, but not so interesting protagonists. The graphics are amazing, so you will need a high end rig to play this on max settings. The shooting on the other hand just feels so pedestrian. The guns have no umpf to them.   Even with an awesome looking LMG you feel like you're shooting a nerf gun....well even shooting a nerf gun is probably more fun. The menus are awful, and were not designed for PC. The game falls flat for me because the story and gameplay are too stripped down for the mass market.
GRAPHICS: The graphical features of the game are among the top this generation. You have the choice of the standard DX9, or the more exciting DX11 features. Textures are excellent, the vegetation is almost photorealistic in some areas, and the water effects are top notch. You will have no complaints in the graphics department, assuming you have the rig to run it.
GAMEPLAY: You're given a good selection of weapons to unlock as you go along. You can either purchase them at vendors,  unlock as a reward for putting radio towers back online, as well as unlocking them by picking up enemy weapons. There is a good mix here, but it seems a bit too easy to unlock everything because you're given so many opportunities.
The shooting is probably the worst part about the game. You have lots of guns to choose from but they feel like toys. You don't feel like you're shooting a powerful weapon. This is probably due to mediocre sound assets. IMO shooting is a core aspect of this game, and without a strong core, the fun factor goes way down.
There are several side mission types you get in the game, but there are too many of them and not enough variation. The story missions however faired better in terms of variation, but it comes at the price of freedom. During a mission you are not allowed to leave the mission area or you fail. This kind of control is unnecessary imo for an "open-world" game.
There is a crafting system, which boils down to these 2 things: Hunt various animals for pelts to increase your inventory, and weapon slots; and harvest various plants for various drugs that help you in battle. This system was too streamlined, and needs more useful variation. The few consumables that you could craft, almost 1/2 of them were not needed.
QTEs are kept to a minimum in this game, but that said they are also used in the wrong places.
STORY: The protagonists are forgettable. They never grow on you, and you never sympathize for them. Considering the plot that is presented to you (essentially young people trapped on an island filled with slavers trying to escape for their lives) it's big missed opportunity by Ubisoft.
CO-OP: While this is not the star of the show, and while it is not open-world co-op, this L4D style up to 4 person cooperative mode is a lot of fun. The unlocks are completely separate from the single player. It's fast paced, with a variety of objective types as you move along this stand alone story.
PORT: The menus for crafting are not optimised for PC. They aren't even that good for consoles for that matter. Far too slow, and interrupts the pacing of the game. Graphics as said before are top notch.

As I grew more powerful characters responded to my progression and I actually felt the need to become even greater. The voice acting was surprisingly amazing, especially of the character Vaas.
Now, I'm not saying this is the greatest game, but it certainly was the most rewarding after finishing it. The story can be short if you pummel through it, but if you take your time to take in the island and do the side missions, it'll become well worth the money.
The multiplayer is nothing short of mediocre, and the gun play isn't anything special; but the tatau feature of power advancements make the game a lot more fun.
Would recommend to others who enjoy a gorgeous game with great scriptwork and a brilliant monologue that brings tingles to my spine.

A Fun and addictive shooter.
Pros
-Engrossing story with some of the most memorable video game villains in recent history.
-Voice acting is top notch
-The graphic is very impressive with great lighting, weather and water effects.
-Large variety of Weapons and upgrades. The game lets you chose the way you want to play.
-Gathering plants lets you create Syringes which have different kinds of effects and bring an element of strategy to gun fight. Syringes such as untouchable make you withstand more bullets.
-Upgrade items such as wallet and ammo bag by hunting animals. Hunting is addictive until you get all upgrades.
-Some skills obtained from levelling are interesting. One skill lets you detonate a grenade off an enemy after you gained a takedown.
-Large island to explore with lots of hidden collectables to discover.
-Around 50 hours of gameplay if you aim for 100 % completion (not counting multiplayer or Co op)
Cons
-Co op and Multiplayer are pointless add-ons
-Environments are too similar. Walking through jungles can get tedious at times.
-Side missions are short and pointless.
-Some skills you obtain are become useless. One skill that lets you obtain twice as much skin but it becomes pointless after you finish upgrading all your gear.

Far Cry 3 takes place on a tropical island where the main character (Jason Brody) and his friends are on vacation until they get kidnapped. Jason has to learn how to kill and save his friends to get them all off the island. The game is a FPS with RPG elements. The game has a skill tree system and unlike many other games, you can actually get every single skill in there by the end of the game. The gunplay is solid and the stealth mechanics are just as good. What surprised me most is how good the driving is on a keyboard and mouse. Far Cry 2 didn't have the best driving but this was great. The singleplayer campaign lasts about 8 or less hours if you rush through it, but if you actually go and do some side quests and explore the game can easily last you over 25 hours to 100% complete. The graphics in the game aren't the best but it has some nice lighting effect but the game is pretty demanding. DX11 is featured in this game but it is nothing great and is way more demanding than DX9. Another problem I had with the game is as soon as you turn on MSAA the game looks much uglier for some strange reason. Another problem the game has is UPlay so if you hate that service or don't have a solid internet connection then as every new Ubisoft game, this is not for you. Graphics and UPlay aside this game was a solid port seeing as it has all the options you would expect out of one and the game feels fantastic on a keyboard and mouse. The storyline in this game was solid with two different endings. Animation in this game was nice for the most part but there were some things that needed more variations of it. Skinning an animal is the same thing every time. The sound in this game was great with good voice acting. I would strongly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun open world shooter with a good story line and a nice length. 97/100

Far Cry 3 is a fantastic open-world FPS that does so many things right. The single player portion is great and the co-op portion is a nice addition but do not get this for the multiplayer portion.
The graphics are great (DX9 looks very close to DX11, so use that for the extra bit of frame-rate), the story and voice acting are surprisingly great (Vaas is one of the best villians this generation), and the musical score is simply one of the best I've heard in years.
As for the gameplay itself, there is plenty to do and plenty of options to accomplish it all. In most games that offer a stealth approach, I decide not to go that route. In FC3 though, I found the stealth takedowns and since of taking out a base with a knife and suppressed weapons very thrilling and tense. But if it is more your style, you can rock out an LMG, grenade launcher, and/or flamethrower and just wreck havoc on the enemy.
The side missions in FC3 are very fun. Hunt certain animals with the provided weapon, race in a car/buggy/ATV/Sea-Doo/and even a mix of these, assasinate leaders with a knife takedown, and more.
I look forward to a FC4 if the improvements of FC3 over FC2 are any indication of quality.

"Did I ever tell you the definition of insanity? Insanity is doing the exact same ♥♥♥♥ing thing over and over again, expecting♥♥♥♥♥♥to change."
Far Cry 3 takes this banter from its megalomaniacal antihero, Vaas, to heart. Whether you're stalking a group of pirates in the lush forest, diving amidst tropical fish and bloodthirsty sharks for sunken treasure, or torching fields of Mary Jane with a flame thrower, there’s plenty to do on Rook Island – losing your sanity included. Far Cry 3 takes the path less traveled with an engaging FPS that entertains the player from beginning to end with smart writing, tight controls, and an immersive environment. As Jason Brody, you play an initially unlikeable protagonist who begins the game as an everyman who’d never even fired a weapon before, let alone kill. Driven by the desire to free his captive friends (who are just as♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥y as Jason is) from Rook Island’s vicious human traffickers, Jason struggles to retain his humanity with his transformation into a bloodthirsty killing machine. Jason’s emotional struggle takes the game to some surprisingly dark places while eccentric characters and astounding voice-acting keep the world alive. Michael Mando’s performance as the charismatic Vaas provides one of the greatest video game villains in recent years.
Gameplay is wicked fun – a plethora of upgradeable weapons, sprawling skill trees, random encounters, and varying play-styles ensures that no two encounters will ever be the same – and gives the player the liberty of handling whatever, however they desire. There’s nothing more exhilarating that stealthily picking off pirates one by one with a bow and silent takedowns as the remaining enemies panic. As Jason and I made the transition from hunted to hunter, I found myself killing not for survival but for fun. As Jason explains killing, “It feels like winning.” Far Cry 3 offers an interesting commentary on the desensitizing sensation that gamers feel while killing, an aspect that most games rarely acknowledge. Other franchises play it safe by releasing a carbon copy of a previous with a new coat of paint. Far Cry 3 boldly screams “♥♥♥♥ THAT” and offers a banquet of violent diversity. Take this game as a cordial invitation into the heart of insanity, down the rabbit hole.

FarCry 3 is a game I wanted to like, every review said it's awesome. So naturally I bought into the hype, normally a single player game either bores me in an hour or two or gets completed in 4-5hours.
FC3 is different, because I want to play the whole damn thing again and the first time took 22hours. It actually is as amazing as reviewers say. It has a nice flow to the story, and you aren't forced into mission after mission, pick them up when you want, have a break, go hunt a bear, regret that decision, but at least you now have a bigger loot bag, or can hold more weapons.
The tiny little interactions, the massive islands to explore and the constant want for more kept me coming back. If one thing bores you, go and try something else in another part, liberate a camp, hunt a croc with a machete.
Along with the fact it's actually a PC game. The visuals are stunning, sure you need a PC to power them, but what would a PC game be if it didn't push hardware. The options to change things like FOV are sorely missed in many games and it's refreshing to see someone, especially Ubisoft, make things right.
TL:DR Farcry 3 is a solid single player experience, with hours upon hours of story and side missions, giving you a choice on how you play the game. Add in the stunning scenery and gorgeous art you will keep coming back for more.

The bad: The crafting system is extremely basic. All of the menus are finnicky at best and late-game inventory management can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ There isn't much of a sense of progression regarding your weapons as you're given access to the vast majority of the game's weapons right off the bat. Money quickly becomes completely useless as you can obtain every single weapon (your primary money sink) by just playing the game. At times the game can feel a bit easy, I personally played through on the hardest difficulty to amend this. I also found myself disappointed by the storyline after the end of the second act. It isn't that the story becomes particularly bad, it's just that I feel like there was so much potential that wasn't taken advantage of.
The good: It's incredibly easy to become immersed in the world partly thanks to the gorgeous graphical fidelity and aesthetic, as well as the impressive first person animations. The sfx on the guns is amazing and makes for some very satisfying gunplay. The stealth takedown system is just as satisfying. The game even rewards you for using stealth which is without a doubt more difficult than going in Rambo style. The way animals interact with each other (and other humans) is pretty awesome too. I also think that the first two acts of the story have some awesome writing.
I figure it would take between 50-60 hours to do absolutely everything in the game, but most people will have gotten to a stopping point in about 35-45. I personally really liked it and think it's worth playing.

One of the best, if not the best, games of 2012. It irons out all of the kinks that previous Far Cry titles have had (e.g. awkward animations and obtrusive game mechanics), delivers an original story with diverse and believable characters, and aso looks damned beautiful to boot. Doing the side missions which unveil different parts of the map are repetitive and sometimes even tedious, but even then the game rewards you with gun unlocks and showing you where to find collectible items. The hunting and crafting system is also a fun time sink, letting you take your gathered items from hunting and gathering and turning them into useful material such as holsters that let you carry more weapons, grenade and rocket packs which let you carry more of each, and even larger rucksacks, which allow you to carry more loot which you can turn into even more stuff. There is even a skill tree which you can turn experience earned for different abilities, and while it is not a particularly new or innovative idea, it is a breath of fresh air for a first person shooter to include one. Far Cry 3 is a refreshing, cathartic experience. Try it out!

Far Cry 3 improves upon its predecessor in almost every way. The map, while still large, does not feel arduous to cross. There is much to see and do on every journey and the fast travel system means you spend more time in firefights and less time driving along empty roads.
The first half of the game gets a little repetitive. Liberate outpost, capture radio tower, complete side missions, rinse repeat. It is in the second half, however, where everything comes to life. The story explodes into a fantastic series of story and mission quests that build towards a very enjoyable finale. Side missions are still available and the path of the hunter quests are worth doing until equipment is fully upgraded. Sadly there is little reason to seek the hidden items apart from a minor experience boost for doing so.
The unique skills in the tattoo tree add some variety but the opportunities to use them are few and far between. More often than not you’ll find yourself picking off enemies with an assault rifle or sniper and then cleaning up with a shotgun or SMG.
One of the best aspects of Far Cry 3 are the rich characters. They have unique personalities that really stand out and give richness to interactions and their parts in the larger story. The best of these is Citra, the alluring and slightly unstable leader of the Rakyat. The contrasts drawn between her and Vaas add some entertainment between missions.
The crafting system in FC3 is accessible and the items created are very useful. Syringes provide valuable boosts and abilities and it is wise to keep a full stock at all times.
Overall I look back at the experience fondly and will remember some of the moments and action sequences for some time to come. Bravo!

An open-world first person shooter with light RPG elements that took a generous dose of LSD. If Far Cry 2 was too serious, Far Cry 3 almost went full retard. At its best, it is brilliant, crazy and fun.
Some characters are excellent (Vaas and Sam), others are hard to tolerate, but in general the characters are varied and interesting. The missions are quite fun as well, the less sense it makes, the more fun they are (that level where you burn a marijuana field with a flamethrower to the sounds of Skrillex). The story is not terrible, but it only works best when the player does not take it seriously and assumes everything is satire, otherwise it's pretty cringe-worthy.
Unfortunately, Far Cry 3 did not inherit some of Far Cry 2's greatest acomplishments. The fire effects, foilage interaction (bending of leaves when you walk through them) and enviroment destructibility are simply not as good as the predecessor, probably the price of polish and console optimization. I'm a bit disappointed to see that NPCs can't be wounded to bait its comrades anymore, but I suppose it doesn't fit the tone of the new game. Buddies are also gone, in favour of more reliable but less impressive scripted sequences. While the AI's ability to detect players in Far Cry 2 was infuriatingly erratic, stealth in Far Cry 3 is a bit on the easy side, that might change when you remove the indicators but the game is built upon the assumption that you have them on. It's nice to see rock throwing is back.
Most other aspects of Far Cry 3 are darn good though. Animations of NPCs are great, the general AAA game standard. Movement feels fluid, you can identify the "grab ledges" easily and they work almost all the time even without you waiting for the "press space to jump" prompt. The classic sprint and slide is accompanied by modern favourites like mantling over low obstacles and they work as intended. I like the inclusion of interactive wildlife and they occasionally result in some very impressive emergent play when they attack either you or the NPCs. Some objectives have caged animals for you to unleash upon the guards, which offers some always welcome variety in clearing the checkpoints. Traversing the map is easy, every checkpoint you capture is a fast travel location, radio towers have zip lines, vehicles are plentiful and many high points have gliders begging to be used. Needless to say, travel is much less tedious than in Far Cry 2. Weapon variety is great and gunplay is very competent, but it's a bit annoying that you have to wait until you reach the second part of the game to unlock all the weapons. You only really spend money on weapon customization and unique weapon variants because deactivating towers gives you free weapons, I actually enjoy this since customizing stuff is fun. Making them free upon deactivating towers is slightly questionable for balance, but greatly reduces the tedium of having to grind money because of the most annoying part of the game: the crafting.
The crafting system is arbitrary and bizzare, you have to skin animals and collect enough skins from specific animals to craft ammo pouches (each type has its own pouch, ie. rockets, arrows, bullets, grenades, etc.). The suspension of logic that a second weapon holster (for example) can only be made from boar and goat skin does not result in the game becoming any more fun or challenging; it is simply tedious. When your crafting recipe requires a certain hide, you need to consult your map with conveniently marked out animal icons and run around the island to find that animal, for each species. Playing a modded version with no animal markers is insanity. Why is the amount of money I hold artificially limited? To justify the crafting of wallets? Why does looting corpses give you unstackable junk that can only be sold for small change? Why not let you stack "small" items like leaves and junk like poker chips and plaing cards? Why have junk at all? Add on a clunky inventory management screen with bad sorting and requires you to double confirm to discard a piece of junk; frustration is bound to occur. It appears to me that the game was designed to be a more hardcore experience (like number 2), but later dumbed down to appeal to the less hardcore player halfway through. There is nothing wrong with making an easy and fun game, but the parts that are stuck in between or contradict are simply annoying to both parties.
The game isn't perfect, but it is fun. Silently taking down a checkpoint or going into an objective guns blazing is satisfying. The game gives you enough options for versatility in playstyle without compromising polish, which is a great achievement.

Excellent game; basically Far Cry 1's environment with an enhanced Far Cry 2's open world gameplay. It doesn't feel at all like a grind and many of the obnoxious repetitive FC2 mechanics have been reworked or removed. The story is good, gameplay is great, and there are plenty of mods on the ubisoft forums that enhance realism and difficulty for those who want a challenge. 80+ hours of gameplay.

In response to the widespread criticism of Far Cry 2, Ubisoft responded with Far Cry 3, which essentially addressed each of the criticisms to the core, and yet I think also by doing so, also sent out a bit of an annoyed message to their consumers that they would rather choose empowerment than a different story. They made a great game though, and before you even read any of my further points, if you like open world FPS's then just put this on your wishlist already because it's as solid as they come and you will not regret it (also, if you want more of a challenge, I'd highly recommend the Ziggy's mod, which removes a lot of the gamey-ness and adds a bit more challenge to what was generally received as a simplistic game).
With that out of the way, it's time to spout nonsense.
Where Far Cry 2 is a game about the sheer lack of power an individual holds within a wider conflict, and the evils war produces, Far Cry 3 is the complete opposite, lauding the power of the individual to fix everything and represent a greater good. It's empowerment gaming at its most blatant, with you gaining mystical powers (such as 'maybe I should stab more than one person at a time) through a tatoo. Instead of Far Cry 2s constantly respawning checkpoints, once you take a checkpoint out in Far Cry 3, the entire area is cleared forever (so be careful if you want to get into plenty of conflict as this can easily lead to a completely safe island devoid of baddies pretty quickly). The weapon degradation is gone from Far Cry 2, and is replaced by the attachments system, allowing a small degree of customisation to your weapons that essentially to me amounted to 'put a silencer and a sight on it, and boom'. Weapon unlocking itself can be through money or the radio towers scattered about the island, which literally rain free guns down onto you, and are in that respect.. quite nice. In fact the only thing I can see that is the same between the two games is the fire mechanics, and the Far Cry trope of being in first person at all times.
So basically they're two very different beasts. I have to admit though the open world is phenomenal, with semi-interesting collectables, a stealth system that is pretty intuitive and works really well in practice, and wildlife that can ♥♥♥♥ up your day or theirs, with hilarious results regardless. The story missions themselves are all very solid, the side missions aren't, though they give nice monetary rewards. The characters in the game are very well written, with the conflict basically being told through a very small set of individuals you can relate to or hate, depending - Vaas of course being an iconic enough figure by now that he needs no such introduction. All in all when it comes to the gameplay and setup itself, you can easily lose hours in this, and that's absolutely great. In fact, my flaws come in very minor situations, that is something I've termed 'melee-locking', and the ever infamous quick time events, which make up the boss battles of this game, and essentially run the incredibly dangerous risk of ruining the scene if you cannot react fast enough (I suspect because they felt the player should at least have some input in their very well crafted cinematic, oh well, I don't think a straight up gun-fight would have been an interesting fight, but I still feel deep down that there must be a better way than QTEs to solve this situation).
As for melee-locking? Well in some games, mostly fighting games, you can stun lock enemies with certain moves, making them unable to react. In Far Cry 3, the melee button is both powerful and capable of instantly killing the enemy, or completely missing, with you then locked in a very slow animation, unable to do anything whilst the enemy gleefully feeds you bullets. It's annoying and the way I most often died in an otherwise unchallenging but fun game. Story wise, they tried to be Spec Ops: The Line, but in the process made something not quite as poignant, but damn good to say the least.
Enough being a misery though, this game is pretty much essential like I said at the beginning, it's crafted very well indeed on most levels, and deserves credit for that at least.

Far Cry 3 is definitely one of the BEST EVER games that I've played.. and This is why:
Story: 10/10 - The story in Far Cry 3 is phenomenal.. I enjoyed ever mission more than the other and it never got boring. Fantastic. Absolutely fantastic. Beautiful visuals, excellent physics, great gunplay and an above average story for a shooter. To be honest, I wasn't expecting much from this game after seeing what they (Ubisoft Montreal) did to Far Cry 2 but I was definitely wrong. Everything that was wrong in Far Cry 2 such as tedious travel, terrible story, horrible checkpoints and saving, they've fixed and expanded on. They've added all sort of animals this time around and they actually serve a purpose instead of just being eye candy. You can skin them to either craft new items or sell them. They've added more RPG elements such as a level up system as well as unlockable skills that you can get as well as numerous quests you can undertake. The main story quest are fantastic though it's thrown at you rather than you casually getting into it. The sidequests not so much. Most of the sidequests are more like minigames in which there are only 3 where you go and kill a wanted criminal, hunt down a dangerous animal, or do this stupid as hell supply drop race where you have to deliver supplies within a limited amount of time.
The real selling point of this game is the massive island you get to explore. It has a living ecosystem (as living as you can get it without it getting boring and/or tedious) in which animals and NPCs interact with each other. It is quite common for NPCs, both friendly and unfriendly, to engage tigers, bears and other danger animals as well as each other. This large area provides you with a number of ways in which you can go about completing your objective. If you want to sneak through undetected such as sneaking through the grass and throwing rocks to distract the enemy, you certainly can. If you want to go in guns blazing, you can certainly do that too in which case you have a sizable arsenal weapons you can use to do so.
The multiplayer is as generic as it gets but with♥♥♥♥♥♥poor hit detection, mostly do it using a peer-to-peer connection rather than using dedicated servers makes multiplayer a forgettable experience. The co-op isn't much better with you being forced to go through this linear environment rather than having the wide open sandbox you have in the single player campaign but it's still playable. The level editor is great and very easy to use.
If you want a great open world FPS with a decent story, this is one of the best to date. If you want multiplayer, you should look elsewhere.

Also, if you take out all of the enemy outposts (which is good, right? less enemies + fast travel spots...), you end up with NO ONE TO FIGHT (except animals, they're still out there).
Co-Op is... Cute, but it's very linear and simple, so it's not very special.
Multiplayer is nice, really, but the thing I can say about it is that it has some good features, it lacks some other features that would make it much better, and that it's destined to be a low population thing after a short while.
Overall, the game is good, but it feels that the things that the marketing of the game capitalized on weren't shown and used enough, so as much as I like the game, it's really quite the disappoitment, at least for me.

It's nice when a Triple A title gets the attention it deserves for PC and they don't just make a lazy port from consoles.  They actually did a great job on utilizing PCs potential without requiring you to have a NASA computer to run it.  Plus it's cheaper on Steam than getting it for a console and you're getting better quality.  I can run this on Ultra settings with no issue, and I don't have a super computer.  They did a great job making sure they could develop their software to grab a wider audience.  And yes you can easily plug in an Xbox 360 wired controller to use, that's what I do. Oh and run it in "borderless window" in the options, it should run even better.  It will still look full screen display.
Note: Crysis was suppose to be the sequel to the 1st Far Cry. A lot of the fans of the 1st game call Crysis "FarCrysis"  So what you can expect is top quality in everything.  the AI will relentlessly search for you if you turn tail and run, basically think of it in their perspective  - "Some dude just ran thru here with a gun and was taking pot shots at us, you better freaking believe we are not going to easily forget this and hunt that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ down." Structures, vegetation and other aspects of the environment are destructible (it can at times remind you of the scene in "Predator" when they are mowing down the jungle)  And they even included a map editor that you can use to make custom maps to share with he community and friends for MP.
The premise, like the other Far Cry titles, has been to attempt to give it a more realistic style without it becoming a simulator.  It borrows on some simulation, but still plays like an FPS.  For this title i think that they wanted to throw the player in a situation like it was You in this particular situation and environment.  The protagonist is not a mercenary nor an ex Green Beret turned mercenary.  He is (you are) at the start,  someone that is thrust into a bad situation and you have to deal as you go through the game.

The beginning of this game is god-awful. I was seriously worried I'd f***ed up with this purchase. The first 3-4 hours of the game are nothing more than a glorified tutorial. "Oh what's that? You've played a shooter before? Well f*** you. Here, have another popup that won't leave your screen until you watch a tutorial on how to aim and shoot. Actually, you'll probably screw it up. You'd better let me do it."
I've never played a game that so badly tried to sabotage all my attempts to actually enjoy it. "What's that? You want to explore the beautiful open world jungle? Well f*** you, you're on another tutorial mission. Leave this general area and you fail and have to restart."
It takes a few hours, but the game does eventually entrust you with the ability to actually play it. Popups become less invasive, the whole 'Don't leave the mission area' bulls*** becomes more relaxed, and you can actually start exploring. Once you get to that part, the game is an absolute blast to play.
My favorite thing to do was take over enemy outposts. Sometimes I ran in guns blazing, sometimes I silently took down my foes with a knife and bow, and sometimes roving bands of tigers or bears killed everyone for me. It sounds ridiculous but it works and is a lot of fun.
The story is awful, though. I mean, none of the Far Cry games have had good stories, but this one is easily the worst. The protagonist isn't even the slightest bit likeable and neither are any of his friends. The supporting characters have more personality and are more enjoyable than anyone from the core story. Which is bad because the game forces you to watch every single cutscene regardless of whether you actually want to, which you won't.
Overall it's a good game and I enjoyed it. But this is definitely one of those instances where you have to give it a few hours before it gets good. The game is at its best when it releases its death grip on the reins and hands them over to you. But be prepared to hate every story mission and cutscene, because they're terrible.

Words cannot describe Far Cry 3. I loved Far Cry 2 but still found several problems that seemed to have been fixed in this latest release. Far Cry 3 is as close to perfect as you can get.

First of all the environment (apparently 10 times larger than the African setting in Far Cry 2) is teaming with life. It really feels like a living breathing world complete with various different animals, plants, biomes, and underwater reefs. There’s even a decent amount of indoor sections such as caves and various buildings. Far Cry 3’s Dunia 2 engine is one of the most impressive engines I've ever seen. They've made sure it’s stable, well optimized and looking great no matter where you go. There’s a day and night cycle with an impressive sky box, creating quite possibly the best looking game world I've ever seen.
The characters and story are primarily why I bought Far Cry 3. The main villain Vaas is a really interesting character and the voice acting for all the characters I've met so far, is spot on. Believable, realistic, I constantly want to know more about these people. I’ve barely touched the main story, but so far it’s extremely interesting and keeps me wanting to find out more.
The gameplay is another amazing thing about Far Cry 3. There’s an in depth stealth system that features tagging enemies, and line of sight to allow for stealthier kills whilst using the environment to hide. It’s quite similar to Hitman Absolution, showing a reticule that fills up as the enemy notices you. I love this added feature, now I can hide in the jungle and take enemies by surprise instead of always starting these huge firefights like in Far Cry 2. The guns (most are customizable) perform so well. They sound realistic and recoil realistically.
Your character can upgrade various stats as he progresses by gaining experience from kills and quests. This just makes the game even more interesting and adds to replayability. This RPG element has given some reviewers the idea that Far Cry 3 is like Skyrim with guns. They’re not far off. FC3 is unique though, all of these good points come together to create a different experience from anything I’ve ever played before. It feels like Far Cry 2, but with so many more added features that make it significantly improved upon.
I’ve already said more than enough to make you buy this game, so go and do it now! You won’t regret the masterpiece that is Far Cry 3.
(Also, I am now genuinely terrified of sharks and crocodiles thanks to this game.)

This game is amazing. It takes the best features from (most) well-known games, presents them within the game in a perfect blend, and stays true to the original Farcry experience with vast exploration and endless hours of fun.
::HUNTING::
Hunting is reminiscent of Red Dead Redemption; you can scour the world for animals and skin them for different kinds of animal loot. Unlike RDR, a majority of FarCry 3's animals have purpose and are deadly. Moreover, the game doesn't revolve around just killing these animals; the beasts can help or hinder you on missions. Hide in the bushes and lure some Komodo Dragons into an enemy camp and watch them get overrun, or be prepared to get ambushed unawares by a jaguar or shark while trying to get somewhere.
::AC Resemblance::
The "Wanted Dead" missions bear similarity to Assassin's Creed, forcing you to stealth/knife kill enemies, however this is made easier in the first-person shooter world via the ability to tag enemies with your camera. Once tagged, an enemy icon indicating that specific enemy's type will display above their heads (sniper, charger, assault) and they will be visible through objects and terrain.
You reveal the world on your map by platforming to the top of radio towers and "syncronizing" your map. Just like in AC, a region around the tower will be revealed on your map, and a beautiful cinematic displaying the area will play. A significant difference between the tower cinematics of both games is that FC3 will glide over cool, interesting, or important places in an effort to highlight them and encourage exploration.
::CRAFTING + CUSTOMIZATION::
The loot gathered from animals is used to upgrade essentials: Wallet Size, Weapon-Carry Capacity, etc. Crafting things from herbs, animals, or parts makes for some interesting upgrades and accessories, but a majority of the customization comes from the skill tree and customizing your weapon in safe houses. There is also customization in Multiplayer.
The Skill tree follows three branches: Combat, Survival, and Stealth. You level up by killing goons, doing missions, or hunting big game. Skills are aesthetically displayed on your character's arm as a tattoo, which grows with each new skill you get (the images on the tattoo depend on the skill you get).
::TRAVEL::
Travel time is reduced by being able to teleport to safe houses. Getting around the world is made less-mundane with the addition of paragliders and a robust selection of land/water vehicles.
::STEALTH::
Stealth is possible on every mission (I'm currently doing it and haven't come across one that is impossible to stealth-win). The ability to tag enemies with your camera makes this easier, but still challenging enough to be fun. Being able to free animals from cages with your bow and arrow and causing mass panic in camps is amazing.
::MULTIPLAYER::
The map editor is pretty awesome, especially considering the graphical beauty of FarCry 3.
Multiplayer is pretty a standard, B-Grade feature in FarCry 3. However, Co-Op is fun and multiplayer paired with the map editor can open doors for some intuitive and interesting gameplay.
::STORY::
Story is a little lacking, but the main villain is pretty awesome. This is a major downside to the game if you are looking for a good story. However, the story isn't so terrible that it will ruin your expierence.
::OVERALL::
Definitely try this game if you are a fan of first person shooters; especially if you liked FarCry 2.
